text_en: that too much was let out in a muddled flood. Then later, meddlesome descendants came along, not knowing to cherish the family treasure; each one staked body and life, raising dust on level ground and stirring waves on clear waters, chaotically scattering flowers in empty space, deceiving and bewildering eyes, passing errors from mouth to mouth. Public cases multiplied in many forms. Tiantong and Xuedou's leftover spittle was already bitter enough and not gathered back in; Yuanwu and Wansong's dream-talk was again too much of it was not awake. Fortunately, the old man Qingliang long understood the calamity of not settling the ancestors' unfinished business. Today his disciples, with ancient countenances, have brought out all the old curios, divided them into four houses, and newly recut the blocks. Alas, stolen goods and private hoards are now in plain sight; the true thieves cannot escape. I dare ask for the vajra jewel-sword to cut it all off at one stroke. Then take these fragmentary commentarial words and, together with the people of the four seas, let them make a song of peace.
Inscribed by Luo Rufang of Jinqi Creek in the Southern City

text_en: still. This is a separate transmission outside the teachings; the true meaning within it is hardly something human language can describe even one ten-thousandth part of. Yet for opening later students, expounding Dharma, and benefiting beings, this is especially apt for meeting capacities and leading them into awakening. The old carved edition of the Four Houses sayings was not very skillfully engraved. Its format was cramped and crude, and the comments and notes were constricted, to the distress of readers. Yet it was already like ascending a great a jewel mountain and entering the Huazang sea, groping with all one’s strength and never begrudging the effort. In the imperial capital, Chan elders often waved their fly-whisks and discoursed on the school, yet recently things have grown blurred and hard to distinguish. The Dharma lecturer Juexu, arousing great vast compassion, wished to commission the block-carvers anew, but his strength did not suffice, so he consulted me. I truly had long cherished this wish, so how could I not give my full effort? Thus workers were gathered and three parts were carved. Like-minded monks and laymen carved the remaining one. Then the old devices of pointed thrusts, staff-shouts, raised brows, and lifted fingers became all the more clear and penetrating in their leaks and openings. Then Master Jue’s intention was fulfilled, and the merit too is boundless. I only fear that I am unable to be of service in this task; what further deliberation is there to be had?

text_en: Preface to Elder Wansong’s Commentarial Chanting on Tiantong Jue’s Verses on Ancient Cases, the Congrong Hermitage Record In former days when I was in the capital, there were many elder Chan masters. Only the Reverend Chenggong of Sheng'an

text_zh: 昔予在京師時。禪伯甚多。唯聖安澄公和尚。 神氣嚴明。言辭磊落。予獨重之。故嘗訪以祖 道。屢以古昔尊宿語緣中所得者叩之。澄公 間有許可者。予亦自以為得。及遭憂患以來。 功名之心。束之高閣。求祖道愈亟。遂再以前 事。訪諸聖安。聖安翻案不然所見。予甚惑 焉。聖安從容謂予曰。昔公位居要地。又儒者 多不諦信佛書。惟搜摘語緣。以資談柄。故予 不敢苦加鉆鎚耳。今揣君之心。果為本分事 以問予。予豈得猶襲前愆不為苦口乎。予老 矣。素不通儒。不能教子。有萬松老人者。儒 釋兼備。宗說精通。辯才無礙。君可見之。予 既謁萬松。杜絕人迹。屏斥家務。雖祁寒大 暑。無日不參。焚膏繼晷。廢寢忘餐者。幾三 年。誤被法恩。謬膺子印。以湛然居士從源 目之。其參學之際。機鋒罔測。變化無窮。巍 巍然若萬仞峯莫可攀仰。滔滔然若萬頃波 莫能涯際。瞻之在前忽焉在後。迴視平昔所 學。皆塊礫耳。噫登東山而小魯。登泰山而小 天下者。豈虛語哉。其未入閫域者。聞是語必 謂。予忘本好異也。唯屏山閑閑。其相照乎。 爾後奉命赴行在。扈從西征。與師相隔。不知 其幾千里也。師平昔法語偈頌。皆法兄隆公 所收。今不復得其󱡐。吾宗有天童者頌古百 篇。號為絕唱。予堅請萬松評唱是頌開發後 學。前後九書。間關七年。方蒙見寄。予西域伶 仃數載。忽受是書。如醉而醒。如死而甦。踴躍 歡呼。東望稽顙。再四披繹。撫卷而歎曰。萬松 來西域矣。其片言隻字。咸有指歸。結欵出眼。 高冠今古。足為萬世之模楷。非師範人天權 衡造化者。孰能與於此哉。予與行宮數友。旦 夕游泳於是書。如登大寶山入華藏海。互珍 奇物廣大悉備。左逢而右遇。目富而心飫。豈 可以世間語言。形容其萬一耶。予不敢獨擅 其美。思與天下共之。京城唯法弟從祥者。與 僕為忘年交。謹致書。請刊行于世以貽來者。 迺序之曰。佛祖諸師。埋根千丈。機緣百則見 世生苗。天童不合抽枝。萬松那堪引蔓。湛然 向枝蔓上。更添芒索。穿過尋香逐氣者鼻孔。 絆倒行玄體妙底脚跟向去。若要脚跟點地 鼻孔撩天。却須向這葛藤裏穿過始得。甲申 中元日。漆水移剌楚才晉卿。敘於西域阿里 馬城。
text_en: had a grave and lucid bearing, and his words were open and forthright. I alone esteemed him deeply, and so I often visited him concerning the ancestral Way. Again and again I questioned him with what I had gained from the sayings and encounter-cases of revered elders of old. Master Chenggong would sometimes approve of them, and I too thought I had attained something. But since meeting with sorrow and hardship, I put away the mind that sought rank and fame on a high shelf, and my search for the ancestral Way grew ever more urgent. So again I took up the former matters and asked Sheng'an about them. Sheng'an reversed the old judgments and no longer saw them that way. I was greatly perplexed. Then Sheng'an calmly said to me: In the past, you held an important post, and moreover Confucian scholars often did not truly trust Buddhist books, but only picked through sayings and cases to furnish topics for talk. Therefore I did not dare apply the hammer and drill too harshly. But now, judging your mind, you truly ask for the sake of the fundamental matter, in questioning me. How could I still repeat my former fault and not speak bitter medicine plainly? I am old now. I have never been versed in Confucian learning and cannot teach you. There is an elder called Wansong, who in both Confucian and Buddhist learning is fully equipped, thoroughly versed in both the school and its teachings, and unhindered in eloquence. You may go see him. I after I had paid respects to Wansong, cut off all visitors and set aside household affairs. Though in bitter cold or great heat, there was not a day without practice. Burning the lamp to continue past daylight, neglecting sleep and forgetting meals, for nearly three years. By mistake I received the Dharma's grace and unworthily bore the seal of a disciple, and as the layman Zhanran Congyuan he regarded me. In the course of training under him, his devices and sharp points were unfathomable, his transformations inexhaustible. Lofty, towering like a ten-thousand-fathom peak none could climb or gaze up to; surging and vast like ten-thousand-acre waves with no one able to reach their shore. Looking at him, he was before me, then suddenly behind me. Turning back to what I had formerly studied, it was all but clods and gravel. Ah, to climb East Mountain and find Lu small, to climb Mount Tai and find all under heaven small, are these empty words? Those who have not yet entered the inner precinct, on hearing such words, will surely say that I have forgotten my roots and delight in the strange. Only Pingshan Xianxian will perhaps understand one another with me. After that I was ordered to go to the imperial camp and accompanied the western campaign. Separated from my teacher, I knew not how many thousands of li lay between us. The teacher's past Dharma sayings and verses were all collected by our Dharma elder brother, Master Long. He had gathered them, but now I could no longer obtain them. In our lineage there is Tiantong, who composed one hundred verses on ancient cases, 󱡐 acclaimed as peerless songs. I earnestly begged Wansong to comment on and sing through these verses to open up later students. In all, through nine letters back and forth, after hardships over seven years, I finally received the favor of having it sent to me. I in the western regions, lonely and adrift for several years, suddenly received this book, and it was like sobering from drunkenness, like reviving from death. Leaping with joy, I cried out in delight, bowed toward the east, read and reread it again and again, stroked the scroll and sighed: Wansong has come to the western regions. Every phrase and every single character has its point and destination, its knot and opening, its eye. It stands above present and past alike, sufficient to serve as a model for ten thousand ages. If not one who can guide humans and gods and wield the balance of creation and transformation, who could have part in this? I and several friends in the traveling palace, morning and evening, swam and wandered in this book, as if climbing a great treasure mountain and entering the Flower Treasury Sea, where rare and wondrous things, vast and complete, were all present. To the left we encountered them, to the right we met them; the eyes were enriched and the heart filled. How could worldly language describe even one ten-thousandth of it? I dared not keep its beauty for myself alone, and wished to share it with all under heaven. In the capital there is only my Dharma younger brother Congxiang, who with me has a friendship beyond age. I respectfully sent him a letter, asking that it be carved and published in the world, to bequeath it to those who come later. Thus I wrote this preface, saying: The Buddhas, patriarchs, and all the masters buried their roots a thousand fathoms deep; in one hundred encounter-cases there appeared seedlings born into the world. Tiantong should not have drawn out branches, and how could Wansong bear to pull out vines? Zhanran upon those branches and vines further added thorny cords, piercing through the nostrils of those who chase fragrance and follow scents. He trips the heels of those who walk mystery and embody subtlety. If you want your heels to touch the ground while your nostrils stir the heavens, then you must pass through this tangle of vines before it can be done. In the jiashen year, on the Zhongyuan day, Yila Chucai Jinqing of Qishui wrote this preface in the western regions, at Ali ma City.

text_en: Letter Sending the Commentarial Chanting on Tiantong’s Congrong Hermitage Record to Layman Zhanran In our tradition there are Xuedou and Tiantong, just as in Confucius' school there were Ziyou and Zixia. Of these two masters'

text_zh: 吾宗有雪竇天童。猶孔門之有游夏。二師之 頌古。猶詩壇之李杜。世謂雪竇有翰林之才。 蓋採我華。而不摭我實。又謂不行萬里地。不 讀萬卷書。毋閱工部詩。言其博贍也。擬諸天 童老師頌古。片言隻字。皆自佛祖淵源流出。 學者罔測也。柏山大隱集。出其事迹。間有疎 闊不類者。至於拈提。苟簡但據款而已。萬松 昔嘗評唱。兵革以來廢其祖󱡐。邇來退居燕 京報恩。旋築蝸舍。榜曰從容庵。圖成舊緒。適 值湛然居士勸請成之。老眼昏華。多出口占。 門人筆受。其間繁載機緣事迹。一則旌天童 學海波瀾。附會巧便。二則省學人檢討之功。 三則露萬松述而不作非臆斷也。竊比佛果 碧巖集。則篇篇皆有示眾為備。竊比圓通覺 海錄。則句句未嘗支離為完。至于著語出眼 筆削之際。亦臨機不讓。壬午歲杪。湛然居士 書至。堅要拈出。不免家醜外揚。累吾累汝也。 癸未年上已日。萬松野老因風附寄。不宣。
text_en: verse comments on old cases, they are like Li Bai and Du Fu in the poetry world. The world says Xuedou had the talent of a Hanlin scholar. Yet this picks my blossoms and does not gather my fruit. It is also said that if one does not travel ten thousand li, and does not read ten thousand scrolls, one should not read the Minister of Works' poetry, speaking of its breadth and richness. As for comparing this to Tian- tong Laoshi's verse comments on old cases, every phrase and every single word flows forth from the deep source of the Buddhas and patriarchs. Students cannot fathom them. The Bai-shan Dayin Collection sets forth his deeds, but among them there are some things sparse, broad, and unlike the truth. As for the bringing up and presenting of cases, it is careless and brief, relying only on headings. Wansong once tried to comment and sing them; since the time of war and arms, this ancestral work was abandoned. Lately, having retired to Yan- jing at Bao'en, I then built a little snail-shell hut and named it the Congrong Hermitage. Planning to complete the old undertaking, just then I met the layman Zhanran, who urged and requested that it be finished. My old eyes are dim and blurred, so much was dictated by mouth. Disciples took it down in writing. In it are abundantly recorded causes, conditions, and biographical incidents: first, to honor Tiantong's vast learning and surging waves, and his skillful aptness in fitting things together; second, to spare students the labor of investigation and review. Third, to show that Wansong transmits and does not invent, and that this is not arbitrary judgment. I privately compare it to Foguo's Blue Cliff Record, in that every section has an address to the assembly in full. I privately compare it to Yuantong Jue's Record of the Sea, in that sentence by sentence it has never been rambling or disjointed, but complete. As for added sayings and critical eye- points, and the moments of writing and trimming, I likewise did not yield when facing the occasion. At the end of the renwu year, Layman Zhanran sent a letter, firmly insisting it be brought forth. So I could not avoid airing family ugliness abroad, burdening me and burdening you. On the Shangsi Day of the guiwei year, the rustic old man Wansong sends this along by the wind and so dispatches it, without further elaboration.

If so, then it has become three stretches already. What is the single stretch of true wind? Moreover, each of you has a share in it, so you may well investigate it carefully. He also says, Unbroken, the transforming mother tends the loom-shuttle. The transforming mother is another name for the transforming artisan who makes things. The Confucian and Daoist teachings take one qi as their source. The Buddhist stream takes as its basis the one mind. Guifeng said: Original qi too is made by mind and all is included within the objective aspect of ālaya- consciousness. Wansong says: This is the true lineage of Caodong, the life-pulse of patriarchs and Buddhas. The pivotal knot bites at the hub-mouth; where it turns is subtle and hidden. Fine thread is spit from the shuttle’s belly. In use it is close-woven and exact. How could it be spoken of in the same day as false causes and causelessness? Then, turning to the later lines, he versifies the World-Honored One’s rich reserve, saying: Woven into ancient brocade, it contains the image of spring. Although it is like insects boring wood and by chance making patterns, still what can one do? Build the cart behind closed doors, and when it goes out the gate it fits the ruts. At the end Mañjuśrī overturned it for him, yet says: Helpless before the East Lord’s leaking out— what can be done? Mañjuśrī strikes the gavel and the World-Honored One immediately descends the seat. But when Kāśyapa strikes the gavel, then hundreds of thousands of Mañjuśrīs appear. Since it is equally such a moment, why is it that the gathering in and letting go differ? Tell me: where is the East Lord’s point of leakage? Earnestly, for untie the clove-knot and let the carefree spring at the branch-tips come forth.

text_en: seven years you should go to China and set forth the great Dharma medicine, directly pointing to those of highest capacity. Be careful not to go too quickly, lest it decline before the sun sets. And when you arrive, do not stay in the South. There they only delight in conditioned merit and do not see the Buddha-principle. Even if you do reach there, you must not remain long. Indeed, there was the matter of roaming Liang and crossing into Wei, lingering dully for nine years. In recent times, in Cizhou, the robe and Dharma were entrusted to Renshan. Shan said, I am not such a man. Zhou said, If you are not such a man, then it will not bring harm upon you. Because Shan's feeling for the milk of the Dharma was deep, he bowed and accepted it. Zhou then said again, Since you are thus, first of all you must not too easily come forth into the world. If you hasten ahead rashly and act lightly, there will surely be obstacles in between. This and Prajnatara's repeated charge to Bodhidharma about the nine years are one and the same in spirit. Zhexi's verse says: Do not begrudge passing through autumn frost, for the sake of making the flavor last long. Even if picked while still raw, in the end it will not be fragrant. This can serve as a warning for those who come later. But if one is a genuine person of the Way, whether to emerge or withdraw, one knows the right time oneself. Although Emperor Wu did not accord, he set forth a line of questioning, which was not without sharpness. To this day, in monasteries everywhere, when opening the hall and striking the gavel, it is still said: O dragons and elephants in this Dharma assembly, you should contemplate the First Principle. But as for the First Principle truth, is it really something that permits contemplation? Does it permit the question and answer of Emperor Wu and Bodhidharma? Wan- song says: Leave the First Principle aside for the moment; what do you want with holy truth? Tianhuang said: Simply exhaust ordinary feelings, and there is no other holy understanding. The Shurangama says: If you make a holy understanding of it, you at once fall prey to a host of false views. Bodhidharma's saying, Vast emptiness, nothing holy, is exactly this. In the flash of flint and lightning, one may well handle it directly and settle it before one's own eyes. Emperor Wu's stubborn drool would not recede, and he asked further, Who is facing me? On the Liang king's side, this too was well-intentioned. But he did not know that from Bodhidharma's side, it was as if he had been spat on full in the face. So Bodhidharma could not avoid offering another answer: I do not know. Already delicate flowers fade easily; how much more so when frost is added atop snow. When Bodhidharma saw his eyes fixed and stirring, he immediately turned around and took another road. The people of old, whether coming forth or remaining hidden, whether silent or speaking, all did so for the Buddha's work. Later, Emperor Wu truly did come to long for the noble one after the fact, and he personally composed a stele inscription which says: Seeing him, I did not see him. Meeting him, I did not meet him. Now and in the past, I regret it and resent it, I do. Though I am but an ordinary man, I dare to take him as my teacher hereafter. Since Emperor Wu suffered disgrace and flight, and since Bodhidharma returned west, no one has raised up the First Principle truth. Fortunately, there is Tiantong, who brings it forth for the assembly. The verse says:

text_en: divergent, it does not accord with ordinary human feeling. At that time the First Patriarch also used but very little expedient means. He did not realize that if the medicine does not daze and confound, the illness will not be cured. From the start he brought down a thunderbolt hand. But now people have long since indulged in private leniency and forbearance. Thus they fail to be like one who swings the hatchet by the nose and wields the axe. Zhuangzi, escorting a funeral, passed by Huizi's tomb, turned and said to his attendants: A man of Ying once had a dab of white plaster spread on the tip of his nose, as thin as a fly's wing, and had Carpenter Shi chop it off. Carpenter Shi swung his hatchet like the wind. Listening and chopping, he closed his eyes and let his hand move freely, removing all the plaster without injuring the nose. The man of Ying stood there without changing expression. Since you, Master, have died, I no longer have anyone to serve as my target. Then there is the one who, when the pot fell, did not turn his head. In the Later Han, Meng Min was living away from home in Taiyuan and once carried a earthen steamer, which fell to the ground. He did not look back and simply left. Guo Linzong saw this and asked his meaning. He replied: The steamer is already broken. What benefit is there in looking at it? Linzong found him extraordinary for this, and so urged him to travel and study. The meaning is that if Emperor Wu had assented on his own, Bodhidharma would never have bent himself to follow another. If the king of Liang did not accord, he would flick his sleeves and leave at once without regret. In the golden palace he let loose a faceless utterance, and only half was spoken. Nine years at Shaolin with his mouth hanging on the wall, only then was it eighty percent complete. Like the clear autumn moon turning into a frosty wheel, he secretly used the Dharma-eye, until at last in the frosty night the moon falls of itself into the stream before us, naturally and freely, illuminating the Way whose ultimate principle admits no comparison. The Milky Way grows pale, and the Dipper handle hangs down in the night. Tiantong, ascending the hall, said: One point within the circle shines on the utmost subtlety. Where wisdom has no function, there knowledge yet remains. When dependent thought is fully purified and nothing remains to be done, at midnight the river of stars and the Dipper's handle hang down. These two lines are like a mute acting as an interpreter, trying to point it out to people yet unable to speak it forth. If even that cannot be expressed, how much less can it bear teacher and disciple transmission, or medicine and illness treating one another? It turns into having no connection at all. How can one fully uphold the true command and carry it through? Empty flowers waste who knows how many tortoise-hair threads, and the stone woman vainly holds up a needle. Hey

text_zh: 3 東印請祖
text_en: 3. East India Invites the Patriarch Addressing the assembly, he said: The opportunity before signs appear in a kalpa before time—like a turtle facing fire. The separate transmission outside the teachings,

text_zh: 示眾云。劫前未兆之機。烏龜向火。教外別傳 一句。碓嘴生花。且道。還有受持讀誦分也無。
text_en: in a single phrase, makes flowers bloom on a pestle-mouth. Tell me, is there still any share here of receiving, upholding, and reciting scripture, or not?
Raising the case: The king of East India invited the Twenty-seventh Patriarch Prajñātāra to a royal feast.

text_zh: 舉。東印土國王。請二十七祖般若多羅齊 往往償口債去也王問曰。何不看經無功受祿寢食不安祖云。貧 道入息不居陰界。出息不涉眾緣。常轉如 是經。百千萬億卷上來講讚無限勝因。
text_en: The king asked, Why do you not read sutras? The Patriarch said, This poor monk Again and again one goes paying off mouth-debts Receiving pay without merit, one cannot sleep or eat at ease on inhaling does not abide in the skandha-realms; on exhaling does not enter into the myriad conditions. I constantly turn such a sutra, hundreds of thousands of myriads of millions of scrolls. Up to this point, the lecture and praise bring limitless excellent causes
The Master said: The Twenty-seventh Patriarch was first named Jeweled Garland Youth. Because the Twenty-sixth Patriarch

text_zh: 師云。二十七祖初名瓔珞童子。因二十六祖 不如蜜多。與東印土堅固王同輦。問童子曰。 能憶往事否。對曰。我憶往劫與師同居。師演 摩訶般若。我持甚深修多羅。以相代正化故。 俟師於此。祖告王曰。此非小聖。大勢至之應 身也。王命登輦至宮供養。以至披削。祖取般 若修多羅事。命名般若多羅。梁朝以達磨為 觀音。西國以祖師為勢至。唯阿彌陀佛至今 無下落。良久云。豐干饒舌。後因皇家展會。尊 者主席。這老漢顯異惑眾。當時好與掀倒。打 斷葛藤。直待問尊者何不看經。果然放不過。 這老漢也無大人相。把葫蘆馬杓翻騰一上 王便禮拜。識甚痛痒。萬松道。國王貪他一粒 米。尊者失却萬年糧。只知鐵脊撑天。不覺腦 門著地。若要扶起。除是天童。頌云。
text_en: Punyamitra rode in the same carriage with King Jiangu of East India, he asked the boy: Can you remember former events? He replied: I remember that in past kalpas I dwelt with the Master. The Master expounded Mahāprajñā, and I upheld the profound sutras. Because we alternated in carrying on the true teaching, I awaited the Master here. The Patriarch told the king: This is no minor sage; he is an emanation-body of Mahāsthāmaprāpta. The king ordered him into the carriage, brought him to the palace, made offerings to him, and eventually had his hair shaved. The Patriarch took the Prajñā- sutra affair as the basis and named him Prajñātāra. In Liang times they took Bodhidharma to be Guanyin; in the western lands they take this Patriarch to be Mahāsthāmaprāpta. Only Amitābha Buddha, to this day, has no trace to be found. After a long pause, he said: Fenggan was too loose-tongued. Later, because of an imperial assembly, the Venerable One took the chief seat. This old fellow displayed marvels and confused the crowd; at the time it would have been best to overturn him and cut off the vines. But once they asked the Venerable One why he did not read sutras, they truly could not let him off. This old fellow too had no great-man bearing; he just flipped up a gourd and horse-ladle trick, and the king immediately bowed. What does he know of itch or pain? Wansong says: The king greedily wanted one grain of rice from him, and the Venerable One lost the food of ten thousand years. He only knew to prop up heaven with an iron spine, not noticing his skull-gate had struck the ground. If one wants to lift him back up, only Tiantong can do it. He versified it, saying:
A cloud-rhino sporting with the moon, bright and holding its radiance; a wooden horse roaming in spring, swift and unbridled. Secretly linked by a single thread, the pattern is already manifest

text_zh: 雲犀玩月璨含輝暗通一線文彩已彰　木馬游春駿不羈 百花叢裏過一葉不沾身眉底一雙寒碧眼不曾趁蛇蜉隊　看經那到 透牛皮過也明白心起曠劫威音前一箭　英雄力破重 圍射透兩重關妙圓樞口轉靈機何曾動著　寒山忘却來 時路暫時不住如同死人拾得相將携手歸須是當鄉人
text_en: Passing through a thicket of a hundred flowers, not one leaf clings to the body Beneath the brows, a pair of cold blue-green eyes; reading sutras, how could one ever Never joined the swarm chasing snakes and mayflies pierce oxhide? Gone too far A clear bright mind rises; with heroic strength from vast kalpas it breaks through layer upon layer of One arrow before King Awesome-Sound encirclement. Shooting through two barriers At the wondrous round pivot-mouth, numinous functioning turns; Hanshan forgets the road by which he came. When was it ever stirred The way he came. For a moment not abiding, like a dead man Shide joins him, and hand in hand they return. It must be a local man
The Master said: The first two lines, opening the topic, have already versified not abiding in the skandha-realms and not entering the myriad conditions.

text_zh: 師云。破題兩句。頌不居陰界。不涉眾緣已了。 且藏教法數。五陰十二處十八界。喚作三科。 尊者略舉首尾。攝其中間。梵語安那般那。譯 云出息入息。其法有六。一數二隨三止四觀 五還六淨。具如天台止觀。預備不虞者不可 不知。溈山警策道教理未甞措懷。玄道無因 契悟。寶藏論可怜。無價之寶。隱在陰入之坑。 何時得靈光獨耀逈脫根塵去。天童雲犀玩 月燦含輝。古詩有犀因玩月紋生角。好言語 可惜。折合向文才情思上。木馬游春駿不羈。 此頌出息不涉眾緣。可謂善行無轍跡也。眉 底一雙寒碧眼。洛浦道。單明自己法眼未明。 此人只具一隻眼。若要雙眼圓明。除是不居 陰界不涉眾緣。無影林中。高懸日月。不萌 枝上。暗辨春秋始得。看經那到透牛皮。長慶 云。眼有何過。楞嚴經云。汝今諦觀此會聖眾。 用目循歷。其目周視。但如鏡中無別分析。這 裏蹉過。藥山道。底牛皮也須穿透。萬松道。却 具金剛眼。明白心超曠劫。三祖道。但不憎愛 洞然明白。一念萬年受持不盡。鹿門道。遍大 地是學人一卷經。盡乾坤是學人一隻眼。以 這箇眼。讀如是經。千萬億劫常無間斷。萬松 道。看讀不易。英雄力破重圍。後漢王莽遣弟 王尋王邑。至昆陽。圍光武數十重。光武兵弱 而欲降尋邑。邑不肯。光武乃益堅諸將。出兵 却戰。尋邑大敗。尊者文武雙全。出將入相。陰 界眾緣。非但重圍也。妙圓樞口轉靈機。爾雅 樞謂之椳。郭璞注云。門扉樞也。流水不腐。中 樞不蠧。言其活也。尊者未點先行。不撥自轉。 這邊那邊無可不可。天童披沙揀金。分星擘 兩。花判了也。末後兩句更有餘才道。寒山忘 却來時路。拾得相將携手歸。此頌國筵海眾 鑽紙穿窓。尊者老婆略與。鉤簾歸乳燕。穴紙 出癡蠅。用寒山詩。若合符節。詩云。欲得安身 處。寒山可長保。微風吹幽松。近聽聲愈好。下 有斑白人。嘮嘮讀黃老。十年歸不得。忘却來 時道。閭丘胤訪後與拾得相携。出松門更不 還寺。有本云。喃喃讀黃老。此頌弱喪忘歸與 迷人指路也。後唐莊宗皇帝。請華嚴休靜禪 師。入內齋。大師大德總看經。唯師一眾默然。 帝問何不看經。靜曰。道泰不傳天子令。時清 休唱太平歌。帝曰。師一人不看即得。徒眾何 亦不看。靜曰。獅子窟中無異獸。象王行處絕 狐蹤。帝曰。大師大德為甚麼總看。靜曰。水母 元無眼。求食須賴鰕。帝大悅。況祖師尊者從 遠劫來。號大勢至。誦甚深脩多羅。因此從師 名般若多羅。元來習氣也不除。輸他華嚴却 有衲僧巴鼻。萬松到此不覺失笑。且道。笑箇 什麼。雲居羅漢披襟處。鞏縣茶瓶接嘴時。
text_en: Now, in the doctrinal teaching’s categories, the five skandhas, twelve sense-fields, and eighteen realms are called the three divisions. The Venerable One briefly raised the beginning and end, thereby including the middle. The Sanskrit ānāpāna is translated as exhalation and inhalation. Its method has six parts: first counting, second following, third stopping, fourth contemplation, fifth returning, sixth purification, all fully set out in Tiantai calming and contemplation. One preparing against what is unforeseen cannot fail to know this. Weishan’s Admonitions says: If one has never set one’s mind on doctrine and principle, the mysterious Way has no basis for matching realization. The Baozang Treatise laments: The priceless jewel lies hidden in the pit of skandhas and sense-fields. When will you attain the numinous light shining alone, far beyond roots and dust? Tiantong’s line, Cloud-rhino sporting with the moon, bright and holding radiance—there is an old poem: The rhinoceros, because it sports with the moon, patterns are born in its horn. Fine words, but sadly they get reduced to literary talent and sentimental cleverness. Wooden horse roaming in spring, swift and unbridled: this versifies exhaling without entering myriad conditions. It may be called good movement without wheel-tracks. Beneath the brows, a pair of cold blue-green eyes. Luopu said: If one alone is clear about oneself, the Dharma-eye is not yet clear. Such a person has only one eye. If you want both eyes perfectly bright, then only by not abiding in the skandha-realms and not entering myriad conditions. In the forest without shadows, suspend sun and moon on high. On the branchless branch, secretly discern spring and autumn—only then will it do. Reading sutras, how could one ever pierce oxhide? Changqing said: What fault has the eye? The Surangama Sutra says: Now carefully observe the holy assembly in this gathering. Use your eyes to look all around; though the eye surveys completely, it is only like reflections in a mirror, with no separate discrimination. Here is where people miss it. Yaoshan said: Even that oxhide must be pierced through. Wansong says: Then one indeed has vajra-eyes. A clear bright mind transcends vast kalpas. The Third Patriarch said: Only do not hate and love, and all becomes openly clear. In one thought, ten thousand years of receiving and upholding are inexhaustible. Lumen said: The whole great earth is the student’s one scroll of scripture; all heaven and earth are the student’s one eye. With this eye, read such a scripture, and through thousands of myriads of millions of kalpas there is never interruption. Wansong says: Reading in this way is not easy. Heroic strength breaks through heavy encirclement. In the Later Han, Wang Mang sent his kinsmen Wang Xun and Wang Yi to Kunyang, where they encircled Guangwu in dozens of layers. Guangwu’s troops were weak, and he wished to surrender to Xun and Yi, but they would not accept it. So Guangwu further rallied his generals and sent out troops to counterattack, and Xun and Yi were greatly defeated. The Venerable One was complete in both civil and martial ways—going out a general, entering a minister. Skandha- realms and myriad conditions are not merely heavy encirclement. At the wondrous round pivot-mouth, numinous functioning turns. The Erya says: A pivot is called a hinge-post. Guo Pu comments: It is the door-leaf’s pivot. Flowing water does not rot; a moving pivot does not decay—this speaks of its living motion. The Venerable One moved before being touched, turned without being pushed. Here or there, there was no can and cannot. Tiantong sifted sand and selected gold, split stars and cleaved both sides, making the distinctions clear. In the last two lines he shows still more surplus skill, saying: Hanshan forgets the road by which he came; Shide joins him, and hand in hand they return. This versifies the court feast and the ocean-like assembly, boring through paper and piercing windows. The Venerable One, old-womanishly kind, gave them a little. Hooking the curtain, the nursing swallow returns; through the hole in the paper the foolish fly comes out. He uses Hanshan’s poem and matches it like tally and token. The poem says: If you would gain a place to settle your body, Hanshan can keep you long. A faint breeze blows through hidden pines; listening close, the sound grows finer. Below there is a grizzled man, muttering as he reads Huang-Lao. For ten years he cannot return, having forgotten the road by which he came. After Lüqiu Yin visited him, he and Shide went hand in hand out the pine gate and no longer returned to the monastery. Some editions read softly murmuring as he reads Huang-Lao. This verse praises losing the way home while wandering weak, and also pointing out the road to the lost. Emperor Zhuangzong of Later Tang invited the Huayan Chan Master Xiujing into the palace for a vegetarian feast. All the great monks and elders read sutras; only the master’s whole group sat silent. The emperor asked, Why do you not read sutras? Jing said: When the Way is at peace, one does not transmit the Son of Heaven’s command; when the age is clear, one need not sing songs of great peace. The emperor said: It may do for you alone not to read, but why do your disciples also not read? Jing said: In a lion’s den there are no other beasts; where the elephant king walks, fox tracks are cut off. The emperor said: Then why do all the other great monks and elders read? Jing said: The jellyfish originally has no eyes; to seek food it must depend on shrimp. The emperor was greatly pleased. Besides, the patriarch-venerable came from distant kalpas, bearing the name Mahāsthāmaprāpta, reciting profound sutras. Therefore, from his teacher he got the name Prajñātāra. So in the end even old habits were not removed. Still, Huayan has him beaten in that there is at least a patchrobed monk’s clue to it. When Wansong gets here, he cannot help but laugh. Tell me, what is he laughing at? At the point where the Luohan of Yunju opens his robe, at the moment when the tea-bottle of Gong County meets the lips.

text_zh: 4 世尊指地
text_en: 4. The World-Honored One Points to the Ground Addressing the assembly, he said: As soon as a single dust-mote is raised, the whole earth is gathered in. With one horse and one spear, one opens frontiers

text_zh: 示眾云。一塵纔舉。大地全收。疋馬單槍。開疆 展土。便可隨處作主。遇緣即宗底。是甚麼人。
text_en: and unfolds the land. One who can be master wherever he is and make the teaching his own on meeting conditions what kind of person is that?
Raising the case: As the World-Honored One was walking with the assembly, he pointed to the ground with his hand and said, This place Turn with his heels

text_zh: 舉。世尊與眾行次隨他脚跟轉以手指地云。此處 宜建梵剎太歲頭上不合動土帝釋將一莖草。插於地 上云。建梵剎已竟修造不易世尊微笑賞罰分明。
text_en: is fit for building a Brahma monastery. Indra took a blade of grass and stuck it into the ground One should not break ground over Tai Sui’s head and said, The Brahma monastery is already built. The World-Honored One smiled faintly. Building and repairing is not easy Rewards and punishments are clear
The Master said: Because the World-Honored One once spread out his hair to cover mud and offered flowers to Dipankara Buddha, that Buddha pointed

text_zh: 師云。世尊因布髮掩泥。獻花於然燈佛。佛指 布髮處云。此一方地。宜建一剎。時有賢首長 者。插標於指處云。建剎已竟。諸天散花。讚歎 庶子有大智矣。天童舉話。大同小異。萬松道。 世尊祖業轉典與然燈。便有長者承頭收後。 如今交付與天童。須要出箇合同文契。頌云。
text_en: to the place where the hair was spread and said, In this patch of ground a monastery should be built. At that time there was an elder named Xianshou who planted a marker at the indicated spot and said, The monastery is already built. The gods scattered flowers and praised him, saying, This noble son has great wisdom indeed. Tiantong raises this story with broad sameness and slight difference. Wansong said: The World-Honored One transferred the ancestral estate to Dipankara, and then there was an elder to take it up at the front and gather it in at the back. Now that it is handed over to Tiantong, there must be a written deed and contract. The verse says:
On the tips of the hundred grasses, boundless spring casually picked up, it is used with intimacy. Jiashan is still here Entering the wild field, do not

text_zh: 百草頭上無邊春夾山猶在　信手拈來用得親入荒田不 揀丈六金身功德聚不審　等閑携手入紅塵逢場作戲 塵中能作主一朝權在手　化外自來賓看取令行時　觸處 生涯隨分足不從人得未嫌伎倆不如人面無慚色
text_en: pick and choose The sixteen-foot golden body, a heap of merit and virtue at ease, hand in hand, enters the red dust. I respectfully inquire Making a play of the occasion In the dust one can be the master; beyond transformation, guests come of themselves. Wherever one touches, Once authority is in hand watch when the command is carried out livelihood is sufficient according to one’s share. Not obtained from another One need not mind that one’s tricks are no match for others. No shame in the face
The Master said: Tiantong first finishes versifying the koan in four lines, then spreads out the broad outline

text_zh: 師云。天童先以四句頌公案了。然後鋪舒梗 概。展演化風。趙州拈一莖草。作丈六金身用。 世尊當風指出。帝釋信手拈來。天童人境交 加頌出。非但古聖。爾即今塵中作得主。化外 亦來賓。且道。風流劉駙馬。起此報恩院。與帝 釋插草同別。師竪起拂子云。千年常住一朝 僧。
text_en: and unfolds the transforming style. Zhaozhou picked up a single blade of grass and used it as the sixteen-foot golden body. The World-Honored One pointed it out right in the wind; Indra casually picked it up. Tiantong intertwines person and circumstance and brings it out in verse. Not only the ancient sages if you right now can be master in the dust, then beyond transformation guests too will come. Tell me then, the elegant imperial son-in-law Liu who built this Baoen Monastery is it the same as or different from Indra sticking in the grass? The Master raised his whisk and said: A thousand-year monastery, and in one morning a monk.

text_zh: 5 清源米價
text_en: 5. Qingyuan on the Price of Rice Addressing the assembly, he said: Jati cut flesh to feed his parents, yet he is not entered in the biographies of filial sons. Devadatta pushed

text_zh: 示眾云。闍提割肉供親。不入孝子傳。調達推 山壓佛。豈怕忽雷鳴。過得荊棘林。斫倒栴檀 樹。直待年窮歲盡。依舊盂春猶寒。佛法身在 甚麼處也。
text_en: a mountain to crush the Buddha how could he fear a sudden thunderclap? If you pass through the thorn forest and chop down the sandalwood tree, then when the year is spent and the old year ends, it is still cold in early spring. The Buddha-Dharma body where is it located?
Raising the case: A monk asked Qingyuan, What is the great meaning of the Buddha-Dharma? Qingyuan Minor officials recite the statutes a lot

text_zh: 舉。僧問清源。如何是佛法大意小官多念律源 云。盧陵米作麼價老將不論兵。
text_en: said, What is the price of rice in Luling? Old generals do not discuss war
The Master said: Chan Master Xingsi of Qingyuan Mountain in Jizhou, when he first visited the Sixth Patriarch, immediately asked,

text_zh: 師云。吉州清源山行思禪。師初參六祖便問。 當何所務即得不落階級。祖云。汝曾作甚麼 來。源云。聖諦亦不為。祖云。落何階級。源云。 聖諦尚不為何階級之有。祖深器之。會下學 徒雖眾。師居首焉。亦猶二祖不言。少林謂之 得髓矣。據這僧問佛法大意。也是本色乍入 叢林底人。要隨文殊遊鐵圍山。清源是聖諦 亦不為底人。却只作尋常相見顧問道。盧陵 米作麼價。有者道。盧陵米價不許商量。殊不 知。已入斛斗行鋪了也。要得不入這保社。問 取天童。頌云。
text_en: What should one practice to avoid falling into stages? The Patriarch said, What have you done before? Qingyuan said, I do not even engage in holy truths. The Patriarch said, Into what stages could you fall? Qingyuan said, If I do not even engage in holy truths, what stages could there be? The Patriarch esteemed him deeply. Though there were many students in the assembly, this master stood foremost among them. It was like the Second Patriarch saying nothing, and Shaolin called it getting the marrow. Judging by this monk’s question about the great meaning of the Buddha-Dharma, he too was a genuine one just entering the monastery groves, wanting to travel with Manjushri through the Iron Encircling Mountains. Qingyuan was a man who did not even engage in holy truths, and yet he only made it into an ordinary greeting and inquiry, saying, Luling rice what price? Some say, The price of Luling rice does not allow deliberation. They do not realize they have already entered the grain-measure shops and stalls. If you want not to enter this guild, ask Tiantong. The verse says:
Peaceful governance leaves no outward sign; the old rustic’s household style is utmost simplicity. Has the comet star appeared yet or not How can it compare to my planting here

text_zh: 太平治業無象旄頭星現也未　野老家風至淳爭如我這裏種 田博飯喫只管村歌社飲窮鬼子快活不徹也　那知舜德堯仁 始成忠孝

The Master said: In the sixth year of Taihe under Emperor Wenzong of Tang, Niu Sengru was prime minister. The emperor asked:

text_zh: 師云。唐文宗太和六年時。牛僧孺為相。上曰。 天下何時太平。孺對曰。太平無象。今四夷不 致交侵。百姓不致離散。雖非至治。亦謂小康。 陛下若別求太平。非臣所及。退而累表請罷。 出為淮南節度使。萬松道。已是起模畫樣。所 以野老家風。擊壤謳歌。禮樂文章。翻成特地。 盧陵米價。可曬深玄。舜德堯仁。淳風自化。村 歌社飲。得其所哉。月白風清。各安其分。還會 麼。逐便歸堂。
text_en: When is the realm at peace? Niu replied: Peace has no outward sign. Now the four border peoples do not encroach upon one another, and the common people are not scattered. Though this is not perfect rule, it may still be called modest prosperity. If Your Majesty seeks some other peace, it is beyond your servant. He withdrew and repeatedly submitted memorials asking to resign. He was sent out as military governor of Huainan. Wansong says: This is already setting up models and drawing patterns, and so the old rustic’s household style, pounding the earth and singing, makes rites, music, and literary refinements turn into something forced. The price of Luling rice can expose deep mystery to the sun. Shun’s virtue and Yao’s benevolence the simple wind transforms of itself. Village songs and communal drink each gets what is fitting. Moon bright, wind clear, each rests in his own place. Do you understand? If so, return to the hall as convenient.

text_zh: 師云。六祖謂讓和尚曰。西天二十七祖讖。汝 足下出一馬駒。踏殺天下人。病在汝心。不須 速說。後磨塼打牛。神駒入廐。號為馬祖。牛 行虎視。引舌過鼻。足下有輪文。法嗣一百三 十九人。各為一方法主。智藏海兄乃西堂百 丈也。看來這僧。也是箇學佛法人。將四句百 非。勘當教外別傳宗旨。攝大乘論說。有是增 益謗。無是損減謗。亦有亦無相違謗。非有非 無戲論謗。四句若離。百非自絕。黃蘗道。欲要 直捷會。一切總不是。萬松道。端的委細會。一 切無不是。翻覆看來。不離四句。不絕百非。西 來祖意。於何不明。龍樹大師道。般若如大火 聚四面不可入。却道。般若如清涼池四面皆 可入。這僧道。離四句絕百非。請師直指西來 意。諸方謂之鎖口問。馬祖不忙只道。我今日 勞倦。不能為汝說。問取智藏去。惜得自己眉 毛。穿却那僧鼻孔。那僧不免被他驅使。真箇 去問。智藏亦不謀而合道。何不問和尚。這僧 不開眉眼。道和尚教來問。藏云。我今日頭痛。 不能為汝說。問取海兄去。可謂非父不生其 子也。僧問海。海云。我到這裏却不會。將謂侯 白更有侯黑。這僧雖無血性。却有首尾。還來 舉似馬祖。祖云。藏頭白海頭黑。這句疑殺天 下人。東林照覺頌云。百非四句絕無言。黑白 分明定正偏。萬松道。暮四朝三。妄生喜怒。一 日三人與南泉玩月。次祖云。正當恁麼時如 何。丈云。正好修行。藏云。正好供養。南泉拂 袖便行。祖云。經入藏禪歸海。唯有普願。獨 超物外。這裏却宜緇素分明。萬松道。藏頭白 海頭黑。鴨頭綠鶴頭赤。十影神駒立海南。五 色祥麟步天北。諸方且莫假狐靈。天童自有 真消息。頌云。
text_en: feet a colt will appear and trample everyone under heaven to death. The illness is in your mind; you need not speak too soon. Later, after polishing tile and beating the ox, the divine colt entered the stable and came to be called Mazu. Ox- gait, tiger-gaze, tongue stretched past the nose, wheel-marks under his feet he had one hundred and thirty-nine Dharma heirs, each a master in one region. Zhizang and Brother Hai were Xitang and Baizhang. Looking at it, this monk too was one studying the Buddha-Dharma, taking the four propositions and hundred negations to test the aim of the separate transmission outside the teachings. The Mahayana Compendium says: affirming being is the slander of addition, affirming nonbeing is the slander of subtraction, affirming both being and nonbeing is the slander of contradiction, affirming neither being nor nonbeing is the slander of idle talk. If the four propositions are left behind, the hundred negations cease of themselves. Huangbo said: If you want a direct and swift understanding, everything altogether is not it. Wansong says: If you want a precise and detailed understanding, everything is not not it. Turning it over and back, one does not leave the four propositions, nor cut off the hundred negations. The Western Patriarch’s meaning in what is it unclear? Nagarjuna said: Prajna is like a great mass of fire, impossible to enter from any side. Yet he also said: Prajna is like a cool clear pool, enterable from every side. This monk said, Apart from the four propositions and beyond the hundred negations, please directly point out the coming-from-the-West meaning. In all quarters this is called a lock-mouth question. Mazu, unhurried, simply said, Today I am tired and cannot explain it for you. Go ask Zhizang. He spared his own eyebrows and pierced the monk’s nostrils. The monk could not avoid being driven about by him and truly went to ask. Zhizang too, without consulting, spoke in accord: Why not ask the master? This monk, with no opening of brows or eyes, said, master told me to come ask. Zang said, Today my head aches. I cannot explain it for you. Go ask Brother Hai. It may be said, no father, no such son. The monk asked Hai. Hai said, When I get here, I do not understand. One might have thought after Marquis White there would also be Marquis Black. Though this monk lacked spirit, he at least had beginning and end, and came back to report it to Mazu. The Patriarch said, Zang’s head white, Hai’s head black. This one phrase has baffled everyone under heaven. Donglin Zhaojue versified it: The hundred negations and four propositions cut off no words. Black and white are clearly divided, fixing the upright and the partial. Wansong says: Four at dusk, three at dawn vainly giving rise to joy and anger. One day the three men were viewing the moon with Nanquan. Then Mazu said, At just such a time, what is it? Baizhang said, Just right for practice. Zang said, Just right for making offerings. Nanquan brushed his sleeves and left. Mazu said, Sutras enter Zang, Chan returns to Hai; only Puyuan alone transcends beyond things. Here it is indeed fitting that black and white be clearly distinguished. Wansong says: Zang’s head white, Hai’s head black. A duck’s head green, a crane’s head red. The divine colt of ten shadows stands south of the sea; the five- colored auspicious qilin paces north of heaven. All quarters, do not borrow a fox’s borrowed might. Tiantong has his own true news. text_en: propositions are also four gates, like a cool clear pool enterable from every side. In former years Wansong served as secretary at Daming. At that time Master Heng of Tanzhe passed through Daming, and in the dark of night knocked at the gate and told the attendant he wished to burn incense and form a connection. Tanzhe at once allowed an interview. Wansong asked for instruction: What is a living phrase? What is a dead phrase? Zhe said: If the secretary understands a dead phrase, it too is a living phrase. If he does not understand a living phrase, it too is a dead phrase. At that time I thought to myself: the methods of an old adept are indeed different. Today, seeing this monk’s question, he was dead set on wanting a separate pointing out of the Patriarch’s meaning beyond the four propositions and hundred negations. The minds of these three old fellows were alike. If one just took it as understanding by leaving the four propositions and cutting off the hundred negations, then one would bury this monk in one pit. Later Tiantong, in versing Yangshan’s gavel-strike in a dream, said: Apart from the four propositions and beyond the hundred negations, Master Ma and his sons’ illness ceases to need medicine. Wansong says: What kind of mind-practice is that? White head, black head sons fit to carry on the house. In the Zhou Yi, in the Meng hexagram, the line Nine in the second place says, The son can carry on the household he can bear the family enterprise. With words, without words cutting off the stream is the mechanism. Wansong says: There are only ripples on clear water, not yet waves that tower to the sky. Majestic and open, they sit and sever the road of the tongue. They should laugh at old gimlet Vimalakirti. The Sanskrit Vi- maliya is translated Broad Adornment, the name of the city where Vimalakirti lived. When Manjushri asked about the gate of nonduality, Vimalakirti was silent. This monk asked Master Ma and his sons, and vines spread all over the ground. Tell me, where is the point where one should laugh? If only one can avoid touching the taboo of the present age, that is still better than the tongue-cutting talent of the former dynasty.

text_en: invitations, a bodhisattva ascends the hall; half a verse and the whole body; a yaksha ascends the seat was this out of craving for Dharma? Chan Master Nan of Huanglong said: Nowadays many people take the Dharma lightly. One wants to treat them like a farmer who lets the field dry from time to time, making it parched and thirsty, and only then irrigates it so that it may become luxuriant and bear fruit. But Yaoshan’s long not ascending the seat was not quite like that. Juefan said: In one hut is deeply hidden a thunderbolt tongue, letting the ten thousand forms each speak for themselves. Yongjia said: In silence he speaks; in speaking he is silent. The great gate of giving stands open without obstruction. The prior missed it at every point, saying, The assembly has longed for instruction; please, master, teach the Dharma for them. In the way of human feeling and proper conduct, and in terms of host and guest, this was not beyond the bounds. Yaoshan ordered the bell struck. One sees only thunder issuing commands. As the assembly gathered, who knew the stars and Dipper were already shining in patterns? Yaoshan ascended the seat, stayed long, descended, and returned to his quarters. This one display of spiritual power was no small thing. The prior followed after and asked, master, you just agreed to teach the Dharma for the assembly. Why did you not let fall a single word? Cuiyan Zhi said: After Yaoshan descended the seat, the prior from the start blamed him for not teaching the Dharma to the assembly. It may be said he misled the whole army. Wansong says: It was exactly because the general’s head was not fierce enough. Yaoshan said, Sutras have sutra teachers, treatises have treatise teachers. Why blame this old monk? Langya Jue said: It is fine to be doubtful when Yaoshan descends the seat, but when the prior presses in, one eye is lost. Wansong says: How many can make it whole again? Yet he did not know that two eyes were gained in exchange. Xuedou said: What a pity for old Yaoshan. He stumbled on level ground, and all the people on earth could not help him up. Wansong says: master too must put out a hand. Wuyu versified it: Before leaving the abbot’s room he had already stumbled; quietly returning, he became all the more forlorn. Sutra teachers and treatise teachers still tell each other; one clause made clear and one summons it oneself. Wansong says: Clerks are easy to examine; the koan is not yet rounded off. text_zh: 師云。涅盤經說。嬰兒啼時。母將黃葉。云與汝 金。兒即止啼。此頌久思示誨與云何不垂一 言。外道問佛。不問有言。不問無言。世尊良 久。外道便作禮云。世尊大慈。開我迷雲。令我 得入。外道去後。阿難問佛。外道見何道理。而 言得入。佛言。如世良馬見鞭影而行。藥山與 世尊。一等舉鞭。院主率眾僧。禮讚有分。却怪 不垂一言。可謂東土衲僧不如西天外道。天 童恁麼頌。萬松恁麼說。盡是止啼黃葉。只為 諸人熱夢未醒。睡輕者一呼便覺。睡重者搖 撼方驚。更有一等。椓抄起來猶自䆿𥊼。比他 藥山睛巢月鶴。清不成眠。雲泥有隔。雖然 如是。睡語不少。
text_en: gold, and the child immediately stops crying. This verse has long been pondered. The instruction and the question, Why not let fall a single word? An outsider asked the Buddha, I do not ask about speech, and I do not ask about no speech. The World-Honored One remained silent for a long while. The outsider then bowed and said, World-Honored One, great compassion has parted my clouds of delusion and enabled me to enter. After the outsider left, Ananda asked the Buddha, What principle did the outsider see, that he said he had entered? The Buddha said, It is like a fine horse in the world that moves when it sees the shadow of the whip. Yaoshan and the World-Honored One alike raised the whip. The monastery superintendent led the monks; there was a share in bowing and praising, yet they instead blamed him for not uttering a single word. It may be said that patch-robed monks in the Eastern Land are not equal to the outsiders of the Western Heaven. Tian- tong versifies in this way, and Wansong explains in this way, all of it being yellow leaves to stop crying, only because all of you have not yet awakened from your fevered dream. Those who sleep lightly wake at a single shout; those who sleep heavily must be shaken before they are startled. There is yet another sort: even when beaten and roused, they still compare themselves with Yaoshan's moon-nesting crane of clear eyes, too pure to sleep. Cloud and mud are far apart. Even so, for all that, sleep-talk is not a little.

text_zh: 舉。百丈上堂。常有一老人。聽法隨眾散去。 閙中取靜一日不去從來疑著這漢丈乃問立者何人事不解交客來 須待老人云。某甲於過去迦葉佛時。曾住此 山元是當家人有學人問。大修行底人還落因果 也無但行好事莫問前程對他道不落因果一句合頭語萬劫繫驢橛墮 野狐身五百生爾道不落因果今請和尚代一轉語著甚 來由丈云。不昧因果一坑埋却老人於言下大悟狐涎猶在。
text_en: One day he did not leave. Baizhang then asked, Who is this standing here? The old man said, In the age of Kashyapa Buddha in the past, I once lived on this Find stillness amid the clamor. All along I have had doubts about this fellow. He cannot manage affairs, yet visitors keep coming. One must wait until— mountain. A student asked me, Does a person of great practice still fall into cause and effect it turns out he is the one in charge. or not? I answered him, He does not fall into cause and effect, and so I fell into Just do good deeds; do not ask about the future. One fitting phrase can become the hitching post for a donkey through ten thousand kalpas. a wild fox body for five hundred births. Now I ask master to give a turning word in my place. Baizhang said, Not blind to cause and effect. At these words the old man had a great awakening. You say it does not fall into cause and effect. What does it matter? The origin. Bury it in a single pit. The fox’s slobber is still there.

text_zh: 師云。洪州百丈山大智禪師每至陞座。常有 一老人。聽法迦葉佛時曾住此山。錯對學人 一轉語。至今墮野狐身。良由自己倚牆貼壁。 送人墮坑落塹。見大智有抽釘拔楔手段。便 舍已從他。請大智代一轉語。大智施無畏辯。 輕輕撥轉道。不昧因果老人言下大悟。據實 而論。不落因果是撥無斷見。不昧因果。是隨 流得妙。稍解教乘者。舉著便見。要且雖脫毛 衣。猶披鱗甲。不見道圓禪師。在南禪師會中。 聞二僧舉此話。一僧曰。只如不昧因果。也未 脫得野狐身。一僧應聲曰。便是不落因果。亦 何曾墮野狐身耶。師悚然異其語。急上黃蘗 積翠菴頭。過㵎忽大悟。見南公敘其事。未終 涕交頤。南公令就侍者榻熱𥧌。忽起作偈曰。 不落不昧。僧俗本無忌諱。丈夫氣宇如王。爭 受囊藏被蓋。一條楖栗任縱橫。野狐跳入金 毛隊。南公大笑。恁麼看來。當初見道今請和 尚代一轉語。只樂道不落因果。免使初心墮 在解穽。百丈至晚。上堂舉前因緣。黃蘗便問。 古人錯答一轉語。墮五百生野狐身。轉轉不 錯。合作甚麼。丈云。近前。與爾道。蘗近前與 丈一掌。丈拍手笑云。將謂狐須赤。更有赤須 狐仰山道。百丈得大機。黃蘗得大用。名不虛 得。溈山舉問仰山。黃蘗常用此機。為復天生 得。從人得。仰云。亦是稟受師承。亦是自性宗 通。溈云。如是如是。看他百丈父子。游行無 畏。如師子王。豈向野狐窠裏作活計。萬松已 是尾骨彌露。更放天童弄爪牙。看。頌云。
text_en: an old man present. In the time of Kasyapa Buddha, while dwelling on this mountain and hearing the Dharma, he once gave a mistaken reply to a student, a single turning phrase, and to this day had fallen into the body of a wild fox. It was truly because he himself leaned against walls and clung to them, sending others tumbling into pits and ditches. Seeing that Dazhi had the skill to pull nails and extract wedges, he then set himself aside and followed him, asking Dazhi to speak a turning phrase in his place. Dazhi bestowed fearless eloquence, and lightly turned it, saying: Not blind to cause and effect. At these words the old man had a great awakening. Speaking according to the facts, not falling into cause and effect is the nihilistic view that denies them. Not being blind to cause and effect is going along with the flow and finding the subtle. Anyone with even a slight understanding of the teachings will see it as soon as it is raised. Even so, though he has shed the fur coat, he still wears scales and armor. Have you not seen Chan Master Yuan, while in Master Nan's assembly, hear two monks bring up this story? One monk said: Even with not being blind to cause and effect, one still has not escaped the fox body. Another monk immediately answered: Then even not falling into cause and effect would also never have fallen into a fox body, would it? The master was startled and found these words extraordinary, so he hurried up to Huangbo's Jicui Hermitage, and on the way suddenly had a great awakening. When he saw Master Nan and told the story, before he had finished tears streamed down his cheeks. Master Nan told him to go warm himself by the attendant's couch. He suddenly rose and made a verse, saying: Not falling, not obscured, monk and lay have originally no taboo. A true man's bearing is like a king's, how could he submit to being bagged and covered over? One chestnut staff, free to go vertical and horizontal; the wild fox leaps into the golden- furred ranks. Master Nan laughed loudly. Seen this way, when at first he said, I now ask the master to speak a turning phrase in my place, it was only good to say not falling into cause and effect, so as to keep beginners from falling into the pit of conceptual understanding. Later, Baizhang ascended the hall and raised this earlier cause and condition. Huangbo then asked: The man of old gave one mistaken turning phrase and fell for five hundred lives into a wild fox body. If each turning phrase is not mistaken, what should happen then? Zhang said: Come closer and I will tell you. Bo came forward and gave Zhang a slap. Zhang clapped his hands and laughed, saying: I thought the fox's beard was red, but here is an even redder-bearded fox. Yangshan said: Baizhang attained the great pivot, Huangbo attained great function. Their fame was not gotten in vain. Guishan raised this and asked Yangshan: Huangbo often used this pivot. Was it innate, or did he get it from another? Yang said: It was both received through teacher and lineage, and also a direct penetration of the self-nature's source. Gui said: Just so, just so. Look at those father-and-son, Baizhang and Huangbo, roaming without fear, like lion kings. How could they make their livelihood in a wild fox den? Wansong has already let his tailbone show all the more; now he lets Tiantong display his claws and fangs. Look. The verse says:
One foot of water, one fathom of waves before five hundred births, there was nothing to be done. Fortunately, the rivers are clear and the seas are calm Had I known it would be like this today,

text_zh: 師云。立修證分因果。一尺水一丈波。墮在五 百生野狐精魅。積翠庵下二僧縱有逸群之 辯。點檢將來。未免撞入葛藤窠裏。天童此句 有兩字未穩。何不道依前撞入野狐窠。阿呵 呵。此頌明百丈悟處。露自己胸襟道會也麼。 但問天童會也未。若是爾灑灑落落。不妨我 哆哆和和。幸有一陰地。何勞不為人。哆哆和 和。嬰兒言語不真貌。又法華釋籤云。多跢學 行之相。嘙和習語之聲。涅盤經有病行嬰兒 行。有本云婆婆和和。石室善道禪師云。涅盤 十六行中。嬰兒行為最。哆哆和和時。喻學道 人離分別取捨心。與下神歌社舞。皆一意也。 且道。是何曲調。萬籟有心聞不得。孤巖無耳 却知音。
text_en: hundred-birth wild fox spirit. Though the two monks beneath Jicui Hermitage had eloquence beyond the common run, when examined closely they still could not avoid crashing into the vine-tangle nest. In Tiantong’s line here, two characters are not quite steady. Why not say, still crashed into the wild fox den? Ah haha this verse clarifies where Baizhang awakened, and Tiantong bares his own chest and says, Do you understand? I only ask whether Tiantong understood or not. If you are open and free and clear, then no harm in my da-da he-he. Since there is fortunately a patch of shade, why not make use of it for people? Da-da he- he this is infant speech, not true in form. Also, in the Notes on the Lotus it says: duo-da is the appearance of learning and practice; po-he is the sound of practicing speech. The Nirvana Sutra speaks of diseased practice and infant- practice. Some editions read po-po he-he. Chan Master Shandao of Stone Chamber said: Of the sixteen practices in the Nirvana, the infant practice is supreme. Da-da he-he describes people studying the Way when they have left behind the mind of discrimination and choosing and rejecting. It is the same meaning as the spirit songs and village dances below. But tell me, what tune is it? The ten thousand sounds, though intent, cannot hear it; the solitary crag, earless, still knows the tune.

text_zh: 9 南泉斬猫
text_en: 9. Nanquan Cuts the Cat Addressing the assembly, he said: Kick over the blue sea and dust flies across the earth. Shout apart the white clouds and empty space

text_zh: 示眾云。踢翻滄海。大地塵飛。喝散白雲。虛空 粉碎。嚴行正令。猶是半提。大用全彰。如何施 設。
text_en: shatters to pieces. Even strict enforcement of the true command is only half the matter. When great function is fully manifest, how is it applied?
Raising the case: One day at Nanquan’s place, the monks of the east and west halls were fighting over a cat. Nan- When people are level they do not speak; when water is level it does not flow.

text_zh: 舉。南泉一日。東西兩堂爭猫兒人平不語水平不流南 泉見遂提起云。道得即不斬誰敢當鋒眾無對直待 雨淋頭泉斬却猫兒為兩段抽刀不入鞘泉復舉前話 問趙州再來不直半文州便脫草鞋。於頭上戴出好與一刀 兩段泉云。子若在。恰救得猫兒心斜不覺口喝。
text_en: quan saw it, picked up the cat, and said, If you can speak, I will not cut it. The assembly had no reply. Nanquan then cut the cat into two. Later Nanquan again raised the earlier story Who dares face the edge? Just wait until rain pours on your head. Drawing the blade and not returning it to the sheath. and asked Zhaozhou. Zhaozhou immediately took off his straw sandals, placed them on his head, and walked out. Nanquan said, If you had been there, you would indeed have saved the cat. Bring it again and it is not worth half a coin. Best to give one slash. Into two pieces. With a crooked mind, one does not notice the mouth shouting.

text_zh: 師云。法雲圓通秀禪師。見二僧並立說話。將 拄杖。到連卓數下云。一片業地。何況兩堂眾 首。因猫致諍。南泉也不與解勸。亦不與懲罰。 本色道人。以本分事。為人遂提起猫兒云。道 得即不斬。正當恁麼時。盡十方界有情無情。 一齊向南泉手中乞命。當時有箇出來展開 兩手。不然攔胸抱住云却勞和尚神用。縱南 泉別行正令。敢保救得猫兒。這一窟死老鼠。 既無些子氣息。南泉已展不縮。盡令而行。遼 朝上人𭣪作鏡心錄。訶南泉輩殺生造罪。文 首座作無盡燈辨誤。救云。古本以手作虛斫 勢。豈直一刀兩段。鮮血淋迸哉。這兩箇批判 古人。文公罪重。𭣪公罪輕。南泉依舊。水牯牛 隊裡。搖頭擺尾。不見。佛日禪師與眾茶座次。 見猫來。袖中擲鵓鴿與之。猫接得便去。日云 俊哉不可也是假作虛用。南泉自念。曲高和 寡。舉前話問趙州。州便脫草鞋於頭上戴出。 果然敲唱俱行。節拍成就。泉云。子若在恰救 得猫兒。這些子用處。雖難會却易見。爾但向 拈匙舉筯處覰破。便見斬猫兒戴草鞋更無 兩樣。不然更看。天童別作甚麼伎倆。頌云。
text_en: his staff, went over, struck several times, and said, One patch of karma-ground, all the more with the assembly heads of two halls who, because of a cat, caused contention. Nanquan neither reconciled them nor offered admonition, nor did he punish them. A true man of the Way, using the proper matter for the sake of others, then lifted up the cat and said, If you can speak, then it will not be cut. At just such a moment, throughout the ten directions, sentient and insentient alike, all together begged for life from Nanquan’s hand. If at that time there had been one who came forth and spread open both hands, or else blocked him at the chest and embraced him, saying, No need to trouble master with miraculous function—even if Nan quan had carried out another true command, I dare guarantee the cat would have been saved. But this whole hole of dead rats— since there was not the slightest breath in them, Nanquan had already extended and did not withdraw, fully carrying out the command. In the Liao dynasty monk Jue wrote the Record of Mirror-Mind, reproaching people like Nanquan for killing living beings and creating sin. Chief Seat Wen wrote the Endless Lamp Correcting Errors to defend him, saying: In old versions, he only made an empty cutting gesture with his hand; how could it really have been one slash into two pieces, with fresh blood spurting everywhere? These two, in judging the ancients—Master Wen’s fault is heavy, Master Jue’s fault is lighter. Nanquan remains as ever, in the herd of water buffaloes, shaking his head and swishing his tail. Do you not see? Chan Master Fori, while seated with the assembly at tea, saw a cat come, and from his sleeve tossed a pigeon to it. The cat caught it and went off. Fori said, Fine indeed, but it still cannot be allowed—it is a contrived empty display. Nanquan himself thought: When the tune is lofty, those who can join are few. So he raised the earlier story and asked Zhaozhou. Zhaozhou then took off his straw sandals, put them on his head, and walked out. Truly, striking and singing went together, and the rhythm was complete. Quan said, If you had been there, you would indeed have saved the cat. This little bit of functioning, though hard to understand, is easy to see. You need only, at the point of picking up the spoon and lifting the chopsticks, look through it and break through; then you will see cutting the cat and wearing straw sandals are no different. Otherwise, look further and see what other device Tiantong makes. The verse says:
Monks of the two halls all fall into wrangling; Master Wang is able to test right and wrong. Being in the right does not depend on a loud voice. A bright mirror.
