text_zh: 師云。兩堂雲水盡紛拏。至今不曾定交。若非 天童會南泉例驗出端倪。往往邪正不分。邪 正分明時如何判斷。便好。利劍斬斷一坑埋 却。非但勦絕一期不了公案。亦使千古之下 風清寰宇。南泉當時師勝。資強。見眾無語。却 舉似趙州。表顯眾中有人。趙州脫草鞋頭上 戴出。果然此道未喪。知音可嘉。孔子云。天將 未喪斯文也。看他師資。道合。唱拍相隨。無以 為喻。諡法。泉源流通曰禹。又受禪成功曰禹。 尚書禹貢。導河積石至於龍門。淮南子。共工 氏兵強兇暴。而與堯帝爭功。力窮觸不周山 而死。天柱為之折。女媧鍊五色石。補天。列 子。陰陽失度名缺。鍊五常之精名補。雲蓋本 拈洞山掇却泰首座果棹話云。洞山雖有打 破虛空底鉆鎚。要且無補綴底針線。南泉如 大禹鑿山透海。顯出神用。趙州如女媧鍊石 補天。圓却話頭。萬松道。趙州十八上解破家 散宅。不知有多少生涯。草鞋頭戴較些些。咄 咄沒去處。作這箇去就。保福展云。雖然如是。 也只是破草鞋。南泉平高就下道。子若在恰 救得猫兒。翠巖芝云。大小趙州只可自救。放 過一著。天童道。異中來也還明鑒。只箇真金 不混沙。只能順水推舡。不解逆風把柁。而今 爾這一隊上來。猫又無。爭甚狗。以拄杖趁下。
text_en: Tiantong understanding Nanquan and testing the pattern to reveal the clues, often right and wrong would not be distinguished. When right and wrong are clearly distinguished, how do you judge? Then it is best to cut with a sharp sword and bury the whole pit. This not only wipes out one unresolved public case, it also lets the world beneath a thousand ages be clear and fresh. At that time Nanquan was superior as teacher, strong in resources; seeing the assembly speechless, he then brought it up to Zhaozhou, showing that among the assembly there was someone. Zhaozhou took off his straw sandals and placed them on his head and went out. Truly this Way was not lost; a knower of the tune is praiseworthy. Confucius said, If Heaven is not about to let this culture perish... Look at that teacher and disciple: their Ways matched, chant and beat followed each other; there is no fitting comparison. In posthumous naming, one whose springs and streams flow freely is called Yu; also one who receives the throne and succeeds is called Yu. In the Yu Gong of the Classic of Documents, he guided the river from Jishi to Longmen. In the Huainanzi, Gonggong was militarily strong and violent, contending with Emperor Yao for merit. When his strength was exhausted, he rammed Mount Buzhou and died; the pillar of heaven broke because of it. Nüwa smelted five-colored stones to mend the sky. In the Liezi, when yin and yang lose their measure, it is called a breach; refining the essences of the five constants is called repair. Yungai originally cited Dongshan’s story of snatching away Chief Seat Tai’s fruit tray, saying: Though Dongshan had a drill-hammer that could smash open empty space, still he lacked the needle and thread for mending. Nanquan was like Great Yu piercing mountains and opening the sea, revealing miraculous function. Zhaozhou was like Nüwa smelting stones to mend the sky, rounding off the topic. Wansong said: From eighteen on, Zhaozhou knew how to break up homes and scatter households—who knows how many livelihoods he had! Straw sandals on his head, worn a little off. Tut, tut—there is nowhere to go, yet he makes this move of going and coming. Baofu Zhan said: Even so, it is only torn straw sandals. Nanquan, leveling the high and meeting the low, said, If you had been there, you truly would have saved the cat. Cuiyan Zhi said: Big or small, Zhaozhou could only save himself. Letting go that one move. Tiantong says: Coming from within difference, still it is a clear mirror. Only this true gold is not mixed with sand. They only know to push the boat with the current, not to steer against the wind. And now you lot come up here—there is no cat either, so why quarrel over dogs? He drove them down with his staff.

text_zh: 10 臺山婆子
text_en: 10. The Old Woman of Mount Tai Instruction to the assembly: There is gathering and releasing; dry wood is at hand. Able to kill, able to give life, the balancing steelyard

text_zh: 示眾云。有收有放。干木隨身。能殺能活。權衝 在手。塵勞魔外盡付指呼。大地山河皆成戲 具。且道。是甚麼境界。
text_en: is in hand. Dusty toils and demonic outsiders are all subject to one pointing command. The great earth and mountains and rivers all become playthings. But tell me: what realm is this?
Raised: On the road to Mount Tai there was an old woman. Whenever a monk asked, Village folk by the city, roadside rabbits.

text_zh: 舉。臺山路上有一婆子傍城庄家夾道兔凡有僧問。 臺山路向什麼處去一生行脚去處也不知婆云。驀直去 未當好心僧纔行著賊也不知婆云。好箇阿師又恁麼去 也爾早侯白僧舉似趙州人平不語州云。待。與勘過水平 不流州亦如前問陷虎之機至來日上堂云。我為汝 勘破婆子了也我更侯黑。
text_en: Which way does the road to Mount Tai go? the old woman said, Go straight on. Traveling all your life and still not knowing where you have gone. As soon as the monk walked off, the old woman said, A fine teacher-monk—off he goes just like that again. Not yet a good intention. Caught by thieves and not even knowing it. The monk told Zhaozhou. Zhaozhou said, Wait, I will examine her for you. Zhaozhou also asked just as before. The next day, in the hall, he said, For you I have You have long been waiting for white. When people are level, they do not speak. When water is level, it does not flow. The device for trapping a tiger. examined through that old woman. I will wait for black instead.
The teacher said: That old woman on the Mount Tai road was used to following Wuzhuo in and out of monasteries, well seasoned in

text_zh: 師云。臺山路上婆子。慣隨無著出寺入寺。飽 參文殊前三後三。凡見僧問臺山路向什麼 處去。便當陽指出長安大道。云驀直去。其僧 不作疑阻便行。婆云。好箇阿師又恁麼去也。 這婆子也鉤錐在手。從來觸誤多少賢良。這 僧既不奈伊何。拈來舉似趙州。州云。待與勘 過。疑殺天下人。這老漢老不歇心。圖箇甚麼。 也要定箇宗眼。州依前恁麼問。婆依前恁麼 答。有底便話作兩橛。前段點這僧扶婆子。後 段點婆子扶趙州。唯玄覺云。前僧也恁麼問 答。後來趙州也恁麼問答。且道。甚處是勘破 處。萬松道。勘破了也。又云。非唯被趙州勘 破。赤被這僧勘破。萬松道。非但累及玄覺。亦 乃累及萬松。瑯琊云。大小趙州去這婆子手 裡。喪身失命。雖然如是。錯會者多。萬松道。 切忌。以已方人。溈山哲云。天下衲僧只知問 路老婆。要且不知脚下泥深。若非趙州老人。 爭顯汗馬功高。雖然須假天童歌揚始得。頌 云。
text_en: consulting Mañjuśrī, before three and after three. Whenever she saw a monk ask where the road to Mount Tai went, she immediately pointed straight out the great road to Chang’an and said, Go straight on. If the monk did not raise doubt or hesitate and just went, the old woman said, A fine teacher-monk—off he goes just like that again. This old woman too had hook and awl in hand; from of old she has tripped up many worthies. This monk, since he could do nothing with her, picked it up and told Zhaozhou. Zhaozhou said, Wait, I will examine her. He leaves all under heaven deeply puzzled. This old fellow, old as he is, still does not rest his mind—what is he after? He also wanted to settle a sect-eye. Zhaozhou asked as before; the old woman answered as before. Some people then split the story into two chunks: in the first part, they say this monk supports the old woman; in the later part, they say the old woman supports Zhaozhou. Only Xuanzhe said: The earlier monk also asked in just this way and was answered in just this way; later Zhaozhou also asked and was answered in just this way. Tell me, where is the point of examining through? Wansong said: He examined through it already. And he also said: Not only was she examined through by Zhaozhou— she was also examined through by this monk. Wansong said: It not only implicates Xuanzhe, it also implicates Wansong. Langya said: Big or small, Zhaozhou in this old woman’s hands lost body and life. Even so, there are many who misunderstand. Wansong said: Absolutely avoid using yourself to measure others. Weishan Zhe said: Monks under heaven only know to ask the old woman for the road, but do not know how deep the mud is under their own feet. If not for old Zhaozhou, how would the great merit of a hard-ridden horse be made manifest? Even so, it still required Tiantong’s praise in song. The verse says:
Old with years, become a spirit—no false transmission: Zhaozhou, an ancient Buddha, heir to Nanquan. Above all, do not bewitch other people's men and women.

text_zh: 年老成精不謬傳切忌魔魅人家男女　趙州古佛嗣南泉 鎮州端的出大蘿蔔枯龜喪命因圖象靈鬼靈神返遭羅網　良駟追風 累纏牽驟風驟雨不免󰊋韁勘破了老婆禪幾箇男兒是丈夫　說向 人前不直錢知根不聖
text_en: Zhenzhou truly produces big radishes. The withered turtle loses its life because of chart and image; the fine steed chasing the wind Clever ghosts and spirits turn around and fall into the net. gets entangled and dragged. Sudden wind and sudden rain still do not escape the reins. He examined through the old woman’s Chan and spoke it out How many men are true men? before others—it is not worth a coin. Knowing the root is not holiness.
The teacher said: Ghosts and demons become spirits through uncanny powers. Spells and medicines become potent through dependent powers. Heavenly

text_zh: 師云。鬼魅以妖通成精。呪藥以依通成精。天 龍以報通成精。賢聖以神通成精。佛祖以道 通成精。南泉趙州乃佛祖向上人。那堪年老。 所以道。年老成精也。趙州古佛嗣南泉。馬祖 道。經入藏。禪歸海。唯有南泉獨超物外。趙州 以長沙為友。以南泉為師。故勘辨中。非得失 勝負之可品格。天下謂之趙州關。也不妨難 過。雖然仲尼有言。神龜能現夢於元君。而不 能免余且之網。智能七十二鑽。而無遺筴。而 不能避刳腸之患。如是則智有所困。神有所 不及也。莊子云。宋元君夢人被髮曰。予自宰 路之淵。予為清江使河伯之所。漁者余且得 予。覺占之。神龜也。漁者果有余且。網得白 龜。其圓五尺。君欲活之。卜之曰。殺龜以卜 吉。乃刳龜。七十二鑽而無遺筴。乃其事也。洛 浦曰。欲知上流之士。不將佛祖言教貼在額 頭。如龜負圖自取喪身之兆。鳳縈金網趨霄 漢。以何期。周穆王八駿。有乘雲而趨行越飛 鳥者。故曰良駟追風也。此頌婆子能勘僧。而 不免趙州勘破。趙州雖能勘婆。而不免瑯琊 點檢。參禪謂之金屎法。不會如金。勘破如屎。 所以道。說向人前不直錢。汝但離却得失勝 負情量。自然平欺婆子。下視趙州。若到萬松 門下。不得點胸檐板。
text_en: dragons become spirits through recompense-powers. Worthies and sages become spirits through miraculous powers. Buddhas and patriarchs through the Way become spirits. Nanquan and Zhaozhou were people above Buddhas and patriarchs—how much more when aged. Therefore it is said: old with years, become a spirit. Zhaozhou, an ancient Buddha, heir to Nanquan. Mazu said: Sutras return to the treasury, Chan returns to the sea; only Nanquan alone transcends things. Zhaozhou took Changsha as friend and Nanquan as teacher. Therefore in his examinations and discernments, it is not a matter of gain and loss, victory and defeat, that can be graded. People everywhere call it Zhaozhou’s Barrier, and indeed it is no obstacle to being difficult to pass. Even so, Confucius said: The divine turtle could appear in a dream to Lord Yuan, yet it could not escape Yu Qie’s net. Its wisdom answered seventy-two drillings without a missed stalk, yet it could not avoid the calamity of having its belly cut open. Thus wisdom has where it is trapped, and spirit has where it does not reach. Zhuangzi says: Lord Yuan of Song dreamed of a man with loose hair who said, I come from the abyss of Zai Road. I was sent by the Clear River at the place of the River Earl. The fisherman Yu Qie caught me. On waking he divined it—it was a divine turtle. And indeed there was a fisherman Yu Qie who netted a white turtle, five feet around. The lord wanted to keep it alive. They divined and it said: Kill the turtle and divine by it, auspicious. So they cut open the turtle. Through seventy-two drillings there was not a missed stalk. That is the story. Luopu said: If you wish to know a person of the highest stream, do not paste the words and teachings of Buddhas and patriarchs onto your forehead. Like a turtle bearing the chart, it takes upon itself the omen of losing its life; like a phoenix caught in a golden net while racing to the heavens. men. What did he mean by that? Among King Mu of Zhou’s eight steeds, there was one that rode the clouds and sped along, surpassing flying birds. Hence it is said, a fine team of horses chases the wind. This verse praises the old woman for being able to test the monk, yet she still could not avoid being seen through by Zhaozhou. Though Zhaozhou could test the old woman, he still could not avoid Langya’s inspection. In Chan study this is called the gold-and-shit teaching. If one does not understand, it is like gold; when it is exposed, it is like shit. Therefore it is said, speaking of it before people is not worth a coin. You need only leave behind notions of gain and loss, victory and defeat, and calculating mind. Then naturally you will stand level with the old woman and look down on Zhaozhou. But if you come to Wansong’s gate, you will not be allowed to beat your chest and strut.

text_zh: 11 則雲門兩病
text_en: Case 11 Yunmen’s Two Illnesses He addressed the assembly, saying: A man without a body falls ill; a man without hands compounds medicine; a man without a mouth takes

text_zh: 示眾云。無身人患疾。無手人合藥。無口人服 食。無受人安樂。且道。膏肓之疾。如何調理。
text_en: food. A man without sensation is at ease. Tell me, how is the disease in the vital region to be treated?

Citation: Great Master Yunmen said, When the light does not break through, there are two kinds of illness. One is that nothing is clear anywhere, and before one there seems to be some thing. Do you still feel your mouth dry?

text_zh: 舉。雲門大師云。光不透脫。有兩般病還覺口乾 舌縮麼一切處不明。面前有物是一白日見鬼莫是眼花 透得一切法空。隱隱地似有箇物相似。亦 是光不透脫早是結胸那堪喉閉又法身亦有兩般病禍不 單行得到法身為法執不忘。已見猶存。墮在 法身邊是一不唯邪祟更有家親直饒透得。放過即不 可養病喪軀子細點檢將來。有甚麼氣息。亦是病 醫博未離門又早𤺛病發。
text_en: Has your tongue shrunk back? Seeing ghosts in broad daylight, is it failing eyesight? The other is that one penetrates the emptiness of all dharmas, yet dimly there still seems to be something there; this too is a failure of the light to break through. Again, the dharma body also has two kinds of illness: having attained the dharma body, one does not forget attachment to dharma; one’s view still remains, and one falls to the side of the Already a knotted chest, how could one bear a blocked throat? Disaster does not come alone. dharma body. This is one. Even if one has penetrated it, to let it go unchecked is still not Not only evil influences, but even one's own family. permissible. If one examines it carefully and asks what breath or trace remains, that too is an illness. Nursing illness and losing the body. 。 Before the skilled doctor leaves the door, the illness flares again.
The master said: Chan Master Qianfeng of Yuezhou was a dharma heir of Dongshan Wuben. Yunmen traveled widely

text_zh: 師云。越州乾峯和尚。法嗣洞山悟本。雲門遍 參曾見師與曹山疎山。此則公案先有來源。 乾峯示眾云。法身有三種病二種光。須是一 一透得。更須知有向上一竅。雲門出眾云。只 如庵內人。為甚不知庵外事。峯呵呵大笑。門 云。猶是學人疑處。峯云。子是甚麼心行。門云。 也要和尚相委悉。峯云。直須恁麼始得穩坐 地。門云。喏喏。乾峯道。法身有三種病。雲門 道。法身有兩種病。萬松行脚時。諸方商量道。 未到走作已到住著。透脫無依。是三種病。今 言二種。少未到走作。後二種病顯然大同。佛 眼和尚道。騎驢覓驢是一。騎驢了不肯下。亦 是病。乃前二病少後一種。師家一期應病施 方。各垂方便。其二種光。與光不透脫有兩般 病。無別。且一切處不明面前有物是一者。洞 山道。分明覿面別無真。爭奈迷頭還認影。若 具把定乾坤眼。綿綿不漏絲毫。方得少分相 應。又道。透得一切法空。隱隱地似有箇物相 似。亦是光不透脫。溈山所謂。無一法可當情。 見猶在境。楞嚴經云。縱滅一切見聞覺知。內 守幽閑。猶為法塵分別影事。南院顒道。我當 時如燈影裏行相似。所以道。亦是光不透脫。 洞上宗風。靜沈死水。動落今時。名二種病。爾 但出不隨應。入不居空。外不尋枝。內不住定。 自然三病。二光一時透脫。然後透脫不透脫。 拈放一邊。子細點檢將來。有甚麼氣息。亦是 病。如何得安樂去。更請天童診候。頌云。
text_en: in his training and had met this master as well as Caoshan and Shushan. This koan therefore has an earlier source. Qianfeng addressed the assembly and said: The dharma body has three kinds of illness and two kinds of light. One must pass through them one by one, and further one must know there is an opening beyond. Yunmen stepped forth and said: Just like a person inside a hut, why does he not know what is outside the hut? Qianfeng gave a hearty laugh. Yunmen said: This is still the student’s point of doubt. Qianfeng said: What sort of mind activity is this of yours? Yunmen said: I also want master to explain it fully. Qianfeng said: Only thus can one sit firmly on the ground. Yunmen said: Yes, yes. Qianfeng said the dharma body has three illnesses; Yunmen said the dharma body has two illnesses. When Wansong was traveling, people in various places discussed it, saying: Before arriving, one runs about; after arriving, one gets stuck; after breakthrough, one rests with nothing to rely on. These are the three illnesses. Now Yunmen speaks of two, omitting the first, the running about before arrival. The latter two illnesses are clearly much the same. Foyan master said: Riding a donkey while searching for a donkey is one; after finding you are riding a donkey, not being willing to dismount is also an illness. That reduces the first two illnesses and omits the last one. Teachers, for a time, prescribe remedies according to disease, each hanging down a skillful means. As for the two kinds of light, they are no different from the two kinds of illness in the failure of the light to break through. As for the phrase nothing is clear anywhere and before one there seems to be something, Dong shan said: Clearly face to face, there is no other truth, but alas, deluded people still take shadows for the head. If one possesses the eye that holds heaven and earth steady, continuous and leaving out not the slightest bit, only then does one gain a small measure of accord. Again he says, one penetrates the emptiness of all dharmas, yet dimly there seems to be some thing there. This too is a failure of the light to break through. This is what Guishan meant by, not a single dharma can match the mind, yet seeing still remains within a realm. The Shurangama Sutra says: Even if one extinguishes all seeing, hearing, awareness, and knowing, and inwardly abides in dark stillness, it is still only differentiating shadow-work of dharma dust. Nanyuan Yong said: At that time I was like walking inside a lamp’s shadow. Therefore it is said, this too is a failure of the light to break through. In the Caodong family style, stillness sinks into dead water; movement falls into the present age. These are called the two illnesses. You need only go out without following conditions, enter without dwelling in emptiness, outwardly not seeking branches, inwardly not abiding in concentration. Then naturally the three illnesses and two lights are all penetrated at once. After that, whether breakthrough or no breakthrough, set both aside. Examine carefully and ask what breath or trace remains; that too is illness. How then can one attain ease? Let us ask Tiantong to diagnose it further. The verse says:
The whole forest of myriad forms may rise in rugged splendor; breakthrough without fixed method still obstructs the eye Let him speak, what hinders you? If you recognize it, there is no grievance.

text_zh: 森羅萬象許崢嶸聽他何礙汝識得不為冤　透脫無方礙眼 睛閃捧著榾桗掃彼門庭誰有力拂迹成痕欲隱彌露　隱人胸 次自成情心疑生暗鬼船橫野渡涵秋碧死水浸却　棹入 蘆花照雪明住岸却迷人串錦老漁懷就市著本圖利　飄 飄一葉浪頭行隨流得妙
text_en: s. In a flash, brandishing the cudgel. Who has the strength to sweep that gate and courtyard? Hidden in a person’s breast Brushing away traces leaves marks; the more you hide, the more it shows. a feeling forms of itself. Doubt in the mind breeds hidden ghosts. A boat lies across a wild ford, holding autumn’s blue; the oar enters Dead water has soaked it through. reeds and blossoms shining bright as snow. Staying on the bank only confuses people. An old fisherman, with brocade strung, heads toward the market, drifting Putting down capital to seek profit. lightly, a single leaf moving atop the waves. Following the current, one finds the subtlety.
The master cited: The Dharma Phrase Sutra says, The whole forest and the myriad forms are stamped by the one dharma. One

text_zh: 師舉。法句經云。森羅及萬象一法之所印。一 即萬萬即一。即此物。非他物。一任崢嶸磊落。 荒田不揀草。淨地却迷人。直饒透脫無方正 是礙眼睛處。圓覺經道。於諸妄心。亦不息滅。 洞山道。靈苗瑞草。野父愁耘。何必掃彼門庭。 空一切法。雲門道。一切處不明。面前有物是 一。不是教爾除幻境滅幻心。別覓透脫處。三 祖道。六塵不惡。還同正覺。與圓覺經知幻即 離。不作方便。離幻即覺亦無漸次。便見作止 任滅。如金剛與泥人揩背也。又道。隱人胸次 自成情。此頌隱隱地似有箇物相似。正是圓 覺存我覺我。潛續如命。細四相病。故普覺云。 大悲世尊快說禪病。舡橫野渡涵秋碧。此頌 得到法身。纜舡於澄源湛水。疎山以法身為 枯樁。此真繫驢橛也。直待撥轉舡子。未免棹 入蘆花照雪明處。到此清光照眼似迷家。明 白轉身還墮位。此頌直饒透得。放過即不可。 到此雲門道盡。天童頌徹也。然後要見雲門 意旨天童眼目。這裏便是計利害處。如何是 雲門意旨。不見道。子細點檢將來。有什麼氣 息。亦是病。雲門但指其病不說治法。如何是 天童眼目。述雲門治方。云。串錦老漁懷就市。 飄飄一葉浪頭行。雲門大意。在入󱈎垂手不 避風波。可謂自病既除。復愍他疾。淨名之心 也。還知麼。病多諳藥性。得效敢傳方。
text_en: is precisely ten thousand, and ten thousand precisely one. It is this thing, not another thing. Let it be as rugged and bold as it may. In a wild field one does not choose among weeds; in a pure ground one instead confuses people. Even if breakthrough has no fixed method, that is exactly where it obstructs the eyes. The Perfect Enlightenment Sutra says: As for all deluded minds, one does not even extinguish them. Dongshan said: Spiritual sprouts and auspicious grasses make the old farmer worry about weeding. Why must one sweep that gate and courtyard? If one empties all dharmas, Yunmen says, nothing is clear anywhere, and before one there seems to be some thing. He is not teaching you to remove illusory objects and extinguish the illusory mind, then seek elsewhere for a place of breakthrough. The Third Patriarch said: The six sense-objects are not evil; they are the same as right awakening. This matches the Perfect Enlightenment Sutra: Knowing illusion, one at once departs from it, without using expedients. Departing from illusion is awakening, and there are no stages. Then one sees that acting and stopping, letting be and extinguishing, are like a vajra rubbing the back of a clay man. Again it says, hidden in a person’s breast a feeling forms of itself. This verse praises that dim sense that there seems to be some thing there; this is exactly the Perfect Enlightenment’s clinging to I and what awakens in me, secretly continuing like life itself, the subtle illness of the four marks. Therefore Pujue said: Great compassionate World-Honored One, please swiftly explain the illnesses of Chan. A boat lies across a wild ford, holding autumn’s blue. This verse praises attaining the dharma body, mooring the boat in clear source and deep waters. Shushan took the dharma body to be a dead stump. This is truly a donkey-tethering post. Only when one turns the boat around does one avoid, yet still not escape, rowing into the place where reed blossoms shine bright as snow. At this point the clear light dazzles the eyes and one seems to lose one’s home. When one clearly turns the body around, one still falls into position. This verse praises: even if you have penetrated it, letting it pass unchecked is not allowed. At this point Yunmen has said all he can, and Tiantong’s verse too has exhausted it. After that, if you want to see Yunmen’s intent and Tiantong’s eye, this is exactly the place where gain and loss are reckoned. What is Yunmen’s intent? Have you not seen him say: Examine carefully and ask what breath or trace remains; that too is illness. Yunmen only points out the illness and does not speak the cure. What is Tiantong’s eye? He states Yunmen’s remedy, saying: An old fisherman, with brocade strung, heads toward the market. Lightly, a single leaf moves atop the waves. Yunmen’s great meaning lies in entering the world with hanging hands and not avoiding wind and waves. It may be said that once one’s own illness is removed, one then pities the illnesses of others. This is Vimalakirti’s heart indeed. Do you understand? One long sick knows the nature of medicines; having found effect, one dares pass on the prescription.

text_zh: 12 地藏種田
text_en: 12 Dizang Plants the Fields He addressed the assembly, saying: Men of talent plow with the brush; eloquent men plow with the tongue. In our house of patched-robe monks, we are too lazy to look at

text_zh: 示眾云。才士筆耕。辯士舌耕。我衲僧家。慵看 露地白牛。不顧無根瑞草。如何度日。
text_en: the white ox in the open ground and pay no heed to rootless auspicious grass. How do we pass our days?
Citation: Dizang asked Head Monk Xiu, Where have you come from? Xiu said: Can you say you do not know where it comes from?

text_zh: 舉。地藏問脩山主。甚處來道不知來處得麼脩云。 南方來好與下載藏云。南方近日佛法如何行說好話 脩云。商量浩浩地低聲藏云。爭如我這裏種 田博飯喫少賣弄脩云。爭奈三界何猶有這箇在藏云。 爾喚甚麼作三界南方猶可北方更曬。
text_en: From the south. Dizang said: How is the Buddha Dharma in the south these days? Best to strike it down. Go on, say fine words. Xiu said: There is vast, bustling discussion. Dizang said: How does that compare with my planting In a low voice. fields here to earn food to eat? Xiu said: But what about the three realms? Dizang said: Show off less. This is still here. What do you call the three realms? The south is still passable; the north is even drier.

text_en: Stone Mountain west of Min City, built Dizang Monastery and invited the master to reside there. After more than a decade he moved to Zhangzhou Luohan, so the master was also called Dizang. Head Monk Xiu, Fayan, Wukong, and Jin the head monk, had made friends beyond the lakes. Reaching Zhangzhou, they were blocked by rain and snow; the streams had risen, so they lodged in the city’s western Dizang Monastery. Sitting around the brazier, they looked at Dizang as if no one were there. Dizang wanted to test them and also came near the fire. Then he said: May I borrow a question about something? Xiu said: If there is something, please ask. Dizang said: Mountains, rivers, and the great earth, together with all the venerable monks, are they the same or different? Xiu said: They are different. Dizang held up two fingers. Xiu hastily said: They are the same, the same. Dizang also held up two fingers and got up to leave. Fayan said: What was the abbot’s meaning in holding up two fingers? Xiu said: Random babble. Fayan said: You must not, with a coarse mind, deceive him. Xiu said: How could a rat’s mouth have elephant tusks? The next day they took leave. Before reaching their lodging place, Fayan said: You brothers go on ahead. I will stay with Dizang. If there is something excellent there, fine; if not, I will come back and find you. Once Fayan had long practiced there, Xiu and the other two also came to Dizang. He then asked: How is the Buddha Dharma in the south these days? At that time it would only have been fitting to say, It is just the same as here on ordinary days. Instead he said, bustling discussion everywhere, and without knowing it he himself stuck his head out. Dizang said: How does that compare with my here planting fields to earn food to eat? At that time it would have been good to say: If so, then not only in the south but elsewhere as well. Instead he further said, But what about the three realms? implicating all those Chan travelers from the south; worldly habits still not removed. Out of compassion, Dizang spoke in a rough, descending way, saying: What do you call the three realms? Better simply to say, This old monk is busy planting fields, and thus avoid receiving a formal charge from Tiantong. The verse says:

text_zh: 師云。清涼道。宗通自修行。說通示未悟。本出 楞伽經。佛告大慧。有二種通。宗通者。為緣自 得勝進相。遠離言說文字妄想。趣無漏界。緣 自覺趣。光明輝發。是名宗通相。云何說通相。 謂說九部種種教法。離異不異有無等相。以 巧方便。如應說法。是名說通相。講徒云。說通。 宗不通。如日被雲籠。宗通。說不通。如蛇入竹 筒。宗通。說亦通。如日處虛空。宗說俱不通。 如犬吠茅叢。既分宗說。已是兩岐。那堪禪分 五派。教列三乘。箇中一亦不立。皆強為也。何 況出口入耳。請益拈頌。葛藤引蔓過新羅。鞏 縣茶瓶湯不絕。非但南方商量浩浩地。若是 道火不燒口底人。辯似懸河元無一字。種田 博飯雖是家常。其奈不是飽參不知其趣。古 人深山裏。钁頭邊。折脚鐺中。煮脫粟飯。富不 過知足。一世不求人。貴不過清閑。何須印如 斗。所以道。參飽明知無所求。子房終不貴封 侯。史記漢六年封功臣。或謂張良未甞有戰 鬪功。高帝曰。運籌帷幄之中。決勝千里之外。 子房功也。使自擇齊三萬戶。良曰。始臣下邳 與上會留。此天以臣授陛下。用臣計而幸時 中。臣願封留足矣。不敢當三萬戶。此頌不必 開堂演法斆南方也。離騷經漁父歌曰。滄浪 之水清兮。可以濯我纓。滄浪之水濁兮。可以 濯我足。此乃猿鶴共處。魚鳥同游。且道。是甚 麼人。本色檐板漢。
text_en: Lankavatara Sutra. The Buddha told Mahamati: There are two kinds of penetration. Penetration in the school is, by relying on one’s own realization, obtaining the marks of superior advance, far removed from delusive imaginings of speech and letters, proceeding toward the undefiled realm, relying on self-awakened approach, with radiant light shining forth. This is called the mark of penetration in the school. What is the mark of penetration in explanation? It means expounding the various teachings of the nine divisions, concerning marks such as difference and non-difference, being and non-being, and so on, using skillful means to teach according to what is appropriate. This is called the mark of penetration in explanation. Lecture monks say: Explanation penetrates, but the school does not penetrate, like the sun enclosed by clouds. The school penetrates, but explanation does not, like a snake entering a bamboo tube. The school penetrates, and explanation also penetrates, like the sun in empty space. Neither school nor explanation penetrates, like a dog barking at a thicket. Once one divides school and explanation, one has already split into two roads. How much worse that Chan is split into five houses and doctrine arranged into three vehicles. Within this, not even one is established; all is forced contrivance. How much more so when it comes out the mouth and enters the ear, asking for instruction, citing and versifying, vines and creepers trailing all the way past Silla. Gong county’s tea-bottle soup never runs dry. It is not only the south where discussions bustle noisily. If one is a person whose words do not burn the mouth, eloquence may be like a hanging river, yet originally there is not a single word. Planting fields to earn food, though it is everyday life, still, unless practice is full, one does not know its flavor. In ancient times people in deep mountains, beside the hoe, in a broken-legged pot, cooked coarse millet rice. Their wealth did not exceed knowing sufficiency. All their lives they sought nothing from others. Their nobility did not exceed pure leisure. Why need seals as big as a peck measure? Therefore it is said: When practice is full, one clearly knows there is nothing to seek; Zhang Liang in the end did not prize enfeoffment as marquis. In the Records of the Grand Historian, in the sixth year of Han, merit officials were enfeoffed. Someone said Zhang Liang had never had military achievements in battle. Emperor Gao said: He devised plans within the command tent and determined victory a thousand li away. That was Zhang Liang’s merit. He was allowed to choose for himself thirty thousand households in Qi. Liang said: At first I, at Xiapi, met Your Majesty at Liu. This was Heaven granting me to Your Majesty. Using my plans, and luckily at the right times they succeeded. I wish only to be enfeoffed at Liu, and that is enough. I dare not accept thirty thousand households. This verse does not require opening the hall and expounding the Dharma in the southern style. In the Li Sao, the Fisherman’s Song says: The waters of Canglang if clear, may wash my tassels; the waters of Canglang if muddy, may wash my feet. This is where apes and cranes dwell together, fish and birds roam together. Tell me, what sort of person is this? A true plank-shouldered fellow.

text_zh: 師云。臨際囑三聖不得滅却吾正法眼藏。此 與興化謂克賓維那汝不久為唱道之師。罰 饡飯出院。機用一般。其實此事。千佛出世不 增。千聖入滅不減。豈一三聖能興滅哉。古人 臨終顯發此事。亦表眾中有人。果然三聖出 云。爭敢滅却和尚正法眼藏。如人被罵不甘 者承頭。當時便與本分草料。正法眼藏。未到 滅却。却道。忽有人問汝作麼生對。當斷不斷。 返招其亂。聖便喝。上代下世。門裏出身。耳聾 三日以來。不似而今這喝。際云。誰知吾正法 眼藏。向這瞎驢邊滅却。當時臨際門風。自有 正令。可惜放過。不知天童如何判斷。頌云。
text_en: is like Xinghua saying to Vinaya Overseer Kebin, Before long you will become a teacher who proclaims the Way, and then punishing After eating gruel and rice he left the hall; the functioning of the device was the same. In truth, this matter is not increased by a thousand Buddhas appearing in the world, nor diminished by a thousand sages entering extinction. How could a single Sansheng make it rise or perish? The ancients, at the time of death, revealed this matter; it also showed there was someone in the assembly. Sure enough, Sansheng stepped forth and said, How would I dare extinguish the Master’s treasury of the true Dharma eye? Like a man insulted who cannot let it pass, he takes it head-on. At that very time he was given his proper fodder. The treasury of the true Dharma eye had not yet been extinguished, yet he said, If suddenly someone asked you, how would you answer? When one should cut but does not cut, one only invites disorder. Sansheng then shouted. In former generations and later ages, those born from this gate have had ringing ears for three days, but they were not like this present shout. Linji said, Who knew that my treasury of the true Dharma eye would be extinguished at the side of this blind donkey? At that time the style of Linji’s house had its own correct command. Mind sealing mind, patriarchs transmitting the lamp, leveling seas and mountains. A smuggler of illicit salt. Boring through the wall to steal light. text_en: and to this day some still do not recognize it. Such a method can truly make the kun and roc transform, and the seas and mountains level out. Dayui Xiu said: The ancients endured until death waiting for one to come; why then did the treasury of the true Dharma eye instead get extinguished at the side of a blind donkey? Linji acted too quickly, and Sansheng too was hasty. Thus father and son forgot their feeling, and later people were left disappointed. If one cannot get flowing water, one should still pass over another mountain. In this record Sansheng then bowed. That was not yet the best move. Linji then gave a verse, saying: The flow does not cease, so how ask what it is? True illumination is boundless, and I speak of it to him. Those beyond form and beyond name do not receive it. Once the hair-blowing sword has been used, it must at once be sharpened. When the verse was finished, he sat upright and passed away. Tiantong, taking up this koan, stops right at the proper place. Sansheng’s bow and Linji’s verse both greatly let things go by, lightly letting go. Is there anyone who can breathe out for the ancients? Dangerous.

text_en: towering to the heavens—why then was he let go? He did not know that to seize an ox you need no rope; to kill a man you need no knife. When was he ever really let off? Old Huanglong said: Deshan feigned deafness and played dumb; though he secretly gained an advantage, Master Kuo covered his ears while stealing a bell— but what can he do about the ugliness seen by bystanders? Wansong said: It is more than stealing a bell—like at the bottom of a ninefold deep abyss, beneath the black dragon’s jaw, plucking the pearl just when the dragon sleeps; if it awoke, he would surely be ground to bits. Dayui Zhe said: If you do not ascend the Dragon Gate, how would you know the vastness of the blue sea? Even if waves strike a thousand fathoms, what can you do if the Dragon King does not care? Wansong said: Tiny scales and scraps of shell are nothing to marvel at. Foguo said: Deshan truly had vicious hands and feet. Seeing this monk was not one to receive hammer and tongs, he therefore just let it rest. Wansong said: When the ancients met situations and faced occasions, each had expedient means. Deshan said to Yantou, Later on you will crap on this old monk’s head. Later Yantou indeed said, Big or small, Deshan does not understand the final phrase. The ancients raised and lowered, released and seized—how could they be bound by gain and loss, victory and defeat? Huanglong and Dayui only lifted the broad outline. Look further: Tiantong’s verse brings out the deep subtleties. The verse says:
When it comes face to face, the adept knows; in such a moment, spark-fire and lightning are too slow. The deluded do not notice. Already past Silla.

text_zh: 師云。從上諸聖。向什麼處去也。大似當面蹉 過。德山道。作麼作麼。德山影草藏身。拈出曜 眼鏡。昔七賢女游屍多林。一女云。屍在這裏。 人在什麼處。一女云。作麼作麼。諸女相顧悉 皆悟道。感得天帝散花供養。德山用此一機。 借路經過。決不得恁麼會。所以道。可中石火 電光遲。德山豈不知侍者放伊不過。下媒求 鴿。著本圖利。果然出他彀中不得。忽有人問 萬松甚麼處去也。攔腮掌云。在這裏。直教飛 龍跛鱉縮項攢蹄。侍者德山亡鋒結舌。還識 德山老漢麼。少年曾決龍蛇陣。潦倒還聽稚 子歌。
text_en: Deshan said, What? what? Deshan hid himself in decoy grass, then produced a dazzling mirror before the eyes. Formerly seven wise women toured the charnel forest. One woman said, The corpse is here— where is the person? One woman said, What? what? The women looked at one another and all awakened to the Way. It moved the heavenly emperor to scatter flowers in offering. Deshan used this same device, passing by on a borrowed road; one absolutely must not understand it that way. Therefore it says: in that very midst, spark-fire and lightning are slow. How could Deshan not know the attendant could not let him pass? He set a go-between to seek the dove, laying out the capital to make profit. Sure enough, he could not escape his snare. If suddenly someone asked Wansong, Where are you going?—I would slap him across the cheek and say, Right here. This would make the flying dragon and lame turtle draw in necks and gather their feet; attendant and Deshan would both lose their edge and tie their tongues. Do you yet recognize old fellow Deshan? In youth he once broke the dragon-serpent battle lines; in decline he still listens to a child’s song.

text_zh: 15 仰山插鍬
text_en: 15. Yangshan Sticks in the Spade Instruction to the assembly: Knowing before words are spoken is called silent discourse. Not clarifying yet revealing itself is called

text_zh: 示眾云。未語先知。謂之默論。不明自顯。謂之 暗機。三門前合掌。兩廊下行道。有箇意度。中 庭上作舞。後門外搖頭。又作麼生。
text_en: the hidden pivot. Joining palms before the monastery gate, walking the way beneath the two corridors—there is a certain meaning there. In the courtyard one dances; outside the rear gate one shakes the head—what about that?
Raised: Guishan asked Yangshan, Where have you come from? Yangshan said, From the fields. It is not that you do not know where it comes from.

text_zh: 舉。溈山問仰山。甚處來不是不知來處仰云。田中 來儞為甚落草山云。田中多少人只父子兩箇仰插下鍬 子。叉手而立放去較危山云。南山大有人刈茆打草 驚蛇仰拈鍬子便行收來太速。
text_en: Guishan said, How many people are in the fields? Yangshan stuck down the spade Why then do you fall among the outlaws? Only father and son, the two of them. and stood with hands crossed. Guishan said, On South Mountain many are cutting thatch. Yangshan picked up the spade and went off. Letting it go is more dangerous. Beat the grass and startle the snake. Pulling it in too quickly.
The master said: Teacher and disciple accorded with the Way; father and son matched in the pivot. The style of the Gui-Yang house is a thousand-year tortoise mirror.

text_zh: 師云。師資合道。父子投機。溈仰家風千古龜 鑑。溈山問仰山。甚處來。溈山豈不知仰山田 中來。垂此一問。要與仰山相見。仰山不負來 問。只道箇田中來。且道。還有佛法道理也。無 溈山深入虎穴。更問田中多少人。仰山插鍬 子叉手而立。便衲僧相見。玄沙云。我當時若 見。便與踏倒鍬子。萬松道。忍俊不禁。投子青 禪師頌云。溈山問處少知音。插地酬他佛祖 沈。踏倒玄沙傍不肯。免教蒼翠帶春深。萬松 道。草枯鷹眼疾。南嶽法輪。平禪師頌云。狹路 相逢避不及。插下鍬時叉手立。過得橋來岸 上行。始覺渾身泥水濕。萬松道。不堪迴首月 明中。二老宿頌處。只有千尺寒松。更看。天童 放出抽條石笋。頌云。
text_en: Guishan asked Yangshan, Where have you come from? Did Guishan not know Yangshan came from the fields? He let down this one question in order to meet Yangshan. Yangshan did not fail the question; he only said, From the fields. Tell me, is there still some Buddhist doctrine in this or not? Guishan went deep into the tiger’s den and again asked, How many people are in the fields? Yangshan stuck in the spade and stood with folded hands; at once patch-robed monks met each other. Xuansha said, If I had been there then, I would have kicked over the spade. Wansong said: Unable to suppress a laugh. Master Touzi Qing in verse said: Few know the tune where Guishan questioned; thrusting the spade into the ground, he answered Buddha and patriarchs and sank them. Xuansha’s kicking it over is a side refusal, lest the green mountains be burdened with deep spring. Wansong said: When the grass is dry, the hawk’s eye is keen. Master Ping of Nanyue Falun wrote: On a narrow road when they meet, there is no room to avoid each other. When he stuck down the spade he stood with folded hands; after crossing the bridge he came to the bank and walked on; only then he realized his whole body was wet with mud and water. Wansong said: One cannot bear to look back in the moonlight. In the verses of these two old worthies there is only a thousand-foot cold pine. Look further—Tiantong lets loose a stone shoot sending out branches. His verse says:
The old awakened one, rich in feeling, thinks of his descendants; now, ashamed, they rise up to continue the household. Too much old-woman concern. For thirty years not

text_en: lacking salt and vinegar. It is necessary to remember the words of South Mountain, carving them into bone and inscribing them in flesh, together repaying the grace. Noble people forget much. A resentful mind does not let go.
The master said: This verse is like Han Yu’s Biography of Mao Ying—principle and event both are manifest, truth and convention both

text_zh: 師云。此頌如韓文毛頴傳。理事雙彰。真俗並 舉。一往觀來。溈山為老覺。仰山以下為子孫。 就裏即不然。僧問長沙岑大蟲。本來人還成 佛否。山云。爾道。大唐天子還割茅刈草否。是 知。刈茆乃臣子邊事。而今慚愧起家門。千年 無影樹。今時沒底靴。住持千嶂月。衣鉢一溪 雲。皆是得力兒孫紹承家業。是知。君臣父子。 非特曹洞創立。溈仰父子已行此令。若不是 溈山點破。一向光影門頭。弄粥飯氣。驢前馬 後。以當平生。甚為可惜。所以天童教。記取南 山刈茆一轉語。鏤骨銘肌報恩不盡。法燈云。 野老負薪歸。催婦連宵織。看他家事忙。且道 承誰力。問渠渠不知。特地生疑惑。傷嗟今古 人。幾箇知恩德。知有後如何。斷臂不覺痛。立 雪不敢倦。所以萬松老來住報恩院。
text_en: are raised together. Looking at it one way, Guishan is the old awakened one, and Yangshan and those below are the descendants. But within it, it is not so. A monk asked Changsha Cen the Great Insect, Can the original person still become a Buddha? Changsha said, Tell me—does the Son of Heaven of Great Tang still cut thatch and mow grass? Thus we know cutting thatch is the business of ministers and sons. Now, ashamed, they rise up to continue the household. A thousand-year shadowless tree; in these times, bottomless boots. Upholding the moon over a thousand peaks; robe and bowl in a stream of clouds—all these are capable descendants inheriting the family enterprise. Thus we know ruler and minister, father and son— this was not first established by Caodong; the father-and-son pair of Gui and Yang had already carried out this command. If it were not for Guishan pointing it out, one would only linger at the gate of light and shadow, playing with the breath of gruel-and-rice Zen, in front of donkeys and behind horses, taking that for one’s whole life—most regrettable. Therefore Tiantong taught: Remember the South Mountain phrase about cutting thatch; carve it into bone and inscribe it in flesh, and still you cannot exhaust repaying the grace. Fadeng said: An old rustic carries firewood home, urging his wife to weave through the night. Look how busy his household affairs are—but tell me, by whose strength is this sustained? Ask him and he does not know; for no reason doubt and confusion arise. Alas for people of past and present— how many know grace and virtue? Once they truly know, what then? Cutting off an arm they do not feel pain; standing in snow they dare not grow weary. Therefore in old age Wansong lived at Bao’en Monastery.

text_zh: 16 麻谷振錫
text_en: 16. Magu Shakes the Staff Instruction to the assembly: Point to a deer and call it a horse; clutch earth and make gold. On the tongue rise wind and thunder; between the brows

text_zh: 示眾云。指鹿為馬。握土成金。舌上起風雷。眉 間藏血刃。坐觀成敗。立驗死生。且道。是何三 昧。
text_en: a bloodied blade is hidden. Sitting, one watches success and failure; standing, one tests life and death. Tell me, what kind of samadhi is this?
Raised: Magu carried his staff to Zhangjing, circled the meditation seat three times, shook the staff once,

text_zh: 舉。麻谷持錫到章敬。遶禪床三匝振錫一下。 卓然而立可曬有禪敬云。是是且信一半谷又到南泉。 遶禪床三匝振錫一下。卓然而立來朝更獻楚王看 泉云。不是不是也且信一半谷云。章敬道是。和尚 為什麼道不是棺木裏睜眼泉云。章敬即是。是汝 不是雪上加霜此是風力所轉終成敗壞殺人須見血。
text_en: and stood straight and still. Zhangjing said, Yes, yes. Magu then went to Nanquan. How laughable—he has “Zen.” For now, believe half of it. He circled the meditation seat three times, shook the staff once, and stood straight and still. Tomorrow, present it again for the King of Chu to see. Nanquan said, No, no. Magu said, Zhangjing said yes—why does master And again, believe only half. say no? Nanquan said, Zhangjing is yes; it is you who are Opening one’s eyes inside the coffin. not. This is turned by the force of the wind and in the end becomes ruin and decay. Frost added on top of snow. To kill a man, you must see blood.
The master said: Formerly Yangshan went to Zhongyi to thank him for the precepts. Zhongyi, on the meditation seat, clapped his

text_zh: 師云。昔日仰山到中邑謝戒。邑於禪床上拍 手云。阿㖿阿㖿仰從西過東。從東過西。復向 中心立。然後謝戒。邑云。甚處得此三昧。仰云。 於曹溪脫印子學來。邑云。汝道。曹溪三昧接 甚麼人。仰云。接一宿覺。仰復問。和尚甚處得 此三昧。邑云。馬大師處得此三昧。蒲州麻谷 寶徹禪師。恰如永嘉初見六祖。持錫到章敬。 遶禪床三匝振錫一下。卓然而立。也如曹溪 脫印子學來。此名三昧王三昧。一切三昧皆 從此生。章敬道。是是。萬松道。有何不可。勝 默光和尚道。是無可是。非無真非。是非無主。 萬善同歸。梟鷄晝夜徒自支離。我無三寸。鱉 得喚龜。迦葉不肯。一任攢眉。萬松道。多愁早 老。麻谷要與諸方勘同。麻谷又曾到忠國師 處。遶禪床三匝振錫而立。國師云。既能如是。 何用更見貧道。谷又振錫。國師云。這野狐精 出去。看他賓主相見。有照有用。有首有尾。良 由熟處難忘慣得其便。又到南泉遶床。振錫 依前而立。南泉却道。不是不是。便似曾與章 敬廝計會來。大溈喆云。章敬道是。落在麻谷 彀中。南泉道不是。亦落在麻谷彀中。大溈即 不然。忽有人持錫遶禪床三匝。卓然而立。但 向伊道。未到這裏好。與三十棒。萬松道。不可 口行人事。便打。谷云。章敬道是。和尚為什 麼。道不是。不妨疑著。泉云。章敬即是。是汝 不是。見機而作。臨險推人。圓通善國師道。麻 谷即是。南泉不是。此語正如鄧峯永庵主問 僧審奇。汝久不見。何所為。奇曰。近見偉藏 主。有箇安樂處。永曰。試舉似我。奇因敘其 所得。永曰。汝是偉未是。奇莫測。歸語於偉。 偉大笑曰。汝非永不非也。奇走質於積翠南 禪師。南亦大笑。永聞之作偈曰。明暗相參殺 活機。大人境界普賢知。同條生不同條死。笑 倒庵中老古錐。覺範云。觀其語言。想見當時 法喜游戲之逸韻。萬松道。麻谷章敬南泉。此 興亦不淺。若聞此是風力所轉終成敗壞。更 是好笑。這王老師。不唯把定乾坤。兼有出身 之路。保寧勇和尚頌云。顏色規模恰似真。人 前拈弄越光新。及乎入火重烹鍊。到了終歸 是假銀。麻谷到此。瓦解氷消。若要氷河發焰 鐵樹花開。須得天童別下一轉語。頌云。
text_en: hands and said, Ah, ah! Yangshan went from west to east, from east to west, and again stood facing the center; only then did he thank him for the precepts. Zhongyi said, Where did you get this samadhi? Yangshan said, I learned it from Caoqi’s cast-off seal. Zhongyi said, Tell me, Caoqi’s samadhi receives what sort of person? Yangshan said, It receives One-Night Enlightenment. Yangshan then asked, Where did master get this samadhi? Zhongyi said, I got this samadhi from Great Master Ma. Magu of Puzhou, Chan master Baoche, was just like Yongjia when he first met the Sixth Patriarch. He carried his staff to Zhangjing, circled the meditation seat three times, shook the staff once, and stood straight and still. It was also like learning from Caoqi’s cast-off seal. This is called the Samadhi-King samadhi; all samadhis are born from this. Zhangjing said, Yes, yes. Wansong said, What is wrong with that? Sheng Moguang the monk said: In yes there is no fixed yes; in no there is no true no. Yes and no have no master. The myriad goods return together. Owl and rooster, day and night, vainly split themselves apart. I have no three-inch tongue; can a turtle be called a tortoise? Kasyapa would not agree; let him knit his brows as he likes. Wansong said: Much sorrow brings early old age. Magu wanted to test and compare with the monasteries everywhere. Magu had also once gone to National Teacher Zhong, where he circled the meditation seat three times, shook the staff, and stood. The National Teacher said, Since you can do thus, what use is there in seeing this poor monk again? Magu shook the staff again. The National Teacher said, This wild fox spirit— get out! Look at how host and guest meet: there is illumination and there is function, there is a head and there is a tail. Truly, from long familiarity it is hard to forget, and habit makes it easy. He then went to Nanquan, circled the seat, and shook the staff, standing as before. Nanquan, however, said, No, no. It was as if he had already made arrangements with Zhangjing. Dayui Zhe said: When Zhangjing said yes, he fell into Magu’s trap. When Nanquan said no, he also fell into Magu’s trap. As for Dayui, it was not so. If suddenly someone carried a staff, circled the meditation seat three times, and stood straight and still, I would only say to him, Better not come to this point, and give him thirty blows. Wansong said: One must not merely speak of acting—just strike. Magu said, Zhangjing said yes; why does master say no? It does no harm to leave him in doubt. Nanquan said, Zhangjing is yes; it is you who are not. Acting on the pivot when it appears, pushing a man at the edge of danger. National Teacher Shanguo of Yuantong said: Magu is yes; Nanquan is not. These words are exactly like when Yong, hermitage master of Dengfeng, asked the monk Shenqi, We have not met for long—what have you been doing? Qi said, Recently I met Treasury Master Wei, and there was a place of ease. Yong said, Try to tell it to me. Qi then related what he had attained. Yong said, You are yes, Wei is not. Qi could not fathom it, and returned and told Wei. Wei laughed loudly and said, You are not, and Yong is not-not. Qi ran to verify this with Nanchan of Jicui. Nanchan also laughed loudly. When Yong heard of it, he made a verse, saying: Bright and dark intermingle in the killing and life-giving pivot; only Samantabhadra knows the realm of great persons. On the same branch one lives, on a different branch one dies. Smile... The old adept in Daoan Hermitage. Juefan said, observing his words, one can imagine the elegant charm of his Dharma-joy play at that time. Wansong said, Magu, Zhangjing, and Nanquan all had no shallow inspiration here. If one hears this as merely something turned by the force of wind and destined to decay and fail, that is even more laughable. This Teacher Wang not only held heaven and earth firmly in hand, he also had a way out. Monk Yong of Baoning praised it, saying: In color and form it seems exactly real; before people it is handled and displayed, newly gleaming. But once it enters the fire and is smelted again, in the end it turns out to be false silver. When Magu reached this point, tiles shattered and ice melted away. If you want icy rivers to burst into flame and iron trees to bloom, you must have Tiantong provide another turning phrase. The verse says:
Is and is not, look well at the snare, seeming to press down, seeming to raise up. The slim-waisted drum is struck from both ends. The prickly point is right in there already.

text_zh: 是與不是細腰鼓子兩頭打　好看棬䙡刺頭在裏許了也　似抑似 揚手擡手捺難兄難弟頭高頭低　縱也彼既臨時翻手是雲　奪 也我何特地覆手是雨金錫一振太孤標脫塵離俗　繩床 三遶閑游戲因行掉臂叢林擾擾是非生矮子看戲　想像 髑髏前見鬼家有白澤之圖必無如是妖怪
text_en: Raising. Hands lift, hands press down. Hard to be elder brother, hard to be younger brother. Even if he seizes in the moment, Heads high, heads low. Turn the hand and it is clouds. if so, why should I make anything special of it? Turn it over and it is rain. One shake of the golden staff, supremely solitary and lofty; around the rope-bed Shedding dust and leaving the ordinary. three circuits, leisurely at play. Swinging the arms while walking along. In the monasteries, bustling and noisy, right and wrong give rise to imaginings; A short man watching the opera. before a skull they see ghosts. If a house has the Baize diagram, there will be no such monsters.
The master said: This public case rests entirely on the point of is and is not. People nowadays all say

text_zh: 師云。此箇公案。全在是與不是處。時人盡道。 麻谷被草敬南泉調弄。唯大溈喆道。章敬道 是。也落在麻谷彀中。南泉道不是。亦落在麻 谷彀中。如金剛寶處於日中光色無定。天童 道。好看棬䙡。且麻谷落棬䙡。南泉落棬䙡。似 抑似揚。難兄難弟。天童道。一往觀來。似抑似 揚。點檢將來。難兄難弟。東漢陳元方子長文。 即陳群也。與季方子孝光。各論其父功德。爭 之不決。咨於太丘。太丘即陳寔。元方季方父 也。太丘曰。元方難為兄。季方難為弟。此謂章 敬左眼半斤。南泉右眼八兩。金錫一振太孤 標。永嘉證道經亦云。不是標形虛事治。如來 寶杖親蹤跡。雪竇道。古策風高十二門。門門 有路空蕭索。錫杖經云。十二環者。用念十二 因緣修行十二門禪。十二緣易知。十二門。四 禪四無量四無色定。古策風高。即太孤標也。 六祖亦云。夫沙門具三千威儀八萬細行。大 德何方而來生大我慢。天童意道。不是標形 亦。非我慢。繩床三遶閑游戲。章敬道是。南泉 道不是。叢林擾擾是非裏走作。若無把定乾 坤眼。盡是髑髏前見鬼。不見。僧問九峯。如何 是把定乾坤眼。峯云。乾坤在裏許。僧云。乾坤 眼何在。峯云。正是乾坤眼。僧云。適來為什 麼。道乾坤在裏許。峯云。若不恁麼。髑髏前見 鬼無數。萬松這裏有箇禁師。卓拄杖一下云。 急急如律令。
text_en: Magu was toyed with by Zhangjing and Nanquan. Only Dawei Zhe said: When Zhangjing said is, he too fell into Magu's trap; when Nanquan said is not, he also fell into Magu's trap. It is like a diamond jewel in the sun, its light and color unfixed. Tiantong said, Look well at the snare. Magu falls into the snare; Nanquan falls into the snare. Is it pressing down or raising up? Hard to be elder brother, hard to be younger brother. Tiantong means that at first glance it seems to suppress and seems to elevate; but when checked in detail, hard to be elder brother, hard to be younger brother. In the Eastern Han, Chen Yuanfang's son was Changwen, namely Chen Qun. Together with Jifang's son Xiaoguang, they each discussed their fathers' merits and could not settle it, so they asked Taiqiu. Taiqiu was Chen Shi, the father of Yuanfang and Jifang. Taiqiu said, Yuanfang is hard to be the elder brother; Jifang is hard to be the younger brother. This means Zhangjing's left eye is half a catty and Nanquan's right eye is eight liang. One shake of the golden staff, supremely solitary and lofty. The Yongjia Song of Enlightenment also says, It is not a matter of displaying outward form and handling empty affairs; it is the Tathagata's precious staff, a personal trace. Xuedou said, The ancient staff's wind is high through the twelve gates; in every gate there is a path, empty and desolate. The Sutra of the Staff says the twelve rings are for contemplating the twelve links of dependent origination and cultivating the twelve-gate meditation. The twelve links are easy to know. The twelve gates are the four dhyanas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless samadhis. The ancient staff's wind being high is precisely this supremely solitary loftiness. The Sixth Patriarch also said, A renunciant possesses three thousand dignified deportments and eighty thousand subtle practices. Great virtue, from where does this great arrogance arise? Tiantong's meaning is: it is not display of form, nor is it arrogance. Three times around the rope-bed, leisurely at play. Zhangjing said is; Nanquan said is not. The monasteries bustle and rush about inside right and wrong. If one lacks the eye that firmly holds heaven and earth, then all of it is seeing ghosts before a skull. Have you not seen: a monk asked Jiufeng, What is the eye that firmly holds heaven and earth? Feng said, Heaven and earth are right here. The monk said, Then where is the heaven-and-earth eye? Feng said, That is exactly the heaven-and-earth eye. The monk said, Why then did you just say heaven and earth are right here? Feng said, If not so, before a skull one sees countless ghosts. Here Wansong has a spell-master. He struck the staff once and said: Quickly, quickly, as by imperial command.

Record of the Congrong Hermitage, volume two. Recorded by the attendant Lizhi. Proofread by the later student Xingyi. Carved by the layman Shengsheng. 17. Fayan: A Hair's Breadth. Address to the assembly: A pair of lone geese beat the air and fly high; a pair of mandarin ducks stand alone by the pond's edge.

text_zh: 示眾云。一雙孤雁搏地高飛。一對鴛鴦池邊 獨立。箭鋒相拄則且致。鋸解秤錘時如何。
text_en: Let us leave aside arrow-points meeting tip to tip. What about when the saw cuts through the balance weight?
Raised: Fayan asked Head Monk Xiu, A hair's breadth of difference and heaven and earth are far apart. How do you understand it?

text_zh: 舉。法眼問脩山主。毫厘有差天地懸隔。汝 作麼生會誰敢動著脩云。毫厘有差天地懸隔閗百 草有甚麼難眼云。恁麼又爭得鐵山橫在路脩云。某甲只 如此。和尚又如何捩轉鼻頭眼云。毫厘有差天地 懸隔將謂別有脩便禮拜將錯就錯。
text_en: Xiu said, A hair's breadth of difference and heaven and earth are far apart. Fayan said, How can that do? Xiu said, I only Who dares to touch it? A hundred dǒu. What is difficult about grass? An iron mountain lies across the road. am like this. How about you, master? Fayan said, A hair's breadth of difference and heaven and earth Twist the nose around. are far apart. Xiu then bowed. I thought there was something else. Take a mistake and make it into another.
The master said: Head Monk Xiu and Fayan studied together under Dizang, and deeply gained the power of close mutual polishing.

text_zh: 師云。脩山主與法眼。同參地藏。深得傍參切 磋之力。這箇公案如折倒則監院悟頭一般。 金陵報恩玄則禪師。法眼問。曾見什麼人來。 恩云。見青峯和尚。眼云。有什麼言句。恩云。 某甲曾問。如何是學人自己。峯云。丙了童子 來求火。眼云。上座作麼生會。恩云。丙丁屬火。 將火求火。如將自己求自己。眼云。與麼會又 爭得。恩云。某甲只如此。未知和尚尊意如何。 眼云。爾問我。我與爾道。恩云。如何是學人自 己。眼云。丙丁童子來求火。恩於言下頓悟。法 眼鉤錐在手。去則印住。住則印破。打破則監 院情關。抽開脩山主識鎖。三祖信心銘。至道 無難。唯嫌揀擇。但不憎愛。洞然明白。毫厘有 差。天地懸隔。法眼將此。問脩山主。作箇敲門 瓦子。今時問著一千箇。一千箇作道理會。不 然一向打在無事界裏。是他不落尋思。只道 箇毫厘有差天地懸隔。也大曬有蘊藉。法眼 方復不許。道恁麼又爭得。此所以為法眼一 派之源也。萬松到此常令學人分身兩下看。 前段脩山主恁麼道。為甚不許。後段法眼却 為甚恁麼道。其間脩山主道。某甲只如此。和 尚又如何。望箇斬新日月別作生涯。是他不 蹉一絲。依前只道。箇毫厘有差天地懸隔。東 禪齊云。山主恁麼祗對。為甚麼不肯。及乎再 請益。法眼亦只恁麼道便得去。且道。誵訛在 什麼處。若看得透。道上座有來由。萬松道。恁 麼又爭得。所以道。只是舊時行底路。逢人說 著便誵訛。脩便禮拜。得即得。情理難容。五祖 戒代法眼。劈脊便打。萬松道。果然有本出法 眼語云。山主徹也。萬松道。弄泥團漢二俱不 了。萬松當時見法眼道恁麼又爭得。向道。久 聞和尚有此機要。不然擺手便行。管取一時 坐斷。待伊不信。試問天童。頌云。
text_en: This case is like the head of awakening in Zhedao the superintendent. Chan master Xuanze of Bao'en in Jinling: Fayan asked him, Whom have you seen come here? Xuanze said, I saw Master Qingfeng. Fayan said, What words were spoken? Xuanze said, I once asked, What is the student's self? Qingfeng said, A Bingding boy comes seeking fire. Fayan said, How do you understand it, venerable one? Xuanze said, Bing and ding belong to fire. To seek fire with fire is like seeking oneself with oneself. Fayan said, To understand it that way, how can that do? Xuanze said, I am only like this. I do not know your venerable meaning, Master. Fayan said, You ask me and I will tell you. Xuanze said, What is the student's self? Fayan said, A Bingding boy comes seeking fire. Xuanze was suddenly enlightened at these words. Fayan held hook and awl in hand: if one goes, he seals it shut; if one stays, he breaks the seal. By breaking it open, he smashed the superintendent's emotional barrier and pulled open Head Monk Xiu's lock of consciousness. In the Third Patriarch's Faith in Mind it says: The great Way is not difficult, only avoid choosing and selecting. If there is no hate and love, all is bright and clear. A hair's breadth of difference and heaven and earth are far apart. Fayan took this and asked Head Monk Xiu, using it as a brick to knock at the gate. If you ask a thousand people nowadays, a thousand will take it as doctrine. Otherwise they just fall into the realm of nothing-to-do. Xiu did not fall into discursive thought; he only said A hair's breadth of difference and heaven and earth are far apart. It had quite a bit of reserve and depth. Yet Fayan still did not approve, saying, How can that do? This is why he became the source of the Fayan lineage. When Wansong gets here, he always tells students to split themselves and look from both sides. In the first part, Head Monk Xiu spoke this way, so why was he not approved? In the second part, Fayan in turn spoke the same way, so why was that so? Meanwhile Head Monk Xiu said, I am only like this. And how about you, Master? He was hoping for a fresh sun and moon, a different way of life. Yet he did not miss by a thread, and still as before only said, A hair's breadth of difference and heaven and earth are far apart. Dongchan Qi said, The head monk answered this way; why was he not accepted? Then when he asked again, Fayan also only said it this way and it worked. Tell me then, where does the discrepancy lie? If you can see through it, you can say the venerable one has a source. Wansong says, How can that do? Therefore it is said: it is only the road one walked before, but when speaking of it to others it immediately goes astray. Xiu then bowed. To get it is to get it, but feeling and reason cannot contain it. Wuzu Jie spoke on Fayan's behalf: split his back and strike him at once. Wansong said, Indeed he has his basis from Fayan. In Fayan's sayings it says, The head monk is through. Wansong said, These mud-ball fellows, neither of the two is finished. If Wansong had been there and heard Fayan say How can that do, he would have said: Long have I heard the Master has this pivotal device. Otherwise I would simply wave my hand and leave, and I guarantee for a time he would be cut off where he sat. If he would not believe it, then ask Tiantong. The verse says:
A fly sitting on the scale's head makes it tilt; for ten thousand ages the balance illuminates what is uneven. Cheat him by not even a star's worth The peck measure is full

text_zh: 秤頭蠅坐便欹傾謾他一星不過　萬世權衡照不平斗滿 秤錘住斤兩錙銖見端的莫錯認　終歸輸我定盤 星領取鉤頭意
text_en: The scale weight settles Catty, liang, zi, zhu reveal the exact point; in the end all submit to my fixed balance-star. Do not mistake it Star. Grasp the meaning at the hook tip
The master said: With one opening line Tiantong already praises A hair's breadth of difference and heaven and earth are far apart.

text_zh: 師云。天童破題一句。便頌毫厘有差天地懸 隔。廬山遠公云。本端竟何從起滅有無際。一 微涉動境。狀此穨山勢。三祖道箇嫌字。先自 憎愛了也。却道。但不憎愛洞然明白。諸人退 步。就己子細點檢看。梵語三摩地。此云等持。 不沈不掉。平等任持也。此可以為萬世權衡 照不平者也。尚書治要圖說。秤有三義。準者 繫也。衡者平也。權者錘也。楞嚴經云。於其自 住三摩地中。見與見緣。并所想相。如虛空花 本無所有。此見及緣。元是菩提妙淨明體。云 何於中有是非是。到此正恁麼時。不須嫌揀 擇離憎愛。尚無毫厘之差。豈有雲泥之隔。斤 兩錙銖者。八銖為錙。三錙為兩。十六兩為斤。 是他權衡在手底人。爾將一斤來。我也一移 教平。將一兩來。也一移教平。稍似錙銖增減 便欹傾也。諸方道。領取鉤頭意。莫認定盤星。 蓋定盤星上。本無斤兩。又如北辰鎮居其所。 鉤頭加減。計在臨時。萬松道。有心而平。未若 無心而不平。所以無星秤上饒人賣。雙陸盤 中信彩贏。還會法眼道山主徹也麼。秤錘移 到徹梢頭。忽然拶落翻斤斗。
text_en: Huiyuan of Mount Lu said, From where does the root finally arise? Birth and death have no boundary. The slightest involvement with the moving realm resembles a collapsing mountain. The Third Patriarch used the word avoid and first already brought in hate and love, then said: only if there is no hate and love, all is bright and clear. All of you, step back a pace and carefully examine yourselves. The Sanskrit samadhi is rendered as even holding. It is neither sinking nor agitation, but equal sustaining. This can serve as the balance for ten thousand ages to illuminate what is uneven. In the Illustrated Essentials of Government it says the scale has three meanings: the beam is what is bound, the crossbar is what levels, and the weight is the hanging mass. The Surangama Sutra says: within one's own abiding samadhi, seeing and the conditions of seeing, together with the forms one conceives, are like flowers in the sky, originally without anything real. This seeing and its conditions are originally the wondrous, pure, luminous body of bodhi. How could there be in it what is and what is not? At just such a time here, there is no need to avoid selecting, nor to depart from hate and love. There is not even a hair's breadth of difference, so how could there be a gulf like cloud and mud? As for liang, zi, and zhu: eight zhu make one zi, three zi make one liang, and sixteen liang make one catty. For one who holds the balance in hand, if you bring one catty, I move once and make it level. If you bring one liang, I also move once and make it level. If there is the slightest increase or decrease by zi or zhu, it tilts at once. The various houses say, Grasp the meaning at the hook's head; do not fixate on the balance-star. For on the balance-star itself there are originally no weights. It is also like the North Star, settled in its place. Increase and decrease at the hook's head are reckoned according to the moment. Wansong says: To level things with intention is not as good as having no intention and yet not being uneven. Therefore on a starless scale one lets people profit in selling; on the backgammon board one trusts fortune to win. Do you understand Fayan's saying, The head monk is through? The scale weight has moved to the very tip of throughness; suddenly it is squeezed off and turns a somersault.

text_zh: 18 趙州狗子
text_en: 18. Zhaozhou's Dog. Address to the assembly: A gourd on water turns as soon as you press it. A jewel in the sun has no fixed color or form.

text_zh: 示眾云。水上葫蘆。按著便轉。日中寶石。色無 定形。不可以無心得。不可以有心知。沒量大 人。語脈裏轉却。還有免得底麼。
text_en: It cannot be attained by no-mind, and cannot be known by mind. In the channels of a measureless great person, words turn and turn. Is there anyone who can avoid it?
Raised: A monk asked Zhaozhou, Does a dog also have Buddha-nature or not? Zhou Blocking the street and chasing scraps

text_zh: 舉。僧問趙州。狗子還有佛性也無攔街趁塊州 云。有也不曾添僧云。既有。為甚麼却撞入這箇 皮袋一款便招自領出頭州云。為他知而故犯且莫招承不是道爾 又有僧問。狗子還有佛性也無一母所生州曰。無 也不曾減僧云。一切眾生皆有佛性。狗子為什麼 却無憨狗趁鷂子州云。為伊有業識在右具如前據款結案。
text_en: said, It has. The monk said, Since it has, why then did it crash into this Not added in the least skin bag? Zhou said, Because it knowingly offends. At one charge he confesses and himself steps forward For now do not confess and admit it is not so Another monk asked, Does a dog also have Buddha-nature or not? Zhou said, No. Born of one mother The monk said, All sentient beings all have Buddha-nature. Why then does the dog Not diminished in the least not have it? Zhou said, Because karmic consciousness is there. A foolish dog chases a hawk The foregoing is fully stated; according to the confession the case is closed
The master said: If you say the dog's Buddha-nature truly is yes, later he still said no.

text_zh: 師云。若道狗子佛性端的是有。後來却道無。 端的是無。前來却道有。若道道有道無且是 一期應機。拶著說出。各有道理。所以道。明眼 漢沒窠臼。這僧問處要廣見聞。不依本分。趙 州道有。以毒去毒。以病醫病。這僧又道既有。 為甚撞入這皮袋。不知自己生。入狗腹中了 也。州云。為他知而故犯。一槌兩當。快便難逢。 這僧將謂。依因判果。若恁麼會。作座主奴。也 未得。後來有僧再問。便却道無。是他得底 人。道有也有出身處。道無也有出身處。這僧 依文按本道。一切眾生皆有佛性。狗子為什 麼却無。似這一拶。敢道。撥天關底手。轉身無 路。是他款款道。箇為伊有業識在。爾且道。這 僧皮下還有血麼。天童不免。向赤肉瘢上。更 著艾燋。頌云。
text_en: If you say it truly is no, earlier he still said yes. If you say saying yes and saying no was only a temporary response to conditions, when pressed and spoken, each has its reason. Therefore it is said: a clear-eyed one has no fixed nest. This monk's questioning sought broad learning and did not rely on his own portion. Zhao Zhou said yes, using poison to remove poison, using sickness to cure sickness. The monk then said, Since it has it, why crash into this skin bag? He did not realize he himself had already been born into a dog's belly. Zhou said, Because it knowingly offends. One hammer blow settles both sides. Such swiftness is hard to meet. That monk thought it was judging the effect by the cause. If you understand it that way, even as a lecturer's servant you still will not do. Later another monk asked again, and he then said no. This is how one who has it acts. Saying yes has a place to emerge; saying no also has a place to emerge. This monk followed the text and pressed the root text: All sentient beings have Buddha-nature, so why does the dog not have it? With a press like this, I dare say it is a hand that stirs Heaven's Gate, leaving no road to turn around. Yet he gently said, Because karmic consciousness is there. Tell me, is there still blood under this monk's skin? Tiantong could not avoid adding moxa on top of the raw flesh scar. The verse says:
The dog's Buddha-nature yes. The dog's Buddha-nature no. A straight hook was originally set Beaten into one lump, forged into one piece

text_zh: 狗子佛性有。狗子佛性無打做一團鍊做一塊　直釣元 求負命魚這僧今日合死逐氣尋香雲水客穿却鼻孔也不知 嘈嘈雜雜作分疎競齧枯骨啀喍噑吠　平展演沒蹺欺休廝誺　大 鋪舒材高語壯莫怪儂家不慎初一言出口駟馬難追　指點瑕 疵還奪璧白拈巧偷秦王不識藺相如當面蹉過
text_en: to seek fish willing to lose their lives. This monk deserves to die today Wayfarers of cloud and water chase scent and seek traces. Even with his nostrils pierced he does not know it Clamorous and noisy, they make distinctions; spread it all flat and display a great Competing to gnaw dry bones, snarling and barking No chance to bluff, so stop deceiving one another broad layout. Great talent, bold words Do not blame our house for not being careful at the start; pointing out flaws, Once a word leaves the mouth, four horses cannot return it he even snatches away the jade disk. Barehanded he steals with clever skill The King of Qin did not recognize Lin Xiangru. He misses it face to face
The master said: The dog's Buddha-nature yes and the dog's Buddha-nature no are two different sections.

text_zh: 師云。狗子佛性有。狗子佛性無。兩段不同。一 併拈出。正如雪竇道。一有多種二無兩般。天 童要與趙州相見。故如是頌。應天真道。直鉤 釣獰龍。曲鉤釣蝦䗫。後來逐氣尋香。如獵犬 相似。嘈雜分疎。枯骨上有甚汁。趙州雖大開 鋪席。要且只是平展商量。天童與趙州解腕。 莫怪儂家不慎初。歸宗問秀才。業何經史。才 云。會二十四家書體。宗向空中一點云。會麼。 才云。不會。宗云。又道。會二十四家書體。永字 八法也不識。刺史李渤問。三乘十二分教即 不問。如何是祖師西來意。宗亦竪拳云。會麼。 李云。不會。宗云。這箇措大。拳頭也不識。萬 松道。翻身師子大家看。不唯狗子佛性道有 道無。只這知而故犯。業識性在。也大曬顧前 盻後。慎初護末。史記趙惠王。得楚和氏璧。秦 昭王以十五城易之。藺相如奉璧入。秦王喜 傳示美人及左右。左右皆呼萬歲。相如視王 無割城之意。乃前曰。璧有瑕。請示之。王授 璧。相如因持起立。倚柱髮上衝冠曰。趙王齋 戒五日。使臣奉璧送書於庭。嚴大國之威。以 修敬也。今見。王禮節甚倨。得璧傳示美人。似 戲弄臣無割城意。故臣復取璧。必欲急臣。臣 頭與璧俱碎於柱矣。王辭謝按圖割城。亦齋 五日。相如使從者衣褐懷璧徑道歸趙。趙州 先縱後奪。有相如手段。天童別曾有頌云。趙 州道有。趙州道無。狗子佛性。天下分疎。面赤 不如語直。心真必定言麁。七百甲子老禪伯。 驢糞逢人換眼珠。趙州心真語直。便是直釣。 元求負命魚。周文王出獵。見姜子牙磻溪之 谷。去水三尺。直鉤釣魚。王異之曰。直鉤如何 得魚。子牙曰。但求負命之魚。驢糞逢人換眼 珠。此如相如奪璧也。佛鑑拈出槵子數珠云。 諸人還見麼。良久云。此是老僧來京師。換得 底。諸人各自歸堂摸𢱢看。佛鑑用槵子。趙州 用驢糞。萬松既無用處。不曾移換。諸人若信 得及。依舊眼在眉毛下。
text_en: Tiantong brings them up together, just as Xuedou said: one yes has many kinds, two no's are not of two sorts. Tian- tong wanted to meet Zhaozhou face to face, so he praised it this way. Yingtian Zhendao said, A straight hook To hook a fierce dragon with a bent hook is to catch only shrimp. Later people chase scents and traces like hunting dogs. Noisy and scattered—what juice is there on dry bones? Though Zhaozhou greatly spread out his mat, in the end it was only a level, open discussion. Tiantong unties wrists with Zhaozhou. Do not blame this old fellow for not being cautious at the start. Guizong asked a scholar, What classics do you study? The scholar said, I know the script styles of twenty-four schools. Zong pointed a dot in the air and said, Do you understand? The scholar said, I do not. Zong said, And yet you say you know twenty-four script styles. Even the eight strokes of the character yong you do not know. Prefect Li Bo asked, As for the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings, I will not ask about them. What is the Patriarch's meaning in coming from the West? Zong likewise raised his fist and said, Do you understand? Li said, I do not. Zong said, This pedant—even a fist he does not recognize. Wansong said, Behold the lion turning over for all to see. It is not only in saying the dog has Buddha-nature or saying it does not. Just this knowing and deliberately violating—karmic consciousness is still there. It is a great display of looking before and glancing behind, being careful at the start and guarding the end. In the Records, King Hui of Zhao obtained the He family jade of Chu. King Zhao of Qin offered fifteen cities to exchange for it. Lin Xiangru carried the jade in. The King of Qin rejoiced and passed it around to the ladies and attendants. All the attendants cried, Long live the king. Xiangru saw the king had no intention of ceding cities, so he stepped forward and said, The jade has a flaw; let me show it. The king handed over the jade. Xiangru then held it, stood up, and leaning against a pillar, with hair bristling against his cap, said: The King of Zhao fasted and purified himself for five days, then sent me to present the jade and deliver a letter at your court, honoring the majesty of the great state to show respect. But now I see Your Majesty's manners are very arrogant. Having gotten the jade, you pass it to the ladies, as if to toy with me, with no intent to cede the cities. Therefore I have taken back the jade. If you would force me, then my head and the jade will both be shattered against this pillar. The king apologized and, looking at the map, assigned cities. He also fasted five days. Xiangru then had an attendant in rough clothes hide the jade in his robe and take the direct road back to Zhao. Zhaozhou first lets go and then snatches back—he has Xiangru's skill. Tiantong once had another verse saying: Zhao- zhou says there is; Zhaozhou says there is not. The dog's Buddha-nature splits the world apart. A red face is not as good as straight speech. If the heart is true, the words will surely be rough. A seven-hundred-cycle old Chan elder— donkey dung, when meeting people, exchanged for eyeballs. Zhaozhou's heart is true and his speech straight: this is straight-hook fishing. He was originally seeking fish fated to die. King Wen of Zhou went hunting and saw Jiang Ziya in the valley of Pan Stream, three feet away from the water, fishing with a straight hook. The king found it strange and said, How can a straight hook catch fish? Ziya said, I only seek fish bearing the fate to die. Donkey dung exchanged for eyeballs— this is like Xiangru seizing back the jade. Fojian held up a rosary of soapberry seeds and said, Do you all see it? After a long pause he said, This is what this old monk got in exchange when he came to the capital. Each of you go back to your hall and feel for it yourselves. Fojian used soapberry beads; Zhaozhou used donkey dung. Wansong, having no use for either, has never exchanged anything. If you all can truly trust it, then as before your eyes are still beneath your eyebrows.

text_zh: 19 雲門須彌
text_en: 19. Yunmen's Sumeru Addressing the assembly, he said: I love Shaoyang's freshly-set devices; all his life he pulled nails and wedges for people.

text_en: Why then does he sometimes open the gate, set out a glue basin, and chisel a pitfall right in the road? Try to choose and discern.

text_zh: 師云。圓通善國師道。此箇公案諸方商量。或 云。纔恁麼問。早是起念。過如須彌。或云。如須 彌山八風吹不動。千古鎮常安。或云。為人難 透。如須彌山。如此商量。要且未會雲門意在。 若是桶子底脫。紅絲線斷。方知總不恁麼。不 見道。三句明一句。一句明三句。三一不相涉。 分明向上路。佛果道。雲門答話多惹人識情。 萬松道。以識情遣識情。非大手段為人。不能 搆副。此須彌山天不能蓋。地不能載。風吹不 入。水灑不著。唯金剛眼睛。一覻覻透。便見七 穿八穴。直得碎如微塵。然後却向眉毛眼睫 上。孤逈逈峭巍巍。白雲端禪師頌云。須彌山 兮塞宇宙。千手大悲看不透。除非自解倒騎 牛。一生不著隨人後。萬松道。仰面獨揚眉。迴 頭自拍手。其山寘和尚頌云。無事投人覓罪 名。即時擒下喪全身。未招情款驅驅者。門外 知他多少人。唯有天童不在此限。頌云。
text_en: say, The very moment he asked like that, a thought had already arisen; the fault is like Sumeru. Others say, Like Sumeru, unmoved by the eight winds, stable and ever at peace through the ages. Others say, For people it is hard to penetrate, like Mount Sumeru. But all such discussion still fails to grasp where Yunmen's meaning lies. If the bottom falls out of the bucket, if the red silk thread is cut, only then will you know it is not like that at all. Do you not see it said: Three phrases illuminate one phrase; one phrase illuminates three phrases. Three and one do not interfere. Clearly, this is the road upward. Foguo said, Yunmen's replies often stir people's discriminating consciousness. Wansong said, Using discriminating consciousness to send off discriminating consciousness—unless one has great skill in dealing with people, one cannot match it. This Mount Sumeru cannot be covered by heaven nor carried by earth. Wind cannot blow into it, water cannot wet it. Only with vajra eyes, one glance straight through, and you see seven holes and eight openings, smashing it to dust. Then on the eyebrows and eyelashes it stands alone—lofty and steep. Chan Master Baiyunduan's verse says: Mount Sumeru fills the universe; even Thousand-Hand Great Compassion cannot see through it. Unless you yourself can ride backward on an ox, all your life you will not avoid trailing behind others. Wansong said: Face up, raise the brows alone; turn back and clap your own hands. Master Qishanzhi's verse says: With nothing to do, you cast yourself at others seeking the name of guilt; at once you are seized and lose your whole body. Before any confession is signed, the bustling ones outside the gate—who knows how many there are? Only Tiantong is not in this category. His verse says:

text_zh: 師云。爾問我不起一念有過無過。我便掇出 一坐須彌山。在爾面前相似。其法施之利。固 非慳悋。永嘉道。大施門開無壅塞。非但今 日也。梵語須彌。此云妙高。四寶所成曰妙。獨 出眾峯曰高。四天下山中。須彌最為第一。爾 若自肯。我便兩手分付。古詩道。待伊心肯處。 是我命通時。其實此事常顯露。如須彌山㟮 屼崢嶸。誰能蓋覆。未分付時。爾豈無分。分付 與爾。豈是新得。不見。長慶道。萬象之中獨露 身。唯人自肯乃方親。天童頌。到這裏大有含 蓄功夫。爾若擬議不來。千里萬里仰望不及。 璩源道。此事如崖穨石裂。壁立千仞。不可攀 攬。其實爾亦不曾離。我亦不曾奪。此與上句 迷悟相反。對偶分明。教中說。須彌山入水八 萬瑜繕那。出水八萬瑜繕那。非娑竭海。不能 涵容。山既古今不動。雲亦出沒常閑。洞山道。 青山白雲父。白雲青山兒。白雲終日倚。青山 總不知。天童餘才。頌須彌山如海闊雲閑。曲 盡奇妙。這裏容得一念起滅麼。所以道。滄海 濶。白雲閑。莫將毫髮著其間。此又與雪竇道 眼裡著沙不得。同參。若論韶陽不慳法施。却 又眼裏著得須彌山也。此須彌山頌中。築著 磕著。血脉貫通。拍拍是令。非妄生穿鑒增長 識情也。其實不起一念底人。豈可更問有過無 過。直饒常在不起一念處。點檢將來。堪作什 麼。所以道。假鷄聲韻難謾我。未肯模胡放過 關。孟甞君入秦為相。人或說王。孟甞君賢。又 齊族也。今相秦必先齊而後秦。秦其危矣。王 囚君欲殺。君因幸姬求解。姬曰。妾願得君狐 白裘。此時裘已獻王。下客能為狗盜者。取裘 獻姬。君得出。夜半至函谷關。關法鷄鳴而出 客。下客憑諼善為鷄鳴。群鷄皆鳴。君脫秦難。 師拈拄杖云。萬松今日把關也。有學鷄鳴者。 出來。復靠却拄杖云。放過一著。
text_en: a whole Mount Sumeru before your face. The benefit of that Dharma-gift is certainly not stinginess. Yongjia said, The gate of great giving stands open without obstruction—not only today. In Sanskrit it is Sumeru; here it is called Wondrous High. Formed of four jewels, it is wondrous; standing alone above all peaks, it is high. Among the mountains of the four continents, Sumeru is foremost. If you can affirm it yourself, I will hand it over with both hands. An old poem says: Wait for the place where the heart agrees— that is when my fate and yours connect. In truth this matter is always plainly revealed, like Mount Sumeru towering and rugged—who can cover it over? Before it is handed over, how could you have no share? When it is handed over to you, how could it be something newly obtained? Do you not see? Changqing said: Amid the ten thousand forms, it alone reveals itself; only when a person affirms it himself does it become intimate. Tiantong's verse, on reaching here, carries great reserved power. If you cannot come without deliberating, then from a thousand or ten thousand miles away you can only look up and never reach. Quyuan said: This matter is like collapsing cliffs and split rock, a sheer wall a thousand fathoms high, impossible to climb or grasp. Yet in truth you have never been apart from it, nor have I ever taken it away. This, together with the previous line, sets delusion and awakening in opposition, the pairing very clear. The teachings say Mount Sumeru goes into the water eighty thousand yojanas, and rises above the water eighty thousand yojanas. Unless it is the Sagara sea, it cannot contain it. Since the mountain is unmoving from old to now, the clouds too come and go in constant leisure. Dongshan said: The green mountain is father to the white clouds; the white clouds are children of the green mountain. The white clouds lean on it all day, yet the green mountain never knows. Tiantong, with leftover talent, praised Mount Sumeru as sea-vast and cloud-idle, completely exhausting the marvelous subtlety. Is there room here for a single thought to arise and cease? Therefore he said: The blue sea is vast, the white clouds at ease—do not lodge so much as a hair between them. This also accords with Xuedou's saying that no sand can be tolerated in the eye. They study together. But if we speak of Shaoyang's unstinting Dharma-gift, then he can even put Mount Sumeru into the eye. In this Sumeru verse, wherever it strikes and bumps, the bloodlines run through. Every beat is command—not some vainly produced clever analysis that only increases discriminating consciousness. In truth, a person in whom not one thought arises—how could he still ask whether there is fault or no fault? Even if one is always abiding where no thought arises, when examined closely, what is it fit to be used for? Therefore he said: A fake rooster's cry is hard to use to fool me; I am not willing to let you muddle through the pass. Lord Mengchang entered Qin to serve as minister. Someone said to the king: Lord Mengchang is worthy, and moreover he is of the Qi royal clan. If he serves Qin, he will surely put Qi before Qin. Qin will be endangered. The king imprisoned him and wanted to kill him. Mengchang sought release through a favored consort. She said, I wish to have your fox- white fur coat. By then the coat had already been presented to the king. A retainer skilled at stealing like a dog took the coat and gave it to the consort. The lord gained release. At midnight they reached Hangu Pass. By law the gate opened only at rooster-crow for travelers to leave. Another retainer, Pingxuan, was good at imitating a rooster; all the roosters crowed, and the lord escaped Qin's danger. The master lifted his staff and said: Wansong today is also guarding the pass. If any among you can imitate a rooster's crow, come forth. Then he leaned the staff back and said: I'll let one move pass.

text_zh: 師云。楊無為問芙蓉楷和尚。相別幾年。蓉云。 七年。公云。學道來參禪來。蓉云。不打這鼓 笛。公云。恁麼則空游山水。百無所能也。蓉 云。相別未久善能高鑒。公大笑。南泉道。道 不屬知。不屬不知。知是妄覺。不知是無記。今 人見道不知最親切。更是法眼悟頭。便一向 不知不會。只這是也。殊不知。古人一句子。如 天普蓋。似地普擎。既不知最親切。荷澤道知 之一字眾妙之門。又作麼生。爾但是則總是。 莫坐在是處。不是總不是。莫坐在不是處。兼 通五位正偏。豈可死在句下。只這法眼悟處。 也是偶爾成文。柏山大隱和尚道。因禍致福 也在。地藏接人手段。鉤在不疑之地。驀下一 釣。法眼猛省。元來却在這裏。磁州老師道。爾 但行裏。坐裏。心念未起時。猛提起覻見即便 見不見。且却拈放一邊。恁麼做功夫。休歇也 不礙參學。參學也不礙休歇。投子青和尚道。 既金龍失水。妙翅急提。地藏時節因緣。絲毫 無間。天童筆端有舌。更為重宣。頌云。
text_en: Seven years. Yang said, Have you come studying the Way, or to practice Chan? Furong said, I do not beat that drum and flute. Yang said, Then you've only wandered mountains and rivers in vain, good for nothing at all. Furong said, We have not been apart long, yet your lofty discernment is excellent. Yang laughed aloud. Nanquan said, The Way does not belong to knowing, nor to not knowing. Knowing is false awareness; not knowing is blank indifference. Now when people hear Not knowing is most intimate, and that this was Fayan's point of awakening, they immediately go one-sidedly into not knowing and not understanding, taking just that to be it. They do not realize that a single saying of the ancients is like heaven universally covering, like earth universally supporting. Since not knowing is most intimate, then Heze's saying that knowing is the gate of myriad wonders—what about that? If you say yes, then all is yes; do not sit in the place of yes. If you say no, then all is no; do not sit in the place of no. Also, you must penetrate the five ranks, the upright and the biased—how could you die beneath a phrase? As for Fayan's awakening here, it too was merely words formed by chance. Master Dayin of Baishan said: Turning misfortune into blessing is also here. Dizang's way of receiving people hooks them in the place before doubt, and with one sudden cast Fayan fiercely awakens: so it was right here all along. The teacher of Cizhou said, You only need, in walking, in sitting, when thought has not yet arisen, to sharply lift it up and look. The very moment you see, whether seen or unseen, set that aside. Practicing like this, resting does not hinder study, and study does not hinder rest. Master Qing of Touzi said, Once the golden dragon has lost the water, the wondrous-winged bird quickly lifts it. Dizang's timing and conditions— not the slightest gap. Tiantong had a tongue at the tip of his brush and proclaimed it again in verse:
Now, having fully practiced, it is like then: strip away every curtain-thread and arrive at not-knowing. I am still the man of old, yet not the man of old
