The master said: The Zongjing says, From the beginning delusion and awakening seemed like delusion; today awakening to delusion is not awakening.

text_zh: 師云。宗鏡道。從來迷悟似迷。今日悟迷非悟。 所以道。悟了還同未悟人。地藏問時。要知發 足道理。法眼答處。亦非謙讓推辭。地藏就 便。一提道。不知最親切。法眼大悟元來這不 知却親切。臨濟問洛浦甚處來。浦云。欒城來。 濟云。有事相借問得否。浦云。某甲不會。濟云。 打破大唐國。覓箇不會底不得。臨濟常用殺 人刀。亦有活人劍。不似地藏殺人見血為人 為徹。這箇不知不會。脫體逈別。直須脫盡簾 纖方到不知不會處。溈山普請開田。仰山問。 這頭得恁麼低。那頭得恁麼高。溈曰。水能平 物。但以水平之。仰曰。水也無憑。和尚但高處 高平。低處低平。溈然云。肇公般若無知論曰。 諸法不異者。豈曰續鳧截鶴夷嶽盈󱐙。然後 為無異哉。所以道。任短任長休剪綴。隨高 隨下自平治。張無盡道。萬般支準費工夫。 一切順隨成善巧。只麼信口便道。信手便用。 信脚便行。春月花開。秋時葉落。恁麼會得。 行甚驢脚。所以玄沙不出嶺。保壽不渡河。 不出門知天下事。覺範頌云。一箇面如楪子 大。眼耳鼻舌分疆界。髑髏裡頭都不知。聽汝 外邊爭揑怪。口問鼻曰。飲食在我。言語在我。 汝有何功。在吾之上。鼻曰。五嶽之中。中嶽 居尊。鼻復問眼。汝何在上。眼曰。吾同日月。 寔有照鑒之功。敢問眉。有何功處於吾上。眉 曰。我寔無功。慚居上位。儻容在下。眼在眉上 看。爾甚麼面孔。是以寶月明禪師上堂云。古 者道。在眼曰見。在耳曰聞。且道。在眉毛。喚 作什麼。良久云。憂則共慼。樂則同歡。人皆知 有用之用。不知無用之大用。且道。賓頭盧尊 者兩手撥眉意旨如何。師撥眉云。猫。
text_en: Therefore it is said: Once awakened, one is still like one not yet awakened. When Dizang asked, he wanted to know the reason for setting out. Fayan's answer was not mere modesty or polite refusal. Dizang then immediately lifted it and said, Not knowing is most intimate. Fayan greatly awakened: this not- knowing was precisely intimacy. Linji asked Luopu, Where have you come from? Luopu said, From Luancheng. Linji said, May I ask you something? Luopu said, I do not understand. Linji said, Break open the whole Tang empire and you still cannot find one who does not understand. Linji often used the killing sword, and he also had the life-giving sword. It is not like Dizang, who in killing someone draws blood, yet for the person's sake cuts through completely. This not knowing, not understanding, is utterly distinct in body. One must strip away every curtain- thread before reaching the place of not knowing and not understanding. During communal field work at Weishan, Yangshan asked, This side is so low; that side is so high—how is that? Wei said, Water can level things; just use water to level it. Yang said, Water too has no fixed standard. Master, just level the high places high, and the low places low. Wei assented. Sengzhao's Treatise on Prajna Without Knowing says: That all dharmas are not different—does this mean lengthening a duck's legs, cutting a crane's, leveling mountains, filling valleys, and only then calling them non-different? Therefore it is said: Let short be short and long be long; do not trim or patch. Follow the high, follow the low, and it levels itself. Zhang Wujin said, All sorts of measuring and adjustment waste effort. Let everything accord and follow, and skillful means are accomplished. Simply speak from trust and speak; use from trust and use. Trust your feet and walk. In spring the flowers bloom; in autumn the leaves fall. If you understand in this way. what donkey-legs are there to fuss over? Therefore Xuansha did not leave the ridge, and Baoshou did not cross the river. Without going out the gate, one knows the affairs under heaven. Juefan praised it, saying: A face like a platter, broad and wide, with eyes, ears, nose, and tongue dividing territories. Inside the skull none of them knows, while you listen to them outside bickering and making strange claims. The mouth asked the nose: food and drink are in me, speech is in me. What merit do you have, to be above me? The nose said: Among the Five Peaks, the central peak holds the honored place. The nose then asked the eyes: why are you above? The eyes said: We are like sun and moon; truly we have the function of illuminating and discerning. I dare ask the brows: what merit have you to be above us? The brows said: I truly have no merit, ashamed to occupy the upper place. If I were allowed to be below, with the eyes above the brows, just look what kind of face you would have. Therefore Chan Master Baoyue Ming ascended the hall and said: The ancients said, in the eyes it is called seeing, in the ears it is called hearing. But tell me, in the eyebrows, what is it called? What do you call it? After a long pause he said: In sorrow they share grief, in joy they rejoice together. People all know the use of what is useful, but do not know the great use of the useless. Tell me then, Venerable Pindola with both hands brushing his brows, what was his intent? The master brushed his brows and said: Cat.

Yan lifted up the broom and said, This Far more than a second one, by the hundreds of millions one, which moon is it? Wu then let it rest and left. Xuansha He sticks his head out from the crystal palace All lies within what is not said said, Precisely the second moon. Yunmen said, A maid seeing another maid, all diligence One person passes on a rumor, ten thousand pass it on as fact and fuss. Following error and pouncing on the winnowing basket
The master said: Daowu bent and turned Yunyan, like Foguo urging and sharpening Fojian. This is what is meant by

text_zh: 師云。道吾屈折雲巖。如佛果激勵佛鑑。所謂 不憤不啟。不悱不發。是他雲巖掃地。道吾閑 點檢他。雲巖道。須知有不區區者。好諸仁者 爾喫飯。煎茶。把針。掃地。時識取箇不區區底。 便得世法佛法打成一片。洞上謂之兼帶去。 時中自不虛過。道吾便見破綻。道恁麼則有 第二月也。雪竇別云。洎合放過。二老人恐人 離却色身別立法身。忠國師謂南方禪客曰。 我此間佛性全不生滅。汝南方佛性半生半 滅。半不生滅。客曰。如何區別。師曰。此則身 心一如。心外無餘。所以全不生滅。汝南方身 是無常。神性是常。所以半生半滅半不生滅。 到這裏須知有箇轉身就父底時節。巖遂竪 起掃󰆠云。這箇是第幾月。此語本出首楞嚴 經。經云。如第二月。誰為是月。又誰非月。文 殊但一月真。中間自無是月非月。道吾便休 去。有本云。道吾拂袖便行。萬松道。勘破了也。 且道。是雲巖勘破道吾。道吾勘破雲巖。明眼 底試點檢看。玄沙云。正是第二月。此老子口 裏有雌黃。舌上有利劍。長慶云。被他倒轉掃 󰆠攔面𢷾。又作麼生。沙休去。羅山云。噫。兩 箇老漢不識好惡。雲巖箇漢縛手脚。死來多 少時也。萬松道。德山門下。不道不得。洞山門 下。要且未在。雪峯行脚時。三到投子。九上洞 山。一日淘米次。洞山問。淘砂去米。淘米去 砂。峯云。砂米一時去。山云。大眾喫箇什麼。 峯乃覆却盆。山云。得即得。須見別人始得。後 果嗣德山。玄沙長慶嗣雪峯。羅山嗣巖頭。皆 出德山門下。故一抑一揚。言逆意順。而今雲 門洞上兩派齊行。豈有優劣者哉。雲門云。奴 見婢殷勤。保福云。雲巖大似泥裏推車步步 區區。二老宿亦嗣雪峯。自然言氣相合。意謂。 雲巖不能用掃󰆠𢷾打斷葛藤。殊不知。爛泥 中有刺。萬松披玩拈提未遍。不覺失笑云。雲 巖道吾。發明洞上機緣。這一隊老漢。眾口銷 金。無一人為渠雪屈。賴有天童拔劍相助。頌 云。
text_en: If one is not indignant, do not enlighten him; if not struggling to speak, do not bring it forth. Yunyan was sweeping the ground, and Daowu casually checked him. Yunyan said, You should know there is one who is not busy. Good people, when you eat rice, brew tea, hold a needle, sweep the ground, at such times recognize the one that is not busy. Then worldly dharma and Buddha-dharma become one piece. In the Dongshan house this is called going with both together. Then your time will not pass in vain. Daowu immediately saw the seam and said, If so, then there is a second moon. Xuedou added instead: Just then they should have let it pass. These two old men feared people would leave the physical body and establish a separate dharma-body. National Teacher Zhong said to a southern Chan traveler: Here our Buddha-nature is wholly unborn and undying. In your South, Buddha-nature is half born and half dying, half unborn and undying. The traveler said, How do you distinguish them? The master said, Here, body and mind are one suchness; outside mind there is nothing else, therefore it is wholly unborn and undying. In your South, the body is impermanent, while spirit-nature is permanent, therefore half born and dying, half unborn and undying. Reaching here, you must know there is a time to turn yourself and go to the father. Yan then raised the broom and said, This one, which moon is it? These words originally come from the Shurangama Sutra. The sutra says: As with the second moon, which is the moon, and which is not the moon? Manjushri says there is only one true moon; in between there is no this-is-the-moon and that-is-not-the-moon. Daowu then stopped and left. Some versions say Daowu flicked his sleeves and departed. Wansong said: One had seen through the other. But tell me, was it Yunyan who saw through Daowu, or Daowu who saw through Yunyan? Those with clear eyes, try inspecting it. Xuansha said, Precisely the second moon. This old fellow's mouth carries yellow pigment for corrections; on his tongue is a sharp sword. Changqing said, If he had reversed the broom and barred his face, then what? Sha let it rest. Luoshan said, Ah! These two old men do not know good from bad. That fellow Yunyan, with hands and feet bound, how long till he dies? Wansong said: Under Deshan's gate, one cannot fail to speak; under Dongshan's gate, still it is not there yet. When Xuefeng was traveling, he went three times to Touzi and nine times up to Dongshan. One day while rinsing rice, Dongshan asked: Are you washing away the sand and keeping the rice, or washing away the rice and keeping the sand? Feng said: Sand and rice go away together. Shan said: Then what will the assembly eat? Feng then overturned the basin. Shan said: It is attained, yes, but you still must see someone else before it will do. Later he indeed succeeded Deshan. Xuansha and Changqing succeeded Xuefeng; Luoshan succeeded Yantou. All came from Deshan's line. Thus one suppresses and one raises, words contrary but intent in accord. And now the Yunmen and Dongshan two branches go forth together. How could there be superior or inferior? Yunmen said, A maid sees another maid being overly diligent. Baofu said, Yunyan is very much like pushing a cart through mud, step by step all busy and toilsome. These two old worthies also succeeded Xuefeng, so naturally their speech and tone agree. Their meaning is that Yunyan could not use the broom to cut off the entangling vines. Yet they do not know that in rotten mud there are thorns. Wansong, while unfolding and playing with this, before even finishing his lifting and bringing out, could not help laughing and said: Yun- yan and Daowu clarified the Dongshan family's workings, yet this whole pack of old fellows, with many mouths melting gold, not one of them righted the grievance for them. Luckily Tiantong drew his sword to help, and praised it saying:
Borrow it for the moment to settle the gate-front; once its use is gained as fitting, then at once let it go. Arising right where you are Ceasing completely wherever you are

text_zh: 借來聊爾了門頭當處發生　得用隨宜即便休隨處滅盡 象骨巖前弄蛇手欲道他人　兒時做處老知羞先治自己
text_en: Before Elephant-Bone Cliff, the snake-handling trick, what one did in youth, in old age one knows to be ashamed of. If you want to speak of others First set yourself right
The master said: If we discuss this matter, it is like a spark from stone or a flash of lightning. Yunyan raised it up to show people.

text_zh: 師云。若論此事。如石火電光。雲巖提起示人。 長慶攔面便𢷾用處雖殊。同歸變滅。洞上所 以貴迴機轉位也。雪峯有象骨巖。雪峯曾示 眾云。南山有一條鼈鼻蛇。汝等諸人切須好 看。雲門以拄杖。攛向面前。作怕勢。此豈不是 奴見婢殷勤也。雲巖掃地。提起掃󰆠云。這箇 是第幾月。盡與從良變為得力兒孫了也。雲 門至今在籬簷下。所以天童放伊不過。道象 骨巖前弄蛇手。兒時做處老知羞。勝默和尚 道。這箇頌子有搜人短處。有為人長處。此天 童勝默。點罰雲門。萬松今日翻案去也。不見。 天童頌弄蛇話。褒獎雲門全機大用雲中不 下。為甚如此。抑揚皆在我。殺活更由誰。
text_en: Changqing blocked him in the face and used it. Though their points of use differ, both return to transformation and cessation. What the Dongshan school prizes is turning the pivot and shifting the position. Xuefeng had Elephant-Bone Cliff. Xuefeng once addressed the assembly saying: On South Mountain there is a turtle-nosed snake; all of you must be very careful and watch it well. Yunmen thrust his staff toward the front and made a gesture of fright. Is this not precisely a maid seeing a maid being diligent? Yunyan swept the ground, raised the broom and said, This one is which moon? All of them turned from the old trade and became capable descendants. Yet Yun- men, to this day, still stands under the eaves and fence, so Tiantong would not let him pass, saying: Before Elephant-Bone Cliff, the snake-handling hand; what was done in youth, in old age one knows shame. Monk Shengmo said: This verse exposes people's shortcomings and also brings out their strengths. Here Tiantong and Shengmo censure Yunmen, but today Wansong overturns the verdict. Have you not seen Tiantong's verse on the snake-handling story, praising Yunmen's complete pivot and great functioning, a cloud in which one does not descend? Why is it so? To suppress or raise is all in me; who else controls killing and giving life?

text_zh: 22 巖頭拜喝
text_en: 22 Yantou Bows to the Shout Instruction to the assembly: People probe with words, water is tested with a staff. Parting grass to watch the wind is an everyday

text_zh: 示眾云。人將語探。水將杖探。撥草瞻風。尋常 用底。忽然跳出箇焦尾大蟲。又作麼生。
text_en: tool. But if suddenly a scorched-tail tiger leaps out, then what?
Raised: Yantou went to Deshan. Straddling the threshold, he immediately asked, Is it ordinary or holy? Shan This thief

text_zh: 舉。巖頭到德山。跨門便問。是凡是聖這賊山 便喝裂破髑髏頭禮拜未當好心洞山聞云。若不是豁 公。大難承當厚幣甘言頭云。洞山老漢不識好惡 却又著忙我當時一手擡一手捺我豈不知。
text_en: immediately shouted. Tou bowed. Dongshan heard of it and said, If not for Huo- Splitting the skull open Not exactly goodhearted gong, it would have been hard to bear. Tou said, That old fellow Dongshan does not know good from bad. Rich gifts and sweet words At that time I raised with one hand and pressed with the other. Yet again he gets flustered How could I not know
The master said: Deshan ordinarily struck like wind and rain. One day Yantou spread out his sitting cloth.

text_zh: 師云。德山尋常打風打雨。一日巖頭展坐具。 德山以拄杖挑向階下。頭下階收坐具便行。 次日上德山侍立。山云。那裏學得這虛頭來。 頭云。某甲終不敢自謾。山云。汝已後向老僧 頭上屙去在。父聞子健恨不殺身。見過於師 方堪傳授。此問諸方謂之跨門之機。未必當 初真跨門問來。昔有外道。手中藏活雀兒。問 世尊曰。手中雀兒為活為死。世尊以足跨門 云。汝道。吾欲出欲入。問是凡是聖。真有此 理。昔日普化曾指聖僧問臨濟。且道。這箇是 凡是聖。濟便喝化云。河陽新婦子。木塔老婆 禪。臨濟小廝兒。却具一隻眼。濟云。這老賊。 化出僧堂云。賊賊。首山云。這兩箇賊有箇正 賊。且道。那箇是正賊。代云。劉盆子巖頭。問 是凡是聖。德山便喝。便是與臨濟商搉。勘同 來相似。頭禮拜。亦與臨濟小廝兒却具一隻 眼一般。雪竇道。當時纔禮拜。劈脊便打。非唯 勦絕洞山。亦乃把定豁老。此又與臨濟道這 老賊同參。洞山聞舉云。若不是豁公。大難承 當。佛果著語云。傍人具眼。又云。只知其一不 知其二。萬松見處即不然。佛果道。洞山傍人 雖具眼。只見錐頭利。萬松道。佛果和尚雖具 眼。不見鑿頭方。洞山故將承當。贓誣巖頭。要 發明當初禮拜有權有實。果然巖頭火到頭 上。急忙撲撒道。洞山老漢不識好惡。我當時 一手擡一手捺。方始點燈喫飯。兩家分明也。 不見。保寧勇和尚頌云。平川走兔放蒼鷹。此 頌跨門之問也。一捺便啗雙眼睛。此頌德山 喝巖頭拜。毒手奪來人買去。此頌洞山著價 利。奈何斤兩未分明。正是萬松道底。欲得斤 兩分明麼。其實佛果萬松不爭頭高頭低。更 看天童稱盤一上。頌云。
text_en: Deshan hooked it down the steps with his staff. Tou went down, gathered the cloth, and left. The next day he went up to attend on Deshan. Shan said, Where did you learn this empty-headedness? Tou said, I would never dare deceive myself. Shan said, Later on, toward this old monk, you may shit on my head. When a father hears his son is strong, he regrets only that he cannot kill himself. When one sees beyond the teacher, only then is one fit to receive transmission. This question is what the various houses call the threshold-crossing device. It may not be that he truly asked it right at the threshold in the beginning. Formerly there was a non-Buddhist who hid a live sparrow in his hand and asked the World-Honored One: Is the sparrow in my hand alive or dead? The World-Honored One crossed the threshold with his foot and said, You tell me, do I wish to go out or to come in? So to ask ordinary or holy truly has this principle. Formerly Puhua once pointed to a monk-image and asked Linji, Tell me, is this one ordinary or holy? Ji immediately shouted. Hua said, Heyang's new bride, Muta's old woman Chan! This little rascal Linji yet has one eye. Ji said, This old thief! Hua went out of the monks' hall shouting, Thief! Thief! Shoushan said, Among these two thieves there is one true thief. Tell me, which one is the true thief? In his place I say: Liu Penzi. Yantou asked, Is it ordinary or holy? Deshan immediately shouted. This is discussing and comparing with Linji, examining how alike they are. Tou bowed; this too is like Linji, the little rascal who yet had one eye. Xuedou said: The moment he bowed, he should have struck him across the back. Not only would this have cut off Dongshan, it would also have pinned down old Huo. This again matches Linji saying, This old thief is a fellow practitioner. Dongshan heard it raised and said, If not for Huogong, it would have been hard to bear. Foguo added a comment: The bystander has eyes. He also said: He knows only one, not the second. Wansong's view is not so. Foguo said: Dongshan, as bystander, though he has eyes, sees only the awl-tip's sharpness. Wansong said: Though Master Foguo has eyes, he does not see the chisel-head's squareness. Dongshan deliberately used bearing-it to frame Yantou, wanting to reveal that Yantou's original bow had both expedient and real. Sure enough, when the fire reached Yantou's head, he hurriedly scattered it off, saying, That old fellow Dongshan does not know good from bad. At that time I raised with one hand and pressed with the other. Only then do we light the lamp and eat rice. The two houses are now clearly distinct. Have you not seen Master Yong of Baoning's verse: Across the level plain a hare runs, and the hawk is loosed. This praises the threshold question. One press and he pecks out both eyes. This praises Deshan's shout and Yantou's bow. With a poisonous hand he snatches it and someone buys it off. This praises Dongshan setting a price. Alas, the weight and measure are not yet clear. This is exactly what Wansong says. If you want the weight and measure made clear, in truth Foguo and Wansong are not contending over whose head is higher or lower. Rather look at Tiantong placing it on the scale. He praised it, saying:

The thrusting device comes, all holding authority; in affairs there is the majesty that must be carried out. When wind moves, the grass bends When the warrant arrives, it is carried out Even the Buddha hand cannot block it

text_zh: 挫來機風行草偃　總權柄符到奉行　事有必行之威佛手遮不 得國有不犯之令誰敢當頭　賓尚奉而主驕下以風刺上 君忌諫而臣佞上以風化下　底意巖頭問德山雖然父子 興師一擡一捺看心行未免干戈相待
text_en: at all In the state there are commands not to be violated; the guest still offers service while the host is proud. Who dares face it head-on Below uses satire to admonish above The ruler shuns remonstrance and the minister flatters. As for the underlying meaning of Yantou questioning Deshan, Above uses influence to transform below Though they are father and son they raise troops one raise and one press reveal the mind's activity. They still cannot avoid meeting with weapons drawn
The master said: In this verse, all three men thrust in with devices and each holds authority. Only Yantou

text_zh: 師云。此頌三人皆挫來機。各總權柄。唯巖頭 德山有必行之威。有不犯之令。賓奉主驕。在 洞山巖頭。君忌臣佞。在巖頭德山。末後兩句。 在洞山巖頭。此箇榜樣。諸方喚作揀詁。水中 擇乳須是鵝王。便見天童針線功夫。巖頭知 德山有必行威不犯令。故不奪機。且順情禮 拜。洞山知巖頭不受探拔。不受點罰。子承父 業。亦有必行威不犯令。故鉤頭著餌道。若不 是豁公。大難承當。豈非尚奉主驕。忌諫臣佞。 臨濟宗風。喚作紅線套索。碧玉穽坑。陷虎之 機。埋兵掉鬪。諸方盡謂。巖頭一擡一捺。洞山 錯下名言。殊不知。洞山一擡一捺。更甚分明。 此非久參作者。決難領略。今時一等脫白沙 彌。見天童頌道一擡一捺看心行。便道怪得 禪家不肯為人說破。元來都是心行。故作機 巧誑賺學人。萬松道。一分心行。是一分慈悲。 不喫一交。不學一便。可謂果從花裏得。甘向 苦中來。巖頭擡捺。洞山賺出。洞山擡捺。萬松 說破。忽有箇出來禮拜。萬松却放過不打。何 也為伊皮下無血。
text_en: and Deshan have the majesty that must be carried out and commands not to be violated. Guest serving, host proud, lies in Dongshan and Yantou. Ruler avoiding remonstrance, minister flattering, lies in Yantou and Deshan. The last two lines lie in Dongshan and Yantou. This model the various houses call picking apart old cases. In water, to separate milk one must be a goose-king. Then you see Tiantong's needle-and-thread workmanship. Yantou knew Deshan had the majesty that must act and commands not to be violated, so he did not snatch the device, but for the moment followed the situation and bowed. Dongshan knew Yantou would accept neither probing and pulling nor censure and punishment. The son inherits the father's work; he too had majesty that must act and commands not to be violated. So he set the bait on the hook and said, If not for Huogong, it would have been hard to bear. Is this not guest serving host, ruler shunning remonstrance, minister flattering? In the Linji school's style, this is called a red-cord snare, a jade-green pitfall, a device for trapping tigers, burying troops and stirring battle. Everywhere they all say Yantou's one raise and one press, and Dongshan's mistaken naming and phrasing. They do not realize that Dongshan's one raise and one press are even clearer. If one is not a long-practiced adept, one will certainly not grasp it. Nowadays a certain sort of freshly shaven novice sees Tiantong's verse say one raise and one press reveal mind-activity, and then says, No wonder Chan people refuse to explain it plainly to others. So after all it is all just mind-activity, and they only make devices and tricks to deceive students. Wansong says: One measure of mind-activity is one measure of compassion. Without taking a fall, one does not learn a lesson. It may be said the fruit comes from the flower, and sweetness comes out of bitterness. Yantou raised and pressed, Dongshan lured it out. Dongshan raised and pressed, and Wansong explained it through. If suddenly someone came out and bowed, Wansong would let him pass and not strike. Why? Because under his skin there is no blood.

text_zh: 23 魯祖面壁
text_en: 23 Luzu Faces the Wall Instruction to the assembly: Bodhidharma for nine years is called wall-gazing. Shenguang's three bows leaked out

text_zh: 示眾云。達磨九年。呼為壁觀。神光三拜。漏泄 天機。如何得掃蹤滅跡去。
text_en: heaven's secret. How can one sweep away the tracks and erase the traces?
Raised: Whenever Luzu saw a monk come, he would immediately face the wall. Nanquan heard of this and said, I They have met

text_zh: 舉。魯祖凡見僧來便面壁相見了也南泉聞云。我 尋常向他道。空劫以前承當不考自招佛未出世 時會取和尚會也未尚不得一箇半箇只為漏栓索他恁 麼驢年去忙者不會。
text_en: ordinarily tell him: Before the empty kalpa, bear it up; before the Buddha appeared in the world, Without interrogation he confesses even to understand at that time, one cannot get even one or half a one. Yet he like this Monk, do you understand or not Only because the peg and rope were let slip will go on till donkey-year. The busy one does not understand

text_zh: 師云。池州魯祖山寶雲禪師。凡見僧來。便面 壁。自達磨九年之後。無人再行此令。且教諸 方問佛。問祖向上向下底。大家識些痛痒。南 泉是他同參。見人針錐不動。便與打傍通注 破。我尋常向他道。空劫以前承當。佛未出世 時會取。不得一箇半箇。意似放開一線。其實 替他侍者傳法旨了也。又道。他恁麼驢年去。 意似責他太孤峻生。其實賞他覿面分付。不 見道。直饒說得十分。爭似一迴親到。所以靈 山如畫月。曹溪如指月。爭似魯祖在水晶宮 中。廣寒殿裡。披襟相見。保福見南泉魯祖破 綻。問長慶道。只如魯祖。節文在什麼處。被南 泉恁麼道。萬松道。保福如何道節文二字來。 若非不萌枝上解辨春秋。難置此問。長慶對 云。退己讓人萬中無一。萬松道。古人得恁麼 眼明。玄覺云。南泉為復是唱和語。不肯語。萬 松道。半遮半掩。謾渠一點不得。翠巖芝云。何 勞如此。萬松道。已是起模畫樣了也。又云。若 有僧來見箇什麼。萬松道。猶嫌少在。復云知 時好。萬松道。若是陶淵明。攢眉便歸去。又 云。我即不然。未具胞胎不得會。會得則打折 爾腰。萬松道。和尚棒教誰喫。羅山云。王老師 當時若見。背上與五火抄。為伊解放不解收。 萬松道。五更侵早起。已有夜行人。玄沙云。我 當時若見。也與五火抄。萬松云。惱亂春風卒 未休。雲居錫云。羅山玄沙。總恁麼道。為復一 般別有道理。萬松道。共計十火抄。又云。若 揀得出。許尚座佛法有去處。萬松道。好與五 火抄。諸仁者爾看。南泉恁麼貶屈魯祖。長慶 却道。正是退己讓人。魯祖把斷關津。羅山却 道。解放不解收。盡是魚前布網。賊過張弓。更 看天童別作甚麼向當。頌云。
text_en: to face the wall. Since Bodhidharma's nine years, no one had carried out this command again. It did at least make those in the various quarters Then he asks about the upward and downward matter of asking Buddha, asking the Patriarchs, so everyone can feel a bit of the ache and itch. Nanquan was his fellow practitioner. Seeing the man would not stir even to a needle or awl, he at once gave a side stroke, opening a side passage and breaking through. I usually tell him: Take it up from before the empty kalpa, before the Buddha appeared in the world, and realize it then. Not one or even half a one can get it. The meaning seems like he is letting out a single thread, but in truth he has already conveyed the Dharma intent for that attendant. He also says: If he goes on like this till donkey-year, the meaning seems to scold him for being too solitary and severe, but actually he praises him for a face-to-face entrustment. Do you not see it said: Even if one speaks it ten parts complete, how can it compare with one direct personal arrival? Therefore Vulture Peak is like painting the moon, and Caoxi is like pointing to the moon. How could it compare to Luzu in the crystal palace, in the Palace of Vast Cold, opening his robe and meeting directly. Baofu saw Nanquan and Luzu laid open and worn through, and asked Changqing: As for Luzu, where are the joints and pattern lines? Since Nanquan spoke like that, Wansong said: How did Baofu come to use the two words joints and pattern? If he were not able to distinguish spring and autumn on a branch where no buds sprout, it would be hard to pose this question. Changqing replied, saying: To withdraw oneself and yield to another, among ten thousand there is not one. Wansong said: The ancients had such clear eyes. Xuanzue said: Was Nanquan speaking in responsive accord, or was he refusing to speak? Wan- song said: Half covered, half revealed, he cannot be deceived in the least. Cuiyan Zhi said: Why labor like this? Wansong said: That is already setting up a mold and drawing a pattern. He also said: If a monk comes, what would he see? Wansong said: I still find it too little. He further said: Knowing the time is best. Wansong said: If it were Tao Yuanming, he would knit his brows and go home. He also said: I am not like that. If one has not yet formed the embryo, one cannot understand; if one does understand, I will break your back. Wansong said: Reverend, who is your staff meant for? Luoshan said: If Teacher Wang had seen it at that time, I would have given him five fiery strokes across the back, because he knows how to let go but not how to gather in. Wansong said: Rising before dawn at the fifth watch, there are already night travelers. Xuansha said: If I had seen it then, I too would have given five fiery strokes. Wansong said: Stirring up the spring wind, in the end it does not cease. Yunju Xi said: Luoshan and Xuansha both speak this way. Is it one and the same, or is there another principle? Wansong said: Counted together, ten fiery strokes. He also said: If you can sort it out, I will allow that your Buddhism has somewhere to go. Wansong said: Good, give him five fiery strokes. Worthies, look here: Nanquan thus belittles and bends down Luzu, while Changqing instead says this is precisely withdrawing oneself and yielding to another. Luzu blocks the passes and ferries, yet Luoshan says he can release but not gather. All of it is casting nets before the fish, drawing the bow after the thief has passed. Still look at what different move Tiantong makes to meet it. The verse says:

text_zh: 師云。昔徒單二駙馬赴南京任。道過磁州大 明。入堂隨喜。見僧面壁而坐。駙馬曰。一箇好 淡漢。詮大師曰。淡中有味。水性本淡。加之以 茶蜜。甘苦生焉。性亦恬憺。派之以迷悟。則凡 聖立焉。雖曰淡中有味。斯乃無味之味。其味 恒然妙超情謂。情字從心。謂字從言。到此言 語道斷。心行處滅。法眼道。理極忘情謂。如何 有喻齊。道德經。谷神不死章云。玄牝之門。是 為天地根。綿綿若存。又曰。吾不知誰子。象帝 之先。衲僧為言。綿綿若存。不可一向斷絕去 也。象帝之先者。空劫以前佛未出世時也。如 愚道貴。暗用雪竇道貴如愚。頌云雨過雲凝 曉半開。數峯如畫碧崔嵬。空生不解巖中坐。 惹得天花動地來。此頌空生宴坐天帝雨花。 今魯祖不能省事。惹得南泉玄沙一隊老漢 點檢。此正是玉雕文以喪淳。不若他珠在淵 而自媚。晉書陸機崇文賦曰。石蘊玉以山輝。 水懷珠而川媚。石中蘊玉而為南泉輩琢開。 水中懷珠而為玄沙輩漉出。幸自十分爽氣 清磨暑秋。剛為一片閑雲遠分天水。萬松不 曾面壁。爾這一隊來覓什麼節文。自代云。聽 說天童頌古。
text_en: he entered the hall to pay respects. He saw a monk sitting facing the wall. The son-in-law said: A fine bland fellow. Master Quan said: There is flavor within blandness. The nature of water is originally bland; add tea or honey, and sweetness and bitterness arise. Nature too is calm and plain; divide it by delusion and awakening, and then ordinary and sage are established. Though one says flavor in blandness, this is the flavor of no flavor. Its flavor is constant, wondrously surpassing feeling and speech. The character for feeling comes from heart, the character for speech from words. Here, the road of language is cut off and the workings of mind are extinguished. Fayan said: Principle at the utmost forgets feeling and speech. How could any metaphor match it? In the Daodejing, in the chapter The valley spirit never dies, it says: The gate of the mysterious female is the root of heaven and earth, continuous as if abiding. It also says: I do not know whose child it is, before the image of the Emperor it comes. For patch-robed monks this means: continuous as if abiding, it must not be cut off in one direction and utterly severed. Before the image of the Emperor means before the empty kalpa, before the Buddha appeared in the world. As for like a fool, the Way is precious, this secretly uses Xuedou's line The Way is precious like a fool. His verse says: After the rain, clouds congeal, dawn half opens, several peaks stand like a painting, blue and towering. Empty-born did not understand sitting in the cliff cave, and so he stirred heaven flowers to flutter down. This verse praises Empty-born seated in meditation while the heavenly emperor rained flowers. Now Luzu could not let the matter rest, and stirred up a whole band of old fellows like Nanquan and Xuansha to inspect and pick at it. This is exactly jade carved with patterns and thus losing simplicity. Better the pearl in the deep, shining of itself. In the Jin History, Lu Ji's Chongwen Fu says: Stone stores jade and the mountain shines. Water holds a pearl and the river is made lovely. The jade hidden in stone was chiseled open by the likes of Nanquan; the pearl hidden in water was dredged out by the likes of Xuansha. Fortunately it was of itself fully fresh and clear, cool enough to grind summer into autumn, and yet it was forcibly turned into one patch of idle cloud dividing sky and water afar. Wansong never faced a wall. You lot here, what joints and patterns are you looking for? In my own place I answer: Listen to Tiantong's verse on the ancient case.

text_zh: 師云。南山鼈鼻雖是死蛇。象骨巖前解弄也 活。雪峯拈來示眾。本要以毒去毒。長慶只解 順水推舡。道今日堂中大有人喪身失命。若 解逆風把柂。雪峯須入涅槃堂始得。玄沙聞 舉云。須是我稜兄始得。這裏有些子誵訛。若 道玄沙許長慶。為甚麼。却道我即不恁麼。不 唯順水推舡。更解逆風把柂。這僧不顧危亡。 便間和尚作麼生。玄沙只道。箇用南山作麼。 這裏便見弄活蛇手。雲門便攛拄杖作怕勢。 用得最親。雲巖掃地話頌中。曾舉象骨巖前 弄蛇手。兒時做處老知羞。為雲門道奴見婢 殷勤。便騎賊馬趁賊。也不妨惡手脚。今日再 頌弄蛇話。誇拏龍手。看他大斧斫了手摩挲。 頌云。
text_en: Xuefeng brought it up before the assembly, originally intending to use poison to remove poison. Changqing only knew how to push the boat with the current, saying there would be many in the hall today who lose body and life. If he had known how to take the helm against the wind, Xuefeng would have had to enter the nirvana hall. Xuansha, hearing of it, said: It must be my elder brother Leng. Here there is a bit of entanglement. If one says Xuansha was approving Changqing, then why did he also say, I would not be like that? He not only knew how to push with the current, he also knew how to steer against the wind. That monk, heedless of danger, immediately asked, How would you do it, Reverend? Xuansha only said: What use is South Mountain? Right here one sees the hand that can make a live snake dance. Yunmen then thrust out his staff in a threatening pose. He used it most intimately. In the verse on the Yunyan sweeping-the-ground story, he once cited the line about before Xianggu Cliff the hand that handles snakes. What one did in youth, one is ashamed of in old age. As for Yunmen saying the servant seeing the maid is over-attentive, he then rides the thief's horse to chase the thief. Even so, it does not hinder rough and capable hands and feet. Today again he verses this snake-handling story, boasting of dragon-grabbing hands. Look at him: after hacking with a great axe, he rubs the hand. The verse says:

text_zh: 師云。玄沙專使馳書上雪峯。峯拆開乃見三 張白紙。示其僧云。會麼。僧云。不會。峯云。不 見道。君子千里同風。僧迴舉似沙。沙云。山頭 老和尚蹉過也不知。玄沙承嗣雪峯。尋常證 父攘羊。當仁不讓。道要南山作麼。此又果毅 無前。太剛之甚。長慶隨邪便道。大有人喪身 失命。不解師子返擲。此真見義不為。是無勇 也。風雲際會頭角生。果見韶陽下手弄。此頌 雲門覿面拈出一條活蛇。不同諸師弓柸現 影。能遣能呼者。俚諺有云。呼蛇即易。遣蛇即 難。有擒有縱者。此頌既攛向面前復作怕勢。 已能擒縱必解遣呼。天童末後道。底事如今 付阿誰。冷口傷人不知痛。但凡拍頌歸於自 己。拈向面前。始是作家。雪竇亦云。如今藏在 乳峯前。來者一一看方便。師高聲喝云。看脚 下。萬松道。雪竇貪觀脚下。不知穿過髑髏。天 童冷口傷人。明人不作暗事。我當時若作雲 門。以拄杖攛向雪峯懷裏。擬議不來。隨後教 伊自作自受親遭一口。為什麼如此。今朝二 月二。暫放龍擡頭。
text_en: sheets of blank paper. He showed them to the monk and said: Do you understand? The monk said: I do not. Xuefeng said: Do you not see it said, A gentleman a thousand miles apart shares the same wind? The monk returned and reported this to Xuansha. Xuansha said: The old monk on the mountain blundered past it and does not even know. Xuansha inherited from Xuefeng. He was always ready to attest for his father and steal the sheep, not yielding when faced with what is right. Saying What use is South Mountain? was again resolute and unmatched, too hard indeed. Changqing, following along crookedly, then said there would be many who lose body and life. He did not understand the lion's backward pounce. This is truly seeing what is right and not doing it, that is lack of courage. When wind and cloud meet at the right time, horns and head arise, and indeed one sees Shaoyang lay hands to it and play. This verse praises Yunmen for producing a live snake right before the face, unlike the other masters, whose bow and cup only cast shadows. As for being able to send and summon, a common saying has it: To call a snake is easy; to send a snake away is hard. As for seizing and releasing, this verse speaks of first thrusting it before the face and then making a threatening gesture. If one can already seize and release, one must also understand sending and summoning. At the end Tiantong says: This matter now to whom is it entrusted? A cold mouth wounds people and they do not know the pain. Whenever one claps out a verse, it returns to oneself. Only when one brings it forth before the face is one truly a master. Xuedou also said: Now it is hidden in front of Rufeng. Those who come should each look at the expedient means. The Master shouted loudly: Watch your feet below. Wansong said: Xuedou greedily watches below his feet, not knowing he has already pierced through the skull. Tian- tong's cold mouth wounds people. A clear-eyed man does nothing in the dark. If I had been Yun- men at the time, I would have thrust the staff into Xuefeng's breast. If deliberation did not come, then afterward I would have had him bear it himself and personally take a bite. Why is it like this? This morning is the second day of the second month, so for now we let the dragon raise its head.

text_en: was of the Tang imperial line. When Xuanzong was still hidden as a monk and was about to visit the Master, the Master foresaw it and told the steward: Strictly forbid idle talk, speak only of ordinary matters. The emperor stayed a long time, then suddenly took leave. The Master secretly said to him: The time has come. Do not remain stuck, coiled in the mud. He also entrusted him with the future affairs of the Buddha-Dharma. After Wuzong's suppression of the teaching for six years, Xuanzong restored it, and the Master had great influence in this. The emperor was about to summon the Master back to the palace for offerings, but the Master had long since passed away. The emperor, in grief, posthumously titled him Wukong Chan Master. One day the Master called to the attendant: Bring me the rhinoceros fan. The attendant said: The fan is broken. This too is plain and straightforward talk between father and son. The Master said: The fan being broken, give me back the rhinoceros. This is the whole body entering the weeds for the sake of raising the child, the occasion for it. The attendant had no reply, yet still by way of the crooked he struck the straight, only he himself did not know it. Touzi answered in his place, saying: I do not refuse to bring it forth, but I fear the head and horns are not complete. Wansong said: Good at patching and mending. Xuedou commented: I want precisely the incomplete head and horns. Wansong said: That is an old thing from our own house. Shishuang said: If it is returned to the Reverend, then there will be none. Wan- song said: He avoids it right in front of him. Xuedou commented: The rhinoceros is still there. Wansong said: Clear eyes are hard to deceive. Baofu said: Reverend, you are advanced in years, better ask someone else. Wan- song said: Much favor, deep resentment. Xuedou commented: A pity, toil without merit. Wan- song said: A good heart gets no good return. Judging by this whole pack of old fellows, they only speak principles in vain. As for the fan and the rhinoceros, in the end they still could not bring them out. Only Zifu drew a circle and wrote the character ox in the middle. Fan and rhinoceros stood there fresh and whole, unmoving. Xuedou commented: Why did he not bring it out just now? In truth, when he said the fan is broken, how had even a hairbreadth been touched? And when he did not bring it out just now, what was ever lacking? Now bringing it out adds nothing at all. Tiantong praised Zifu for bringing it out and using it intimately. Marking the name and making the invitation, he specially prepares a serving of tea. The verse says:

text_zh: 師云。諸方謂。扇畫犀牛玩月。或云。犀角為 扇。或云。以犀為柄。皆得名為犀牛扇也。鹽官 當時開箇舖席。各人拈出一柄。獨資福親手 新樣。脫體偏別。師甞示眾云。隔江見資福剎 竿便迴後。脚跟下好與三十棒。豈況過江來。 時有僧纔出。師云。不堪共語。大抵講肆貴說 到。宗門貴用到。以棬攣中字最有來由。玄沙 示眾云。吾有正法眼藏。付囑摩訶迦葉。猶如 畫月。曹溪竪拂子。猶如指月。桂轂乃月也。涅 盤經世尊放月愛光。阿闍世王熱惱清涼。所 以道。誰知桂轂千年魄。妙作通明一點秋。可 謂大柄若在手。清風常及身。犀牛扇話。拈頌 最多。要且端的不曾與鹽官相見。萬松若作 侍者。見道與我過犀牛扇子來。有甚羽蒲紙 竹綾絹椶𤛆。信手拈來便與一柄。何者縱有 千般巧。終無兩樣風。
text_en: fan. Or some say it had a rhinoceros-horn handle; in either case it is called a rhinoceros fan. Yanguan at that time opened a whole stall of them, each person producing one fan. Only Zifu, with his own hand, made a new style, wholly distinct from the rest. The master once instructed the assembly, saying, When one sees Zifu’s temple-banner across the river, one should turn back at once; under his heels he well deserves thirty blows. How much more if he crosses the river and comes here. At that time, as soon as a monk stepped out, the master said, Not fit to talk with. In general, lecture halls value speech reaching its point; the school gate values function reaching its point. The character crooked and curled has the deepest source. Xuansha instructed the assembly, saying, I have the treasury of the true Dharma eye and entrust it to Mahākāśyapa; it is like painting the moon. Caoxi raising the whisk is like pointing to the moon. The cassia wheel is the moon itself. In the Nirvāṇa Sūtra, the World-Honored One emitted the moon of loving light; King Ajātaśatru’s feverish affliction was cooled. Therefore it is said, Who knows that the cassia wheel’s thousand-year soul wondrously becomes one bright point of autumn. It may be called: if the great handle is in hand, the clear wind constantly reaches the body. Of the rhinoceros fan case, the raised verses are the most numerous, yet in truth they have never met Yanguan face to face. If Wansong were the attendant, and heard him say, Bring me the rhinoceros fan, what feather, cattail, paper, bamboo, silk gauze, plain silk, or palm fan—whatever came to hand, I would pick one up and hand it over. Why? Even if there are a thousand clever kinds, in the end there are not two kinds of wind.

text_en: 26. Yangshan Points to Snow Instruction to the assembly: Ice and frost are one color; snow and moon interweave their light. It freezes the Dharma-body to death and chills away

text_zh: 師云。古人臨機遇物。發明空劫以前一段大 事。法華經云。純一無雜具足清白梵行之相。 說者以謂。白是眾色之本。一乘是諸乘之源。 而不說白色向上更有事在。故仰山指雪師 子。示眾云。還有過得此色者麼。且白是眾色 之本。雪色至白。如何更有過此色者。萬松道。 既稱為色。必與眼對。過白之色。唯無色者。不 與眼對。雲門所以道。當時便與推倒。若便向 至白無白處。認著正是墮在無色界中。雪竇 所以別指出一條活路。向推倒處。却教扶起。 佛眼云。若向這裏扶持起來。甚生次第事。萬 松道。若是他宗異派。不道不得。更須知有洞 上宗風正倒時便起。正起時便倒底時節。然 後起倒同時。起倒不立。更買草鞋。行脚三十 年不見。佛覺頌云。一色無過指示人。白銀世 界裏頻申。超然推倒還扶起。爭似東風煦日 新。萬松道。日出後一場懡㦬。一等學人。見雲 門推倒雪竇扶起。便作機鋒轉換。大用無方 會。見向一色邊不得色邊會。以為宗旨血脈。 已有佛覺為證。如或不信。更問天童。頌云。
text_en: The Lotus Sūtra says: Purely one, without mixture, fully endowed with the marks of pure white brahma-conduct. Commentators say white is the root of all colors, and the One Vehicle is the source of all vehicles. But they do not say that above white there is yet another matter. Therefore Yangshan pointed to the snow lion and instructed the assembly, saying, Is there anyone who can pass beyond this color? Now white is the root of all colors; the color of snow is utmost white. How can there still be one who gets past this color? Wansong says: Since it is called a color, it must stand opposed to the eye. The color beyond white is only colorless—one that does not stand opposed to the eye. That is why Yunmen said, At that moment I would have pushed it down. If you then head straight toward the place of utmost white where there is no white and take hold there, you have fallen precisely into the formless realm. Xuedou therefore separately pointed out a living road: at the very place of pushing down, he instead teaches setting it up. Foyan said, If one supports and raises it here, what an orderly sequence of living activity. Wan- song says: For other schools and different lineages, this must indeed be said. But you must further know the Dongshan house style: at the very time of falling, it rises; at the very time of rising, it falls to the bottom. Only then are rising and falling simultaneous; rising and falling do not stand. Then buy more straw sandals and wander thirty years and still not see it. Fojue’s verse says: One color with nothing beyond, pointed out to people; in a white silver world he repeatedly stretches it forth. Transcendently push it down and then set it up again—how can that compare with east wind and warming sun bringing freshness? Wansong says: After sunrise, one whole muddle. A certain kind of student, seeing Yun- men push down and Xuedou set up, immediately makes it into turning sharp exchanges and boundless great function. Or seeing it, they understand toward the side of one color, or toward the side beyond color, taking that as the lifeblood of the school. Fojue already stands as witness. If you still do not believe it, ask Tiantong again. He verses:
One falls, one rises—the snow-court lion; cautious in transgressing, yet cherishing benevolence. Just like a living one

text_zh: 師云。雲門一倒。雪竇一起。仰山指師子。要過 此色。三箇鼎足闕一不可。三玄三要盡在於 茲。仰山恐人坐在明白裏。豈非慎犯懷仁也。 指似於人令過此色。豈非勇為見義也。魯語 曰。見義不為無勇也。雲門又恐坐在一色邊 也。豈非慎犯懷仁。便與推倒。亦勇為見義也。 雪竇恐人只解推倒。乃慎犯懷仁也。更能扶 起。勇為見義也。不見。趙州道。老僧不在明 白裏。良以清光照眼猶自迷家。明白轉身未 免墮位。只解推倒不解扶起。而堪作什麼。本 色衲僧如珠走盤。雖同死同生而不居生死。 雖無彼無此而權立彼此。末後兩句。有時。太 陽門下。有時。明月堂前。萬古長空。一朝風 月。朝菌蟪蛄。且道。而今是什麼時節。且隨 老木同寒瘠。將逐春風入燒瘢。
text_en: this color. The three are the tripod’s legs; one missing will not do. The Three Mysteries and Three Essentials are all contained in this. Yangshan feared people would sit in mere clarity—is this not cautious transgression with benevolence? Pointing it out to people to make them pass this color—is this not bold action in seeing what is right? The Analects says: To see what is right and not act is lack of courage. Yunmen again feared people would sit on the side of one color— is this not cautious transgression with benevolence? So he immediately pushed it down, also boldly acting on what is right. Xuedou feared people would only know how to push down—that too is cautious transgression with benevolence. Then he could further set it back up: bold action in seeing what is right. Have you not seen Zhaozhou say, This old monk is not in bright clarity. Truly, clear light shining in the eyes still bewilders the home. Turning within bright clarity still does not avoid falling into position. If one only knows pushing down and not setting up, what use can he be? A true-color patch-robed monk is like a pearl rolling on a tray: though sharing death and life, he does not abide in death and life. Though there is no this and no that, provisionally he sets up this and that. In the final two lines, at times it is at the gate of the sun; at times before the hall of the bright moon. The eternal vast sky, one morning’s wind and moon; morning mushrooms and summer cicadas. Tell me: what season is it now? For now, follow the old trees in the same cold leanness, then chase the spring wind into the burned scars.

text_en: the blind. Fayan said, One gained, one lost. Dongchan Qi said, Venerable, how do you understand it? Some say: because they did not understand the intent, they just went to roll the blind. Others say: the one pointed to understood, and the one who went without being pointed to lost. Is understanding it this way acceptable or not? Since this understanding is not allowed, then tell me: which one gained, and which one lost? Wansong says: washing a clod of earth in mud. This is not only Fayan. One day Nanquan said to a monk, Last night there was a good wind. The monk also said, Last night there was a good wind. Quan said, It blew down a pine tree before the gate. The monk also said, It blew down a pine tree before the gate. Next Nanquan said to another monk, Last night there was a good wind. The monk said, What kind of wind? Quan said, It blew down a pine tree before the gate. The monk said, What pine tree? Quan said, One gained, one lost. The pointing-to-the-blind story is an extremely skillful device for people. The two monks rolling the blind—on each man’s own side, there are naturally two roads. Fayan first gave them one seal; once sealed and fixed, there is no further change. On Fayan’s side, brightness and darkness interpenetrate. The device of killing and giving life—the realm of a great person is known by Samantabhadra. Everywhere people take leaving gain and loss, forgetting right and wrong, as supreme. Fayan runs into the sea of right and wrong and the pit of gain and loss and makes a livelihood there. For only one beyond gain and loss can determine the gain and loss of all under heaven. Wan- song too, speaking thus, also has gain and loss. You all, coming up like this, also have gain and loss. Only one who deeply understands the roots of benefit and harm can weigh their loss and gain. Sunge called this a ready-made gong’an, needing no further testing. text_zh: 師云。古人不得已。強名本分事。松直。棘曲。 鵠白。烏玄。本出楞嚴經。天童點化鶴長𠒎短。 莊子云。長者不為有餘。短者不為不足。是故 𠒎脛雖短續之則憂。鶴脛雖長。斷之則悲。俗 諺云。要不悶依本分。豈直羲皇世人俱忘治 亂。孔子謂。西方有大聖人。不治而不亂。治亂 者得失也。三祖云。得失是非一時放却。周易 乾卦。初九潛龍。勿用。九四或躍在淵。秦臺記。 王次仲年弱冠。變蒼頡古文為隷書。秦始皇 徵之不起。上怒檻車囚之赴國。路化作鳥脫 羈絆。飛至西山落二翮。今媯川縣有大翮碢。 即其處也。此頌上古之風。出處行藏。各安其 分。佛未出世。有多少經論公案。及至祖師 西來。便有得有失。何不向未指簾時會取。隨 風轉空。截流到岸。此二句點出二僧得失。天 童大有功夫不易。恁麼道。若無活人手。爭能 殺得人。是故又道。箇中靈利衲僧。看取清涼 手段。且道。據什麼令。便得如此。待爾喫棒 了。向爾道。
text_en: Swans white, crows black—this originally comes from the Śūraṅgama Sūtra. Tiantong transformed it into cranes long and short. Zhuangzi says: What is long is not excessive, what is short is not insufficient. Therefore though a duck’s legs are short, if you lengthen them there is sorrow; though a crane’s legs are long, if you cut them there is grief. A common saying says: If you want no vexation, abide in your proper lot. Is it only the people of Fuxi’s age who forgot order and disorder? Confucius said: In the West there is a great sage who governs not, yet there is no disorder. Order and disorder are gain and loss. The Third Patriarch said: Put down gain and loss, right and wrong, all at once. In the Zhouyi, the Qian hexagram says: First nine, hidden dragon, do not act. Ninth in the fourth, perhaps leaping in the deep. The Record of Qin Terraces says: Wang Cizhong, in his youth, changed Cangjie’s ancient script into clerical script. Qin Shihuang summoned him, but he would not rise. The emperor grew angry, caged him in a cart and sent him to the capital. On the road he transformed into a bird and escaped his restraints, flying to the western mountains, where two feathers fell. Now in Guichuan county there is the Great Feather Mound— that is the place. This verse praises the wind of high antiquity: appearing or withdrawing, acting or hiding, each settled in its proper lot. Before the Buddha appeared in the world, how many sūtras, treatises, and gong’an were there? When the ancestral teacher came from the West, there was at once gain and loss. Why not understand it before the blind was pointed to? Turning with the wind, empty; cutting the current, reaching shore—these two lines point out the gain and loss of the two monks. Tian- tong’s effort is great and not easy. Saying it this way: if there were no living hand, how could one kill a man? Therefore he again says: Keen patch-robed monks within this should look at Qingliang’s methods. Tell me, by what command may one be thus? Wait till you have taken a beating, then I will tell you.

text_zh: 28 護國三懡
text_en: 28. Huguo’s Three Muddleings Instruction to the assembly: A man who hangs not an inch of thread is exactly a naked ascetic outsider. A fellow who chews not

text_zh: 示眾云。不挂寸絲底人。正是裸形外道。不嚼 粒米底漢。斷歸焦面鬼王。直饒聖處受生。未 免竿頭險墮。還有掩羞處麼。
text_en: a grain of rice surely belongs to the scorched-faced king of ghosts. Even if he is born in a holy place, he still cannot avoid the perilous fall from the top of the pole. Is there still any place to cover one’s shame?
Raised: A monk asked Huguo, What is it like when a crane stands on a withered pine? Guo Step by step, climbing high is easy

text_zh: 舉。僧問護國。鶴立枯松時如何步步登高易國 云。地下底一場懡㦬心心放下難僧云。滴水滴凍 時如何法身無被不禁寒國云。日出後一場懡㦬雪消露出 死人來僧云。會昌沙汰時。護法善神向甚麼 處去也點即不到國云。三門頭兩箇一場懡㦬到即 不點。
text_en: said, Under the ground, one whole muddle. The monk said, What about when dripping water drips into ice? Hard to let go, mind after mind. Guo said, After sunrise, one whole muddle. The monk said, During the Huichang suppression, where did the good guardian gods of the Dharma The dharma body has no covering and cannot withstand the cold. When the snow melts, it is revealed. A dead man comes. go? Guo said, At the temple gate, the two of them were one whole muddle. If you point, you do not reach it. If you reach it, then you do not point.
The master said: Huguo Jingguo Great Master of Suicheng Mountain in Suizhou, personal name Shoucheng, together with

text_zh: 師云。隋州隋城山護國淨果大師。諱守澄。與 二世演化大師諱知遠。同在湖南報慈。慈陞 座。師問如何是真如佛性。慈曰。誰無。參退。 首座問。汝適來問和尚話還會麼。師曰。不會。 座曰。和尚恁麼慈悲。汝為什麼不會。真如佛 性誰無。乃至四生六道悉皆具足。師曰。感謝 首座為某說破。淨果在傍齩齒曰。這老漢自 家無眼更瞎他人。乃召師問。首座適來說箇 什麼。師曰。某當時不會得他說破。具如前舉。 淨果曰。上座佛法不是這箇道理。汝若不信 去問取堂頭。師上堂頭具說前解。慈亦曰。佛 法不是這箇道理。師曰。適來問第三座。他亦 不肯。故教來問。且望慈悲為某決破。慈曰。汝 去問取第三座去。師下來禮問。淨果曰。汝但 問來。師便問。如何是真如佛性。淨果曰。誰有。 師於言下契悟。再拜謝了。乃曰。首座或在眾。 或出世。某誓願佐助。後遂相繼住持。此話諸 方謂之護國三懡㦬。與保福四謾人為對。未 透關者。極難奔湊。不見。僧問雲居簡禪師。孤 峯獨宿時如何。居云。九間僧堂裏不臥。誰教 爾孤峯獨宿。此話雖無玄妙甚有開發。舉此 一隅。三隅可見。洞山玄中銘。峯巒秀異。鶴不 停機。靈木迢然。鳳無依倚。這僧却問。鶴立孤 松時如何。這僧癡坐功夫既到。將這些子本 地風光。貼在額頭。逢人呈似。殊不知。孤危不 立。道方高。天台教中謂之頂墮。所以護國道。 地下底一場懡㦬。這僧不向孤危處作活計。 又將氷枯雪老處呈上。又不知乾嚗嚗時。還 生津潤。冷清清處。却要溫和。所以道。日出後 一場懡㦬。這僧戈中兩翻。上來兩被護國格 下。既沒奈何。却問教門興廢。疑難道。會昌沙 汰時。護法善神向什麼處去也。唐武宗好仙。 沙汰僧尼二十六萬五百人。會昌五年八月 下旬。勒令歸俗。帝服方士丹藥。性加躁急。喜 怒不常。至六年三月初。纔及半年以丹毒死。 宣宗即位。佛寺復增三倍之多。以神道為論。 不假武宗小廢。何致宣宗大興。善神權巧之 方斷非凡下可及。若以衲僧見處。法門本無 興廢。善神豈有去來。所以道。三門頭兩箇一 場懡㦬。萬松恁麼道。錯為人下注脚了也。又 不見。僧問。心法雙忘時如何。國云。不洗面。 僧云。月落寒潭時如何。國云。不洗面。僧云。 光境俱忘時如何。國云。不洗面。不可總從頭 注解將去也。不注解時如何。自有天童頌古。
text_en: the Second-Generation Yanhua Great Master, personal name Zhiyuan, were both at Baozi in Hunan. Baozi ascended the seat. The master asked, What is true suchness Buddha-nature? Baozi said, Who does not have it? He withdrew from interview. The head monk asked, Do you understand the abbot’s words just now? The master said, I do not. The head monk said, The abbot is so compassionate—why do you not understand? True suchness Buddha- nature, who lacks it? Even the four kinds of birth and the six paths all fully possess it. The master said, Thanks to the head monk for explaining it for me. Jingguo, standing nearby, ground his teeth and said, This old fellow himself has no eyes, and he further blinds others. Then he called the master and asked, What did the head monk just now say? The master said, I did not understand then, and he explained it for me, exactly as stated above. Jingguo said, Venerable, the Buddha-Dharma is not this kind of principle. If you do not believe it, go ask the abbot. The master went up to the abbot and fully recounted the earlier explanation. Baozi also said, Buddha- Dharma is not this kind of principle. The master said, I just asked the third seat, and he also did not approve, so he told me to come ask. I only hope, out of compassion, you will decide and break it open for me. Baozi said, You go ask the third seat. The master came down and bowed to ask. Jingguo said, Just ask. The master then asked, What is true suchness Buddha-nature? Jingguo said, Who has it? At these words the master awakened in accord. He bowed again in thanks and then said, Whether the head monk remains in the assembly or goes forth to head a temple, I vow to assist him. Later they succeeded one another as abbots. This story the various houses call Huguo’s Three Muddles, paired with Baofu’s Four Deceptions. For those who have not yet passed the barrier, it is extremely hard to approach. Have you not seen a monk ask Chan Master Yunju Jian, When alone lodging on a solitary peak, how is it? Yunju said, If you do not sleep in the nine-bay monks’ hall, who told you to sleep alone on a solitary peak? Though this saying has no mystery, it is greatly opening. Raise this one corner, and the other three can be seen. In Dongshan’s Inscription on the Mystery Within Mystery: Peaks and ridges stand lofty and distinct; the crane does not the mechanism comes to rest. The numinous tree stands far off; the phoenix has nothing to perch on. Yet this monk asks, When a crane stands on a lone pine, what then? This monk, having reached a stage in his dull seated effort, takes this bit of his original native scenery and sticks it on his forehead, showing it to everyone he meets. He does not realize that at solitary peril one does not stand; only then is the Way truly high. In Tiantai teaching this is called falling from the summit. Therefore Huguo said, down on the ground, another bout of muddle. This monk did not make his living in the place of solitary peril, and instead presented a place of ice-dry and snow-withered deadness. He also did not know that when all is dry and parched, there can still arise moisture and savor; in a cold and desolate place, warmth and harmony are still required. So it is said, after the sun comes out there is another bout of muddle. This monk was turned over twice on the spear-point; when he came up he was twice checked by Huguo and cast down. Having no recourse, he then asked about the rise and decline of the teaching, raising this difficulty: during the Huichang suppression of the sangha, where did the good guardian deities of the Dharma go? Emperor Wuzong of Tang loved immortality arts. He purged 260,500 monks and nuns. In the eighth month of the fifth year of Huichang, in the latter part of the month, he ordered them to return to lay life. The emperor took alchemical elixirs from adepts; his temperament grew more irritable and hasty, his joy and anger were unpredictable. By early third month of the sixth year, in barely half a year, he died of elixir poisoning. Xuanzong ascended the throne, and Buddhist temples increased again to more than triple. Judged from the standpoint of divine agency, without Wuzong's small suppression, how could there have been Xuanzong's great revival? The expedient skillful means of the good deities are not something ordinary people can reach. But from the patch-robed monk's point of view, the Dharma gate originally has no rise or decline. How could the good deities come or go? Therefore it is said, at the temple gate there are two more bouts of muddle. When Wansong talks this way, he has wrongly added footnotes for people again. And do you not see? A monk asked, What about when mind and dharmas are both forgotten? Guo said, Not washing the face. The monk said, What about when the moon sets in the cold pool? Guo said, Not washing the face. The monk said, what about when both light and objects are forgotten? Guo said, Not washing the face. You must not explain it all away from the beginning with annotations. If not annotating it, then what? Tiantong himself has a verse on the old case.

A stalwart man, sharp and severe, with sideburns not yet autumn-white; if a man is not indignant, he will not be enfeoffed as a lord. Resenting that heaven cannot be reached. Greedy to make the journey too quickly.

text_zh: 壯士稜稜鬢未秋恨天不到　男兒不憤不封侯貪程太速 翻思清白傳家客已太多生　洗耳溪頭不飲牛末後太過
text_en: Then turn and think of the man who hands down pure integrity in his house: he washes his ears by the stream and will not let the ox drink. Already too many lifetimes. At the end it goes too far.
The master said: The Third Patriarch said, The Great Way's body is broad, with neither easy nor hard; petty views are fox-like doubts.

text_zh: 師云。三祖道。大道體寬無易無難。小見狐疑。 轉急轉遲。昔有二僧同行。性急者在前。呼在 後者云。光陰迅速疾走上來。後僧云。大道廣 濶。忙作甚麼。萬松甞見。圓通善國師手書二 頌云。光陰迅速疾走上來。路頭踏著。優鉢花 開。大道廣濶。忙作什麼。放開肚皮。一時包裹。 此圓通善國師二頌。如這僧恁麼問護國恁麼 答。各具一隻眼。天童頌中前兩句。如銳氣貪 榮。後兩句如退身致仕。後漢班超家貧常傭 寫書。乃投筆曰。大丈夫當効張騫傅介子立 功異域。以取封侯萬里之外。焉能久事於筆 硯間乎。後討西國。封定遠侯。此喻這僧三問 探頭太過也。後漢楊震任荊州太守。性公廉 不受私謁。子孫蔬食步行。故舊長者欲開產 業。震不肯曰。使後世稱為清白吏子孫。以此 遺之。不亦厚乎。史記。許由隱於箕山。依山而 食。就河而飲。堯讓帝位。由聞之臨河洗耳。巢 父飲牛問曰。凡人洗面。公獨洗耳。由曰。聞堯 請我為九州長。故洗是非。父曰。豫章之木生 於高山。工人莫得。子欲避世。何不深藏。今游 人間苟求名譽。行待下飲。恐污牛口。乃牽上 流飲之。天童以楊震許由巢父三人。頌三懡 㦬。却被同安道濁者自濁。清者清。菩提煩惱 等空平。這僧與護國放下了也。不干諸人事。 各請逐便。
text_en: The more hurried, the more delayed. Long ago two monks traveled together. The impatient one walked ahead and called to the one behind, saying, Time flies swiftly, hurry up and come on. The monk behind said, The Great Way is vast and broad; what is the rush for? Wansong once saw two verses written in the hand of National Teacher Yuantong Shan: Time flies swiftly, hurry up and come on. If on the road you set your foot just right, the udumbara flower blooms. The Great Way is vast and broad, what is the rush for? Let your belly go loose and at once it all gets wrapped up. These two verses by National Teacher Yuantong Shan are like this monk asking in this way and Huguo answering in this way: each has one eye. In Tiantong's verse, the first two lines are like sharp vigor greedily seeking glory; the latter two lines are like retiring from office and withdrawing. In Later Han, Ban Chao was poor and often hired out copying texts. Then he threw down his brush and said, A true man should emulate Zhang Qian and Fu Jiezi, establishing merit in foreign lands and gain enfeoffment ten thousand li away. How can I long remain occupied with brush and inkstone? Later he campaigned in the Western Regions and was enfeoffed as Marquis Dingyuan. This is a metaphor for this monk's three questions poking his head out too far. In Later Han, Yang Zhen served as governor of Jingzhou; by nature he was upright and incorruptible, accepting no private visits. His sons and grandsons ate vegetables and went on foot. Elder old friends wished to set up an estate for the family, but Zhen would not permit it, saying, Let later generations call them descendants of a pure and honest official; by this I bequeath to them, is that not generous enough? In the Records of the Historian, Xu You hid at Mount Ji, living by the mountain for food and drinking from the river. Yao offered him the imperial throne; when Xu You heard this he went to the river and washed his ears. Chao Fu was watering an ox and asked, Ordinary people wash their faces; you alone wash your ears. Xu You said, I heard Yao asked me to be lord of the nine provinces, so I wash away right and wrong. Fu said, Timber of yuzhang grows on high mountains, where craftsmen cannot reach it. If you wish to avoid the world, why not hide more deeply? Now you wander among men vainly seeking fame and reputation. I was just about to let my ox drink downstream, but I fear you have fouled the ox's mouth, so I will lead it upstream to drink. Tiantong uses Yang Zhen, Xu You, and Chao Fu, these three men, to praise the three bouts of muddle, yet he is caught by Tong'an's saying: the muddy are muddy of themselves, the clear are clear; bodhi and affliction are equally empty and level. This monk and Huguo have already put it all down; it has nothing to do with the rest of you. Each of you may go as you please.

text_zh: 29 風穴鐵牛
text_en: 29. Fengxue's Iron Ox Instruction to the assembly: Slow moves in chess and dull action rot away the axe handle. Eyes turn and the head gets confused, and the ladle handle is snatched away.

text_zh: 示眾云。遲棊鈍行。爛却斧柯。眼轉頭迷。奪將 杓柄。若也打在鬼窟裏。把定死蛇頭。還有變 豹分也無。
text_en: If you get struck into a ghost cave and grab fast to a dead snake's head, is there still any share in changing into a leopard or not?
Cited case: Fengxue, in the government office at Yingzhou, ascended the hall and said: The Patriarch's mind-seal is shaped

text_zh: 舉。風穴在郢州衙內。上堂云。祖師心印狀 似鐵牛之機針剳不入去即印住拽迴鼻孔住即印破截斷 脚跟只如不去不住。印即是。不印即是泥裏洗土 塊時有廬陂長老出問云。某甲有鐵牛之機。 請師不搭印宛有逆水之波穴云。慣釣鯨鯢澄巨浸。 却嗟蛙步𩥇泥沙引魂幡子搐氣袋陂佇思已過鬼門關穴 喝云。長老何不進語已臨崖岸更與一推陂擬議許多時節甚處 去來穴打一拂子云。還記得話頭麼。試舉 看為人為徹殺人見血陂擬開口猶自不伏燒埋穴又打一拂子 仍少三十棒牧主云。佛法與王法一般不會做官看傍州例穴 云。見箇什麼却好與一拂子牧云。當斷不斷返招其 亂自罵自招穴便下座得意濃時正好休。
text_en: like the mechanism of an iron ox: if you go, it seals you fast; if you stay, it shatters the seal. But if neither going nor staying, is sealing it right, or is not sealing it right? Then Elder Lupi came forth and asked: I have the iron ox mechanism. A needle cannot be stuck in. Drag the nostrils back. Cut off the heel. Washing dirt in mud. Clods. I ask the master not to apply the seal. Fengxue said: Used to fishing for whales in the clear great deep, As if there were waves running against the current. yet I lament a frog's gait in mud and sand. Lupi stood thinking. Fengxue Waving the soul-summoning banner, jerking the breath bag. Already past the ghost gate pass. shouted: Elder, why do you not speak? As Lupi hesitated, Fengxue struck him with a whisk and said: Do you still remember the opening words? Try raising them. Already at the cliff edge, and still given another push. After so much time, to what place did he go and come? Lupi was about to open his mouth; Fengxue struck him again with the whisk. For the sake of others, thoroughgoing, killing and seeing blood. Still not submitting to burning and burial. The governor said: The Buddha-Dharma and the king's law are the same. Fengxue Still short of thirty blows. If you do not know how to be an official, look at the neighboring prefecture's precedent. said: What have you seen? The governor said: If one should cut off and does not cut off, it instead invites its Then it is just right to give one whisk. own disorder. Fengxue then descended from the seat. Cursing yourself and inviting it yourself. When satisfaction is strongest, that is exactly when to stop.
The master said: Layman Wujin cited this: Linji took leave of Weishan, and Yangshan attended at his side.

text_zh: 師云。無盡居士。舉。臨際辭溈山。仰山侍其傍。 溈曰。此人他日法道如何。仰曰。他日法道大 行吳越。遇風即止。又問其嗣之者何人。仰曰。 年代深遠未可言耳。溈固問之曰。吾亦欲知。 仰云。經不云乎。將此深心奉塵剎。是則名為 報佛恩。居士曰。吾以此知。風穴仰山之後身 也。穴初參雪峯五年。一日請益臨際會下兩 堂上座舉頭相顧各下一喝。僧舉問際。未審 具賓主眼否。際曰。雖然如是。賓主歷然。雪峯 敘與巖頭欽山。進途而值臨際已逝不及參。 則曰。汝欲會當問取他子孫。穴舉似南院顒。 院云。雪峯古佛也。師後住汝州風穴山廣慧 禪院。五代離亂。郢州牧主請師衙內住夏。一 日牧主請陞座。示眾云。祖師心印。狀似鐵牛 之機。不同石人木馬玄唱玄提。直下如鐵牛。 無爾近傍處。爾纔去鉤迴。纔住打教百雜碎。 只如不去不住。印即是。不印即是。可謂鉤頭 有餌。盧陂長老亦是際下兒孫。便拈轉他話 頭。置問不妨奇特。道某甲有鐵牛之機。請師 不搭印。其奈風穴據令而。行便道。慣釣鯨鯢 澄巨浸。却嗟蛙步𩥇泥沙。鯨鯢橫海大魚也。 莊子任公子五十犗為餌。曾得此魚。蛙步𩥇 泥沙。有說。漢武帝時有暴利長。渥洼水傍見 群野馬。中有奇者來飲水。因作土人。持勒絆 于傍。習以為常。以人代之。收得其馬。欲神異 其馬。謂從水出。遂傳為龍種。穴謂馬出清水 反偃𩥇泥沙中。此說迂迴風穴眾吼集。明作 蛙步。不見。雪竇頌犀牛扇話了。復云。若要清 風再振。頭角重生。請禪客下轉語乃云。扇子 既破。還我犀牛兒來。時有僧出云。大眾參堂 去。竇喝云。拋鉤釣鯤鯨釣得箇蝦䗫。以此兩 句對風穴上下兩句。蛙字無疑也。陂佇思。問 話呈機。要與風穴相見。而忽遭點。要別尋出 長投。至爾施呈槍法。一樬檐打倒也。此不解 奪機行令賓主互換之過也。牧主久參風穴。 不無見處道。佛法與王法一般。風穴收得安 南。又憂塞北。便問牧主道。見箇什麼。這裏便 好。與盧陂雪屈。却只道。當斷不斷反招其亂 也。不妨說到。風穴為伊是俗官。飲氣吞聲便 下座。二尊宿一龍一蛇。做剛做柔。篁鼓臨際 宗風。更著天童斷和。頌云。
text_en: Wei said: How will this man's Dharma way be in later days? Yang said: In later days his Dharma way will greatly flourish in Wu and Yue; when it meets the wind it will stop. Wei also asked, Who will succeed him? Yang said: The time is far off and cannot yet be spoken of. Wei pressed him and said: I too wish to know. Yang said: Does not the scripture say, With this deep mind one serves lands as numerous as dust motes; this is called repaying the Buddha's kindness? The layman said: From this I know Fengxue was Yangshan's later body. Fengxue first studied under Xuefeng for five years. One day he asked about a case from Linji's assembly involving two head-seat monks who lifted their heads, looked at each other, and each gave a shout. A monk raised this and asked Linji, I do not know whether they possessed the eye of host and guest. Linji said: Though it is so, host and guest are clearly distinct. Xuefeng told this to Yantou and Qinshan. He set out on the road, but Linji had already passed away and he could not meet him. Then he said: If you want to understand, ask his descendants. Fengxue raised this to Nanyuan Yong. Nanyuan said: Xuefeng is an ancient Buddha. Later the master lived at Guanghui Chan Monastery on Fengxue Mountain in Ruzhou. Amid the disorder of the Five Dynasties, the governor of Yingzhou invited the master to spend the summer in the government office. One day the governor requested him to ascend the seat. He instructed the assembly, saying: The Patriarch's mind-seal is like an iron ox's mechanism. It is not like the mysterious chanting and subtle lifting of stone men and wooden horses. Directly it is like an iron ox: there is no place for you to draw near. The moment you go, it hooks and pulls you back; the moment you stay, it smashes you into a hundred mixed pieces. But if neither going nor staying, is sealing right, or not sealing right? This can be called bait on the hook's tip. Elder Lupi was also a descendant under Linji, so he turned the words around and posed a question, truly a striking one: I have the iron ox mechanism; I ask the master not to apply the seal. But Fengxue, standing on authority and acting, immediately said: Used to fishing for whales in the clear great deep, yet I lament a frog's gait in mud and sand. Whales and great fish cross the seas. In Zhuangzi, Prince Ren used fifty oxen as bait and once caught such a fish. Frog-gait in mud and sand: one explanation says that in Emperor Wu of Han's time there was an official of Baoli who, by the Wowa waters, saw a herd of wild horses, among them an extraordinary one coming to drink. So he made a clay man holding bridle and tether nearby. After the horses grew accustomed to it, he replaced it with a man and captured the horse. Wanting to make the horse seem miraculous, he claimed it came out of the water, and so it was passed down as a dragon breed. Fengxue means: the horse came from clear water yet instead sprawls in mud and sand. This explanation is roundabout. In Fengxue's collected sayings it is plainly written as frog-gait. Do you not see? After Xuedou had versified the rhinoceros fan story, he also said: If you want the clear wind to rise again and horns to regrow, I ask a Chan traveler below to give a turning word. Then he said: The fan is already broken; give me back my rhinoceros. At that time a monk came forth and said: Let the assembly go to the hall to practice. Xuedou shouted: Casting the hook to catch leviathans, you caught a shrimp! Using these two lines to match Fengxue's upper and lower lines, there is no doubt about the word frog. Lupi stood thinking; in the question he had presented his mechanism, wanting to meet Fengxue face to face; but he was suddenly marked and struck, so he sought another way out, trying a long thrust. But when he displayed his spear-technique, one roof-beam blow knocked him over. This was because he did not understand seizing the mechanism and issuing command, the fault of not being able to exchange host and guest. The governor had long studied with Fengxue, so it was not that he had no insight when he said, The Buddha-Dharma and the king's law are the same. Fengxue, having secured the south, still worried about the northern frontier, and so asked the governor, What have you seen? Right here it would have been good to redress Lupi's humiliation. But he only said, If one should cut off and does not cut off, it instead invites disorder. That too can stand as talk. Fengxue, because he was a secular official, swallowed his breath and voice and simply descended the seat. Two venerable adepts, one dragon and one snake, one hard and one soft, drummed out Linji's house style. Then add Tiantong's judgment and response. The verse says:
The iron ox mechanism seals and shatters the seal, passing through the crown of Vairocana, Has it roared yet or not? Hook and awl in hand.

text_zh: 鐵牛之機哮吼也未　印住印破鉤錐在手　透出毘盧頂𩕳 行將上不足却來化佛舌頭坐匹下有餘　風穴當衡世情看冷 暖盧陂負墮人面逐高低　棒頭喝下豈容分說　電光石火 不待消停歷歷分明珠在盤不撥自轉　眨起眉毛還蹉過 和聲便打
text_en: walking there. Raised up, it is not enough. Then returning, he sits on the tongue of the transformation Buddha; Fengxue stands at the balance-beam. Matched below, it is more than enough. Worldly feeling sees coldness and warmth. Lupi falls defeated; beneath the staff and shout are lightning and flint-sparks. People's faces follow high and low. How could it allow discrimination and explanation? Without waiting for it to settle. Clearly, distinctly, like pearls on a tray; blink and raise your brows, and you have already missed it. Without being stirred, it turns by itself. At the sound of agreement, strike at once.
The master said: The iron ox mechanism seals and shatters the seal. The Min king sent an envoy to deliver a vermilion credential.

text_zh: 師云。鐵牛之機。印住印破。閩王遣使送朱記 到。保福上堂曰。去則印住。住則印破。僧曰。 不去不住。用印奚為。保福打之。僧曰。恁麼則 山鬼窟裏全因今日也。保福默然。萬松道。可 惜龍頭蛇尾。風穴若不超證無住無依大解 脫門。不能透出毘盧頂𩕳行也。唐肅宗問忠 國師。如何是無諍三昧。國師云。檀越踏毘盧 頂上行。此明法身向上非枯椿邊事。風穴先 據此令。却來佛事門中。掌莫大威權。斷不了 公案。掃除凡聖情量。坐斷報化佛頭。臨際廣 語云。山僧見處。坐斷報化佛頂。恁麼當衡。直 饒盧陂作家亦有時負墮也。西天外道立義。 不成者謂之負墮。斬頭截臂。以謝不敏。此棒 頭喝下鈷鎚。電光石火機變。皆暫時光境。慎 勿以定奪得失決斷勝負。如珠走盤。眨眼蹉 過也。師以拂子擊禪床云。了。
text_en: When it arrived, Baofu ascended the hall and said: If you go, it seals you; if you stay, it shatters the seal. A monk said: If neither going nor staying, why use the seal? Baofu struck him. The monk said: If so, then ending up in the mountain ghost cave is entirely because of today. Baofu was silent. Wansong said: Alas, a dragon's head and a snake's tail. If Fengxue had not transcended and realized the great gate of liberation of no-abiding and no-reliance, he could not have passed through and walked upon Vairocana's crown. Emperor Suzong of Tang asked National Teacher Zhong: What is the samadhi of no-contention? The National Teacher said: Patron, tread upon Vairocana's crown and walk. This clarifies that beyond the dharma-body is not a matter of dead-tree stillness. Fengxue first stood on this command, then came back into the gate of Buddha-work, wielding immense authority, yet he could not finish off the case. Sweep away the calculations of ordinary and holy, sit cutting off the heads of reward and transformation Buddhas. In Linji's extensive sayings he says: As for this mountain monk's seeing, I sit cutting off the crowns of reward and transformation Buddhas. Standing at the balance like this, even if Lupi were a master, there would still be times he falls defeated. In India, non-Buddhist debaters set up doctrines; when they failed, it was called defeat and downfall. They cut off head or arm to apologize for their inadequacy. This staff and shout, this cudgel-hammer, these lightning-and-flint transformations of function, are all temporary scenes of light. Be careful not to judge gain and loss, decide victory and defeat by them. Like pearls rolling on a tray, in a blink you miss it. The master struck the Chan seat with the whisk and said: Finished.

text_zh: 示眾云。絕諸對待。坐斷兩頭。打破疑團。那消 一句。長安不離寸步。太山只重三斤。且道。據 甚麼令。敢恁麼道。
text_en: even one phrase? Chang'an is not a single inch away; Mount Tai weighs only three catties. Tell me then, by what command does one dare to speak this way?
Cited case: A monk asked Dasui, When the kalpa fire blazes and the great chiliocosm is all destroyed, I do not know

text_zh: 舉。僧問大隨。劫火洞然大。千俱壞。未審 這箇壞不壞愁人莫向愁人說隨云。壞早是那堪僧云。恁麼 則隨他去也目前可驗隨云。隨他去下坡不走更與一推僧問 龍濟。劫火洞然大千俱壞。未審這箇壞不 壞同病相憂濟云。不壞打破契頭捩轉鼻孔僧云。為甚不壞又恁 麼來濟云。為同大千生鐵鑄成。
text_en: whether this one is destroyed or not. Dasui said: Destroyed. The monk said: Then A sorrowful person should not speak to a sorrowful person. Already, how could it be borne? it goes along with it? Dasui said: It goes along with it. A monk asked It can be tested right before your eyes. Not walking downhill, so give another push. Longji, When the kalpa fire blazes and the great chiliocosm is all destroyed, I do not know whether this one is destroyed or not. Longji said: Not destroyed. The monk said: Why is it not destroyed? Longji said: Because it is the same as the great chiliocosm. Those with the same illness worry for each other. Smash the tally and twist the nostrils around. Again in this way. Cast from raw iron.
The master said: Chan Master Fazhen of Dasui in Yizhou—some say Xiyuan in Fuzhou, also

text_zh: 師云。益州大隨法真禪師。或云福州西院。亦 曰長慶。大安之子。百丈大智之孫。參見六十 餘員尊宿。在溈山會中。作火頭。溈問。子在此 數年。不解致箇問頭。隨云。教某甲問箇甚即 得。山云。爾不解問道如何是佛。隨以手掩溈 山口。山云。爾以後有片瓦蓋頭。覓箇掃地人 也無。後於棚口路。煎茶接待往來三年。開山 住大隨。僧問。劫火洞然大千俱壞。未審這箇 壞不壞。此問本出仁王護國經。斑足王信外 道羅陀語。取千王頭。淫祀塚間摩訶迦羅大 黑天神。冀延國祚。普明王請一日假。依七佛 法齋百法師。第一法師為王說偈。劫火洞然 大千俱壞。此偈凡三十二句。王赴死轉為諸 王說。斑足疑問。亦聞此偈心開悟解。以國付 弟出家得忍。據教中說。三千大千世界同一 成壞。漢武帝鑿昆明池。得灰問東方朔。朔曰。 請問西域道人。至後漢明帝。摩騰竺法蘭來。 問之曰劫灰也。雲庵問講師。火災起時世間 虛空。許多灰燼將置何處。罕有答者。止觀。羅 漢如炭。辟支如灰。菩薩如餘少灰。佛如劫火 無炭無灰。此問這箇壞不壞。佛果道。這僧元 來不知話頭落處。且道。這箇是甚麼。隨云。壞。 此語反常合道。極難咬嚼。僧云。恁麼則隨他 去也。這僧也好笑。不知執鞭墜鐙多少時也。 隨云。隨他去。萬松道。僧隨大隨去。大隨隨僧 去。雪竇與脩山主同時。未見脩山主答。後段 不壞為同大千話。單頌大隨話云。劫火光中 立問端。衲僧猶滯兩重關。這句人多錯會道。 大隨道壞是一重關。脩山主道不壞。是兩重 也。爾不看前話。單頌大隨。雪竇未見脩山主 語錄。但以問頭這箇壞不壞已是兩重關也。 可憐一句隨他語。萬里區區獨往還。此頌這 僧不會大隨語直往舒州。問投子。子云。西川 有古佛出世。汝速迴彼。僧迴隨已化。唐僧景 遵題云。了然無別法。唯道印南能。一句隨他 語。千山走衲僧。雪竇用此聯意。道頌後一聯 也。寒蛩嗚砌葉。靜夜禮龕燈。吟罷孤窓月。徘 徊恨不勝。天童頌古。更添脩山主話道不壞 為同大千。有本道。為他不同大千。這話最好 看。道同也得。不同也得。將錯就錯無可不可。 脩山主又云。壞也礙塞殺人。不壞也礙塞殺 人。萬松道。大隨道壞。也有出身處。脩山主 道不壞。也有出身處。不是一向無意度。不可 一向情識會。不見。江西志徹禪師。問六祖涅 盤經中常無常義。祖曰。無常者佛性也。有常 者善惡一切諸法分別心也。徹曰。經說佛性 是常。和尚却言無常。善惡諸法乃至菩提心 皆是無常。和尚却言是常。此即相違。令學人 轉生疑惑。祖曰。佛性若常。更說甚善惡諸法。 吾說無常。正是佛說真常之道也。又一切諸 法若無常者。則物物皆有自性。容受生死。而 真常性有不遍處。吾說常正是佛說真無常 義也。今時初心。見大隨道壞隨他去。未免䁝 惑。傍參六祖。可以無疑也。況大隨百丈親孫。 脩山主地藏嫡子。超情離見。曲為今時。雪竇 當時只頌一半。天童今日始得完全。頌云。
text_en: called Changqing—was a son of Da'an and a grandson in Dharma of Baizhang Dazhi. He studied with more than sixty venerable teachers. In Weishan's assembly he worked as cook. Wei asked: You have been here several years and cannot even bring forth a question. Dasui said: Tell me what to ask and then I will ask it. Wei said: Why don't you ask, What is Buddha? Dasui covered Weishan's mouth with his hand. Wei said: Later, when you have but a single roof tile over your head, you will not find even one person to sweep the ground. Later he stayed by the roadside at Pengkou, boiling tea and receiving travelers for three years, then opened a monastery and dwelt at Dasui. A monk asked: When the kalpa fire blazes and the great chiliocosm is all destroyed, I do not know whether this one is destroyed or not. This question originally comes from the Humane King Sutra for Protecting the Nation. King Spot-Foot believed the heterodox teacher Luotuo's words and took the heads of a thousand kings, making licentious sacrifices in graveyards to Mahakala, the great Black God, hoping to prolong his dynasty. King Puming asked for a one-day reprieve and, according to the Seven Buddhas' rite, arranged a feast for a hundred Dharma masters. The foremost Dharma master spoke a verse for the king: The kalpa fire blazes, the great chiliocosm is all destroyed. This verse has thirty-two lines in all. As the king went to his death he in turn recited it for the other kings. Spot-Foot, full of doubt, also heard this verse, and his mind opened in understanding and awakening. He entrusted the kingdom to his younger brother, left home, and attained forbearance. According to the teaching, the three-thousand great-thousand world system is one formation and destruction. Emperor Wu of Han dug Kunming Pool and found ashes, and asked Dongfang Shuo. Shuo said, Please ask a Daoist from the Western Regions. Later, in the Later Han under Emperor Ming, Matanga and Dharmaratna came. When asked, they said they were kalpa-ashes. Yun'an asked a lecturer, When the fire disaster arises and the world and empty space are burned, where are all those ashes to be placed? Few could answer. In Zhiguan it says: arhats are like charcoal; pratyekabuddhas are like ash; bodhisattvas are like a little remaining ash; a Buddha is like the kalpa-fire, with no charcoal and no ash. This question asks whether this thing is destroyed or not destroyed. Foguo said, This monk from the start did not know where the point of the saying landed. But tell me, what is this thing? Dasui said, Destroyed. This saying goes against the ordinary yet accords with the Way; it is extremely hard to chew through. The monk said, If so, then let it go along with it. This monk is laughable too; he does not know how long ago he had already dropped the whip and fallen from the stirrup. Dasui said, Let it go with it. Wansong said, The monk followed Dasui and went; Dasui followed the monk and went. Xuedou and Master Xiushan were contemporaries. He had not seen Master Xiushan's reply. In the later section, the saying not destroyed means the same as the great chiliocosm. He only praised Dasui's saying, saying: In the light of the kalpa-fire he sets up the point of questioning; patchrobed monks are still stuck at a double barrier. Many people wrongly understand this line, saying Dasui's destroyed is one barrier, and Master Xiushan's not destroyed is a second barrier. But if you look at the earlier case, he was only praising Dasui alone. Xuedou had not seen Master Xiushan's recorded sayings. The very wording of the question, this thing destroyed or not destroyed, is already two barriers. Pitiful, with one line let it go with it, he toiled alone for ten thousand li, going and returning. This praises that monk who did not understand Dasui's words and went straight to Shuzhou to ask Touzi. Touzi said, In Xichuan an ancient Buddha has appeared in the world; go back there quickly. The monk returned, but Dasui had already passed away. The Tang monk Jing Zun inscribed: Clearly there is no other Dharma; only Daoyin Nan was able. With one line let it go with it, he sent a patchrobed monk running across a thousand mountains. Xuedou used the sense of this couplet and then praised with another couplet: Cold crickets chirp among the stepside leaves; in the still night he bows before the shrine lamp. Chanting done, by the lonely window moon, he paces back and forth, regret beyond bearing. Tiantong, in praising the old case, further added Master Xiushan's saying not destroyed as the same as the great chiliocosm. Some editions read: because it is not the same as the great chiliocosm. This saying is best to examine. To say same is fine; to say not same is also fine. Following error with error, there is no yes and no. Master Xiushan also said, Destroyed too blocks and chokes people to death; not destroyed also blocks and chokes people to death. Wansong said, Dasui saying destroyed also has a way out; Master Xiushan saying not destroyed also has a way out. It is not something to be taken only as no meaning whatsoever, nor can it be understood solely through emotional consciousness. Have you not seen Chan Master Zhiche of Jiangxi ask the Sixth Patriarch about the Nirvana Sutra's meaning of permanence and impermanence? The Patriarch said, Impermanence is Buddha-nature; permanence is the discriminating mind regarding good and evil and all dharmas. Zhiche said, The sutra says Buddha-nature is permanent, yet you say impermanent. Good and evil dharmas and even the bodhi-mind are all impermanent, yet you say permanent. This is contradictory and causes students to give rise to doubts. The Patriarch said, If Buddha-nature were permanent, why speak further of good and evil dharmas? My saying impermanent is precisely the Buddha's teaching of true permanence. And if all dharmas were impermanent, then each thing would have a self-nature, capable of undergoing birth and death, and the truly permanent nature would fail to pervade everywhere. My saying permanent is exactly the Buddha's teaching of true impermanence in meaning. Beginners nowadays, seeing Dasui say destroyed, let it go with it, cannot avoid confusion. If they also consult the Sixth Patriarch, they can be free of doubt. Besides, Dasui is Baizhang's true grandson in the Dharma, and Master Xiushan is Dizang's direct son. They transcend feeling and leave views behind, yet bend themselves for people of this age. Xuedou at that time only praised half; Tiantong today finally makes it complete. The verse says:
Destroyed or not destroyed, let it go with it; the line of the great chiliocosm Even the Buddha's hand cannot pick it out. Turned about within the vein of speech of a measureless great man.

If there is no fixed is, then no thing is not is. Since no thing is not is, it is and yet no is. Since no thing is not fitting, it is fitting and yet no fitting. Therefore the sutra says: One fully sees all dharmas and yet there is nothing seen.
