The master said: When Huangbo first visited Baizhang, Baizhang said, Lofty and hall-like — what have you come for?

text_zh: 師云。黃蘗初參百丈。丈云。巍巍堂堂。來為何 事。蘗云。巍巍堂堂不為別事。巍堂磊落。皆大 丈夫相。干戈叢裡橫身直過。荊棘林中擺手 便行。脚跟下無五色線。舌頭上無十字關。鼻 端無泥痕。眼中無金屑。豈不是安樂快活底 漢。試將天童莫道著三字。換萬松四箇不字。 便見一字法門海墨書而不盡。德山道。一大 藏教。是拭不淨故紙。為已了者恐透牛皮也。 千年故紙中合藥者。為未了者不妨遮眼也。 慈覺道。圓覺楞嚴恒為已伴。況世尊入滅至 庚辰歲。已二千一百七十年。豈但千年故紙。 仙傳葛由能刻木羊。騎羊上綏山。後遇浮丘 公。曰。若不脚下線斷。爾也不得自由。暗合永 嘉放四大莫把捉。寂滅性中隨飲啄。諸行無 常一切空。即是如來大圓覺。雖然如是。猶欠 作云何梵在。
text_en: Huangbo said, Lofty and hall-like, I have not come for anything else. Lofty, hall-like, rugged, open — all are the marks of a great man. Amid spears and halberds he turns his body sideways and goes straight through; in a forest of thorns he swings his arms and simply walks on. Under his heels there is no five-colored line; on his tongue there is no crossbar gate. At the nose-tip there is no trace of mud; in the eyes no flecks of gold. Is he not a fellow at ease and delight, carefree and lively? Try taking Tiantong’s three words do not say it and swapping them for Wansong’s four nots. Then you will see that the gate of a single character cannot be exhausted even with ocean-ink writing. Deshan said, The whole treasury of teachings is merely old paper for wiping filth. For those already finished, I fear it would pierce even oxhide. As for compounding medicine in thousand-year-old paper, for those not yet finished, it does no harm to cover the eyes. Cijue said: The Perfect Enlightenment and Śūraṅgama are always my companions. Besides, from the World-Honored One’s passing until the gengchen year, it has already been 2,170 years. Why speak only of thousand-year-old paper? In immortals’ lore, Ge You could carve a wooden sheep and ride the sheep up Mount Sui. Later he met Fuqiu Gong, who said: If the line beneath your feet is not cut, you too cannot be free. It secretly accords with Yongjia’s Release the four great elements, do not clutch them. In the quiescent nature, follow drinking and pecking. All conditioned things are impermanent, all is empty — this is precisely the Tathāgata’s great perfect enlightenment. Though it is thus, still one phrase is lacking: How then is Brahmā present?

text_zh: 46 德山學畢
text_en: 46. Deshan Finished with Study Addressing the assembly, he said: For ten thousand miles not an inch of grass — the pure ground misleads people. In the eight directions not a scrap of cloud —

text_zh: 示眾云。萬里無寸草。淨地迷人。八方無片雲。 晴空賺汝。雖是以楔去楔。不妨拈空挂空。腦 後一槌。別看方便。
text_en: the clear sky deceives you. Though it is a wedge removing a wedge, still it does no harm to lift emptiness and hang emptiness. Behind the head, one hammer-blow — look at the expedient in another way.
He cited: Great Master Yuanming of Deshan addressed the assembly, saying, When all is exhausted, With this present,

text_zh: 舉。德山圓明大師。示眾云。及盡去也有這箇在 直得三世諸佛口掛壁上留取喫被猶有一人呵 呵大笑且道是誰若識此人是何面目參學事畢與椀茶喫。
text_en: such that the mouths of the Buddhas of the three times hang on the wall, still there is one person who goes ha-ha, keep it for eating when hungry. laughing loudly. If you recognize this person, the matter of study is finished. Tell me, who is it? What face is it? Give him a bowl of tea to drink.
The master said: Yuanming of Deshan in Dingzhou was the ninth-generation master there, personal name Yuanmi. Among Yunmen’s

text_zh: 師云。鼎州德山第九世圓明大師。諱緣密。雲 門嗣中唯師傳嗣最廣。師創三句。函蓋乾坤。 截斷眾流。隨波逐浪。今傳為雲門三句者。檢 討不審也。一日示眾云。及盡去也。直得三世 諸佛口掛壁上。此言廣長舌相話會不及。猶 有一人呵呵大笑。且道。是何人笑箇甚麼。若 識得此人。參學事畢。是真箇更有事在。投子 青和尚拈云。藏盡楚天月。猶存漢地星。萬松 道。車也去了。藉甚油缸。此可與竿頭進步者 道。寶峯照和尚道。直須如大死底人死了更 死。僧云。莫是死中却活麼。師云。爾且死莫 活。爾但喫飯裏急自去屙屎。爾飯也未喫。早 問屙屎作麼。此乃貴大休大歇親到自證。說 得一丈。不如行取一尺也。只如行不得處作 麼生說。問取天童。頌云。
text_en: heirs, only this master’s line spread most widely. The master created the three phrases: covering heaven and earth, cutting off all streams, following waves and chasing swells. What is now transmitted as the Three Phrases of Yunmen — on examination, is not exact. One day he addressed the assembly, saying: When all is exhausted, to the point that the Buddhas of the three times have their mouths hanging on the wall — this means even the broad-long tongue-mark cannot reach it in speech. Still there is one person laughing ha-ha. Tell me, who is this person, and what is he laughing at? If you recognize this person, the matter of study is finished. Truly, there is yet another matter present. Touzi Qing master commented: Though the moon in Chu skies is hidden away, stars still remain in Han lands. Wansong said: The cart is already gone — what use is the axle-grease jar? This may be said to one who advances atop a hundred-foot pole. Baofeng Zhao said: You must be like one greatly dead — having died, die again. A monk asked, Could it be coming alive again in death? The master said, For now, you just die — do not come alive. You ought first to eat your meal and then hurry off to shit. You have not even eaten yet, and already you ask about shitting — what for? This values great rest and great cessation, personally arrived at and self-verified. To speak a full ten feet is not as good as practicing one foot. But when it comes to where one cannot act, how do you speak of it? Ask Tiantong. The verse says:
Gather it in and cut off the throat; wind polishes, clouds wipe — the waters are cold, Where will you put it? Just right for turning around and breathing out. Even the finest dust must go.

text_zh: 收向甚處著　把斷襟喉正好轉身吐氣也　風磨雲拭纖塵必去　水冷 天秋打成一片錦鱗莫謂無嗞味腥羶不少　釣盡滄浪 月一鉤不犯清波意自殊
text_en: and the sky is autumn. Beat it into one piece. Do not say the brocade-scaled fish has no savor — hook away the blue waves, There is no lack of stench. one moon-hook. Without troubling the clear waves, the meaning is naturally distinct.
The master said: Yuanming’s address did not need much; Tiantong adds a single gather, and with Yuanming

text_zh: 師云。圓明示眾不消。天童下箇收字。和圓明。 盛在布袋裏也。思大云。三世諸佛被我一口 吞盡。何處更有眾生可度。此水洩不通。凡聖 路絕也。正恁麼時。盡空法界。如一面古鏡用 壞劫毘嵐風。磨瑩成劫金藏雲揩拭。水天一 色。雲月交光。皆取純清絕點邊事。這裏言淡 而無味。如月鉤雲餌。魚龍無可吞噉。成湯祝 網從君意。呂望垂鉤信我緣。不見道。山田脫 粟飯野菜。淡黃韲。喫則從君喫。不喫任東西。
text_en: packs it all into a cloth sack. Si Da said: The Buddhas of the three times are swallowed by me in one gulp. Once all are swallowed, where are there any beings left to save? Here the water cannot leak through; the road of ordinary and sage is cut off. Right at such a time, the whole empty Dharma-realm is like an ancient mirror, using the kalpa-destroying Vairambha wind to polish it bright, and the kalpa-forming golden-store clouds to wipe it clean. Water and sky become one color; cloud and moon interweave their light. All of this takes up the utterly pure matter beyond any speck. Here the words are bland and without flavor, like a moon-hook and cloud-bait; fish and dragons have nothing to swallow. King Cheng Tang’s prayer over the net said, Let it go according to your will. Lü Wang hanging his hook trusted my affinity. Have you not heard: On mountain fields, husked millet rice and wild greens, pale yellow pickles — if you eat, then eat as you wish; if you do not, go whichever way you please.

text_zh: 47 趙州柏樹
text_en: 47. Zhaozhou’s Cypress Tree Addressing the assembly, he said: The cypress tree in the courtyard, the wind-banner on the pole — like one flower speaking boundless

text_zh: 示眾云。庭前柏樹。竿上風幡。如一華說無邊 春。如一滴說大海水。間生古佛。逈出常流。不 落言思。若為話會。
text_en: spring, like one drop speaking the waters of the great sea. A primordial Buddha born among men, far beyond the common stream, not falling into words or thought — how will you meet it in speech?
He cited: A monk asked Zhaozhou, What is the Patriarch’s meaning in coming from the West? Zhou Doluo fusses idly.

text_zh: 舉。僧問趙州。如何是祖師西來意多羅閑管州 云。庭前柏樹子焦塼打著連底凍。
text_en: said, The cypress tree in the courtyard. Struck by a burnt brick, frozen through to the bottom.
The master cited: One day Zhaozhou ascended the hall and said, In this matter, people of truly great capacity beyond measure

text_zh: 師舉。趙州一日。上堂云。此事的的沒量大人。 出這裏不得。老僧到溈山。僧問。如何是祖師 西來意。溈云。與我將床子來。若是宗師。須以 本分事接人始得。僧便問。如何是祖師西來 意。州云。庭前柏樹子。僧云。和尚莫將境示 人。師云。不將境示人。僧云。然則如何是祖師 西來意。師云。庭前柏樹子。楊州城東光孝寺。 慧覺禪師。到法眼處。眼問。近難何處。覺曰。 趙州。眼曰。承聞趙州有柏樹子話是否。覺曰。 無。眼曰。往來皆謂。僧問如何是祖師西來意。 州曰。庭前柏樹子。上座何得道無。覺曰。先師 實無此語。和尚莫謗先師好。諸方名為覺鐵 嘴。勝默和尚。必須教人先過此話淘汰知見。 甞曰。三玄五位。盡在其中。真如方禪師悟此 話。直入方丈。見瑯琊廣照覺禪師。照問。汝作 麼生會。如曰。夜來床薦煖。一覺到天明。廣照 可之。真如悟得此話最好。天童頌得此話亦 不惡。頌云。
text_en: cannot get out of here. When this old monk was at Weishan, a monk asked, What is the Patriarch’s meaning in coming from the West? Wei said, Bring me the bench. If one is a true lineage teacher, one must use one’s proper matter to receive people. Then the monk asked, What is the Patriarch’s meaning in coming from the West? Zhou said, The cypress tree in the courtyard. The monk said, Master, do not use objects to show people. The master said, I do not use objects to show people. The monk said, Then what is the Patriarch’s meaning in coming from the West? The master said, The cypress tree in the courtyard. At Guangxiao Monastery east of Yangzhou city, Chan Master Huijue went to Fayan. Fayan asked, Where have you come from lately? Jue said, Zhaozhou. Fayan said, I have heard Zhaozhou has a cypress-tree saying — is it so? Jue said, No. Fayan said, Everyone coming and going says that when a monk asked the Patriarch’s meaning in coming from the West, Zhou said, The cypress tree in the courtyard. How can you, Reverend, say there is none? Jue said, My former teacher truly had no such saying. Master, please do not slander my former teacher. Monasteries everywhere called him Jue Iron- Beak. Shengmo always had to make people first pass through this saying to wash out their views and knowledge. He once said, The Three Mysteries and Five Ranks are all within it. Chan Master Zhenru Fang awakened to this saying and went straight into the abbot’s room to see Chan Master Guangzhao Jue of Langya. Zhao asked, How do you understand it? Fang said, Last night the bed mat was warm; in one sleep I reached dawn. Guangzhao approved him. Zhenru understood this saying best; Tiantong’s verse on this saying is also not bad. The verse says:
Bank-brows cross with snow, river-eyes contain autumn, a sea-mouth beats up waves; He has eaten more salt than rice. A single point is hard to conceal. There is a phrase,

text_zh: 岸眉橫雪喫鹽多如喫米　河目含秋一點難謾　海口鼓浪有句 非宗旨航舌駕流無言絕聖凡　撥亂之手也是柏樹　太平之 籌也是柏樹老趙州老趙州為甚不應　攪攪叢林卒未休 天童第二徒費工夫也造車合轍將來使用恰好　本無伎倆 也塞壑填溝買盡風流不著錢
text_en: but it is not the school’s meaning. a boat-tongue rides the current; the hand that quells disorder, the strategy of great peace — No words, and saints and ordinary are cut off. It is also the cypress tree. the plan. It is also the cypress tree. Old Zhaozhou, old Zhaozhou — stirring and churning the Chan groves, never yet at rest. Why does it not answer? Tiantong, second Mere wasted effort! Yet building the cart to fit the ruts is originally no special skill; Bring it forth for use, just right it too is filling ravines and stuffing ditches. Buy up all elegance without spending a coin
The master said: Seven hundred sexagenary cycles — he has seen many things. Therefore bank-brows crossed with snow. The ancients

text_zh: 師云。七百甲子。經事多矣。所以岸眉橫雪。古 人以眉目為巖電。天童用河眸海口故事。成 四句偈。如見活趙州指柏樹子相似。眉如蘆 花岸。眼如秋水碧。古句野水淨於僧眼碧。遠 山濃似佛頭青。海口鼓浪。航舌駕流。浪即能 覆航。航即能駕浪。一言可以興邦。一言可以 喪邦。故次之。以撥亂之手。太平之籌。州甞 云。有時將一莖草。作丈六金身。用有時將丈 六金身。作一莖草。用此話本與人決疑。而今 多少人疑著。趙州豈欲攪叢林哉。人見趙州 答話應聲便對。如不假功用。唯天童知八十 行脚。三歲孩童勝如我。我從他學。此乃閑時 造下。忙時用著。不是苦辛人。不知臥輪有伎 倆。能斷百思想。對境心不起。菩提日日長。六 祖道。慧能無伎倆。不斷百思想。對境心數起。 菩提作麼長。恁麼看來塞壑填溝底事。又作 麼生。如今拋擲西湖裏。下載清風付與誰。
text_en: took brows and eyes as cliff and lightning. Tiantong uses the old image of river-pupils and sea-mouth to form a four-line verse, as if seeing living Zhaozhou pointing to the cypress tree. Brows like reed- flower banks; eyes like autumn waters, blue. An old verse says, Wild waters are clearer than the blue of a monk’s eyes; distant mountains are deeper than the green of a Buddha’s head. Sea-mouth beating waves, boat-tongue riding currents — waves can overturn a boat, and a boat can ride waves. One word can raise a state; one word can ruin a state. Therefore he follows with the hand that quells disorder and the plan of peace. Zhou once said, Sometimes I use one blade of grass as a sixteen-foot golden body; sometimes I use the sixteen-foot golden body as one blade of grass. This saying was originally to settle people’s doubts, but now how many people are stuck in doubt over it. Did Zhaozhou wish to stir up the Chan groves? People see Zhaozhou answer on the spot, responding the instant the question sounds, as if it required no effort. Only Tiantong knew that eighty years of pilgrimage means even a three-year-old child surpasses me, and I learn from him. This is what one fashions in idle times, to use when busy. If one has not endured hardship, one does not know Wolun’s trickery: He can cut off a hundred thoughts; facing conditions, the mind does not arise; bodhi grows day by day. The Sixth Patriarch said, Huineng has no tricks: he does not cut off a hundred thoughts; facing conditions, the mind repeatedly arises. How could bodhi grow? Seen this way, the business of filling ravines and stuffing ditches — then how is it? Now tossed into West Lake, below it the clear wind — to whom shall it be entrusted?

text_zh: 48 摩經不二
text_en: 48. Vimalakīrti Sutra on Nonduality Addressing the assembly, he said: Wondrous function has no fixed way; there are places where one cannot lay a hand. Eloquence is unhindered,

text_zh: 示眾云。妙用無方。有下手不得處。辯才無礙。 有開口不得時。龍牙如無手人行拳。夾山教 無舌人解語。半路抽身底是甚麼人。
text_en: yet there are times when one cannot open the mouth. Longya was like a man without hands throwing punches; Jiashan taught a tongueless man to speak. Who is the one who withdraws halfway along the road?
Raised: Vimalakirti asked Manjushri, What is a bodhisattva's entry into the gate of nonduality?

text_zh: 舉。維摩詰問文殊師利。何等是菩薩入不 二法門問處第幾文殊師利曰好與劈口𡎺如我意者醞造 將來於一切法更嫌少無言無說把火照看無示無識有也 來離諸問答面皮厚多少是為入不二法門如何是 於是文殊師利問維摩詰言。我等各自說 已能說快說仁者當說。何等是菩薩入不二法門 一遞一刮不賭惡發維摩默然甚麼處去也。
text_en: Manjushri said, As I see it: in regard to all dharmas, no words, no explanation, no indication, no knowing, apart from all questioning and answering — this is entry into the gate of nonduality. At the point of questioning, which rank Best to strike straight at the mouth Brewed Bring it forth Still think it too little Tend the fire and watch There is Come How thick is your hide What is Thereupon Manjushri asked Vimalakirti, saying: We have each spoken already; benevolent one, now you should speak. What is a bodhisattva's entry into the gate of nonduality? If you can speak, speak quickly Vimalakirti remained silent. One pass, one scrape, not fearing a foul flare-up Where are you going
The master said: In Sanskrit, Vimalakirti; here it is rendered Stainless Fame, also called Pure Name. His wife

text_zh: 師云。梵語維摩詰。此云無垢稱。亦曰淨名。妻 名金姬。子名善思。女名月上。僧問雲居簡和 尚。維摩是金粟如來。為甚麼却預釋迦會下 聽法。居云。他不爭人我。廣本維摩經。三萬二 千菩薩。各說不二法門。今唯三十二菩薩。末 後文殊無卓錐之地。維摩錐也無。保福展云。 文殊也似掩耳偷鈴。力盡烏江。維摩一默。未 出化門。萬松道。人出是非難。又云。大小維 摩。被文殊一坐。至今起不得。萬松道。要起有 甚難便掌。瑯琊覺云。文殊恁麼讚善也是。杓 卜聽虛聲。維摩默然。爾等諸人。不得鑽龜打 瓦。萬松道。杜撰不少。唯雪竇於文殊問罷處。 不言默然良久據座。直云維摩道甚麼。復云。 勘破了也。萬松道。不解作鬼。白日現身。天依 懷頌。維摩不默不良久。據坐商量成過咎。至 今諸方見呈似此事。猶曰良久云。有僧問一 師。錄中多云良久者。良久乃何人也。答云。良 久乃梁八之弟也。傳者以為笑。天依後兩句。 忒曬峭拔。道吹毛匣裏冷光生。外道天魔皆 斬首。萬松道。暗度神鋒。不覺痛痒。白雲端頌 云。一箇兩箇百千萬。屈指尋文數不辦。暫時 留在暗窓前。明日與君重計算。萬松道。有甚 閑功夫。天童頌馬祖藏頭白海頭黑話。末後 道。堂堂坐斷舌頭路。應笑毘耶老古錐。今日 維摩來也。不管面譽。頌云。
text_en: was named Golden Lady; his son, Good Thought; his daughter, Moon Above. A monk asked Yunju Jian: Vimalakirti is the Tathagata Golden Millet — why then did he still join Shakyamuni's assembly to hear the Dharma? Ju said: He did not contend over self and others. In the expanded Vimalakirti Sutra, thirty-two thousand bodhisattvas each expound the gate of nonduality. Here there are only thirty-two bodhisattvas. At the end, Manjushri has nowhere to stick an awl; Vimalakirti has no awl either. Baofu Zhan said: Manjushri too is like covering his ears while stealing a bell; his strength exhausted at Wu River. Vimalakirti's single silence still had not gone beyond the gate of expedients. Wansong said: It is hard for people to get out of right and wrong. He also said: Big or little Vimalakirti, once seated by Manjushri, to this day cannot rise. Wansong said: If he wants to get up, what is so hard? Just a slap. Langya Jue said: Manjushri's praise like that is just ladling divination and listening for empty sounds. Vimalakirti was silent. All of you people, do not drill the turtle and strike the tile. Wansong said: There is no shortage of made-up talk. Only Xuedou, at the point where Manjushri finished asking, did not say "silent for a long while, seated in place"; he directly said, What did Vimalakirti say? Then again he said: Exposed and broken through! Wansong said: He does not know how to play ghost; he appears in broad daylight. Tianyi Huai versified: Vimalakirti was not silent, nor was it a long while; sitting there discussing becomes fault and blame. To this day in all quarters, when people present this matter, they still say, "After a long while..." A monk asked a certain master: In the records they often say "a long while" — who is this "Long While"? He answered: "Long While" is Liang Ba's younger brother. Those who transmitted it took it as a joke. Tianyi's last two lines are extremely steep and sharp: he said, In the case of the hair-blowing sword, cold light is born in the box; outsiders and heavenly demons are all beheaded. Wansong said: The divine blade passes in secret; one does not feel pain or itch. Baiyun Duan's verse says: One, two, hundreds, thousands, ten-thousands — bending the fingers to seek the wording, you cannot finish counting. For now, leave it before the dark window; tomorrow I will reckon it again with you. Wansong said: What idle effort! Tiantong, in his verse, uses Mazu's "head white, sea-head black" talk, and at the end says: Majestically seated, he cuts off the road of tongues; he should laugh at old Vimalakirti of Vaisali. Today Vimalakirti has come — no concern for face-to-face praise. The verse says:
Manjusri asks about illness; old Vaisali. The gate of nonduality opens — watch the adept. In the way of benevolence and righteousness In the patchrobed monk's portion

text_zh: 曼殊問疾老毘耶仁義道中　不二門開看作家衲僧分上 珉表粹中誰賞鑒大辯若訥　忘前失後莫咨嗟大智 若愚區區投璞兮楚庭臏士獻直得曲　璨璨報珠兮 隋城斷蛇夜光投人鮮不按劍休點破幸自完全　絕玼瑕一任指點　俗 氣渾無却較些相上觀人失之多矣
text_en: Coarse stone outside, pure jade within — who can appreciate it? Forget what is before, lose what is after; do not sigh. Great eloquence seems slow of speech Great wisdom Seems foolish Earnestly presenting the uncut jade — in the Chu court the man is maimed; glitteringly repaying with a pearl — Present straight and get back crooked in Sui city, the severed snake. Cast a night-shining jewel before men and few will not grasp their swords Do not point it out and break it — cut off blemish and flaw, the worldly Luckily still whole Let them point and judge as they please air is wholly absent, yet still there is a little to compare. Looking at people by appearances misses by a lot
The master said: Wenshushili and Manshushili are just different Chinese renderings of the Sanskrit sound. Here it is rendered

text_zh: 師云。文殊師利。曼殊室利。梵音楚夏也。此云 妙吉祥。毘耶離廣嚴城名。肇公涅盤無名論。 釋迦掩室於摩竭。淨名杜口於毘耶。須菩提 唱無說。以顯道。釋梵絕聽而雨華。斯皆理為 神御故口。以之默。豈曰無辯。辯所不能言也。 燕珉次玉者。今𣵠郡靠水石也。亦名奪玉石。 維摩外雖似訥。其不言之辯。精粹其中。言其 石隱玉也。忘前失後者。永嘉集奢摩他頌。第 四云。今言知者。不須知知。但知而已。則前 不接滅。後不引起。前後斷續中間自孤。無盡 燈末。未詳法嗣中。有開封府夷門山廣智禪 師。諱本嵩。別無語緣。全舉此段。文公不知出 永嘉集。謂嵩創設。因辨之於此。學者知之。此 箇忘前失後。正是三祖信心銘。言語道斷。非 去來今也。韓子卞和於荊山崐岡谷得璞。獻 楚厲王。王曰。石也遣刖一足。及武王即位又 獻之。又刖一足。至文王立。和抱璞哭於荊山 之下。王召問。和曰。不怨刖足。而怨真玉以為 凡石。忠事以為慢事。王使剖石乃真玉也。文 王歎曰。哀哉二先君。易刖人足。難剖於石。今 果是璧乃國寶也。史記隨侯祝元暢。因之齊。 見一斷蛇將死。遂以水洗摩之。傅之神樂而 去。忽一夜中庭現光。意謂有賊。遂按劍視之。 乃見一蛇𭊷珠在地而往。知蛇感報也。維摩 橫身為眾。不免禍出私門。那堪文殊點破已 靈瑕玼。直饒天童道現居俗塵而無俗氣。也 是掩鼻偷香。
text_en: Wonderful Auspiciousness. Vairali is the name of the city Vast Adornment. In Sengzhao's Treatise on Nameless Nirvana: Shakyamuni closed his chamber in Magadha; Pure Name shut his mouth in Vaisali. Subhuti proclaimed no-speaking to reveal the Way. Indra and Brahma ceased listening and flowers rained down. In all these, principle acted as the spirit's charioteer, so the mouth was silent. How could this be called lack of eloquence? It is eloquence speaking what cannot be spoken. The Yan stone that is next to jade is a local riverside stone now; it is also called jade-seizing stone. Though Vimalakirti outwardly seemed tongue-tied, the eloquence of his not speaking was refined essence within. This is called stone concealing jade. As for forgetting what is before and losing what is after: in Yongjia's Collection, in the Shamatha Verse, the fourth says: When we now speak of knowing, there is no need to know knowing; just know, that is all. Then the former does not connect to cessation, and the later does not draw up arising. Before and after are cut off; the middle stands alone. In the Ending of the Unending Lamp, in the section on unclear Dharma heirs, there is Chan Master Guangzhi of Yimen Mountain in Kaifeng Prefecture, whose taboo name was Bensong. There are no other recorded sayings; this whole passage is quoted. Lord Wen did not know it came from Yongjia's Collection and thought Song had originated it, so I clarify it here, that students may know. This forgetting what is before and losing what is after is exactly the Third Patriarch's Faith in Mind: the path of words is cut off, not past, coming, or present. Hanzi says Bian He found an uncut jade in the valleys of Jing Mountain and Kun Ridge, and presented it to King Li of Chu. The king said, It is a stone, and had one foot cut off. When King Wu took the throne he again presented it, and again had one foot cut off. When King Wen ascended, He embraced the jade and wept at the foot of Jing Mountain. The king summoned and asked him. He said: I do not resent the cutting off of my feet; I resent that true jade was taken for common stone, and loyal service was taken as insolence. The king had the stone cut open, and it was indeed true jade. King Wen sighed: Alas, my two former lords — easy to cut off a man's feet, hard to split a stone. Now it truly is a jade disk, a national treasure. In the Records, Sui Marquis Zhu Yuanchang, traveling to Qi, saw a severed snake about to die, so he washed and rubbed it with water, applied divine medicine to it, and left. Suddenly one night a light appeared in the courtyard; he thought there were thieves, so he pressed his sword and looked. Then he saw a snake pearl on the ground, and the snake departed. He knew it was the snake repaying kindness. Vimalakirti threw himself across for the sake of the multitude, yet could not avoid trouble coming from his own gate. How could he bear Manjushri pointing it out and exposing the spiritual flaw and blemish? Even if Tiantong says he appeared dwelling in worldly dust yet without worldly taint, still it is covering the nose while stealing fragrance.

text_zh: 49 洞山供真
text_en: 49. Dongshan Makes an Offering to the Portrait Addressing the assembly, he said: It cannot be sketched, it cannot be painted. Puhua then turns a somersault. Longya

text_zh: 示眾云。描不成畫不就。普化便翻斤斗。龍牙 只露半身。畢竟那人是何體段。
text_en: only reveals half his body. After all, what kind of person is that?
Raised: While Dongshan was making offerings to Yunyan's portrait, he then brought up the earlier story of asking about the true likeness. Who says it is false

text_zh: 舉。洞山供養雲巖真次誰道是假遂舉前邈真話 一迴拈出一迴新有僧問。雲巖道祇這是。意旨如何且喜 不錯認山云。我當時幾錯會先師意以己方人僧云。 未審雲巖還知有也無折草量天山云。若不知有。 爭解恁麼道日出連山若知有爭肯恁麼道月圓當戶。
text_en: A monk asked: Yunyan said, Just this is it — what was the meaning? Dongshan said: At that time I almost misunderstood my late teacher's meaning. The monk said: Each time it is brought up, each time it is new For now, rejoice Do not mistake it Measure others by yourself I do not know whether Yunyan knew there is this or not. Dongshan said: If he did not know there is, Bend grass to measure the sky how could he speak thus? If he knew there is, how could he consent to speak thus? The sun rises over connected mountains The full moon faces the door
The master said: When Dongshan took leave of Yunyan, he asked: After the master's passing, if someone asks

text_zh: 師云。洞山辭雲巖。山問。和尚百年後。人問還 邈得師真否。如何祇對。巖良久云。祇這是。山 沈吟。巖云。价闍梨。承當這箇大事。直須子細。 山亦不言便行。後因過水覩影。方始悟徹。乃 作頌曰。切忌從他覓。迢迢與我疎。我今獨自 往。處處得逢渠。渠今正是我。我今不是渠。應 須恁麼會方得契如如。山在眾。供養雲巖真。 舉前邈真話了。僧問雲巖。道祇這是意旨如 何。山曰。我當時幾錯會先師意。若向良久祇 這是處領略。正是替名通事。所以見影知形。 過水方悟。僧曰。未審雲巖知有也無。若道一 向知有。是左右人。不見道。知有底人始解奉 重。若道一向不知有。這裏有利害。有全不知 有有知有了却不知有有不知有去成知有山 云若不知有。爭解恁麼道。若知有爭肯恁麼 道。華嚴宗謂理圓言偏言生理喪。此乃重玄 復妙。兼帶叶通。不偏枯。無滲漏底血脈也。山 於唐大中末。初住新豐百吉。後遷豫章高安 之洞山。為第一代。因為雲巖作忌齋。僧問。師 於先師處得何指示。山曰。雖在彼中。不蒙他 指示。僧曰。又用設齋作麼。山曰。雖然如是。 焉敢違背。僧曰。和尚發跡南泉。為甚却與雲 巖設齋。山曰。我不重先師道德佛法。只重他 不為我說破。僧曰。和尚嗣先師。還肯他也無。 山曰。半肯半不肯。僧曰。為甚麼不全肯。山曰。 我若全肯。則辜負先師。萬松道。雲巖二十年。 在百丈。却嗣藥山。洞山發跡南泉。却嗣雲巖。 一等異苗翻茂。密固靈根。得芙蓉而宗派中 興。至天童而文彩方備。那箇是具文彩。頌云。
text_en: whether they can portray the master's true likeness, how should I answer? Yunyan paused a long while and said: Just this is it. Dongshan sank into thought. Yunyan said: Acarya Jie, in undertaking this great matter, you must be very careful. Dongshan also said nothing and simply left. Later, when crossing water and seeing his reflection, only then did he fully awaken. Then he composed a verse: Most taboo is seeking from another; far, far it grows distant from me. I now alone go on, and everywhere I meet him. He is now precisely me; I now am not he. One must understand it in this way to accord with Thusness. When Dongshan was in the assembly making offerings to Yunyan's portrait, after bringing up the earlier story of the true likeness, a monk asked about Yunyan's saying "Just this is it" and its meaning. Dongshan said: At that time I almost misunderstood my late teacher's meaning. If one grasps it at "after a long while" and "just this is it," that is merely passing along the title and official wording. Therefore he saw the reflection and knew the form; crossing the water, only then he awakened. The monk said: I do not know whether Yunyan knew there is this or not. If one says he always knew, that is just an attendant at his side. Did you not hear it said: only one who knows there is can begin to know how to revere it? If one says he completely did not know, there is danger here: there is complete not-knowing-there-is, there is knowing-there-is and then yet not knowing-there-is, and there is going from not-knowing-there-is to becoming knowing-there-is. Dongshan said: If he did not know there is, how could he speak thus? If he knew there is, how could he consent to speak thus? In the Huayan school it is said: principle is complete, words are partial; once words arise, principle is lost. This is layered mystery upon further wonder, carrying both and harmonizing through, not one-sided and dry — a bloodline without leakage. Dongshan at the end of Tang Dazhong first dwelt at Baiji in Xinfeng, and later moved to Dongshan in Gao'an of Yuzhang, becoming the first generation there. Because he held a memorial feast for Yunyan, a monk asked: Master, what instruction did you receive from your former teacher? Dongshan said: Though I was among him, I did not receive his instruction. The monk said: Then why hold a memorial feast? Dongshan said: Even so, how dare I go against him? The monk said: You began your career under Nanquan; why then do you instead hold the feast for Yun- yan? Dongshan said: I do not esteem my former teacher's virtue or Buddha-Dharma; I only esteem that he did not explain it fully for me. The monk said: You inherited your former teacher — do you approve of him or not? Dongshan said: Half approve, half do not. The monk said: Why not fully approve? Dongshan said: If I fully approved, I would betray my former teacher. Wansong said: Yunyan spent twenty years with Baizhang, yet inherited Yaoshan. Dongshan began under Nanquan, yet inherited Yunyan. From one kind, different shoots turn luxuriant; the numinous root is dense and firm. With Furong, the lineage in the school flourished; by Tiantong, literary brilliance was fully prepared. Which one is furnished with literary brilliance? The verse says:
How could he speak thus? At fifth watch the cock crows; the home woods dawn. How could he In the dark, pull out the crossbone The golden crow rises in the east

text_zh: 爭解恁麼道暗裏抽橫骨　五更鷄唱家林曉金烏東上　爭 肯恁麼道明中坐舌頭千年鶴與雲松老玉兔西沈　寶鑑 澄明驗正偏事窮的要玉機轉側看兼到交互明中暗　門 風大振兮規步綿綿西天令嚴父子變通兮聲光 浩浩見過於師方堪傳授
text_en: consent to speak thus? In brightness, sit on the tongue The thousand-year crane and the cloud-pines grow old; the jeweled mirror The jade rabbit sinks in the west clear and bright tests the upright and the partial. When the matter is exhausted, hit the vital point The jade loom turns and shifts — see the gate of reaching both together. Mutual interchange, dark within the bright The house style greatly flourishes; measured steps continue unbroken. The order from the Western Heaven is strict Father and son adapt and transform; sound and light vast and vast. Only when one surpasses the teacher is one fit to receive transmission
The master said: Dongshan instructed Caoshan, saying: From my former teacher Yunyan I personally received the seal of the Precious

text_zh: 師云。洞山囑曹山云。吾於雲巖先師。親印寶 鏡三昧。事窮的要。今付授汝。汝善護持。寶鑑 澄明驗正偏。豈非鷄唱家林。鶴老雲松。正偏 之驗耶。鏡雖明而有背面。唯玉機轉側遞相 綺。互雙明雙暗兼到之方也。易繫辭曰。道窮 則變。變則通。通則久。洞山父子規行矩步。至 今門風大振者。源深流長之效歟。
text_en: Mirror Samadhi. The matter reaches its essential point. Now I transmit it to you; guard and uphold it well. The jeweled mirror clear and bright tests upright and partial — is this not the cock crowing in the home woods, the crane old among cloud-pines, the verification of upright and partial? Though the mirror is bright, it still has front and back. Only when the jade loom turns and shifts, mutually interweaving, is there the method of mutual double brightness and double darkness, reaching both together. The Appended Phrases of the Yi says: When the way is exhausted, then it changes; changing, it penetrates; penetrating, it endures. Dongshan and his descendants walked by rule and measured step, and to this day the house style greatly flourishes — is this not the effect of a deep source and long current?

text_zh: 50 雪峯甚麼
text_en: 50. Xuefeng's What Addressing the assembly, he said: The final phrase is what first reaches the impregnable barrier. Yantou, trusting himself, above did not

text_zh: 示眾云。末後一句。始到牢關。巖頭自負。上不 肯於親師。下不讓於法弟。為復是強生節目。 為復別有機關。
text_en: yield to his own teacher, below he did not defer to his Dharma brother. Was this merely forcing out complications, or was there another mechanism?
Raised: When Xuefeng was living in a hermitage, two monks came to pay respects. Xuefeng, seeing them Seeking scent, chasing traces

text_zh: 舉。雪峯住庵時。有兩僧來禮拜尋香逐氣峯見 來以手托庵門。放身出云。是甚麼此猶是拋身勢隱身 勢作麼生僧亦云。是甚麼果然不識峯低頭歸庵莫道無語好 僧後到巖頭傳消寄息頭問。甚麼處來不鑽不穴僧云。 嶺南這裏是嶺北頭云。曾到雪峯麼熟處難忘。僧云。 曾到更諱不得頭云。有何言句不醋不休僧舉前話一字入公 門八牛拽不出頭云。他道甚麼却好低頭便出僧云。他無語。低 頭歸庵恁麼則不曾到雪峯頭云。噫當時不向他道末 後句而今道了未若向伊道。天下人不奈雪老何 何不道我便是雪老僧至夏末。再舉前話請益好酒醒人遲頭 云。何不早問貪瞌睡僧云。未敢容易可曬慣叢林頭 云。雪峯雖與我同條生。不與我同條死 索另者先窮要知末後句只這是旋蒸熱賣。
text_en: come, braced the hermitage door with his hand, leaned out, and said: What is this? The monks also said: What is this? Xuefeng lowered his head and returned to the hermitage. This is still the posture of casting off the body and hiding the body What is the posture then Sure enough, you do not recognize it Do not say silence is good Later the monks went to Yantou. Yantou asked: Where do you come from? The monks said: Passing news and sending word No drilling, no boring through From Lingnan. Yantou said: Did you visit Xuefeng? The monks said: This is north of the ridge What is familiar is hard to forget We did. Yantou said: What words were spoken? The monks raised the previous exchange. Yantou said: What did he say? The monks said: He said nothing; he lowered Still cannot hide it No vinegar, no end to it One word enters the public court Eight oxen cannot drag it out of the gate Better just lower your head and go out his head and returned to the hermitage. Yantou said: Ah! At that time you should have told him the final If so, then you have never reached Xuefeng phrase. If you had told him that, people in the world could do nothing to old Xue. And now, have you said it or not At the end of the summer retreat, the monks again brought up the previous exchange and asked Yantou for instruction. Why not say, I am Old Xue myself Good wine sobers a man slowly Yantou said: Why didn't you ask earlier? The monks said: We did not dare do so lightly. Yantou Fond of drowsing Can weather the monastery grove well enough said: Though Xuefeng and I are born on the same branch, we do not die on the same branch. If you want to know the final phrase, it is just this. Those seeking something else go broke first Steam it fresh and sell it hot
The master said: Yunyan studied alongside Daowu; Xuefeng studied alongside Yantou. A gentleman is not ashamed

text_zh: 師云。雲巖傍參道吾。雪峯傍參巖頭。君子不 恥下問。今雲巖雪峯之道大行。亦退己讓人 之餘慶也。而巖頭天資英邁。抑揚德山之道。 天下橫行。無敢當鋒者。蓋見處洞達蘊養成 就。故得如是。看他二僧。雪峯門下。箭鋒相 直。也是箇行脚漢。為甚直至夏末。尚疑末後 句。只為眼鈍頭迷當面蹉過。巖頭與他說出 許多道理。雪峯與我同條生。不與我同條死。 一法雖無異。三人乃見差。這僧與雪峯。一時 道是甚麼。及至論末後句。說與也不知。豈非 差之毫釐失之千里也。且道。這僧實不會。要 放這話行。溈山哲云。大小雪峯巖頭。却被這 僧勘破。萬松道。冷眼不防。巖頭雪峯。猶可 恕也。後來又點德山亦不會末後句。直是難 甘。是故天童兩次頌出。頌云。
text_en: to ask below. Today the ways of Yunyan and Xuefeng flourish greatly; this too is the leftover blessing of yielding oneself and letting others stand forth. As for Yantou, his natural endowment was heroic and outstanding; he raised and spread Deshan's way. He strode across the world; none dared meet his edge. This is because his insight was penetrating and his cultivation well matured, and so he could be like this. Look at those two monks from Xuefeng's gate — arrowpoints facing straight on — they too were traveling monks. Why then, all the way to the end of summer, did they still doubt the final phrase? Only because their eyes were dull and their minds confused; right before them, they missed it. Yantou explained to them so much reasoning: Xuefeng and I are born on the same branch, but we do not die on the same branch. Though the one Dharma is not different, in three people there appears difference. These monks and Xuefeng, at one time, all said, What is this? But when it came to the final phrase, even when told, they still did not know. Is this not missing by a hair's breadth and losing by a thousand miles? Tell me, did these monks truly not understand, or did they want to let this saying circulate? Weishan Zhe said: Big Xuefeng and Yantou were instead tested through by these monks. Wansong said: A cold eye does not guard against it. Yantou and Xuefeng may still be excused. Later he even criticized Deshan too as not understanding the final phrase — that is truly hard to swallow. Therefore Tiantong brought it out in verse twice. The verse says:
Cutting, filing, carving, polishing; transformations mixed and mistaken — the staff that turned into a dragon at Gebei. If not for one thing One does not gain one bit of wisdom

text_zh: 切瑳琢磨不因一事　變態殽訛不長一智　葛陂化龍之杖 已聞過海穿雲陶家居蟄之梭猶見倚牆貼壁　同條生兮有數 世相近也同條死兮無多習相遠也　末後句只這是且信一半 風舟載月浮秋水切忌垛根
text_en: Already heard of crossing seas and piercing clouds The Tao family’s hibernating shuttle; to live on the same branch has its number. Yet still seen leaning on walls and clinging to them In worldly form they are close To die on the same branch is not many; the final phrase is only this. In habits they are far apart For now, believe half of it A wind-borne boat carries the moon, floating on autumn waters. Above all avoid piling up roots
The master said: In the Mao Odes, Qiao of the Qi praises the virtue of Duke Wu. He was cultured and also able

text_zh: 師云。毛詩淇奧美武公之德也。有文章又能 聽其規諫。以禮自防。故能入相於周。美而作 是詩也。瞻彼淇奧。綠竹猗猗。有匪君子。如切 如瑳如琢如磨。註曰。治骨曰切。象曰瑳。玉曰 琢。石曰磨。德山雪峯得巖頭。發明末後句。至 今此話大行。切磨通變之力也。雪峯如化龍 之杖。這僧如居蟄之梭。巖頭點出至今不知。 所以同條死者無多也。或謂巖頭如化龍之 杖。雪峯如居蟄之梭者。請細看前話。雪竇佛 果以雙明雙暗。頌此話。非飽參者不知。東漢 方術傳。費長房。汝南人。甞為市掾。遇壺公。 斷青竹杖。偽為長房縊死於家。遂同入深山。 學道不成。辭歸。公與竹杖。騎此至家。投葛 陂。長房投杖於陂。化龍而去。又晉陶侃少時。 漁於雷澤。網得一梭。掛壁。後聞雷電。化為龍 而去。雪峯如杖。這僧如梭。巖頭如風舟載月。 萬松似箇甚麼。鞏縣茶瓶。
text_en: to heed admonition, guarding himself with ritual. Therefore he could become minister under Zhou. In praise of him this poem was made. It says: Look at that bend of the Qi, the green bamboo lush and graceful. There is a noble gentleman, as if cut, as if filed, as if carved, as if polished. The note says: working bone is called cutting; working ivory is called filing; working jade is called carving; working stone is called polishing. Deshan and Xuefeng, upon meeting Yantou, had the final phrase clarified. To this day this story is widely circulated. It is the power of cutting and polishing into transformative penetration. Xuefeng is like the dragon-transforming staff; this monk is like the hibernating shuttle. Yantou pointed it out, yet even now they do not know. Therefore there are not many who die on the same branch. Some say Yantou is like the dragon-transforming staff, and Xuefeng like the hibernating shuttle; please look carefully at the earlier story. Xuedou and Foguo, using double illumination and double concealment, versified this case. Those not fully seasoned in practice do not know it. In the Eastern Han Records of Magicians: Fei Changfang, a man of Runan, once served as a market clerk and met Hu Gong. He cut a green bamboo staff, made it appear Changfang had hanged himself at home, and then they entered the deep mountains together. Changfang failed to complete the Way and took leave to return. Hu Gong gave him a bamboo staff; riding it he reached home and threw it into Ge Marsh. Changfang threw the staff into the marsh, and it changed into a dragon and departed. Also, when Jin’s Tao Kan was young, he fished at Lei Marsh and netted a shuttle. He hung it on the wall. Later, when thunder and lightning sounded, it transformed into a dragon and left. Xuefeng is like the staff; this monk is like the shuttle; Yantou is like a wind-boat carrying the moon. What is Wansong like? A tea bottle from Gong County.

text_zh: 51 法眼舡陸
text_en: 51. Fayan: By Boat or By Land Instruction to the assembly: In worldly dharmas, how many awaken; in Buddha-dharma, how many are confused.

text_zh: 示眾云。世法裏悟却多少人。佛法裏迷却多 少人。忽然打成一片。還著得迷悟也無。
text_en: If suddenly it is all struck into one piece, can confusion and awakening still adhere or not?
Cited: Fayan asked Senior Monk Jue, Did you come by boat or by land? Jue said, It very much seems like there are two kinds

text_zh: 舉。法眼問覺上座。舡來陸來大似有兩般覺云。 舡來深談實相善說法要眼云。舡在甚麼處恐怕不實覺云。舡 在河裏果然有下落覺退後。眼却問傍僧云。爾道 適來這僧。具眼不具眼可惜許。
text_en: By boat. Fayan said, Where is the boat? Jue said, The boat Deeply discussing true reality, adept at explaining the essentials of Dharma I fear it is not solid is in the river. After Jue withdrew, Fayan asked a nearby monk, Sure enough, there is a landing place Tell me, did that monk just now have the eye, or not? What a pity
The master said: Huanglong Huitang asked. When Huang Luzhi was in difficulty, a man arrived.

text_zh: 師云。黃龍晦堂問。黃魯直正窘迫次。一人至。 堂問。誰遣汝來。人云。大林葉秀才。問。有書 否。人云。有。又問。書何在。人即引手背。抽衣 領舉書。呈堂。堂云。學道到此人田地方可。黃 有愧色。法眼問覺上座。舡來陸來。覺云。舡 來。眼云。舡在甚麼處。這裏一百箇。九十九 箇。呈機顯示。是他穩實平貼底人。那裏與爾 干戈相待。是他道舡在河裏。磁州老師道。恰 似沙地裏放箇八脚𨫼子。更無些子不穩當 處。覺退後眼却問傍僧云。爾道。適來這僧。具 眼不具眼。只這一問大曬誵訛。若道具眼。有 甚奇特玄妙。若道不具眼。見甚麼破綻。試教 天童定當看。
text_en: Huitang asked, Who sent you? The man said, Scholar Ye of Dalin. He asked, Is there a letter? The man said, Yes. He asked again, Where is the letter? The man immediately drew the back of his hand, pulled open his robe collar, brought out the letter, and presented it to Huitang. Huitang said, To study the Way up to this field is acceptable. Huang looked ashamed. Fayan asked Senior Monk Jue, By boat or by land? Jue said, By boat. Fayan said, Where is the boat? Here, out of a hundred, ninety-nine would display wit and show off. But he was a steady, solid, level man. How could he meet you with weapons drawn? He said, The boat is in the river. Master Cizhou said, It is just like setting an eight-legged creature on sandy ground; there is not the slightest instability anywhere. After Jue withdrew, Fayan asked a nearby monk, Tell me, that monk just now, did he have the eye or not? This one question greatly airs out confusion. If you say he had the eye, what is so strange or mysterious? If you say he lacked the eye, what flaw did you see? Let Tiantong judge it and see.
Water does not wash water; gold does not trade for gold. Ignoring coat color, one gets the horse. Cut off all specks, clear and pure Refined into one lump

text_zh: 水不洗水絕點澄清　金不博金鍊做一塊　昧毛色而得馬 不得相取靡絲絃而樂琴非可聲求　結繩畫卦有許事法出 姦生喪盡真淳盤古心弄巧成拙
text_en: It cannot be grasped by appearances Dispensing with silk strings, one delights in the qin. Knotting cords and drawing trigrams bring so many affairs. It cannot be sought through sound When law comes forth Craftiness arises They utterly lose the pure simplicity of Pangu’s mind. Cleverness backfires into clumsiness
The master said: Water does not wash water; gold does not barter for gold. Buddha does not seek Buddha; Dharma does not speak

text_zh: 師云。水不洗水。金不博金。佛不求佛。法不說 法。此談其神駿。略其玄黃。得琴趣者。忘其絃 徽。淮南子秦穆公。使伯樂舉九方堙求馬。三 月而返曰。得馬在沙丘。牡而黃。及馬至則牝 而驪。公謂伯樂。子所求馬者。毛色牡牝。不知 敗矣。伯樂太息曰。以至於此乎。堙之所觀者 天機也。得其精。而忘其麁。見其內而忘其外 也。果千里馬。晉陶潛字淵明。不解琴蓄素琴 一張。絃徽不具。曰。但得琴中趣。何勞絃上 聲。易云。上古結繩而治。後世聖人易之以書 契。又云。古者包犧氏之王天下也。仰則觀象 於天。俯則觀法於地。觀鳥獸之文。與地之宜。 近取諸身。遠取諸物。於是始畫八卦。萬松道。 盤古初分天地。已成對待。結繩畫卦。轉喪真 淳。釋迦未出世。祖師不西來。還有真諦俗諦 世法佛法麼。舒州海會齊舉禪師。得法之後。 甞到瑯琊覺處。覺問。上座近離甚麼處。舉曰。 浙江。覺曰。舡來陸來。舉曰。舡來。覺曰。舡在 甚麼處。舉曰。河裏。覺曰。不涉程途。一句作 麼生道。舉曰。杜撰長老如麻似粟。便下去。萬 松道。行說好話。洞山初和尚問僧。甚處來。 僧曰。汝州。山曰。此去多少。僧曰。七百。山曰。 踏破幾䩫草鞋。僧曰。三䩫。山曰。甚處得錢 買。僧曰。打笠子。山曰。參堂去。僧應喏。萬松 道。便是手眼通身看爾不破。且道。這僧眼在 甚麼處。眉毛下。
text_en: Dharma. This speaks of the divine steed while omitting black and yellow markings. One who gets the qin’s flavor forgets its strings and tuning marks. In the Huainanzi, Duke Mu of Qin sent Bole and then Jiufang Yin to seek a horse. After three months he returned and said, I found a horse at Shaqiu, a yellow stallion. But when the horse arrived it was a mare and black. The duke said to Bole, The horse he sought, its coat color and sex, he did not know— he has failed. Bole sighed deeply and said, Has he reached this point? What Yin observed was the heavenly mechanism. He grasped the essence and forgot the coarse, saw the inner and forgot the outer. Indeed it was a thousand-li horse. Jin’s Tao Qian, styled Yuanming, did not know how to play the qin, yet kept an unadorned qin of one piece, without complete strings or tuning marks. He said, If one only gets the qin’s inner flavor, why toil over sounds on the strings? The Yi says: In high antiquity they governed by knotted cords; later sages replaced this with written tallies. It also says: In ancient times, when Baoxi ruled the world, he looked up and observed images in heaven, looked down and observed patterns on earth, observed the markings of birds and beasts and what suited the land. Taking what was near from the body and what was far from things, he then first drew the eight trigrams. Wansong said: When Pangu first split heaven and earth, duality was already formed. Knotting cords and drawing trigrams further lost true simplicity. Before Shakyamuni appeared in the world, before the patriarch came from the West, were there still ultimate truth and conventional truth, worldly dharma and Buddha-dharma? Chan Master Qiju of Haihui in Shuzhou, after receiving the Dharma, once went to Langya Jue. Jue asked, Reverend, where have you lately come from? Ju said, Zhejiang. Jue said, By boat or by land? Ju said, By boat. Jue said, Where is the boat? Ju said, In the river. Jue said, Without involving the road, in one phrase how would you say it? Ju said, Bogus elders are as hemp and millet, and then he went down. Wan- song said: A fine saying while walking. In the beginning, Dongshan asked a monk, Where do you come from? The monk said, Ruzhou. Dongshan said, How far is it from here? The monk said, Seven hundred. Dongshan said, How many straw sandals did you wear out? The monk said, Three. Dongshan said, Where did you get the money to buy them? The monk said, Making hats. Dongshan said, Go to the hall and practice. The monk assented. Wansong said: This is hands-and-eyes through the whole body, and still you cannot see through him. Tell me, where is this monk’s eye located? Under the eyebrows.

text_zh: 52 曹山法身
text_en: 52. Caoshan: The Dharma Body Instruction to the assembly: Those with wisdom understand by analogy. But when it comes to what cannot be compared

text_zh: 示眾云。諸有智者。以譬喻得解。若到比不得 類難齊處。如何說向他。
text_en: and is hard to match, how do you speak to them?

Cited: Caoshan asked Senior Monk De, The Buddha’s true dharma body is like empty space, responding to things and manifesting form like the moon in water. How would you speak of this responding The authorities do not

text_zh: 舉。曹山問德尚座。佛真法身猶若虛空官不 容針應物現形如水中月私通車馬作麼生說箇應 底道理叉手近前云喏德云。如驢覻井落花有意隨流水山云。 道即大曬道只道得八成欲窮千里目德云。和尚 又如何更上一層樓山云。如井覻驢流水無心送落花。
text_en: Allow even a needle Yet in private carts and horses pass through principle? De said, Like a donkey looking into a well. Caoshan said, With folded hands step forward and say yes Fallen flowers, with intent, follow the flowing water You speak well enough, but you have spoken only eighty percent. De said, Master, To exhaust the view for a thousand miles then how about you? Caoshan said, Like the well looking at the donkey. Climb one more story Flowing water, without intent, carries off the fallen flowers
The master said: Chan Master Benji of Caoshan in Yihuang, Fuzhou, was perhaps also named Danzhang; likely

text_zh: 師云。撫州宜黃曹山本寂禪師。或名耽章。必 是賜名諡號。初離洞山。入曹溪。禮祖塔。迴吉 州之吉水。眾嚮山名。遂請開法。師擬曹溪。凡 隨所居立曹為號。洞山之宗至師最隆。故有 曹洞之稱焉。山問德上座。佛真法身猶若虛 空。應物現形如水中月。作麼生說箇應底道 理。此四句讚佛。本出古本金光明經。既如虛 空。如何應物。覺範贊提婆尊者道。應緣而現。 不落思惟。是故鉢水以針投之。德云。如驢覻 井。此豈情識計校可及。非久經淘鍊具衲僧 巴鼻。不許到這田地。若是小作無向上關棙 子。滿口許他也。山云。道即大曬道。只道得八 成。如秤稱斗量來相似。德云。和尚又如何。這 一拶詞窮理盡。敢道出他驢覻井一句不得。 是他款款地。只與倒過。可謂觸類而長之。此 所以稱曹洞宗派之源也。天童愛此兩轉語。 翻覆一時頌出。頌云。
text_en: a bestowed name or posthumous title. When he first left Dongshan, he entered Caoxi, paid homage at the patriarch’s stupa, and returned to Ji shui in Jizhou. The assembly revered the mountain’s name and invited him to open the Dharma. The master modeled himself on Caoxi; wherever he resided, he established Cao as the designation. In Dongshan’s lineage, it was under him that it flourished most, hence there is the name Caodong. Caoshan asked Senior Monk De, The Buddha’s true dharma body is like empty space, responding to things and manifesting form like the moon in water. How would you speak of the principle of response? These four lines praising the Buddha originally come from an old version of the Golden Light Sutra. Since it is like empty space, how does it respond to things? Juefan praised the Venerable Deva, saying: Manifesting in response to conditions, not falling into thought. Therefore it is like dropping a needle into bowl-water. De said, Like a donkey looking into a well. How could this be reached by emotional consciousness and calculation? Unless one has long been tempered and has a patch-robed monk’s handle and grip, one is not permitted to reach this field. If one is of small capacity, without the upward turning-key, I would still grant him full approval. Caoshan said, You speak broadly enough, but have spoken only eighty percent. It is as if weighing by scales and measuring by pecks. De said, Then how about you, Master? This one pressing question exhausted words and reached the end of principle. I dare say he could not utter that donkey-looking-in-the-well line. Yet he calmly and gently only turned it over. This can be called extending it by analogy. This is why he is called the source of the Caodong lineage. Tiantong loved these two turning phrases, and in one sweep flipped them over and versified them. The verse says:

The donkey looks at the well, the well looks at the donkey; wisdom contains all without outside. Rising early in the fifth watch Yet there are still travelers in the night Patchrobed monks under heaven cannot leap

text_zh: 驢覻井五更侵早起　井覻驢更有夜行人　智容無外天下衲僧跳不 出淨涵有餘萬象莫能逃影質　肘後誰分印天眼龍睛不可窺 家中不蓄書真文不醋　機絲不掛梭頭事花又不損　文彩 縱橫意自殊蜜又得成
text_en: Out Pure clarity contains more than enough; who can divide the seal behind the elbow? The ten thousand forms cannot escape shadow and substance Heavenly eyes and dragon pupils cannot spy it out In the house no books are stored; loom-thread is not hung on the shuttle-tip affair; literary colors The true pattern needs no vinegar The flowers are not harmed cross and crisscross, yet the meaning is naturally distinct. And the honey is made as well
The master said: Prajna is without knowing, yet there is nothing it does not know; therefore pure clarity overflows. In the Jin

text_zh: 師云。般若無知。靡所不知。故淨涵有餘也。晉 元帝永昌元年。王敦鎮武昌。舉兵犯闕。刀協 勸帝。盡誅王氏。王導帥群從。詣臺待罪。周顗 將入朝。導呼之曰。伯仁以百口累汝。顗不顧。 及入極論導忠誠。申救甚至。及出導尚在門。 又呼之不應。乃曰。今年殺賊奴。取金印如斗 大。繫肘後。尋又上表。明導無罪。導不知甚恨 之。敦兵既至。乃問導。周顗可得生否。導不應。 敦乃殺顗。導後料中書。見顗救已表。流涕曰。 幽冥之中負此良友。叢林又有肘後符。春秋 後語。趙簡子告諸子曰。吾藏肘後寶符於常 山上。先得者賞。諸子馳山上。求無所得。唯襄 子母䘏還曰。䘏已得之符矣。他人皆不可分。 簡子請奏之。母䘏曰。從常山上下臨代可取 也。簡子曰。母䘏賢矣。立為太子。雲巖示眾 云。有箇人家兒子。問著無有道不得底。洞山 出云。他屋裏有多少書籍。巖云。一字也無。洞 山云。得恁麼多知。巖云。日夜不曾眠。洞山又 云。問一段事得也無。巖云。道得即不道。肘 後誰分印。深密自得之道。他人皆不可分也。 家中不蓄書。得恁多知。生而知之上。學而知 之次也。這驢覻井。井覻驢。還許分割領覽分 也無。還許學解傳布也無。夾山云。聞中生解。 意下丹青。目下即美。久蘊成病。青山與白雲。 從來不相到。機絲不掛梭頭事。文彩縱橫意 自殊。嘉祥一路智者知疎。瑞草無根賢者不 貴。天童末後全用夾山一聯。以明此話不落 思惟。文彩自備。且道。具何三昧。便得如斯。 只箇無巴鼻。諸般沒奈何。
text_en: Emperor Yuan’s first year of Yongchang, Wang Dun guarded Wuchang and raised troops to attack the court. Diao Xie urged the emperor to execute the Wang clan completely. Wang Dao led his relatives and attendants to the palace terrace to await judgment. Zhou Yi was about to enter court. Dao called to him, Boren, I burden you with a hundred mouths. Yi did not look back. Once inside, he argued strongly for Dao’s loyalty and pleaded for him earnestly. When he came out, Dao was still at the gate. Dao called again, but he did not answer. Then he said, This year I will kill the bandit slaves and take a gold seal as big as a peck, and tie it behind my elbow. Soon after, he submitted another memorial clearly declaring Dao innocent. Dao, not knowing this, hated him deeply. When Dun’s troops arrived, he asked Dao whether Zhou Yi could be spared. Dao gave no reply. Dun then killed Yi. Later Dao reviewed the secretariat documents and saw Yi’s memorial saving him, and wept, saying: In the dark beyond I have betrayed this good friend. In the Chan groves there is also the talisman behind the elbow. In the Spring and Autumn Later Sayings, Zhao Jianzi told his sons: I have hidden a precious talisman behind the elbow on Mount Chang. Whoever gets it first will be rewarded. The sons raced up the mountain and found nothing. Only Xiangzi’s mother returned and said, I have already obtained the talisman. Others cannot share in it. Jianzi asked her to explain. She said, From Mount Chang one can look down over Dai and take it. Jianzi said, The mother is worthy, and established Xiangzi as heir. Yunyan instructed the assembly, There is a family’s son—when questioned, there is nothing he cannot speak of. Dongshan came forth and said, How many books are in his house? Yunyan said, Not a single character. Dong- shan said, How then does he know so much? Yunyan said, He has never slept day or night. Dongshan again said, Can I ask him about one matter or not? Yunyan said, If it can be said, then I do not say it. Behind the elbow, who can divide the seal? It is the deeply hidden way of self-attainment; others cannot share it. In the house no books are stored, yet there is such much knowing. To know by birth is highest; to know by learning is secondary. This donkey looking at the well, the well looking at the donkey—do you permit dividing it up, grasping and surveying it in parts, or not? Do you permit learned understanding and transmission, or not? Jiashan said, From hearing arises understanding. Beneath the thought, painted colors; before the eyes, immediate beauty. Long stored, it becomes a sickness. Green mountains and white clouds have never reached each other. Loom-thread is not hung on the shuttle-tip affair; literary colors cross and crisscross, while meaning is naturally distinct. On the Jiaxiang road, the wise know it as sparse; auspicious grass without root, the worthy do not prize it. At the end Tiantong wholly uses Jiashan’s couplet to clarify that this saying does not fall into discursive thought, and its literary colors are complete of themselves. Tell me, possessing what samadhi does one become like this? Just this lack of handle and grip—nothing at all can be done about it.

text_zh: 53 黃檗噇糟
text_en: 53. Huangbo Eats Dregs Instruction to the assembly: Facing the moment, one does not see Buddha. In great awakening, one does not keep the teacher. A sword that settles heaven and earth

text_zh: 示眾云。臨機不見佛。大悟不存師。定乾坤 劍沒人情。擒虎兕機忘聖解。且道。是甚麼人 作略。
text_en: has no human sentiment. In the device that seizes tigers and rhinos, holy understanding is forgotten. Tell me, what kind of person’s maneuver is this?
Cited: Huangbo instructed the assembly, All of you are nothing but dregs-eating fellows.

text_zh: 舉。黃蘗示眾云。汝等諸人盡是噇酒糟漢 黃蘗門下與麼行脚何處有今日今既不如昔後當不如今還知 大唐國裏無禪師麼眼高四海時有僧出云。只 如諸方匡徒領眾。又作麼生黃蘗兼身在蘗云。不 道無禪。只是無師且救得一半。
text_en: Traveling about like this, where will there be a today? Do you still know Under Huangbo's gate If now is not as before, later will not be as now that in the Great Tang there are no Chan masters? Then a monk came forth and said, But Eyes high over the four seas what about all the various places guiding students and leading assemblies? Huangbo said, It is not that there is no Chan— Huangbo himself is there too I only say there are no teachers. At least half is saved
The master said: This case is abbreviated. If stated in full, it would say: One day, ascending the hall, he said, You

text_zh: 師云。此話就簡。若全舉當曰。一日上堂云。汝 等諸人欲何所求。仍以棒趁之。眾不散。師乃 曰。汝等諸人盡是噇酒糟漢。唐時愛罵人。噇 酒糟漢。齊桓公讀書於堂上。輪扁斵輪於堂 下。釋椎鑿。上問。敢問公之所讀何言耶。公 曰。聖人之典。曰聖人在乎。公曰已死矣。曰然 則君之所讀古人糟粕矣。公曰。寡人讀書。輪 人安得議乎。有說則可無說則死。扁曰。臣也 以臣事觀之。臣斵輪徐則甘而不固。疾則苦 而不入。不徐不疾。得之於手。而應於心。口不 能言。有數存於其間。臣不能喻臣之子。子亦 不能受於臣。是以行年七十。而老斵輪。古之 人與其不可傳者死矣。然則君之所讀者。古 人之糟粕矣。又云。恁麼行脚取笑他人。但見 八百一千人處便去。不可只圖熱鬧也。山僧 行脚時。或遇草根下有箇漢。便頂上一錐看 他。若知痛痒。可以布袋盛米供養。可中總似 汝等如此容易。何處更有今日事也。汝等既 稱行脚。亦須著些精神好。還知道大唐國裏 無禪師麼。黃蘗以來。巖頭羅山愛行此令。近 代佛日。北來慶壽顗公。至死無可意者。寧絕 嗣無人。香山俊和尚叔祖兒孫。亦行此令。不 知者喚作點胸。可中要箇不憤底出來承頭。 果有一僧出云。諸方尊宿盡聚眾開化。為甚 道無禪師。蘗曰。不道無禪。只是無師。溈山問 仰山云。作麼生。仰云。鵞王擇乳。素非鴨類。 溈云。此實難辨。五祖戒出僧語。謝和尚說得 道理好。萬松道。生言孰語冷脣淡舌。石門聰 云。黃蘗垂示不妨奇特。纔被布衲挨拶。失却 一隻眼。萬松道。換了那僧兩隻眼。承天宗云。 五祖戒眼照四天下。萬松道。也只是一隻眼。 要見黃蘗。猶未可。萬松道。果然。若要扶竪正 法眼藏。須是黃蘗宗師。萬松道。錦上更添花。 翠巖真云。諸方商搉便道。黃蘗坐却這僧。萬 松道。不知扶起這僧。又道。黃蘗被這僧上來。 直得分析不下。萬松道。緇素轉分明。何謂也。 翠巖輒生擬議。霧豹澤毛。未甞下食。庭禽養 勇。終待驚人。萬松道。後五日看。蘗又云。闍 梨不見。馬大師下有八十餘人。坐道場箇箇 阿轆轆地。得大師正眼者。止三兩人。唯歸宗 最較些子。夫出家須知從上來事分。且如四 祖下。牛頭融大師橫說竪說。猶未知向上關 棙子。有此眼腦。方辨得邪正宗黨。略舉至此。 要見此話始末。其後尚有百十餘言。此是最 初。出世示人之語。故諸方盛行。雪竇頌。佛果 評唱。最詳。尚闕本錄上堂正意。天童頌出。極 盡善盡美。頌云。
text_en: people—what is it you seek? Then he drove them off with a staff. The assembly did not disperse. The master then said, All of you are dregs-eating fellows. In Tang times they liked to curse people as dregs- eaters. Duke Huan of Qi was reading in the hall above, while Wheelwright Bian was hewing a wheel below the hall. He set down his mallet and chisel and asked from below, May I ask what words my lord is reading? The duke said, The classics of the sages. Bian said, Are the sages present? The duke said, They are dead. Bian said, Then what my lord reads is the dregs and husks of the ancients. The duke said, I am reading, and a wheel- wright dares to discuss it? If you can explain, all right; if not, you die. Bian said, I look at it from my own work. If I hew slowly, it is easy but not firm; if too fast, it is hard and does not fit. Neither slow nor fast, I get it in my hands and respond in my mind. The mouth cannot speak it. There is a knack preserved in between. I cannot explain it to my son, and my son likewise cannot be received from a minister. Therefore, at seventy years of age, Wheelwright Bian was still hewing wheels. What the men of old died with, along with what could not be transmitted. Thus what my lord reads is the dregs of the ancients. He also said: If you travel about like this, you only become a laughingstock to others. Whenever you see a place with eight hundred or a thousand people, you go there at once. You must not merely seek bustle and excitement. When this mountain monk was traveling, if I met some fellow down among the weeds and roots, I would give him a jab on the crown and see how he was. If he knew pain and itch, he could be fed with a cloth sack full of rice. But if all are like you all, taking things so easily, then where would there even be the matter of today? Since you all call yourselves itinerant monks, you must bring forth some spirit. Do you know that in the Great Tang there are no Chan masters? Since Huangbo, Yantou and Luoshan loved to enforce this command. In later times, Fori and Master Yi of Qingshou who came from the north, up to their deaths found no one satisfactory. Rather than have heirs without worthy people. Monk Jun of Xiangshan and his Dharma descendants also enforced this. Those who do not know call it chest-pointing. Among them they want someone not indignant to come forward and take it up. Sure enough, a monk came out and said: The venerable elders everywhere all gather communities and teach. Why then say there are no Chan masters? Huangbo said: I do not say there is no Chan, only that there are no teachers. Guishan asked Yangshan: How is it? Yangshan said: The king goose selects the milk; by nature it is not of the duck kind. Gui said: This truly is hard to distinguish. Wuzu Jie cited the monk’s words: Thank you, master, you explained the principle well. Wansong said: Raw words and dead phrases, cold lips and bland tongue. Shimen Cong said: Huangbo’s instruction is indeed extraordinary, but as soon as he was pressed by this patched-robe monk, he lost one eye. Wansong said: He changed out both of that monk’s eyes. Chengtian Zong said: Wuzu Jie’s eye illumines the four quarters. Wansong said: It too is only one eye. If you want to see Huangbo, still not yet possible. Wansong said: Indeed. If you want to uphold and establish the true Dharma-eye treasury, you must have a master like Huangbo. Wansong said: Adding flowers atop brocade. Cuiyan Zhen said: People everywhere discussing it then say Huangbo silenced this monk. Wan- song said: They do not know he raised this monk up. Again they say Huangbo, when this monk came forward, was unable to analyze it. Wansong said: Black and white become even clearer. What does this mean? Cuiyan immediately gives rise to speculation. The mist-leopard moistens its fur and has never yet descended to feed; the courtyard bird nurses its courage, in the end waiting to startle men. Wansong said: Watch in five more days. Huangbo also said: Venerable monks, do you not see? Under Master Ma there were more than eighty people. Sitting in their training seats, every one of them rolled on busily, but those who got the Master’s true eye were only two or three. Only Guizong came somewhat close. A renunciant must know the inherited matter from above. For example, under the Fourth Patriarch, Master Niutou Rong spoke crosswise and lengthwise, yet still did not know the upward turning hinge. With this eye and brain, only then can one distinguish heterodox and orthodox lineages. Briefly I cite this much. If you want to see the beginning and end of this saying, afterward there are still over a hundred more words. This is the very first discourse he gave upon appearing in the world to instruct people, so it flourished everywhere. Xuedou versified it, and Foguo commented on it most fully, yet the main intent of the original hall talk was still lacking. Tiantong’s verse brings it out, bringing it to utter perfection. The verse says:
Branching paths and dyed silk are far too busy; leaves linked to flowers ruin the ancestral line. When you know fewer matters, you have fewer troubles

Watch when the command is carried out Cutting away the tangled fragments, trimming off the downy fuzz, A great elephant does not travel rabbit paths Great awakening is not bound by Small details star-balance and ornate mirror, jade ruler and golden knife, old Huangbo examines the autumn Not the slightest thing is obscured Measure and insight are deep and clear hair-fine tip. You cannot fool him by even a speck Seated, he cuts off the spring wind and does not let it rise high. Prepare for what is unforeseen

text_zh: 師云。列子說符篇楊子之隣人亡羊。既率其 黨。又請楊子之豎子追之。楊子曰。一羊何追 者之眾。隣人曰。多岐路。既返問獲羊乎。曰亡 之矣。曰奚亡之。曰岐路之中又有岐焉。墨子 梁惠王時。有道之人。出行見素絲染從餘色。 悲之曰。人湛然同於聖體。為居惡俗。染之成 累。岐分絲染太嘮嘮。勅交切鬧嘮嘮也。或作 勞亦可。葉綴花聯者。達磨初祖頌云。吾本來 此土。說法救迷情。一花開五葉。結果自然成。 一花五葉。便是岐分絲染也。若大唐國裏無 禪師。達摩也無出頭分。宗鏡錄司南之車。本 示迷者。照膽之鏡。為鑑邪人。古今注。黃帝與 蚩尤。戰於涿鹿。蚩尤作大霧。迷於四方。帝在 車以指指南而示。士卒擒蚩尤而斬之。遂號 指南車。甄陶。陳留風俗記。舜陶甄河濱。其後 為氏。今姓甄。音真也。此玄鑪陶乎群象。智海 總乎萬流也。屏割繁碎。剪除氄毛。去岐分之 差路。剪綴葉之旁枝。斗為衡星。以運平四時 也。藻鑑文明之鑑也。秤所以定輕重。鑑可以 辨妍媸。玉尺。拾遺記。禹遊龍門。八神探玉 簡。以授之。長尺二寸可以度量天地。金刀。 古有金錯刀錢金刃書。此頌黃蘗品第諸方。 秤尺在手。更兼聰聞蟻鬪明察秋毫。防微杜 漸。坐斷春風不放高也。大聖安彝和尚竹笋 詩。便好臨根下斤斧。免教節外更生枝。
text_en: companions and also asked Yangzi’s servant boy to pursue it. Yangzi said: For one sheep, why are so many pursuing it? The neighbor said: There are many branching roads. When they returned, he asked, Did you get the sheep? They said, It was lost. He said: How was it lost? They said: Among the branching roads, there were more branches. In Mozi, in the time of King Hui of Liang, a man of the Way went out and saw plain silk being dyed by various colors. He lamented it, saying: People in their clarity are the same as the sage-body, but dwelling in corrupt customs, they are dyed and become defiled. Branching paths and dyed silk are all too noisy and busy. The pronunciation note says lao-lao means clamorous bustle. It may also be written with the character for toil. As for leaves linked and flowers joined, the First Patriarch Bodhidharma’s verse says: I originally came to this land to speak Dharma and save deluded beings. One flower opens five leaves; the fruit naturally ripens. One flower and five leaves is precisely branching paths and dyed silk. If in the Great Tang there were no Chan masters, even Bodhidharma would have had no chance to emerge. The Record of the Source Mirror speaks of the south-pointing chariot, originally to show the way to the lost. The gall-illuminating mirror is to examine the crooked. In Ancient and Modern Notes, the Yellow Emperor and Chiyou fought at Zhuolu. Chiyou made a great fog, and all four directions were lost. The Emperor then made a chariot that pointed south to guide them. The soldiers captured Chiyou and beheaded him. Thus it was named the south-pointing chariot. As for pottery shaping, the Customs of Chenliu says that Shun made pottery by the riverbank; afterward it became a clan name, now the surname Zhen, pronounced zhen. This is the dark furnace molding the myriad forms, the sea of wisdom gathering all streams. Cutting off the tangled fragments and trimming away the down, it removes the branching-road side paths and cuts the side-branches from the linked leaves. The Dipper is the balancing star, moving to regulate the four seasons. The ornate mirror is the mirror of bright discernment. A scale determines light and heavy; a mirror can distinguish beauty and ugliness. As for the jade ruler, the Records of Gathered Remnants says: When Yu toured Dragon Gate, eight spirits brought forth a jade tablet and gave it to him, one chi and two cun long, by which he could measure heaven and earth. As for the golden knife, in ancient times there were gold-inlaid knife coins and writings inscribed with a golden blade. This verse praises Huangbo for ranking the schools. With scale and ruler in hand, and moreover keen hearing of ants fighting, clearly perceiving the finest autumn hair, he guards against the subtle and blocks what gradually grows. Thus he sits cutting off the spring wind, not letting it rise high. In Great Sage Anyi’s poem on bamboo shoots, It is best to bring axe and adze down at the root, lest more branches grow beyond the joints.

Raising the case: Yunyan asked Daowu, What does the Bodhisattva of Great Compassion do with so many hands and eyes?

text_zh: 舉。雲巖問道吾。大悲菩薩用許多手眼作 麼爾恁麼問圖个甚麼吾云。如人夜間背手摸枕子一上神通 不同小小巖云。我會也且莫詐明頭吾云。汝作麼生會果然 放不過巖云。遍身是手眼無空缺處吾云。道即大曬 道即得八成某甲舌頭短巖云。師兄作麼生理長即就吾 云。通身是手眼無隔礙處。
text_en: Daowu said: It is like a person in the night reaching back with the hand to feel for a pillow. Yunyan said: I understand. Daowu said: How do you understand? Yunyan said: The whole body is hands and eyes. Daowu said: You have said it, but Asking like this, what are you after Once it reaches spiritual powers It is not a small matter For now, do not feign understanding Sure enough Cannot let it pass There is no gap anywhere you only got eighty percent. Yunyan said: Elder brother, how about you? My tongue is short When the principle is long, it comes together Daowu said: The entire being is hands and eyes. There is no obstruction anywhere
The master said: Li Ao asked Ehu, What does Great Compassion use a thousand hands and eyes for? Ehu said:

text_zh: 師云。李翱問鵞湖。大悲用千手眼作麼。湖云。 今上用公作麼。昔有無目山人。貨卜。雨過泥。 途著鮮白鞋入市。人問。山人失明。如何泥不 污鞋。山人舉拄杖云。拄杖頭上有眼。以山人 為證。夜間摸枕子。手上有眼。喫飯時舌上有 眼。聽語識人耳中有眼。蘇子瞻與聾人說話。 寫字而已。復笑云。我與彼皆異人也。我以手 為口。彼以眼為耳。佛說六根互用。信乎不疑。 無盡居士潞州紫巖大悲殿記。舉大悲經楞 嚴經。最為詳細。甞見一說。大悲昔為妙善公 主。乃天人為宣律師說。然三十二應。百億化 身。亦隨見不同。各據其說也。天覺曰。千手者 示引迷接物之多也。千眼者示放光照暗之廣 也。苟無眾生無塵勞。則一指不存。而況千萬 臂乎。一瞬不具。而況千萬目乎。遍身通身。何 必不必。似有淺深。實無損益。雲居示眾曰。老 僧二十年前住三峯庵時。興化來曰。權借一 問以為影草時如何。老僧當時機思遲鈍道 不得。為伊致得箇問頭。奇特不敢辜他。當時 伊曰。想庵主答這話不得。不如禮拜了退。而 今思量當時不消道箇何必。萬松道。若教容 易得。後有化主到興化處。化問。山中和尚住 三峯庵時。老僧曾問伊話祇對不得。而今道 得也未。化主舉前話了。化曰。雲居二十年只 道得箇何必。興化即不然。爭如道箇不必。萬 松道。鬪兔角之短長。三聖云。雲居二十年道 得。猶較他興化半月程。萬松道。競空花之濃 淡。僧問覺範。如諸老宿所示有同異否。範云。 佛令訥鈍比丘誦苕菷。一日大悟得大辯才。 於此當見先德為物之心。天童分上又作麼 生。頌云。
text_en: What does the emperor use you for? Formerly there was a blind mountain man who sold fortunes. After rain, on muddy roads, he wore bright white shoes into the market. People asked: Mountain man, you are blind. How is it that mud does not stain your shoes? The mountain man raised his staff and said: At the tip of the staff there are eyes. Taking this mountain man as proof, when feeling for a pillow at night, there are eyes in the hand. When eating, there are eyes on the tongue. When listening to speech and recognizing a person, there are eyes in the ears. Su Zizhan, when speaking with a deaf man, simply wrote characters. Then he laughed and said: He and I are both unusual people. I use my hand as a mouth; he uses his eyes as ears. The Buddha spoke of the six faculties functioning interchangeably. Believe it without doubt. Layman Wujin, in the inscription for the Great Compassion Hall at Ziyan in Luzhou, cites the Great Compassion Sutra and the Leng- yan Sutra in greatest detail. I once saw an account saying Great Compassion was formerly Princess Miaoshan, which a heavenly being told to Vinaya Master Xuan. Yet the thirty-two responses and the hundred million transformation bodies also differ according to what is seen, and each account has its own basis. Tianjue said: A thousand hands indicate the many ways of guiding the lost and receiving beings. A thousand eyes indicate the breadth of shining light into darkness. If there were no sentient beings and no defilements, then not even one finger would remain, much less thousands and myriads of arms. If one glance were not complete, much less thousands and myriads of eyes. Whole body, entire being, what need of must or need-not? It seems there is shallow and deep, but in truth there is no loss or gain. Yunju addressed the assembly, saying: This old monk, twenty years ago when living at Sanfeng Hermitage, Xinghua came and said: I will borrow a question for the moment as a sketching line. What about it? At that time this old monk’s faculties and thought were dull, and he could not answer. He brought forth a marvelous question-head for me; I did not dare fail him. At that time he said: I suppose the hermitage master cannot answer this saying. Better bow and withdraw. And now, thinking it over, back then there was no need to say, Why must it be so? Wansong said: If you let it be easy, it is too easily gotten. Later a fundraiser monk came to Xinghua’s place. Xinghua asked: When the mountain monk lived at Sanfeng Hermitage, this old monk once questioned him and he could not respond. Can he now answer or not? The fundraiser repeated the former story. Xinghua said: For twenty years Yunju only managed to say Why must it be so? Xinghua is not like that. Better to say There is no need. Wan- song said: Contesting the length of rabbit horns. Sansheng said: Yunju in twenty years came to say it, yet he was still half a month behind Xinghua. Wansong said: Competing over the depth of sky-flowers’ colors. A monk asked Juefan: Are the teachings of the old worthies the same or different? Fan said: The Buddha had a dull monk recite broom. One day he greatly awakened and gained great eloquence. From this you should see the former worthies’ heart for beings. As for Tiantong’s part, how is it? The verse says:

One opening, empty and penetrating; eight-sided lattices, clear and open. Without form, without partiality, spring enters Vertically exhausting the three times Horizontally pervading the ten directions

Pure jewel-eyes, meritorious Letting it fall naturally into the front stream virtue-arms. Looking ahead and behind, picking east and gathering west How does whole-body compare to entire-being? Here before us, hands Cannot sort it out clearly and eyes reveal the complete function. The thief's loot is already exposed Great function goes freely in all directions; what taboo could there be?
