The master said: Tiantong says, from one opening being empty and penetrating, one then gains eight-sided openness.

text_zh: 師云。天童道。由一竅虛通。便得八面櫺櫳 也。且如柳塘花塢暖日和風。春在何處。作何 形段。然能應物乘時不留不礙。如月當天任 運而轉。知。通身遍身。背手摸枕底是甚麼人。 傀儡棚中。必有抽牽線索者。楞嚴說八萬四 千清淨寶目。八萬四千姥陀羅臂。八萬四千 爍迦羅首。興化墮馬折臂頌云。大悲菩薩有 千手。大丈夫兒誰不有。且道。那箇是通身底 手眼。師以手擘眼云。猫。
text_en: For example, by willow ponds and flowered banks, in warm sun and gentle wind, where is spring? What shape does it take? Yet it can respond to things and accord with the time, without lingering or obstruction, like the moon in the sky moving by its own course. Know this: entire-being and whole-body. Who is it that reaches back to feel for the pillow? In the puppet booth there must be one who pulls the strings. The Lengyan says there are eighty-four thousand pure jeweled eyes, eighty-four thousand mudra arms, and eighty-four thousand heads of Shakra. Xinghua, after falling from a horse and breaking his arm, versified: Great Compassion Bodhisattva has a thousand hands; what real man does not have them? Tell me, which one is the hand-and-eye of the entire being? Hand and eye. The master pried open his eye with his hand and said: Cat.

text_zh: 55 雪峯飯頭
text_en: 55. Xuefeng the Rice-Cook. Addressing the assembly, he said: Ice is colder than water; indigo blue comes from indigo. Only when one surpasses the teacher can one be fit

text_zh: 示眾云。氷寒於水。青出於藍。見過於師。方堪 傳授。養子不及父。家門一世衰。且道。奪父 之機者是甚麼人。
text_en: to receive transmission. If a son does not match his father, the family declines in one generation. Tell me, the one who seizes the father’s function, who is that person?
Raising the case: When Xuefeng was serving as rice-cook under Deshan, one day the meal was late. Deshan If young and not diligent

text_zh: 舉。雪峯在德山作飯頭少不努力一日飯遲。德山 托鉢至法堂老不歇心峯云。這老漢鐘未鳴鼓未 響。托鉢向甚麼處去教得孩兒會罵娘山便歸方丈盡在 不言中峯舉似巖頭家返宅亂頭云。大小德山不會 末後句父為子隱直在其中山聞令侍者喚巖頭問。汝 不肯老僧那潑油救火巖遂啟其意人間私語天聞若雷山乃 休去果然不會至明日陞堂果與尋常不同隨風倒柁巖 撫掌笑云。且喜老漢會末後句家醜外揚他後天 下人不奈伊何鼻孔為甚在我手裏。
text_en: carried his bowl to the Dharma hall. Xuefeng said: This old fellow, the bell has not rung and the drum has not Old yet the mind does not rest sounded, so where are you taking your bowl? Deshan then returned to the abbot’s quarters. Xuefeng told Yantou. Yantou said: Big old Deshan does not understand Teach the child and he learns to curse his mother All lies in What is not spoken The house is turned back into disorder the final phrase. Deshan heard of it and had the attendant call Yantou, asking: You A father shields his son, and straightness is right in it do not approve of this old monk? Yantou then explained his meaning, and Deshan thereupon Pour oil to put out a fire Private whispers among men are heard in heaven like thunder let it rest. The next day, when he ascended the hall, it was indeed unlike usual. Yan- Sure enough, you do not understand Turn the rudder with the wind tou clapped and laughed, saying: Good! The old fellow understands the final phrase. Hereafter the people under heaven Family shame spread outside will have no way to do anything to him. Why is your nose in my hands
The master said: Xuefeng lowered his head and returned to the hut; Deshan immediately returned to the abbot’s quarters. This is best investigated.

text_zh: 師云。雪峯低頭歸庵。德山便歸方丈。最好參 詳。巖頭密啟其意。爾且道。道甚麼。德山又休 去。可謂。相逢不拈出。舉意便知有。山至來日 上堂。果與尋常不同。也是將錯就錯。頭下至 僧堂前。拊掌大笑曰。且喜老漢會末後句。他 後天下人不奈伊何。切忌。蓋覆將來雖然如 是。也只得三年。德山果三年遷逝。天覺頌。鐘 鼓聲沈捧鉢迴。巖頭一拶語如雷。果然只得 三年活。莫是遭他授記來。萬松道。知爾被底 穿。曾共同床臥。明招代德山云。咄咄。沒處去。 沒處去。萬松道。鼻孔在他人手裏。雪竇云。曾 聞說箇獨眼龍。元來只具一隻眼。殊不知。德 山是箇無齒大蟲。若不是巖頭識破。爭得明 日與作日不同。諸人要會末後句麼。只許老 胡知不許老胡會。半遮半掩漏逗。也不知。大 溈喆云。巖頭大似高山石裂。直得百里走獸 潛蹤。若非德山度量深明。爭得昨日與今日 不同。萬松道。無齒大蟲。爪距尚在。魯祖凡見 僧來便面壁。南泉聞云。我尋常向他道。空劫 已前承當。佛未出世時會取。尚不得箇半箇。 他恁麼。驢年去。若識得南泉。便見巖頭。更與 天童把臂共行。頌云。
text_en: Yantou secretly revealed his meaning. Now you tell me, what did he say? Deshan again let it rest. It may be said: When they met, they did not bring it out; once the intent was raised, they knew it was there. When Deshan on the next day ascended the hall, it truly was unlike usual. Yet this too was making use of a mistake upon a mistake. Yantou then went down to the front of the monks’ hall, clapped his hands, and laughed loudly, saying: Good! The old fellow understands the final phrase. In the future people under heaven will have no way with him. A grave warning: do not cover it over. Even though it is so, he only got three years. Deshan indeed passed away after three years. Tianjue’s verse: Bell and drum sounds sink as he returns holding the bowl; Yantou’s one pressing phrase was like thunder. Sure enough, he only got alive after three years. Could it be he received that prediction? Wansong said: I know your underside is exposed through and through. We once slept in the same bed. Mingzhao, speaking for Deshan, said: Tut, tut! No place to go. No place to go. Wansong said: his nostrils are in another man's hands. Xuedou said: I once heard tell of a one-eyed dragon; it turns out he really had only one eye. Little did they know, Deshan was a big toothless tiger. If Yantou had not seen through him, how could there be a clear difference between yesterday and today? People, do you want to understand the final phrase? It is only permitted that old Hu know it, not that old Hu understand it. Half covered, half concealed, it leaks out. Yet they do not know. Da- Weizhe said: Yantou was like a mountain rock splitting apart, so that beasts for a hundred li hid their tracks. If not for Deshan's deep and lucid measure, how could yesterday and today be different? Wansong said: though a toothless tiger, its claws and fangs are still there. Whenever Luzu saw a monk come, he would immediately face the wall. When Nanquan heard of it, he said: I usually tell him, before the empty kalpa take it up; realize it before the Buddha appeared in the world. Even then you do not get even half of one. If he goes on like that, it will take till the year of the donkey. If you know Nanquan, then you will see Yantou, and further walk arm in arm with Tiantong. The verse says:
As for the final phrase, did they understand or not? Deshan and his son were too vague. Here, whether you understand or not, your waist gets broken

text_zh: 末後句會也無這裏不得會不會打折腰　德山父子太含胡 外明不知裏暗座中亦有江南客勿謂秦無人　莫向人前唱 鷓鴣休得也
text_en: Bright outside, not knowing the dark within Among those seated there are also guests from Jiangnan; do not sing before people Do not say Qin has no men. the partridge song. Stop right there.
The master said: The final phrase is like this, hard to understand. Stern and severe like Deshan, keen and brilliant like

text_zh: 師云。末後句如此。難明峻硬若德山。頴俊如 巖頭。至今分雪不出。不見道。出身猶可易。脫 體道應難。鄭谷詩。花月樓臺近九衢。清歌一 曲倒金壺。座中亦有江南客。莫向春風唱鷓 鴣。天童用後兩句。不勞再舉底意也。舉著後 如何。師下座便歸方丈。
text_en: Yantou, to this day they cannot fully distinguish and explain it. Have you not heard it said: Getting out is still easy; shedding the body and speaking the Way is hard. In Zheng Gu's poem: Flower-and-moon towers stand near the nine streets; one clear song overturns the golden jug. Among those seated there are also guests from Jiangnan; do not toward the spring wind sing the partridge song. Tiantong used the last two lines, meaning there was no need to raise it again. After raising it, what then? The master stepped down from the seat and returned to the abbot's quarters.

text_zh: 56 密師白兔
text_en: 56. Master Mi and the White Rabbit Addressing the assembly, he said: Better to sink forever through kalpas than seek liberation from the various sages. Devadatta

text_zh: 示眾云。寧可永劫沈淪。不求諸聖解脫。提婆 達多。無間獄中受三禪樂。欝頭藍弗。有頂天 上墮飛狸身。且道。利害在甚麼處。
text_en: in the Avici hell receives the bliss of the third dhyana. Udraka Ramaputra, in the Highest Heaven, fell into the body of a flying civet. Tell me, where do benefit and harm lie?
Raised: Elder Master Mi was walking with Dongshan when they saw a white rabbit run across in front of them.

text_zh: 舉。密師伯與洞山行次。見白兔子面前走 過。密云。俊哉爭奈荒草裏走山云。作麼生怪儞遲也密云。 如白衣拜相自地昇空易山云。老老大大作這箇 語話幾乎放過密云。爾又作麼生人無害虎心虎無傷人意山云。 積代簪纓。暫時落薄從空放下難。
text_en: Mi said: Handsome indeed! Dongshan said: In what way? Mi said: Yet he runs off into the wild grass. No wonder you are late. Like a commoner appointed prime minister. Dongshan said: At your age, and you say such a thing? Rising from the ground into the sky is easy. Mi said: And you, what would you say? Dongshan said: You almost let it pass. Man has no mind to harm the tiger; the tiger has no intent to hurt man. A noble house for generations, temporarily fallen into poverty. Coming down from the empty sky is hard.
The master raised another saying: Dongshan and Chan Master Mi of Shenshan in Tanzhou were crossing water. Dongshan asked:

text_zh: 師舉。洞山與潭州神山僧密禪師過水。山問。 過水事作麼生。密云。不濕脚。山曰。老老大大 作這箇語話。密曰。汝又作麼生。山云。脚不 濕。教中有性修二門。洞上名借功明位。大抵 因修而悟。從凡入聖。白衣庶民直拜冢宰。若 先悟後修。從聖入凡。積代簪纓本來尊貴。雖 飄零萬狀。骨骼猶存。所以道。貧子喻中明此 道。獻珠偈裏顯張羅。汝等諸人。要見二尊宿 見處麼。看取天童一狀領過。頌云。
text_en: What is the matter of crossing water? Mi said: The feet do not get wet. Dongshan said: At your age and you say such words? Mi said: And you, what would you say? Dongshan said: The feet are not wet. In the teachings there are two gates, nature and cultivation. In the Dong school this is called borrowing function to illuminate position. In general, one awakens through cultivation, entering sagehood from the ordinary; a commoner in white is directly made chief minister. If one awakens first and cultivates later, one enters the ordinary from sagehood; a line of nobility for generations is originally honorable. Though scattered and fallen in ten thousand ways, the frame is still there. Therefore it is said: the parable of the poor son makes this Way clear; the jewel-offering verse displays it openly. All of you, if you want to see where these two venerable ones saw, look at how Tiantong receives and passes it through in one statement. The verse says:
Resisting frost and snow, he walks level into the clouds; Liu Xiahui left his state. In poverty, one cultivates oneself alone. In success, one aids all under heaven.

text_zh: 抗力霜雪貧則獨善一身　平步雲霄達則兼濟天下　下惠出國 苦瓠連根苦相如過橋甜瓜徹蒂甜　蕭曹謀略能成漢葵花向日 巢許身心欲避堯柳絮隨風　寵辱若驚深自信悟須實悟 參須實參真情參跡混漁樵未免靈龜曳尾
text_en: A bitter gourd is bitter to the root. Xiangru crossed the bridge; Xiao and Cao by strategy could establish Han. A sweet melon is sweet to the stem. Sunflowers turn toward the sun. Chao Fu and Xu You in body and mind wished to avoid Yao. Favor and disgrace startle like alarm, yet deep self-trust remains. Willow floss follows the wind. Awakening must be real awakening. Inquiry must be real inquiry. True feeling mingles traces, mixed among fishermen and woodcutters. Still not free of the sacred turtle dragging its tail.
The master said: Weeds crave rain and dew; pines and cypresses endure wind and frost. Only in the year's cold do we know

text_zh: 師云。蓬蒿貪雨露。松柏耐風霜。歲寒然後知 松柏之後凋。此隨緣不變之旨。簪纓落薄之 談。有力大人堪任此事也。平步雲霄。一超直 入如來地。已是太遲也。殊不知。積代簪纓本 來富貴。論語柳下惠為士師。三黜人曰。子未 可以去乎。曰。直道而事人安往而不三黜。枉 道而事人。何必去父母之邦也。司馬相如字 犬子。少喪父母。九歲與人牧猪。聞藺相如為 卿相。改名相如。棄猪就學。猪主杖之。先生問 知賢。留門外草庵。十年無書與讀。遣去。過昇 仙橋。題柱曰。若不乘駟馬車。不過此橋。後造 得子虛賦。將軍楊得意。夜宿殿中。誦此賦。帝 曰。朕恨不與此人同時。將軍奏曰。見在蜀地。 帝命往召。同乘駟馬車過橋。封侍中。蕭何曹 參。成漢高祖帝業。巢父許由。避堯洗耳飲牛。 老子云。寵辱若驚。得之若驚。失之若驚。以上 四雙八事。皆一句密老。一句洞山。妙哉圭峯 舉喻。譬如皇族淪落微賤。習以性成。後遇薦 拔。雖復本位。三端六藝。要重更改習學力用 方全。雖然天童分上猶落階級。不見道。寵辱 若驚深自信。真情參跡混漁樵。
text_en: that the pine and cypress are the last to wither. This is the meaning of adapting to conditions without changing, and the talk of noble houses fallen low. Only a person of great strength can bear this matter. To stride level into the clouds, in one leap directly enter the Tathagata ground, is already too late. They do not realize that nobility for generations is originally rich and honorable. In the Analects, Liu Xiahui was a magistrate and was dismissed three times. Someone said: Should you not leave? He said: If I serve people by the straight Way, wherever I go would I not be dismissed three times? If by a crooked way I serve people, why need I leave the land of my parents? Sima Xiangru, style name Quanzi, lost his parents young. At nine he herded pigs for others. Hearing that Lin Xiangru became a high minister, he changed his name to Xiangru. He abandoned the pigs and went to study. The pig owner beat him with a staff. The teacher asked and recognized his worth, keeping him in a grass hut outside the gate. For ten years he had no books to read. Then he was sent away. Passing Sheng- xian Bridge, he wrote on a pillar: If I do not ride a four-horse carriage, I will not cross this bridge again. Later he composed the Zixu Fu. General Yang Deyi, lodging overnight in the palace, recited this fu. The emperor said: I regret I did not live at the same time as this man. The general replied: He is now in Shu. The emperor ordered him summoned. He rode with a four-horse carriage across the bridge and was enfeoffed as palace attendant. Xiao He and Cao Can helped accomplish Emperor Gaozu of Han's enterprise. Chao Fu and Xu You avoided Yao, washing ears and watering oxen. Laozi says: Favor and disgrace are like alarm; gaining them is alarming, losing them is alarming. The above four pairs and eight matters are all one line for old Mi, one line for Dongshan. How subtle is Guifeng's analogy: It is like an imperial clan fallen into lowliness, habit made into nature, later meeting recommendation and promotion. Though restored to its original rank, the three virtues and six arts still require renewed training and effort before all is complete. Even so, on Tiantong's side it still falls into stages. Have you not seen it said: Favor and disgrace startle like alarm, yet there is deep self-trust; true feeling joins with traces, mixed among fishermen and woodcutters.

text_zh: 57 嚴陽一物
text_en: 57. Yanyang's One Thing Addressing the assembly, he said: To toy with the shadow wearies the form, not knowing the form is the root of shadow. To raise a voice to stop an echo,

text_zh: 示眾云。弄影勞形。不識形為影本。揚聲止響。 不知聲是響根。若非騎牛覓牛。便是以楔去 楔。如何免得此過。
text_en: not knowing the sound is the echo's root. If it is not riding an ox to look for the ox, then it is using a wedge to remove a wedge. How can one avoid this fault?
Raised: Venerable Yanyang asked Zhaozhou: When one thing is not brought along, what then?

text_zh: 舉。嚴陽尊者問趙州。一物不將來時如何 猶是分外州云。放下著貼体衣衫會須脫却嚴云。一物不將來。 放下箇甚麼人不知己過牛不知力大州云。恁麼則擔取去 喚不回頭爭奈何。
text_en: Zhou said: Put it down. Yan said: I did not bring a single thing. It is still extra. Even close-fitting clothes must be taken off. What is there to put down? Zhou said: In that case, carry it away. A person does not know his own faults; an ox does not know its great strength. 。 If called and he will not turn back, what can be done.
Venerable Yanyang of Xinxing in Wuning County, Hongzhou, first visited Zhaozhou and asked:

text_zh: 洪州武寧縣新興嚴陽尊者。初參趙州。問一 物不將來時如何。此與僧問報慈。情生智隔。 相變體殊。情未生時如何。慈云隔。暮故底。道 情也未生隔箇甚麼。此與一物不將來放下 箇甚麼。孟八郎漢大同。州云放不下則擔取 去者。言下大悟。佛果法語舉。黃龍頌云。一物 不將來。兩肩擔不起果云。明眼人難謾言下忽知非退步墮深 坑心中無限喜如貧得寶毒惡既忘懷無始宿業盡時清淨蛇虎 為知己異類等解寥寥千百年。清風猶未已誰不景仰師 所居常一蛇一虎手中與食。故如得果人。尊 者稱之。趙州古佛與尊者。不測聖凡底人。出 一言發一問。千古之下。與人為龜鏡。天童見 近日師僧麁心轉盛。所以打草驚蛇。頌云。
text_en: When one thing is not brought along, what then? This is like the monk who asked Baozi: When feeling arises, wisdom is obstructed; as phases change, substance differs. What about before feeling arises? Ci said: Obstructed. The old bottom of Mu said: If feeling has not yet arisen, what is obstructed? This is the same as One thing not brought along, put down what exactly? Meng Balan, that fellow, is just the same. Zhou said: If you cannot put it down, then carry it away. At these words he had great awakening. In Foguo's sayings it is cited, and Huanglong's verse says: One thing not brought along, both shoulders cannot carry it. At once he suddenly knew the wrong and endless joy filled his heart. Venom and malice forgotten, he cherished snake and tiger Guo said, clear-eyed people are hard to fool. Step back and you fall into a deep pit. Like a poor man finding treasure. When beginningless past karma is exhausted, there is purity. as intimate friends. Through sparse hundreds and thousands of years, the clear wind has still not ceased. The master Even those of other kinds alike understand. Who would not admire it. where he lived always had a snake and a tiger, which he fed by hand. Therefore, like one who attained the fruit, the venerable was so called. Zhaozhou the Ancient Buddha and this venerable one were men beyond measuring by sage or ordinary. One uttered a word, one posed a question, and for a thousand ages thereafter they serve people as tortoise-shell and mirror. Tiantong saw that in recent days among teachers and monks coarse minds are increasingly rampant, so he beat the grass to startle the snake. The verse says:

Failing to guard subtle conduct, he loses the first move; aware his mind is coarse, he is ashamed and strikes his head. Before black and white are distinguished, it is still the biased within the upright.

text_zh: 不防細行輸先手黑白未分前猶是正中偏　自覺心麁媿撞 頭虎口裏下子局破腰間斧柯爛且道如今甚麼時節　洗清凡 骨共仙游頭輕眼明
text_en: Head-bumping shame. Make a move in the tiger's mouth. The game is broken; at his waist the axe-handle rots away. Washed clean of the ordinary bones, Tell me, what time is it now. he wanders with immortals. Head light, eyes clear.
The master said: Old Wang Jiefu, holding a hidden saying on chess, said: He also dares not go first; this one

text_zh: 師云。王介甫老。持棊隱語云。彼亦不敢先。此 亦不敢先。唯其不敢先。是以無所爭。唯其無 所爭。是故入於不死不生。棊乃爭先法。贏則 贏箇先手。輸則輸箇頭撞。趙州於爾未下子 以前。早先見數著。嚴陽只管橫飛直逴。剩 占幾路。不知斧柯已爛也。王氏神仙傳。晉隆 安時。信安縣王質。採薪至眩室坂。見石室 四童子弈棊。與質物。如棗子。含之不飢。棊終 斧柯爛於腰間。衣袂隨風。抵暮還家。已數十 年矣。趙州放下著。擔取去兩轉語。抽筋拔髓。 換骨洗膓。便與趙州。把手共行。步虛輕舉也。 有底道。清閒真道本。無事小神仙。雖然莫將 無事為無事。往往事從無事生。
text_en: also dares not go first. Precisely because neither dares go first, therefore there is nothing to contend over. Precisely because there is no contention, therefore one enters the unborn and undying. Chess is indeed the method of contending for first move. If you win, then you win a first move; if you lose, you lose with a bumped head. Zhaozhou, before you had even placed a stone, had already seen several moves ahead. Yanyang only kept leaping sideways and darting straight, needlessly occupying a few lines, not knowing the axe-handle had already rotted. In Wang's Biographies of Immortals, during Jin Long- an times, Wang Zhi of Xin'an County went gathering firewood to Xuanshi Slope and saw in a stone chamber four boys playing chess. They gave Zhi something like jujubes; holding them in his mouth he did not hunger. When the game ended, the axe-handle at his waist had rotted. His sleeves fluttered in the wind. By dusk he returned home, but already several dozen years had passed. Zhaozhou's two turning words, Put it down and Carry it away, pull the sinews and draw the marrow. They change bones and wash the guts; then one can walk hand in hand with Zhaozhou, lightly ascending through empty space. Some say: Leisure and quiet are the true basis of the Way, carefree little immortals. Even so, do not take no affair as truly no affair; often affairs arise from no affair.

text_zh: 58 剛經輕賤
text_en: 58. The Diamond Sutra on Being Despised Addressing the assembly, he said: If you explain meaning by relying on the sutra, you wrong the Buddhas of the three times. If you depart from the sutra by one word, you turn out the same as

text_zh: 師云。見聞為種。八難超十地之階。解行在躬。 一生圓曠劫之果。圭峯科此經。為轉罪成佛。 此菩提煩惱。不二。生死涅盤不二。梁昭明太 子。科判此經。為能淨業障分。傅大士頌。先身 有報障。今日受持經。暫被人輕賤。轉重復還 輕。此正是依經解義也。後面四句便有衲僧 氣息。道。若了依他起。能除遍計情。常依般若 觀。何慮不圓成。前四句功德力。後四句觀行 力。六祖口訣云。佛言。持經之人。合得一切人 恭敬供養。為多生有重業障故。今生雖持此 經。常被人輕賤。不得敬養。自以持經故。不起 我人等相。不問冤親。常行恭敬。有犯不校。常 修般若波羅蜜。歷劫重罪悉皆消滅。又約理 而言。先世即是前念妄心。今世即是後念覺 心。以後念覺心。輕賤前念妄心。妄不能住。故 云先世罪業即為消滅。妄念既滅罪業不成。 即得菩提。此理事二解皆約觀行也。僧問雲 居。承教有言。是人先世罪業應墮惡道。以今 世人輕賤。故先世罪業即為消滅。此意如何。 居云。動則應墮惡道。靜則為人輕賤。崇壽稠 云。心外有法。應墮惡道。守住自己。為人輕 賤。萬松道。兩箇老漢俗氣也不除。且道。天童 分上又作麼生。頌云。
text_en: In one lifetime one may complete the fruit of vast kalpas. Guifeng classified this sutra as turning sin into Buddhahood. Here bodhi and affliction are nondual; birth-and-death and nirvana are nondual. Prince Zhaoming of Liang divided this sutra and called it the section on purifying karmic obstructions. Layman Fu's verse says: In former lives there were karmic obstacles; today one upholds this sutra. Temporarily despised by others, the heavy is turned and becomes again light. This is precisely explaining meaning by relying on the sutra. But in the later four lines there is already the breath of patch-robed monks: It says: If one understands dependent arising, one can remove imagined feelings. Constantly relying on prajna contemplation, why worry about not perfecting realization? The first four lines are the power of merit; the latter four are the power of contemplative practice. The Sixth Patriarch's oral teaching says: The Buddha said, a person who upholds this sutra ought to receive from everyone reverence and offerings; but because of heavy karmic obstacles from many lives, though in this life he upholds this sutra, he is often despised by others and does not receive reverence and support. Because he upholds the sutra, he does not arouse the marks of self and person. Without asking whether enemy or kin, he always acts respectfully. If offended, he does not contend. He always cultivates prajna-paramita. Heavy sins through kalpas are all extinguished. Further, in terms of principle, former life is just the previous thought of deluded mind; this life is just the later thought of awakened mind. With the later thought of awakened mind despising the previous thought of deluded mind, delusion cannot abide. Therefore it says former-life karmic offenses are thereby extinguished. Once deluded thoughts are extinguished, karmic offenses do not form. Then one attains bodhi. These two explanations, by principle and by phenomena, both concern contemplative practice. A monk asked Yunju: According to the teaching it says, This person's former-life karmic offenses should have fallen into evil paths, but because in this life people despise him, those former-life karmic offenses are thereby extinguished. What is the meaning of this? Ju said: In movement, one should fall into evil paths; in stillness, one is despised by others. Chongshou Chou said: If there is dharma outside mind, one should fall into evil paths. If one guards and clings to oneself, one is despised by others. Wansong said: These two old fellows have still not gotten rid of vulgarity. But tell me, on Tiantong's side how is it? The verse says:
Clinging, clinging to merit and fault; sticky, sticky with cause and effect; outside the mirror madly running, Only excepting those who awaken suddenly. Even the Dharma does not comply.

text_zh: 師云。功即持經。過即先業。既立妄因。必招妄 果。楞嚴云。豈不聞。室羅城中。演若達多。忽 於晨朝。以鏡照面。愛鏡中頭眉目可見。嗔責 己頭不見面目。以為魑魅。無狀狂走。於意云 何。此人何因無故狂走。富樓那言。是人心狂。 更無他故。此迷真執妄也。般若觀照真也。功 過因果妄也。真智現前。妄業消滅。阿耨菩提 皎然本具。此正教意。衲僧分上如何。嵩嶽破 竈墮和尚。山塢有廟。殿安一竈。烹宰祭祀不 輟。墮領侍者入廟。以杖敲竈三下咄云。此竈 泥瓦合成。聖從何來靈從何起。恁麼烹宰物 命。又打三下。竈乃傾墮破落。安國師號為破 竈墮。須臾有一人。青衣峨冠設拜云。我本廟 神久受業報。今日蒙師說無生法。脫此處生 在天中。特來致謝。師曰。是汝本有。非吾強 言。神再拜而沒。土瓦合成。聖從何來。無我人 相。般若智也。以真智為妄業。從來辜負。今日 相賀。烹宰物命極多全無福利。禪老敲三拄 杖便得生天。咄。鬼怕惡人難展掌。賊憑贓物 易承頭。
text_en: effects. The Shurangama says: Have you not heard? In Sravasti city, Yajnadatta suddenly one morning looked at his face in a mirror, loved that in the mirror his head, brows, and eyes were visible, and angrily blamed his own head for not seeing its face and features, taking it for a demon, and ran off madly for no reason. What do you think? Why did this man run mad without cause? Purna said: It was his mind gone mad; there was no other reason. This is deludedly abandoning the real and clinging to the false. Prajna contemplation is the real. Merit, fault, cause, and effect are false. When true wisdom appears before you, false karma is extinguished. Anuttara bodhi is clearly originally complete. This is exactly the teaching's meaning. But on the side of patch-robed monks, how is it? Songyue's Stove-Breaker monk, Pozuoduo: in a mountain hollow there was a temple, and in the hall stood a stove. Cooking and sacrificial slaughter never ceased. Duo led his attendant into the temple, struck the stove three times with his staff and shouted: This stove is made of mud and tiles. From where comes its sanctity? From where arises its spirit? In this way you butcher living beings, taking life. He struck it three more times, and the stove then collapsed and broke apart. National Teacher Anguo gave him the title Stove- Breaker. After a short while a man appeared, in blue robes and a high cap, bowed and said: I was originally the temple's The spirit has long undergone karmic retribution. Today, receiving the master's teaching of the unborn Dharma, I am freed from rebirth here and am born in heaven. I have come especially to give thanks. The master said, This is what you originally have; it is not something I forced upon you by words. The spirit bowed twice again and vanished. Earth and tiles join to form it; whence does holiness come? No self and no person- mark: this is prajna wisdom. Taking true wisdom for delusive karma, one has betrayed it all along. Today we celebrate together. Slaughtering living beings in great numbers brings no merit at all. The old Chan master struck three times with his staff and thereby gained rebirth in heaven. Bah. Ghosts fear evil men and cannot spread their hands; thieves rely on stolen goods and are easily seized by the head.

text_en: Wuben. Ben asked, Where have you recently come from? Lin said, Wuling. Ben said, The Way in Wuling, how does it compare with here? Lin said, In barbarian lands, bamboo shoots sprout in winter. Ben said, Steam fragrant rice in another pot and make an offering to this man. The master then withdrew. Ben said, This fellow will later run the whole world ragged. While Lin was planting pines at Dongshan, there was an old man Liu who asked the master for a verse. The master showed him this: Tapering, a little over three feet; lushly dense, it covers the wild grass. I do not know what age's man will behold this old pine. The old man presented it to Wuben. Ben said, Congratulations on your joy. This man is Dongshan's third generation. Lin took leave of Wuben and went to Qingcuo Mountain in Shannan Prefecture, living in a hermitage for ten years. Suddenly he recalled Wuben's parting words and said, One should benefit the many who are unenlightened; how could I be bound by petty details? So he went to Suizhou. Responding to causes and conditions and the assembly's request, he stayed at Tumen Xiaoqinglin Monastery, and was therefore called Qing- lin. He once said: All of you must directly investigate apart from mind, intention, and consciousness, beyond the paths of ordinary and holy learning. Only then can you preserve and uphold it. If not so, you are not my descendants. A monk asked, What about when a student goes straight on? This monk, from below the Hall of Great Compassion, wanted to go to the central capital. He even boasted of knowing a direct and essential road. Little did he know that what is straightaway is already far too roundabout. Lin blocked him with a dead snake across the road. The monk, heedless of danger and death, said, What if one faces it head-on? He was already poisoned. Some say, Why did he not use blows and shouts to enforce the command? But when did Lin ever let him off? He said, You lose your life-root. The monk felt a little sting and ache, and sought a way out, saying, What if one does not face it head-on? Lin said, There is no place to avoid it either. Even Qinglin himself cannot escape it. The monk with sinews slack and strength exhausted said, At just such a time, when there is nothing to be done either way, what is it then? Lin said, You miss it. A living man's method is seen here: able to send, able to call, with both seizing and releasing distinguished. If it is put on your body, you cannot pluck it off; if for you it is picked away, then there is somewhere it lands. The monk said, I do not know where it has gone. Lin said, The grass is deep; there is nowhere to seek it. It is not that there is none; it is just not visible. This monk too was strange, saying, Reverend, you too must be on guard. Qinglin, taking a dead snake, teased and prodded this monk, but in the end got it wrapped round his waist and feet. Then he clapped once and said, A single kind of poisonous vapour. Wansong said, It fumes the sky and scorches the earth. Wujindeng says, Qing- lin's pivotal activity was swift and severe, not merely a brilliance of one time, but also a model for ages to come. Wansong said, The spring wind's vexing tumult has not yet ceased. Look further: Tiantong blows flowers, sways willows. The verse says:
The old boatmen secretly turn the rudder; the lone boat turns back at night; reed flowers on both banks, The night ravine hides the boat. At the clear source, set the oar.

Following the current, one attains the subtle. Flute notes call the moon down over the blue islet. Letting it go, it falls into the stream ahead.

text_zh: 師云。丹霞淳禪師頌。長江澄徹印蟾華。滿目 清光未是家。借問漁舟何處去。夜深依舊宿 蘆花。二老同頌澄源湛水尚棹孤舟。丹霞用 雪竇頌玄沙和尚云。本是釣魚舡上客。偶除 鬚髮著袈裟。祖佛位中留不住。夜來依舊宿 蘆花。萬松道。將謂別有。古今詩話云。川峽呼 梢翁篙手。為長年三老。杜詩云。蜀鹽吳麻自 古通。萬斛之舟行若風。長年三老長歌裏。白 晝攤錢高浪中。此事如人行舡相似。不著兩 岸。不住中流。丹霞夜宿蘆花。天童信風橫管。 且道。轉柁迴舟時作麼生。夜深不向蘆灣宿。 逈出中間與兩頭。
text_en: pure radiance is not yet home. I ask, where does the fishing boat go? Deep in the night it still lodges among reed flowers. These two elders both praise a clear source and deep water, still poling a lone boat. Danxia uses Xuedou's verse on Master Xuansha, which says: Originally a guest on a fishing boat, by chance he shaved off beard and hair and put on the robe. He could not remain in the rank of patriarchs and buddhas; at night he still lodged among reed flowers. Wansong said, One would think there was something different. Ancient and modern poetic talk says: In the river gorges they call the stern oldman and pole-handlers the long-year old boatmen. Du's poem says: Shu salt and Wu hemp have from ancient times flowed together; a ten-thousand-hu ship moves like wind. Amid the long songs of the old boatmen all year, in broad daylight they spread coins upon the high waves. This matter is like a man piloting a boat: not clinging to either bank, not staying midstream. Danxia lodges at night among reeds; Tiantong trusts the wind and plays the transverse flute. But tell me, when turning the rudder and bringing the boat back, how is it? Deep at night he does not lodge in Reed Bay. He strides far beyond the middle and the two ends.

text_en: bestowing titles, this was masters recognizing each other. Though she was a nun, she had long studied under Weishan. Ten li from the mountain she built a hermitage. One day she visited Zihu. Hu asked, Are you perhaps Liu Tiemo? Mo said, I would not dare. Hu said, Turn left or turn right? Mo said, Reverend, don't topple over yourself. Hu immediately struck her. See how with Weishan and him: when releasing, both release; when gathering, both gather. Foguo called this a phrase across the body: the meaning connects, while the words are apart. If you want to know whether meaning and phrase both arrive, then look further at Tiantong's full-bodied verse. The verse says:

The biography of Chen Fan in the Eastern Han says: Fan could establish a noble reputation, challenge the corrupt customs in argument, and yet race about amid peril and hardship, contending with mutilated men and rotten fellows. text_zh: 師云。越州乾峯禪師。僧問。十方薄伽梵。一路 涅盤門。未審路頭在甚麼處。此問本出楞嚴 經第五。此阿毘達磨。十方薄伽梵。一路涅盤 門。未審路頭門戶在甚麼處。若依經解此義。 如來自說。與圓通張本。第六卷中。文殊方揀 圓通也。若衲僧分上。天童曾道。十方無壁落。 從本來元沒遮欄。四面亦無門。只這裏便是 入處。所以乾峯一畫云。在這裏。不知者往往 喚。作乾峯與這僧指路。不然道。與這僧畫斷 更不他游。決不是這箇道理。爾不見。雲門注 解得。八米九糠。黃龍南云。乾峯一期指路。曲 為初機。雲門乃通其變。故使後人不倦。萬松 道。曹溪波浪如相似。無限平人被陸沈。雲門 久在乾峯曹山疎山。這僧謂必知乾峯用處。 故求請益。若却用乾峯針線。乃繫驢橛也。忽 然拈出睦州秦時𨍏輅鑽。只得盞子落地。楪 子成七片。這僧不會乾峯意。雲門別與一條 活路。大似潑油救火。鼓扇消氷。竹庵早曾點 破。頌云。乾峯不用指陳。雲門休打骨董。自然 東海鯉魚。築著帝釋鼻孔。竹庵更比雲門。忒 曬慈悲。人越難會。不如。天童於冷眼不防却 較些子。頌曰。
text_en: the gate of nirvana; where is the roadhead? This question originally comes from the Surangama Sutra, fascicle five: In this Abhidharma, the Bhagavans of the ten directions have one road, the gate of nirvana. I do not know where the roadhead and gateway are. If one explains this meaning according to the sutra, the Tathagata himself speaks it as a preface to Perfect Penetration; in fascicle six, Manjusri then selects the Perfect Penetration. But on the side of patch-robed monks, Tiantong once said: In the ten directions there are no walls. From the start there has never been any barrier. On all four sides there is no gate either. Just here itself is the place of entry. Therefore Qianfeng made one stroke and said, It is here. Those who do not know often take it as Qianfeng pointing out the road to this monk. Or else they say he drew a line to cut off any further wandering. This is definitely not the principle. Do you not see? Yunmen explained it as eight parts rice, nine parts chaff. Huanglong Nan said, Qianfeng for one occasion pointed out the road, bending himself for beginners. Yunmen then made its transformation flow through, and thus later people do not tire of it. Wansong said, The waves at Caoxi seem alike, yet countless ordinary people are drowned on dry land. Yunmen had long been with Qianfeng, Caoshan, and Shushan. This monk thought he must surely know Qianfeng's use, so he sought instruction. But if he had merely used Qianfeng's needle and thread, it would have been just a donkey-tethering stake. Suddenly pulling out Muzhou's Qin-era awl, all that can happen is the cup falls to the ground and the plate breaks into seven pieces. This monk did not grasp Qianfeng's meaning, so Yunmen gave him another living road. It is very much like throwing oil on a fire to put it out, or fanning to melt ice. Zhugan long ago already pointed this out, with a verse: Qianfeng need not point and explain; Yunmen need not peddle curios. Naturally the East Sea carp strikes Indra's nostril. Zhugan, compared to Yunmen, is even too openly compassionate; people find it all the harder to understand. Better Tiantong's cold-eyed way, unexpectedly a bit closer. The verse says:
Taking it in hand, he still treats the dead horse; the reviving-soul incense is about to stir your peril. Use thunderbolt hands and wolf-tiger medicine.

text_zh: 師云。乾峯死馬醫。醫不可。這僧已是喪身失 命底人。雲門收得返魂香。能令已死者再甦。 拾遺傳。漢延和元年。西胡月氏音之國。遣使 獻香四兩。大如雀卵。色如桑椹。至始元年。京 城大疫。死者太半。帝取香焚之。其死未三日 皆活。香氣三月不歇。香出聚窟洲人鳥山。樹 如楓。香聞數里。名返魂樹。伐根玉釜煮汁黑 粘。一名驚精魂。二名返生。三名振檀。四名 却死。天童小參云。十分收得返魂香。一等來 撾塗毒鼓。雲門一落索。天童道。是返魂香。諸 方變為塗毒鼓。直教轉身吐氣不得。把斷咽 喉。塞却鼻孔。也百體汗流一場。誌公云。忽悟 本性元空。恰似熱病得汗。雖然萬松眉毛有 幾莖。
text_en: Yunmen obtained the reviving-soul incense, able to make the already dead come back to life. The Record of Collected Omissions says: In the first year of Han Yanhe, the Western Hu state of the Yuezhi sent envoys Give voice to it. to present four liang of incense, as large as sparrow eggs, colored like mulberries. By the first year of Shiyuan, the capital suffered a great plague, and more than half had died. The emperor took the incense and burned it; those dead less than three days all revived. The fragrance did not cease for three months. The incense came from Reniao Mountain on Juku Isle. The tree was like a maple; its scent could be smelled for several li. It was called the Reviving-Soul Tree. They cut the root and boiled the sap in a jade cauldron into a black resin. One name was Startle-Essence Soul; a second, Return-to-Life; a third, Shaking Sandal; a fourth, Repel-Death. In a brief talk Tiantong said: Fully obtaining the reviving-soul incense, all alike come to beat the poison-smeared drum. Yunmen's single loose drop, Tiantong says, is reviving-soul incense. In all quarters it changes into a poison-smeared drum, making you unable to turn around or breathe out, cutting off the throat and plugging the nostrils, yet all the limbs pour out sweat in one great burst. Zhigong said, Suddenly awakening to the original nature's emptiness is just like a fever breaking in sweat. Though Wansong's eyebrows have only a few hairs.

text_zh: 師云。京兆米禪師。一曰米七師。一曰米胡。俗 舍第七美髯。因有二名。八方珠玉。嗣雪峯。今 據仰山同參。嗣溈山。這僧正問。自古上賢還 達真正理麼。胡曰。達。僧云。只如真正理作麼 生達。此與假悟底時節不殊。胡云。當時霍光 賣假銀城。與單于契書。是甚麼人做。佛果稱 胡。為大善知識。名不虛傳。僧曰。某直得杜 口無言。胡曰。平地教人作保。只如米胡道達。 仰山道。悟即不無爭奈落第二頭何。若不假 悟。又道唯人自肯乃方親。勝默和尚常謂。投 子拈古。內秀俏措無賽。甞拈此話云。然仰山 恁麼道即得。還免得自己落麼。若免得。更 有一人。大不肯在。若免不得。亦落第二頭。米 胡雖然肯他。自己還有出身之路也無。諸人 試點檢看。若點檢得出。兩人瓦解氷消。若點 檢不得。且莫造次。頌云。碧岫峯頭借問人。指 山窮處未安身。雖然免得重陽令。爭似靈苗 不犯春。萬松道。不得春風花不開。及至花開 又吹落。忠國師問紫璘供奉。佛是何義。璘曰。 是覺義。國師曰。佛曾迷否。璘曰。不曾迷。國 師曰。用覺作麼。璘無對。此亦本無迷悟之意 也。常愛雪竇道。本無迷悟。數如麻。獨許靈 雲是作家。悟即落第二頭不悟又唯人自肯。 如何即是。天童自有方便。頌云。
text_en: he was the seventh son and had a beautiful beard, hence the two names. A jewel among the eight directions, he was heir to Xuefeng. Now according to Yangshan, who was a fellow student and heir to Weishan, this monk was precisely asking whether the superior worthies of old still Have you reached the true principle or not? Hu said, Reached. The monk said, Just as for the true principle, how does one come to reach it? This is no different from the occasion of false awakening. Hu said, At that time Huo Guang sold a fake Silver City and made a treaty document with the Chanyu. What sort of man did that? Foguo praised Mi Hu as a great spiritual friend; his name was not falsely handed down. The monk said, I am simply brought to seal my mouth, with no words. Hu said, On level ground you make a man stand guarantor. As for Mi Hu saying Reached. Yangshan said, Awakening is not absent, but what can be done about falling into the second head? If one does not rely on false awakening, then again it is said only when one accepts for oneself is it intimate. Monk Shengmo often said, Touzi handling old cases had inward elegance and graceful turns beyond compare. Once he raised this saying and said, Still, Yangshan can speak this way well enough, but did he avoid falling himself or not? If he avoided it, then there is another person who utterly refuses to agree. If he did not avoid it, then he too falls into the second head. Mi Hu, though he approved him, did he himself still have a road of emergence or not? All of you try to inspect it. If you can inspect it clearly, the two men shatter like tiles and melt like ice. If you inspect and cannot, then for now do not be hasty. The verse says: On the peak of green ridges he borrows a question from a man, pointing to where the mountain ends, yet he has not settled his body. Though he escapes the Double Ninth command, how can it compare to the numinous sprout that does not violate spring? Wansong said, Without spring wind the flowers do not open, but when the flowers open they are blown down again. National Teacher Zhong asked Attendant Zilin, What is the meaning of Buddha? Lin said, It means awakening. The National Teacher said, Was Buddha ever deluded? Lin said, Never deluded. The National Teacher said, Then what use is awakening? Lin had no reply. This too originally has no meaning of delusion and awakening in it. I have always loved Xuedou saying, Originally there is no delusion or awakening, yet their numbers are like hemp; only Ling yun is acknowledged as a master. If awakened, one falls into the second head; if not awakened, then only self acceptance. What then is it? Tiantong has his own expedient means. The verse says.

text_zh: 師云。第二頭分悟破迷。明來暗謝。智起惑亡。 皆是途中事。周易略例。罤者所以在兔。得兔 而忘罤。筌者所以在魚。得魚而忘筌。然則言 者象之罤也。象者意之筌也。存言者非得象 者也。存象者非得意者也。若向第二頭。道少 他悟。達一迴不得。爭奈道。設有妙悟亦須吐 却。快須撒手到家更無一物。始忘罤捨筌。功 夫智識。盡屬第二頭。及盡功夫。不可智知。始 得少分相應。莊子外篇駢拇第八云。駢於足 者。連無用之肉。枝於手者。樹無用之指。注駢 拇足大指。連第二指也。枝指六指也。功若不 盡。如駢拇連無用之肉也。春秋。楚文王伐申 過鄧。鄧祁侯曰吾甥也。止而享之。騅甥聃甥 養甥。請殺楚子。鄧侯弗許。三甥曰。亡鄧國者 必此人也。若不早圖。後君噬臍。注云不及也。 智不到處。智不能知。兔老圓月也。丹霞淳和 尚道。水澄月滿道人愁。氷盤秋露泣。戀著即 不堪也。大荒經。崑崙丘上。有琅玕玉樹。結子 如珠而小也。玄中銘。靈木迢然鳳無依倚。與 鶴不停機。皆不許守戀坐著也。鳥寒而凄。不 欲落他根株枝葉也。詩抑篇。白珪之玷尚可 磨也。玉內病曰瑕。體破也。外病曰玷。色污 也。此頌。仰山貴白珪無玷。不落第二頭。如何 是第一頭。大悟後方知不是。
text_en: All are matters on the road. In the Brief Commentary to the Zhouyi: The snare exists for the rabbit; once the rabbit is gotten the snare is forgotten. The fish trap exists for the fish; once the fish is gotten the trap is forgotten. Thus words are the snare for images, and images are the trap for meaning. One who keeps the words has not gotten the image, and one who keeps the image has not gotten the meaning. If toward the second head one says one has some awakening, then not even one time is true penetration attained. Yet it is said, Even if there is marvelous awakening, it too must be spat out. One must quickly let go; arriving home there is not a single thing. Only then are snare and trap forgotten and cast away. Effort and knowledge all belong to the second head. When effort is exhausted, it cannot be known by knowledge. Only then is there a small measure of accord. In the Outer Chapters of Zhuangzi, Joined Toes chapter eight, it says: What is joined on the foot is attached useless flesh; what branches on the hand is a useless finger grown out. The note says joined toe means the big toe joined to the second toe; branch finger means a sixth finger. If effort is not exhausted, it is like joined toes attaching useless flesh. In the Spring and Autumn: King Wen of Chu attacked Shen and passed through Deng. Marquis Qi of Deng said, He is my nephew, and stopped to feast him. Zui-nephew and Dan-nephew and Yang-nephew asked to kill the ruler of Chu, but the marquis of Deng would not permit it. The three nephews said, The one who will destroy Deng will surely be this man. If you do not plan early, later my lord will bite his navel. The note says this means it will be too late. Where knowledge does not reach, knowledge cannot know. The old rabbit means the full moon. Monk Danxia Chunhe once said, When water is clear and the moon is full, the practitioner grieves. On the ice platter autumn dew weeps. If one clings to it, then it is unbearable. In the Classic of the Great Wilderness, atop Kunlun Hill there is a jade tree of langgan, bearing fruit small like pearls. In the Inscription of the Mysterious Center: The numinous tree stands far off, and the phoenix has nowhere to rest. And the crane does not stop its loom. All this does not permit guarding, clinging, and sitting fixed. The bird is cold and mournful, not wanting to land on another's roots, trunk, branches, and leaves. In the Shi, the Yi section: A blemish on white jade may still be polished away. An inner flaw in jade is called a defect, a break in substance; an outer flaw is called a blemish, a stain of color. This verse esteems Yangshan's white jade without blemish, not falling into the second head. But what is the first head? Only after great awakening does one know it is not so.

text_en: Chan Master. He happened to meet him pacing in the hall, and stepped forward, bowed, and asked, The hidden meaning of coming from the West, Master, how is it shown to people? Cuiwei paused his steps and looked at him. Touzi said, I beg the Master to point it out. Cuiwei said, Do you want a second ladle of foul water too? Touzi suddenly awakened in accord. He bowed in thanks and withdrew. Cuiwei said, Do not fall away. Touzi said, When the time comes, root and sprout of themselves grow. Another day he happened to ask, What is Buddha principle? Cuiwei said, Buddha does not reason. Touzi said, Does that not fall into emptiness? Cuiwei said, True emptiness is not empty. Thereupon he gave a prophetic verse, saying, When has Buddha principle ever reasoned? True emptiness is again not empty. Datong will dwell at Jizhu and spread and expound my school. Touzi returned to his home region at Tongcheng, to Touzi Mountain. Zhaozhou first in Tongcheng met him. Zhou said, Could you be the hermitage master of Touzi? Touzi said, Tea overseer, give me one coin in alms. Zhou went up the mountain first; Touzi carried an oil bottle and came after. Zhou said, I long heard of Touzi, but on arriving I see only an old oil seller. Touzi said, You only see the oil seller, and do not yet know Touzi. Zhou said, What is Touzi? Touzi lifted up the oil bottle and said, Oil, oil. Touzi set out a tea seat to receive him, and himself passed a sesame cake to Zhao zhou. Zhou paid no attention. Touzi had the attendant pass the sesame cake. Zhou bowed to the attendant three times. Tell me, what was his meaning? Chan Master Yongguang Zhen of Suzhou, ascending the hall, said, If the point of speech is off even slightly, your home country is ten thousand li away. This is like the usual saying about not escaping a beating with the white willow stick; in wording and intent they seem alike. In the Lou Tan scripture, there is a great stone forty li square. Every hundred years the devas come and brush it with gauze cloth; the stone is worn away, yet the kalpa is still not exhausted. Exhausting these mustard city and kalpa stone only reaches the exhaustion of the present time, and only then returns to before the empty kalpa. Only then is the eye alive. Ring center comes from Zhuangzi: The hinge first gets its ring center, thereby responding to the inexhaustible. This means cycling without end and obtaining its ring center. The empty place in the ring center is the body, and endless cycling is its function. The Poetry Commentary says: the large one is called hong. The small one is called yan. An envoy of the Western Han said to the Chanyu, The Son of Heaven shot in Shanglin and got a goose, and on its foot Su Wu had tied a letter. Because of this the Chanyu did not dare deceive him. Han's Cai Bojie had a daughter named Yan, style Wenji, wife of Dong Si. At the frontier there was disorder. While Si was on patrol he was seized by tribesmen, and Yan became consort to their king. Longing for home, she wrote a letter and sealed it in wax pellet and tied it to a goose's neck. When the goose reached Han territory, it drank water, the pellet fell, and a fish swallowed it. A fisher man cut open the fish and got the letter, thus learning where Yan was. In this verse, Night travel is not allowed; at dawn you must arrive. One must never spread family shame abroad by recklessly sending messages. Even so, to report upward to Tiantong, just now the attendant thanked him for transmitting Dharma instruction.

text_en: who had formerly discussed old and new matters with him, was inwardly angered and immediately led a group specially to Fuzhou to challenge him. Fayan, knowing this, led the assembly out to greet them and gave special courtesy, receiving them as guests. In host and guest seats, each hung a whisk. During tea, Zhao suddenly changed expression and loudly said, Elder, when you opened the hall, whose lineage did you inherit? The master said, Dizang. Zhao said, Why so greatly wrong former teacher Changqing? I was together under him for several decades, discussing ancient and current matters, never with any gap between us. Why then did you instead inherit Dizang? This matter is not in many years, nor is it in long study. As with Yisu Jue and Gaoting Jian, how could outsiders judge and measure? Head monk Zhao, taking sides to protect his school style, could not discuss the matter and only raised slander. Fa yan at that time deeply pitied these people who did not understand the great method, and wrote the Treatise on Ten Regulations to admonish them. Students must not fail to read it. Human sentiment and the power of the Way differ as widely as heaven and earth. Therefore he answered him with the matter of his own portion, saying, I do not understand one turning word and its causal nexus. This is the bearing of one from a great house, not debating and not contending. Yet Zhao took what they had formerly long discussed under Changqing and used it as proof. Because Fayan treated him by the old friendship, once pressed a little, Zhao split apart in all directions. His attendants rushed to rescue him, making it look even more unbearable. It may be said that in rout they could not withstand even a broom of reeds. Zhao and the group withdrew in shame. Fayan then somewhat checked them and stopped them, saying, Head monk, killing father or mother still allows repentance, but slandering Great Prajna is truly hard to repent. Zhao in the end had no reply. From then on he instead studied under Fayan, and clarified his own understanding, and never again opened a hall. The ancients answered evil with goodness, anger with compassion, and then with the equal wisdom of Buddha brought people forth. Even if this head monk Zizhao later inherited Fayan, it still was not enough to repay that deep virtue and wash clean his original intention. The Avatamsaka Sutra says: There is a great scripture scroll, equal in measure to the three thousand worlds, within a single mote of dust. All dust motes are likewise. There is a clear eyed person who breaks the dust and brings out the scripture scroll, benefiting and saving all people. Tiantong draws on two great scriptures and gathers them into one paired verse. As for sweeping away the myriad forms, tell me, who are the myriad forms the myriad appearances. Uniquely exposed, who is uniquely exposed? This is a ready-made koan. The family style is always preserved. Who would further set up gates and courtyards, open doors and windows? In the Huayan school, three boats viewing the moon each follow their own boat. Traveling one course, the clear river for a thousand li answers alone. In Huichong's poem: The river divides, the ridge's force is cut off. Spring enters and the burn marks turn green. In Xie Xuanhui's poem: The remaining glow scatters into brocade; the clear river is pure like white silk. The moon follows three boats, spring follows the hundred grasses. The three boats and hundred grasses are the myriad appearances. The moon and spring are what is uniquely exposed. In Tiantong's verse, seeing whether to brush away or not brush away, there is much rough mindedness. Here one should only be careful and detailed in admonition. Have you not seen? Senior monk Zifang also came from Changqing to Fayan. Fayan also brought up the earlier saying and asked; Fang also raised the whisk. Yan said: If it is like this, how can it do? Fang said: What is the honored meaning of the master? Yan said: What do you call the myriad appearances? Fang said: The ancients did not brush away the myriad appearances. Yan said: Amid the myriad appearances, the body is uniquely exposed. What talk is there of brushing away or not brushing away? Fang suddenly awakened. In Fayan's earlier saying at the end he said, Amid the myriad appearances, the body is uniquely exposed, eh? At the end of this saying he further said, Amid the myriad appearances, the body is uniquely exposed; what talk is there of brushing away or not brushing away? It can be said, wishing to leave, then return. Returning, one then attains. Reckoned out, the field is bitterly not much. Master Zhao and Master Fang, in the end, though subtle, missed the source. It is the fault of turbid intellect spinning on. In Tao Yuanming's Return Home: The three paths are nearly overgrown, yet pines and chrysanthemums still remain. Jiang Xu, styled Yuanqing, opened three paths, and only Yang Zhong and Qiu Zhong came and went as friends. This verse praises Fayan's meeting the school through the words, and opens forth the marvel of the two masters without losing Changqing's intent. What is Changqing's intent? The myriad appearances amid which the body is uniquely exposed.

Shoushan then stepped down and left. The attendant entered the room and asked for instruction, saying: Why did Nian Fahua not answer the master? Fengxue said: Nian Fahua understood. Next day Shoushan and head gardener Zhen stood attending together. Fengxue said: How is it that the World-Honored One spoke without speaking? Guanghui of Ruzhou. True indeed. Zhen said: The turtledove cries atop the tree; its meaning is in the hemp field. Fengxue said: What use is it for you to make so much foolish blessing? Why not investigate the words and phrases? He then asked Shoushan: What do you make of it? Shoushan said: In stirring countenance he reveals the ancient road; he does not fall into the silent mechanism. Fengxue said to Zhen: Why do you not look at Nian Fahua's reply? Later, after Shoushan came forth in the world, he ascended the hall and said: If you want intimacy, do not bring a question. The question is in the place of the answer; the answer is in the place of the question. If you bring a question, this old monk is under your feet. If you deliberate, there is no connection. One day he held up a bamboo comb and said: If you call it a bamboo comb, you hit it; if you do not call it a bamboo comb, you turn away from it. All of you, what will you call it? Master Sheng of Yexian snatched it and broke it into two pieces, threw it down the steps, and then said: What is this? Shoushan said: Blind fellow! Xian then bowed. Various places call this the barrier of turning away and hitting. A common saying goes: Upside down, topsy-turvy: the bride rides the donkey, the mother-in-law leads it. Foguo's verse says: Shoushan has a saying, through old and modern times transmitted. Do not say this saying is merely upside-down inversion. The bride, drunk, rides the donkey away; at that time people laugh the mother-in-law to death as she leads it. It is not like Tiantong's verse, which is delightfully apt. The verse says:
The bride rides the donkey, the mother-in-law leads; in form and style the grace is perfectly natural. No need to bring up grasses and trees. It cannot be sketched,

text_zh: 師云。筠州九峯道虔禪師。福州官懷人。姓劉 氏。雖遍經法席。而受印于石霜。初住九峯。玄 徒尤盛。後居洪州泐潭而終。勅諡大覺。一日 僧問。如何是頭。若是道眼不通明。差別智不 具。論箇頭尾先後。心懵然不知下落。峯云。 開眼不覺曉。曾有僧問。人人盡言請益。未審。 師將何法拯濟。峯云。汝道鉅嶽還曾乏寸土 麼。僧云。恁麼則四海參尋。當為何事。峯云。 演若迷頭心自狂。僧云。還有不狂者麼。峯云。 有。僧云。如何是不狂者。峯云。突曉途中眼不 開。這箇便是開眼。不覺曉底榜樣。僧云。如何 是尾。峯云。不坐萬年床。又有僧問。如何是然 燈前。峯云。勤勞不得力。僧云。如何是正然 燈。峯云。頭大尾小。僧云。如何是然燈後。峯 云。退位不知閑。此是不坐萬年床底榜樣也。 僧云。有頭無尾時如何。峯云。終是不貴。開眼 覺曉也。僧云。有尾無頭時如何。峯云。雖飽無 力。退位知閑也。僧云。直得頭尾相稱時如何。 峯云。兒孫得力。飽而有力也。室內不知。終 是尊貴也。宗鏡錄曰。入吾宗中先須知有。然 後保任。又曰。頭尾須得相稱。不可理行有闕。 心口相違。若入宗鏡。理行俱圓。石霜九峯師 也。示眾云。初機未搆大事。先須識取頭。其 尾自至。疎山出問。如何是頭。霜曰。直須知 有。疎曰。如何是尾。霜曰。盡却今時。疎曰。有 頭無尾時如何。霜曰。吐得黃金堪作甚麼。疎 曰。有尾無頭時如何。霜曰。猶有依倚在。疎 曰。直得頭尾相稱時如何。霜曰。渠不作箇會 解。亦未許渠在。故九峯曰。諸上座古人說箇 頭。也只令汝知有。說箇尾只教汝盡却今時。 有如許多不相應底事。所以教汝向這裏。屏 當却銷磨却。令汝今日相應去成辦去。若是 當人體爾。真實恒如。不可更恁麼說話也。雖 然如是。須是箇人始得。且莫異口同音。快須 努力珍重。萬松以九峯公案。證九峯公案。注 也注了。說也說破。其餘意味分付天童。頌云。
text_en: Though he had gone through the Dharma seats everywhere, he received the seal from Shishuang. At first he resided at Jiufeng, and dark-clad disciples were especially numerous. Later he lived at Letan in Hongzhou and died there. By imperial decree he was posthumously named Great Awakening. One day a monk asked, What is the head? If one's eye of the Way is not clear and penetrating, and discriminating wisdom is not complete, then when speaking of head and tail, before and after, the mind is muddled and does not know where it lands. Jiufeng said: Opening the eyes, one does not notice dawn. Once a monk asked: Everyone speaks of seeking instruction, but I do not yet know, by what Dharma does the master save and aid? Jiufeng said: Tell me, has a great mountain ever lacked an inch of earth? The monk said: If so, then why do people all over the world come in search? Jiufeng said: Yajnadatta lost his head and his mind went mad by itself. The monk said: Is there one who is not mad? Jiufeng said: There is. The monk said: What is the one who is not mad? Jiufeng said: On the road at break of dawn, the eyes do not open. This is precisely the model of opening the eyes and not noticing dawn. The monk said: What is the tail? Jiufeng said: Not sitting on the ten-thousand-year bed. Another monk asked: What is before the lamp is lit? Jiufeng said: Toil and labor, yet no strength. The monk said: What is the proper lighting of the lamp? Jiufeng said: Head large, tail small. The monk said: What is after the lamp is lit? Jiufeng said: Having withdrawn from position, one does not know leisure. This is the model of not sitting on the ten-thousand-year bed. The monk said: When there is head without tail, how is it? Jiufeng said: In the end it is not precious. Opening the eyes and noticing dawn, that is it. The monk said: When there is tail without head, how is it? Jiufeng said: Though full, there is no strength. Having withdrawn from position and knowing leisure, that is it. The monk said: If one reaches where head and tail match, how is it? Jiufeng said: Sons and grandsons gain strength, full and yet strong. Within the room it is not known; in the end it is noble and precious. The Record of the Source Mirror says: Entering our school, first one must know there is this. Then afterward preserve and foster it. It also says: Head and tail must be proportionate; principle and practice must not be lacking. Mind and mouth must not contradict each other. If one enters the Source Mirror, principle and practice are both complete. Shishuang was Jiufeng's teacher, and he instructed the assembly saying: Beginners who have not yet grasped the great matter must first recognize the head. The tail will come by itself. Shushan came forth and asked: What is the head? Shishuang said: You must directly know that there is this. Shu said: What is the tail? Shishuang said: Exhaust this present time. Shu said: When there is head without tail, how is it? Shishuang said: Even if you spit out gold, what can it be used for? Shu said: When there is tail without head, how is it? Shishuang said: There is still something relied upon. Shu said: If one reaches where head and tail match, how is it? Shishuang said: He does not make an understanding of it, yet still I do not approve him. Therefore Jiufeng said: Worthies, when the ancients spoke of the head, it was only to make you know there is this. When they spoke of the tail, it was only to teach you to exhaust the present time. There are so many things in you that do not correspond, therefore they teach you here to set aside, block off, and wear them away, so that today you may become corresponding and complete the matter. If it is your own body realizing it, truly and constantly thus, then such talk can no longer be used. Even so, it must be the right person for it to work. Do not merely share one sound with different mouths. You must quickly make effort and take care. Wansong uses Jiufeng's koan to verify Jiufeng's koan. The commentary is already commented; the saying has already been fully explained. The remaining flavor is entrusted to Tiantong. The verse says:

text_zh: 師云。縱橫得妙。左右逢原底人。莊子所謂。 圓者中規。方者中矩。子謂顏淵曰。用之則行。 舍之則藏。唯我與爾有是夫。如其不然。則膠 柱調絃。刻舟記劍也。寶藏論。夫進脩之由。中 有萬途。困魚止泊。鈍鳥棲蘆。其二者不識於 大海。不識於叢林。人趣乎小道。其義亦然。周 易大壯卦。上六羝羊觸藩。不能退。不能進。無 攸利。艱則吉。喫別人家飯。臥自己床。如云喫 官飯放私駝。又云解將冷口喫人熱食者。難 得出則為雲為雨。入則氷結霜凝。此乃乍出 乍入。未是作家。直得針線貫通。毫芒綿密。機 絲不挂。文彩縱橫。正當石女機停時。已早木 人路轉。正當夜色向午處。已早月影移央。此 末後兩句。只是一句。今時儒學文章士。謂之 隔句對。萬松恁麼離堅合異。要與天童相見。 諸人不得辜負九峯。
text_en: The round accords with the compass, the square accords with the rule. The Master said to Yan Yuan: Used, one goes; set aside, one hides. Only you and I have this. If not so, then it is like gluing the tuning pegs to tune the strings, or notching a boat to mark a sword. The Treatise on the Precious Treasury says: As for the path of advancing in cultivation, within it there are ten thousand routes. A trapped fish comes to rest in shallow water; a dull bird perches in reeds. These two do not know the great sea, nor do they know the forest. When people head toward petty paths, the meaning is likewise so. In the Zhou Changes, the hexagram Great Strength, top six: the ram butts the fence, unable to retreat, unable to advance. There is no advantage. In difficulty there is good fortune. Eating another's rice and lying on one's own bed is like saying, eating government rice while tending one's private camel. It is also said: One who knows how to use a cold mouth to eat another's hot food is hard to find. Coming out, one becomes cloud and rain; going in, ice forms and frost congeals. This is merely just coming out and just going in, not yet the work of a true master. One must reach the point where needle and thread pass through, fine hairs are close-knit, and the loom's silk does not snag, while pattern and color spread freely. Just when the stone woman's loom stops, already the wooden man's road has turned. Just when the night's color tends toward noon, already the moon's shadow has shifted past center. These final two lines are really one line. Scholars of Confucian learning and literature nowadays call this a separated-line pairing. Wansong, in this way separating what is joined and joining what is different, wants to meet Tiantong face to face. All of you must not let Jiufeng down.

text_zh: 師云。華嚴大疏首尾。清涼大師。科此段經。名 開因性。普賢行願疏。名開物性源。如何開耶。 出現品云。佛子無一眾生而不具有如來智 慧。但以妄想顛倒執著。而不證得注云凡夫妄想權小執著顛倒 通上二種若離妄想。一切智自然智無礙智。則得 現前。便舉一塵包含大千經卷之喻。前頌萬 象之中獨露身。離念見佛破塵出經。正是此 科經也。又云。爾時如來以無障礙清淨智眼。 普觀法界一切眾生。而作是言。奇哉奇哉。此 諸眾生。云何具有如來智慧。愚痴迷惑。不知 不見。我當教以正道。令其永離妄想執著。自 於身中得見如來廣大智慧。與佛無異。清涼 大疏云。眾生包性德而為體。攬智海以為源。 但相變體殊。情生智隔。今令知心合體。達本 忘情。故談斯經而為顯示。釋曰。此則兼明眾 生迷真之由也。譬如福德智慧具足相貌之 人。忽然夢見貧病苦身。即相變也。不見本身。 即體殊也。執認云是我身。即情生也。不信自 身福德端正。即智隔也。僧問報慈。情生智隔。 相變體殊。情未生時如何。慈云。隔。諸方罔知 出處。多以相為想。就便辨之。學者應知。仰山 勘香嚴。如來禪許師兄會。祖師禪未夢見在。 且道。如來禪相去多少。試將華嚴經文。參我 天童頌意。頌云。
text_en: opening the causal nature. In the Commentary on Samantabhadra's Practices and Vows, it is called opening the source of beings' nature. How is it opened? The Appearance chapter says: Children of Buddha, there is not a single sentient being that does not possess the Tathagata's wisdom. Only because of deluded thinking, inversion, and attachment, they do not realize it. If they depart from deluded thinking, all-knowledge, natural wisdom, and unobstructed wisdom then Note says ordinary folk have delusive thoughts; the provisional and lesser cling in inversion This applies to the two kinds above appear before them. Then it raises the analogy of one mote of dust containing the scripture scrolls of a great thousand worlds. The earlier verse on the myriad appearances and the uniquely exposed body, seeing Buddha apart from thought, breaking the dust and bringing forth the sutra, is exactly this scriptural section. It also says: At that time the Tathagata, with unobstructed and pure wisdom-eyes, universally surveyed all beings in the Dharma realm and spoke these words: Wondrous indeed, wondrous indeed! These sentient beings, how is it that they possess the Tathagata's wisdom, yet in foolish delusion they do not know and do not see? I shall teach them the right path, causing them forever to leave deluded thoughts and attachments, and themselves Within one’s own body one can see the Tathagata’s vast great wisdom, no different from the Buddha’s. Qingliang in the Great Commentary says: Sentient beings take inherent virtue as their substance and gather the sea of wisdom as their source. Only the appearances change and the substance differs; feeling arises and wisdom is separated. Now this teaches one to know the mind and unite with the substance, to realize the root and forget feeling. Therefore this scripture is spoken in order to make it manifest. Explanation says: This also explains the reason sentient beings are deluded about the true. It is like a person of complete blessings, virtue, wisdom, and fine appearance who suddenly dreams of a poor, sick, suffering body; that is appearance changed. Not seeing the original body, that is substance differing. Clinging to it and taking it as my body, that is feeling arising. Not believing one’s own body is blessed, virtuous, and upright, that is wisdom being cut off. A monk asked Bao-ci, Feeling arises and wisdom is cut off; appearance changes and substance differs. Before feeling arises, how is it? Ci said, Cut off. Monasteries everywhere did not know the source of this. Many take appearance to mean thought; so I clarify it here. Students should know. Yangshan tested Xiangyan: Tathagata Zen I allow elder brother understands; Patriarchs’ Zen you have not yet even dreamed of. Tell me, how far apart is Tathagata Zen?
