text_zh: 師云。巖頭道。直須向自己胸襟流出。將來與 我蓋天蓋地。今言天蓋地載。何其顛倒也。蓋 就人情而言之。人情皆謂天地生人。謂之三 才。佛教反以人生天地。所以三界唯心萬法 唯識。這裏打做一團。鍊做一塊。周法界無邊 表。楞嚴經。佛告阿難。汝觀地性。麁為大地。 細為微塵。至隣虛塵。析彼極微色邊際相。七 分所成。更析隣虛。即實空性。萬松常舉。信心 銘。極小同大。忘絕境界。極大同小。不見邊 表。或有人問世間何物最大。當曰真空。何以 故極大同小。不見邊表故。或有人問世間何 物最小。當曰真空。何以故極小同大。忘絕境 界故。嗚呼三祖何人哉。出一則語。天下衲僧 跳不出。僧問趙州。如何是玄中玄。州云。汝玄 來多少時也。僧云。玄之久矣。州云。若不是老 僧幾乎玄殺。洞山玄中銘。向道莫去。歸來背 父。既周法界。打成一塊。豈勞塵外別有玄微。 豈有前後向背。佛不出世。也不曾減。佛出世 指示演說。也不曾添。譽海之寬。誇日之明。 不足可言。並為增語。南泉杉山。普請擇蕨菜 次。南泉拈起一莖曰。這箇大好供養杉山云。 非但這箇。百味珍羞。他亦不顧。南泉云。雖然 如是。箇箇須甞過始得。大陽明安。上堂云。莫 行心處路。莫坐無處功。有無二俱離。廓然天 地空。所以南泉道。大家喫一莖菜。更覓一莖 入地獄如箭射。萬松道。今日人七。
text_en: cover heaven and cover earth. Now it says heaven covers and earth bears, how upside down it is. Covering is spoken according to human convention. People all say heaven and earth give birth to man, calling them the three powers. Buddhism instead takes man as giving birth to heaven and earth. Therefore the three realms are mind-only and the myriad dharmas are consciousness-only. Here they are beaten into one lump, forged into one clod, pervading the Dharma realm with no boundary or outer mark. In the Surangama Sutra the Buddha told Ananda: Observe the nature of earth; coarse, it is the great earth. Fine, it is minute dust. Reaching adjacent-void dust, analyze the boundary-form of that utmost subtle matter; it is made of seven parts. Further divide adjacent-void dust and it is in truth empty nature. Wansong often cited the Faith in Mind Inscription: The extremely small is the same as the great, forgetting all boundaries; the extremely great is the same as the small, no boundary is seen. If someone asks what is greatest in the world, one should say true emptiness. Why? Because the extremely great is the same as the small, so no boundary is seen. If someone asks what is smallest in the world, one should say true emptiness. Why? Because the extremely small is the same as the great, forgetting all bounds and realms. Ah, what kind of person was the Third Patriarch? He uttered one saying, and the patch-robed monks of the world cannot jump out of it. A monk asked Zhaozhou: What is the mystery within mystery? Zhou said: How long have you been mysterious? The monk said: Mysterious for a long time. Zhou said: If not for this old monk, you would almost be killed by mystery. Dongshan’s Inscription on the Mystery Within says: As you go, do not depart; returning, do not turn your back on the source. Since it pervades the Dharma realm and is beaten into one clod, why toil to seek some separate subtle mystery beyond the dust? How could there be before and after, toward and away? Before Buddhas appeared in the world, it was never diminished. When Buddhas appeared in the world and pointed out and expounded it, it was never increased. Praising the ocean’s breadth or boasting of the sun’s brightness is not worth speaking of; all are added words. Nanquan and Shanshan, in a communal work period picking bracken greens, at that time, Nanquan picked up one stalk and said: This is excellent for an offering. Shanshan said: Not only this one; a hundred flavors of delicacies he also would not regard. Nanquan said: Even so, each and every one must be tasted before it is so. Dayang Ming-an ascended the hall and said: Do not travel the road of mind-made places. Do not sit in the achievement of nowhere. Being and nonbeing both left behind, vast and open, heaven and earth are empty. Therefore Nanquan said: Everyone eats a single stalk of greens. Seek one more stalk, and you enter hell like an arrow shot. Wansong said: Today’s people are seven parts...

text_zh: 68 夾山揮劍
text_en: 68 Jiashan Wields the Sword Addressing the assembly, he said: Within the realm, the Son of Heaven issues edicts; beyond the frontier, the general gives commands. Sometimes at the gate

text_zh: 示眾云。寰中天子勅。閫外將軍令。有時門頭 得力。有時室內稱尊。且道。是甚麼人。
text_en: there is power; sometimes within the room one is called the honored one. Tell me, who is this?
Raised: A monk asked Jiashan, When brushing away dust and seeing Buddha, how is it? Shan said: Why must it be so

text_zh: 舉。僧問夾山。撥塵見佛時如何何必。山云。 直須揮劍果然。若不揮劍漁父棲巢坐則非佛。僧 舉。問石霜。撥塵見佛時如何見即不撥撥即不見霜云 渠無國土。何處逢渠不坐即佛僧迴舉似夾山往來 不易山上堂云。門庭施設不如老僧。入理深 談猶較石霜百步各得一橛。
text_en: You must directly wield the sword. If you do not wield the sword, a fisherman will nest there. The monk Just so indeed If sitting, then not Buddha then raised this and asked Shishuang, When brushing away dust and seeing Buddha, how is it? Shuang said: If seen, do not stir it; if stirred, it is not seen He has no country; where will you meet him? The monk returned and reported this to Jiashan. Jiashan ascended the hall and said: In gate-front arrangements he does not match this old monk; in deep talk of entering principle Not sitting, then Buddha Coming and going Not easy he is still a hundred paces beyond Shishuang. Each gets a stake
The teacher said: Chan Master Shishuang Qingzhu of Tanzhou was at first rice steward at Weishan.

text_zh: 師云。潭州石霜慶諸禪師。初在溈山充米頭。 方篩米次。溈曰。施主物不可拋棄。霜曰。不拋 棄。溈於地拾一粒示之曰。爾道不拋棄。這箇 甚處得來。師無對。溈曰。莫欺這一粒。百千粒 從這一粒生。霜曰。然則這一粒。自何處生。溈 大笑歸方丈。晚上堂曰。大眾米裏有蟲。後參 道吾。問觸目菩提。吾喚沙彌添淨瓶水。悟如 前舉。霜在道吾。兩夏而受印。會昌之厄。混跡 潭州瀏陽陶家坊。朝游夕處。大中初有僧。自 洞山至舉。洞山初秋夏末。兄弟或東或西。直 須向萬里無寸草處去。良久曰。只如萬里無 寸草處。又作麼生去。霜曰。出門便是草。僧復 舉似洞山。山曰。此是一千五百人善知識語。 且大唐國裏能有幾人。囊錐始露住石霜道 場。果符悟本之記。二十年海眾千餘。往往長 坐不臥。屹若株杌。枯木堂名自茲立焉。僧問 撥塵見佛。所問是一。夾山道。若不揮劍漁父 棲巢。石霜道。渠無國土何處逢渠。萬松道。入 理深談不如石霜。門庭施設猶較夾山百步。 莫有兩彩一賽底麼。天童道甚。頌云。
text_en: Once while sifting rice, Wei said: Donors’ goods must not be wasted. Shuang said: I am not wasting it. Wei picked up a grain from the ground and showed it, saying: You say you do not waste it. This one, where did it come from? The master had no reply. Wei said: Do not slight this one grain; hundreds of thousands of grains come from this one grain. Shuang said: Then this one grain, from where is it born? Wei laughed loudly and returned to the abbot’s quarters. That evening he ascended the hall and said: In the assembly’s rice there are bugs. Later he studied with Daowu and asked, Bodhi before the eyes. Wu called a novice to add water to the pure-water vase. He awakened as in the earlier cited case. Shuang was with Daowu for two summers and received the seal. During the Huichang persecution he hid his traces at Taojia Ward in Liuyang, Tanzhou, roaming by day and lodging by night. At the beginning of Dazhong, a monk came from Dongshan and recounted: At the end of summer, early autumn, Dongshan said, Brothers, whether east or west, you must directly go to a place where for ten thousand miles there is not an inch of grass. After a long pause he said, But if in a place for ten thousand miles with no inch of grass, how do you go? Shuang said: As soon as you go out the gate, it is grass. The monk again reported this to Dongshan. Shan said: This is the speech of a good teacher of fifteen hundred people. In the Great Tang, how many such men can there be? As the awl in the bag first showed its point, he took up residence at Shishuang’s monastery, truly matching Wuben’s prediction. For twenty years the ocean-like assembly numbered over a thousand, often practicing long sitting without lying down, rigid like stumps. The name Dead Tree Hall was established from this. A monk asked about brushing away dust and seeing Buddha; the question asked was one and the same. Jiashan said, If you do not wield the sword, a fisherman will nest there. Shishuang said, He has no country, where will you meet him? Wansong said: In deep talk of entering principle Jiashan is not equal to Shishuang; in gate-front arrangements Shishuang is still a hundred paces behind Jiashan. Is there no one who can match both colors in one contest? What did Tiantong say? The verse says:
The sword-energy brushes the Dipper and Ox, heaven washes the weapons; martial might settles disorder. To whom does the merit return, after all? Peace was originally brought by the general

text_zh: 拂牛劍氣洗兵威太平本是將軍致　定亂歸功更是誰 不許將軍見太平一旦氛埃清四海但盡凡情　垂衣皇化自 無為別無聖解
text_en: Yet the general is not allowed to see peace Once the dust and haze are cleared throughout the four seas, with robes hanging down the imperial transformation is of itself Just exhaust ordinary feelings effortless. There is no separate holy understanding
The teacher said: In the Linji school style, the vajra-king precious sword kills Buddha and kills patriarchs. Jiashan

text_zh: 師云。臨濟宗風。金剛王寶劍。殺佛殺祖。夾山 截斷老葛藤。打破狐窠窟。晉書。雷煥善天文。 張華因望斗牛間。常有異氣。邀煥。夜登樓仰 視。煥曰。僕察之久矣。寶劍之精上於天。在豫 章酆城縣界。華乃薦雷。為鄷城令。修獄掘基。 得石匣。有雙劍。光甚艶發。送一與華。留一自 佩。華被誅失劍。煥卒子為州從事。佩父劍至 延平津。劍躍墮水。使人投之。見兩龍有文章。 投者懼迴。說苑。武王伐紂遇雨。散宜生曰。此 非妖歟。王曰。非也。天洗兵也。此頌若不揮劍 漁父棲巢。易曰。黃帝堯舜垂衣裳。而治天下。 無為之化不令而行。此頌無巢可棲。渠無國 土。無劍可揮。何處逢渠也。同安察禪師道。妙 體本來無處所。通身那更有蹤由。萬松道。許 爾親見石霜。猶較夾山百步。要見夾山麼。劍 為不平離寶匣。藥因投病出金瓶。
text_en: cuts off old vines and smashes fox dens. In the Jin History, Lei Huan was skilled in astronomy. Zhang Hua observed that between the Dipper and Ox there was often a strange vapor, so he invited Huan, and at night they climbed a tower and looked up. Huan said: I have observed it long. The essence of a precious sword rises to heaven; it is in the bounds of Fengcheng County in Yuzhang. Hua then recommended Lei as magistrate of Fengcheng. While repairing the jail and digging foundations, they found a stone casket with a pair of swords. Their light shone brilliantly. He sent one to Hua and kept one for himself to wear. Hua was executed and the sword was lost. After Huan died, his son, serving as a provincial officer, wore his father’s sword and came to Yanping Ford. The sword leapt and fell into the water. He sent someone to dive after it, and two dragons with patterned markings were seen. The diver, frightened, returned. In the Garden of Sayings, when King Wu attacked Zhou and met rain, San Yisheng said: This is not an omen? The king said: No, Heaven is washing the weapons. This verse on if one does not wield the sword and the fisherman nests. The Yi says: The Yellow Emperor, Yao, and Shun let their robes hang down and thereby ruled the world. The transformation of nonaction proceeds without command. This verse says there is no nest to perch in; he has no country. There is no sword to wield; where will you meet him? Chan Master Tong-an Cha said: The wondrous body originally has no place. Through the whole body there is no further trace or cause. Wansong said: I allow that you have personally seen Shishuang, yet you are still a hundred paces from Jiashan. Want to see Jiashan? The sword leaves the jeweled casket because of injustice; medicine comes out of the golden bottle because of the sickness cast before it.

text_zh: 69 南泉白牯
text_en: 69 Nanquan’s White Ox Addressing the assembly, he said: Becoming Buddhas and patriarchs is still burdened with a tainted name. Wearing horns and hair, one is instead placed

text_zh: 示眾云。成佛作祖。嫌帶污名。戴角披毛。推居 上位。所以真光不耀。大智若愚。更有箇便宜 聾。佯不采底。知是阿誰。
text_en: in the highest seat. Therefore true light does not shine, and great wisdom seems foolish. There is another convenient one, deaf and pretending not to notice. Do you know who it is?
Raised: Nanquan addressed the assembly saying: The Buddhas of the three times do not know there is the fox-slave Only because one knows there is

text_zh: 舉。南泉示眾云。三世諸佛不知有只為知有狸 奴白牯却知有只為不知有。
text_en: white ox, yet the white ox does know there is. Only because one does not know there is
The teacher said: Dharma Master Jiezhu of Feishan wrote Discussion on the Mind-Dharma of Separate Transmission and criticized Nanquan,

text_zh: 師云。飛山法師戒珠。作別傳心法議。毀斥南 泉曰。若願輩。不嗜學不知本。不足以語如來 教。無盡燈附集依通。率易辯敘南泉初習律。 次聽華嚴楞伽。入中百門觀。聞馬祖傳言外 道。屢扣其旨頓獲忘筌。一日行粥。馬祖問。桶 裏是甚麼。泉曰。這老漢合取口。作恁麼語話。 泉臨機不讓馬祖。如此後來。却向趙州手裏 償債。泉問座主。涅盤經以何為極則。主曰。 以如如為極則。泉云。喚作如如早是變也。今 時沙門須向異類中行始得。趙州於僧堂前 問。異則不問。如何是類。泉乃兩手托地。州以 脚一踏。泉便倒地。州走入延壽寮。叫云悔悔。 泉令侍者問州。悔箇甚麼。州云。悔不更與兩 踏。泉上堂云。王老師自小。養一頭水牯牛。擬 向溪東牧。不免食他國家水草。溪西牧亦不 免食他國家水草。如今不免隨分納些子。總 不見得。泉一日見浴主燒浴云。齋後請水牯 牛浴。浴主去請。泉云。將得繩索來麼。州以手 拽泉鼻。泉云。是即是太麁生。州問。知有底人 向甚麼處去。泉云。向山前檀越家。作一頭水 牯牛去。州云。謝師指示。泉云。昨夜三更月到 窓。泉將順世。首座問。和尚百年後向何處去。 泉云。山下作一頭水牯牛去。座云。某甲隨和 尚去得否。泉云。汝若隨我。須㘅取一莖草來。 此異類話。南泉首唱。溈山和之。道吾雲巖傳 授。今為曹山三墮。道吾到南泉。泉問。闍梨名 甚麼。吾云。宗智。泉云。智不到處作麼生宗。 吾云。切忌道著。泉云。灼然道著即頭角生。三 日後與雲巖。在後架把針次。泉過乃問。前日 道智不到處切忌道著。道著即頭角生。合作 麼生行履。吾便抽身入僧堂。泉便去。巖問吾。 師弟適來為甚。不祗對和尚。吾云。爾得恁麼 靈利。巖不薦。却去問泉云。適來公案。智頭陀 作。麼不祗對和尚。泉云。他却是異類中行。巖 云。如何是異類中行。泉云。不見道。智不到處 切忌道著。道著即頭角生。直須向異類中行。 巖亦不會。吾知巖不薦乃云。此人緣不在此。 便同迴藥山。巖遂舉前話。山云。子作麼生。 會他這箇時節。便迴來。巖無對。山乃大笑。 巖便問。如何是異類中行。山云。吾今日困。 別時來。巖云。某甲特為此事歸來。山云。且 去。巖便出。吾在方丈外。聞巖不薦。不覺咬得 指頭血出。却下來問。師兄問和尚那因緣。作 麼生。巖云。和尚不為某甲說。吾便低頭。二人 侍立。山問智不到處切忌道著道著即頭角 生。吾便珍重出去。巖遂問山。智師弟為甚麼。 不祗對和尚。山云。我今日背痛。是他却會。爾 去問取。巖遂問。師弟適來為甚麼。不祗對和 尚。吾云。我今日頭痛。爾去問取和尚。后雲巖 遷化。遣人馳辭書至。吾覽後曰。雲巖不知有。 悔當時不向伊道。然雖如是。要且不違藥山 之子。玄覺云。古人恁麼道。還知有也未。雲巖 當時不會。甚麼處是不會處。翠巖芝云。道吾 道。雲巖不知有。悔當時不向伊道。只如恁麼 道。道吾還知有也無。萬松道。雲巖為洞山之 師。一派之源。再四再三。不知有此事。萬松具 錄。也要與後人傍。參助一半力。豈唯雲巖不 知有。翠巖芝道。道吾還知有也無。萬松道。非 但道吾。翠巖還知有也未。不見。僧問長沙。為 甚三世諸佛不知有。沙云。未入鹿苑時。猶較 些子。僧云。狸奴白牯。為甚麼却知有。沙云。 汝爭怪得伊。萬松到此只可傍觀。大小天童 讚歎有分。頌云。
text_en: saying: Men like Yuan do not delight in learning and do not know the root; they are unfit to speak of the Tathagata’s teaching. The Supplement to the Infinite Lamp, relying on common understanding, casually narrates that Nanquan first studied the Vinaya, then listened to Huayan and Lankavatara, entered the Hundred Gates Contemplation of the Middle, and hearing that Mazu transmitted a teaching beyond words, repeatedly questioned him on its meaning and suddenly attained forgetting the fish-trap. One day while serving gruel, Mazu asked: In the bucket what is there? Quan said: This old man ought to shut his mouth, speaking such words. Quan did not yield to Mazu in the moment; yet later he had to repay the debt in Zhaozhou’s hands. Quan asked a scripture-seat master: In the Nirvana Sutra, what is taken as the ultimate rule? The master said: Taking thusness as the ultimate rule. Quan said: Calling it thusness is already a change. Now a shramana must practice among other kinds before it will do. In front of the monks’ hall, Zhaozhou asked: I will not ask about other; what is kind? Quan then placed both hands on the ground. Zhou with his foot gave one stomp and Quan fell to the ground. Zhou ran into the infirmary, shouting: Regret, regret! Quan had an attendant ask Zhou: What do you regret? Zhou said: I regret not giving him two more stomps. Quan ascended the hall and said: Teacher Wang, from childhood, raised a water buffalo, intending to graze it east of the stream, but it could not avoid eating the state’s water and grass. Grazing it west of the stream also could not avoid eating the state’s water and grass. Now I cannot avoid paying some portion according to my share; in all, it cannot be seen. One day Quan saw the bath steward heating the bath and said: After the meal, invite the water buffalo to bathe. The bath steward went to invite it. Quan said: Did you bring rope? Zhou with his hand tugged Quan’s nose. Quan said: Yes indeed, but it is too rough. Zhou asked: A person who knows there is, where does he go? Quan said: To the donor’s house before the mountain, to become a water buffalo. Zhou said: Thanks for the master’s instruction. Quan said: Last night at the third watch the moon came to the window. As Quan was about to accord with the world and pass away, the head monk asked: After the master’s hundred years, where will you go? Quan said: Below the mountain, I will become a water buffalo. The head monk said: May I follow the master or not? Quan said: If you follow me, you must bring a single stalk of grass. This talk of other kinds was first sung by Nanquan, echoed by Weishan, and transmitted by Daowu and Yunyan. Now it became Caoshan’s three falls. Daowu came to Nanquan. Quan asked: What is your name, Reverend? Wu said: Zongzhi. Quan said: Where wisdom does not reach, how do you make lineage there? Wu said: By all means avoid speaking of it. Quan said: Exactly; if spoken of, horns at once grow. Three days later, while with Yunyan in the back room threading a needle, Quan passed by and asked: The other day we said where wisdom does not reach, avoid speaking of it; if spoken of, horns grow. How should one practice and conduct oneself? Wu immediately withdrew into the monks’ hall. Quan then left. Yan asked Wu: Brother, why just now did you not answer the master? Wu said: You are so quick and sharp. Yan did not get it, and went to ask Quan: In the case just now, why did Head-Monk Zhi not answer the master? Quan said: He is one who walks among other kinds. Yan said: What is walking among other kinds? Quan said: Did you not hear it said? Where wisdom does not reach, by all means avoid speaking of it. If spoken of, horns grow. You must directly walk among other kinds. Yan still did not understand. Wu, knowing Yan did not get it, said: This person’s affinity is not here. So they returned together to Yaoshan. Yan then raised the previous story. Shan said: How do you understand him at such a moment, that you came back? Yan had no reply. Shan then laughed loudly. Yan then asked: What is walking among other kinds? Shan said: I am tired today. Come another time. Yan said: I came back specially for this matter. Shan said: Just go for now. Yan then went out. Wu was outside the abbot’s quarters; hearing Yan did not get it, he unconsciously bit his finger until blood came out. Then he came down and asked: Elder brother, in that exchange when you asked the master, how did it go? Yan said: The master would not explain it for me. Wu then lowered his head. The two stood attending. Shan asked about where wisdom does not reach, avoid speaking of it, if spoken of horns grow. Wu then bowed and withdrew. Yan then asked Shan: Why did Brother Zhi not answer the master? Shan said: My back hurts today. He is the one who understands. You go ask him. Yan then asked: Brother, why just now did you not answer the master? Wu said: My head hurts today. Go ask the master. Later Yunyan passed away and sent a messenger with a farewell letter. After reading it, Wu said: Yunyan did not know there is. He regretted that at the time he had not said it to him. Even so, still it did not go against Yaoshan ’s lineage. Xuanjue said: When the ancients spoke thus, did they know it or not? Yunyan did not understand at the time. Where exactly was the place of not understanding? Cuiyan Zhi said: Daowu said Yunyan did not know it, and regretted not telling him then. But speaking this way, did Daowu himself know it or not? Wansong said: Yunyan was Dongshan’s teacher, the source of one whole branch. Again and again, he did not know of this matter. Wansong records it in full also to help later people from the side, lending half their effort in inquiry. Is it only Yunyan who did not know it? Cuiyan Zhi said: Did Daowu know it or not? Wansong said: Not only Daowu alone, did Cuiyan know it or not? Have you not seen a monk ask Changsha: Why do the Buddhas of the three times not know it? Changsha said: Before entering Deer Park, they were still somewhat closer. The monk said: Then why do the cat and the white ox know it? Changsha said: How can you blame them for it? At this point Wansong can only stand by and watch. Great or small, Tiantong has a share in praising it. The verse says:

text_en: said: Master, stop making monkeys of people. Yaoshan rolled up the sutra and said: What time of day is it now? He said: The sun is right at noon. Yaoshan said: You still have this bit of literary polish. He said: I have none at all. Yaoshan said: You are greatly airing your cleverness. He said: I am only thus; what is the venerable master’s meaning? Yaoshan said: I limp and drag along, with a hundred uglinesses, a thousand clumsinesses, and just get by like this. Guanxi Xian’s verse says: Shaken out for many years, this tattered robe half its threads frayed away chasing the clouds. I pick it up and throw it over my shoulders; still better than people of the time wearing brocade. In a hundred ways not worth taking, fit for nothing; among the assembly, just like a hundred clumsy ones, all life long he is an idle man. Silently he himself knows the ground is stable; easygoing, who says his belly is stupid? Wang Fanzhi wrote it in reverse, and people all said it was wrong. Better to stab your eyes than hide my feet. Wang Fanzhi was a strange man; these words spread widely among people. It may be called a skin lantern-ball, bright within and dark without. In the final line of the verse, full practice reaches the ground of rotten odds and ends; on eyebrows and eyelashes are all grains of rice. One day when the scabby belly bursts open, all the five viscera and heart-liver are spewed out.

The master said: Chan Master Hongjin, head of Qingxi Mountain in Xiangzhou, was the chief seat under Master Dizang Chen

text_zh: 師云。襄州清溪山主洪進禪師。為地藏琛和 尚第一座。時有二僧俱禮地藏。藏曰。俱錯。 二僧並無語。下請益脩山主。主曰。汝自巍巍 堂堂却禮拜他人。豈不是錯。進聞之不肯曰。 汝自迷暗焉可為人。脩憤然上堂頭請益。藏 指廊下曰。典座入庫下去也。脩乃省過。進一 日問脩曰。明知生不生性。為甚麼。為生之所 留。菴提遮女。婆羅門種。舍衛城西二十餘里 長提村婆私膩長者女也。因家作大會。命佛 及僧。提遮故得振其嘉聲焉。文殊大士問頗 有明知生不生相前作性為生所留者否。女曰。有 之。雖自明見。其力未充。而為生所留者是也。 脩山主答筍畢竟成竹去。而今作篾使得麼。 篾竹皮束物竹索也。筍嫰無力。蒼竹有力。筍 力未充。不堪作蔑。覺範觀音贊。憫我心明力 不迨。時時種子發現行。如人因酒而發狂。戒 飲輒復逢嘉醞。此亦言其力未充也。慚愧古 人熟爛教乘。出辭吐氣。與脩多羅合。進山主 要拈轉話頭。方復不許道。汝向後自悟去在。 脩曰。某甲見處只如此。上座意旨如何。脩公 先向四平八滿處坐定。進公遣起必然別有 一條活路。遂指道。這箇是監院房。那箇是典 座房。且道。明得生不生性。明不得生不生性。 且道。為生所留。不為生所留。脩便禮拜。他參 活句不參死句。此與典座入庫下去也。更無 兩樣。諸方皆言法眼下一味平實。體中玄。請 看前話。天童見此話出格奇特。所以盡情徹 底頌出。頌云。
text_en: and served as first seat. At that time two monks both bowed to Dizang. Dizang said: Both are wrong. The two monks had no reply. Later they asked Head Monk Xiu for instruction. He said: You yourselves are majestic and upright, yet you bow to someone else; is that not wrong? Jin heard this and did not agree, saying: You yourself are confused and dark; how can you guide others? Xiu, indignant, went to the hall to ask. Dizang pointed to the corridor and said: The cook has gone down into the storehouse. Xiu then awakened. One day Jin asked Xiu: Clearly knowing the nature of birth and non-birth, why is one still detained by birth? Amtizhe Woman was of Brahmin stock, the daughter of elder Posi-ni, in Changti Village over twenty li west of Shravasti. Because her household held a great assembly, they invited the Buddha and the sangha, and so Tizhe’s good name was widely renowned. Great Bodhisattva Manjushri asked whether there were any who clearly know the marks of birth and non-birth yet are detained by birth. The woman said: There are. Previously taken as nature Though they see it clearly themselves, their strength is not yet full, and so they are detained by birth. Head Monk Xiu answered: Shoots in the end become bamboo, but can they be used as strips right now? Bamboo strips are bamboo skin used to bind things, bamboo cords. Shoots are tender and lack strength; mature bamboo has strength. A shoot’s strength is not yet full, so it cannot serve as binding strips. In Juefan’s Hymn to Guanyin: Pity me, my mind is clear but my strength does not reach it; again and again old seeds manifest in action. Like a man who goes mad from wine, though he forbids drinking, he keeps encountering fine brew. This too speaks of strength not yet full. For shame, the ancients had the teachings thoroughly digested; in every word and breath they matched the sutras. Head Monk Jinshan wanted to turn the saying around, so he would not allow it and said: Later on, you yourself will realize it. Xiu said: My understanding is only this. What is the venerable one’s intent? Master Xiu had first settled himself in a place all even and complete. Master Jin, making him rise, surely had another living road. So he pointed and said: This is the steward’s room; that is the cook’s room. Tell me then: Does this clearly know the nature of birth and non-birth, or not clearly know it? Tell me also: Is it detained by birth, or not detained by birth? Xiu then bowed. He studied the living phrase, not the dead phrase. This and The cook has gone down into the storehouse are no different. Everywhere they say the Fayan school is uniformly plain and real, mysterious within the body. Please look at the foregoing story. Tiantong saw this saying as extraordinary and unique, so he fully and thoroughly brought it out in verse. The verse says:

text_zh: 師云。此頌進山主這箇是監院房。那箇是典 座房。亡依倚時自然廓落。不羈縻處法爾高 閑。平怗家邦幾人能到。須是無煩惱可斷。無 禪道可參。十二時中除著衣喫飯是閑用心 處。據進公問意。亦微有徵古驗今分階級。定 力量底鉤線。然其蕩蕩身心。本絕是非也。脩 公也不妨會如來禪平實商量本分說話。爭 奈百丈道。依經解義三世佛冤。所以微分力 量。權立階梯。道筍則嫰無力用。竹則篾引千 鈞。言迹之興也。是非所以成。進公為渠剗却。 別指生機一路。殊非開戶牖立軌轍欺誣道 伴。脩公設拜以謝不敏。還識二公當家鑪鞴 麼。入火更須精鍛鍊。上砧方耐重鉆鎚。
text_en: cook’s room means: when reliance is gone, there is naturally openness; where nothing binds, there is inherently lofty ease. How many can reach the level and peaceful homeland? One must have no afflictions to cut off, no Zen path to investigate. In the twelve hours of the day, apart from putting on clothes and eating, this is the place of idle mind-use. Judging from Master Jin’s question, there is also a slight tracing of old and testing of present, dividing stages and ranks, fixing lines and hooks of strength. Yet his vast and open body-mind is originally beyond right and wrong. Xiu also may indeed understand the Tathagata-Zen, in plain and straightforward discussion of fundamental talk. But as Baizhang said, To explain meaning by relying on scripture wrongs the Buddhas of the three times. Therefore a slight division of strength, provisionally setting up steps: to speak of shoots is tender and strengthless use; bamboo as strips can pull a thousand jun. When words and traces arise, right and wrong are thereby formed. Master Jin cut that away for him, separately pointing to a road of living function. This is not at all opening windows and doors, setting tracks and ruts, deceiving fellow practitioners. Master Xiu offered a bow to thank him for what he had missed. Do you yet recognize these two masters’ household forge and bellows? Enter the fire and you still must be finely tempered; only on the anvil can you endure heavy hammer and chisel.

text_zh: 師云。明州翠巖永明大師。諱令參。湖州人。蒙 雪峯記別。大張法席。一日上堂曰。自一夏以 來。為兄弟東語西話。看。翠巖眉毛在麼。諸方 多道。本欲首身不覺兩重公案。更見保福道 作賊人心虛。一向道背底插柴自隱口過。佛 果云。人多錯會道。青天白日說無向當話。無 事生事。先自說過。免得別人點檢。且喜沒交 涉。長慶云生也。萬松道。依舊在眼上。雲門關 字。普字號一字禪。三箇皆嗣雪峯。見當家人 說無外話。見翠巖示眾奇特。故大家唱和。古 人下語。不犯手勢。有座主就華嚴講下。請巖 齋。巖云。山僧有箇問頭。若答得即齋。乃拈起 胡餅云。還具法身麼。主云。具。巖云。恁麼則 喫法身也。主無對。當講法師代云。有甚麼過。 巖不肯。雲門代云。特謝和尚降重空筵。覺範 謂雲門大師僧中王也。果然天童一串穿來 從頭頌出。頌云。
text_en: Snowpeak’s recognition and transmission, and widely spread the Dharma seat. One day he ascended the hall and said: Since one summer ago, I have talked east and talked west for you brothers. Look: are Cuiyan’s eyebrows still there? Everywhere many say he originally meant to present himself, but unknowingly made a double koan. Then seeing Baofu say, A thief has a guilty heart, they keep saying he tucked firewood behind his back to hide his verbal fault. Foguo said: Many people misunderstand and say that in broad daylight he spoke words not fitting the occasion, making trouble where there was none; first he confessed his own fault, so others would not inspect him. Fortunately there is no entanglement. Changqing said, They grow. Wansong said: They are still right above the eyes. Yunmen’s Barrier is the one-character Zen, universally famed. All three were heirs of Snowpeak. Seeing the householder speak with no outside talk, and seeing Cuiyan’s address to the assembly as extraordinary, they all joined in response. The ancients’ comments did not violate the gesture. A lecture master from a Huayan teaching seat invited Cuiyan for a meal. Cuiyan said: This mountain monk has a question; if you answer it, then I’ll attend. He then picked up a sesame cake and said: Does this possess the dharma-body? The lecturer said: It does. Cuiyan said: If so, then you are eating the dharma-body. The lecturer had no reply. A teaching master then answered in his place: What fault is there? Cuiyan did not approve. Yunmen answered in his place: Special thanks to master for condescending to come to this empty feast. Juefan called Great Master Yunmen the king among monks. Indeed, Tiantong strings it all together and from start to finish brings it out in verse. The verse says:
A thief’s heart, a man’s courage; clear and sharp, crossing freely, responding to the occasion. The stolen goods are already exposed Acting as if no one else were there Barehanded snatch

text_zh: 師云。雪竇道。善竊者鬼神不知。既為保福天 童覻破。翠巖不是好手。殊不知。許大雲門長 慶。都被翠巖用一莖眉毛。一時穿却鼻孔。若 藏頭露影。算甚太手強人。故能歷歷縱橫對 機應感。保福云。作賊人心虛。雲門云關。皆衲 僧鼻孔長也。千里已聞乾屎殠。三冬猶嗅爛 瓜香。翠巖道眉毛在麼。長慶便道生也。乃壁 上高僧一呼便噟。瓶中養鵞隨聲。已出底時 節。豈識情可卜度也。此所以道脩眉映眼。 冷地看人。一點謾他不得。有底道。一夏葛藤 上生枝引蔓。而今剪草除根。一齊剗却。殊不 知。三十年後。此話大行去在。何必囊藏被蓋。 飲氣吞聲。恁麼則面牆擔板。累及先宗也。諸 方道。徐六擔板只見一邊。尚書不學牆面。疏 面牆無所覩見。君不見。靈山放出白毫相。照 見東方萬八千。
text_en: saw through it, Cuiyan was not a good hand. But they do not realize that as great as Yunmen and Chang- qing were, Cuiyan used a single eyebrow hair to pierce all their nostrils at once. If you hide the head and show the shadow, what sort of strong-handed fellow is that? Thus he could clearly and freely respond to conditions. Baofu said, A thief has a guilty heart; Yunmen said, Barrier. Both are long-nosed monks indeed. A thousand miles away one already smells dry shit; through three winters one still sniffs rotten melon fragrance. Cuiyan said, Are the eyebrows there? Changqing immediately said, They grow. Like a painted monk on the wall, called once, he responds at once; like a goose raised in a bottle, following the sound, already out at just that moment. How could it be measured by conscious thought? Therefore it says, Long brows reflect the eyes. Looking at people from a cold place, not one bit can deceive him. Some say: All summer the vine-talk sprouted branches and spread tendrils, and now he cuts the grass and pulls the roots, wiping it all out at once. They do not know that thirty years later this saying will be greatly current. Why hide it in the sack and cover it with a quilt? Swallowing breath and voice like this is facing the wall carrying a board, dragging down the ancestral school. Various places say: Xu Liu carrying a board sees only one side. The minister did not imitate wall-facing. Shu says wall-facing sees nothing at all. Have you not seen? On Vulture Peak the white tuft mark was emitted, illuminating the eastern direction for eighteen thousand.

text_zh: 師云。朗州統要鼎州中邑洪恩禪師。馬祖八十餘員 大善知識之一。仰山之叔祖也。仰山江陵受 戒。迴往謝戒。邑見山年幼。以獼猴應六窓。說 佛性義。如拍大嬭諕小孩兒。山埋兵掉鬪。忍 俊不禁。禮謝畢曰。今蒙和尚譬喻。無不明了。 更有一事。只如內獼猴瞌睡。外獼猴欲相見 時。如何奇哉。真師子兒便露法窟爪牙。邑不 覺自下禪床。執仰山手。作舞云。狌狌與爾相 見了也。何不說箇比喻。雲居錫云。中邑當時。 不得仰山這一句。何處有中邑也。先師與勝 默師伯。二十餘歲。叢林敬畏。鄭州寶和尚。名 震河洛。先師遍參往見。州云。兄弟年俊。正宜 叩參。老僧當年念念。常以佛法為事。先師避 席進曰。和尚而今如何也。州云。如生冤家相 似。先師曰。若不得此語。幾乎枉行千里。州下 禪床。握先師手曰。作家那。遂留數日。夾山謂 佛日死灰裏一粒豆爆。蓋謂此也。玄覺云。若 不是仰山。爭得見中邑。且道。甚麼處是仰山 得見中邑處。萬松道。報恩法堂上。崇壽稠云。 還有人定得此道理麼。若定不得。只是箇弄 精魂脚手。佛性義在甚麼處。萬松道。向弄精 魂脚手上辨取。佛鑑云。仰山放憨。中邑賣俏。 俏措賣來憨癡。憨癡放來俏措。雖然獼猴睡 著。其奈肚裏惺惺。直饒杜絕六窓。狌狌何處 不相見。諸人要見二老誵訛麼。各各面皮厚 三寸。萬松道。覓箇識慚愧漢不可得。唯天童 老人較些些。頌云。
text_en: great spiritual friends. He was Yangshan’s grand-uncle in the Dharma. After Yangshan received the precepts at Jiangling, he returned to offer thanks for the precepts. Seeing Yangshan was young, Zhongyi used the monkey at the six windows as a metaphor to explain the meaning of buddha-nature, like clapping one’s hands and jingling things to scare a little child. Yangshan had hidden troops and a ready blade; he endured it as long as he could, but his sharpness could not be contained. After bowing in thanks, he said: Now that I have received your analogy, there is nothing I do not understand. But there is one more matter. Suppose the monkey inside dozes off, and the monkey outside wants to see it— at such a time, what then? Marvelous indeed! A true lion cub at once bared the claws and fangs of the Dharma cave. Zhongyi unconsciously stepped down from the Chan seat, took Yangshan by the hand, danced, and said: The ape has met with you, it has seen you already! Why not give an analogy for that? Yunju Xi said: If, at that time, Zhongyi had not gotten that one sentence from Yangshan, where would Zhongyi have been? My late teacher and Master Shengmo, my Dharma-uncle, were only in their twenties, yet the monasteries respected and feared them. Reverend Bao of Zhengzhou, whose name shook the He-Luo region—my late teacher, while traveling to visit teachers, went to see him. Bao said: Brother, you are young and gifted; this is precisely the time to knock and inquire. In my younger years, this old monk, moment after moment, always took the Buddha-Dharma as his business. My late teacher left his seat and stepped forward, saying: And how is it for you now, Reverend? Bao said: Like meeting a living enemy. My late teacher said: If I had not gotten this saying, I would almost have traveled a thousand miles in vain. Bao stepped down from the Chan seat, grasped my teacher’s hand, and said: A true adept! He then stayed there several days. Jiashan called this a bean popping in dead ashes on Buddha Sun Mountain—surely this is what he meant. Xuanjue said: If it were not for Yangshan, how could one ever see Zhongyi? Tell me then, where was it that Yangshan got to see Zhongyi? Wansong said: In Bao’en’s Dharma hall. Chongshou Chou said: Is there anyone who can settle this principle? If you cannot settle it, you are only manipulating ghostly tricks and gestures. Where is the meaning of buddha-nature in that? Wansong said: Discern it right on those ghostly tricks and gestures. Fojian said: Yangshan played the fool; Zhongyi sold cleverness. Cleverness, when sold, comes out as foolishness; foolishness, when released, comes out as cleverness. Though the monkey may be asleep, still, in its belly it is wide awake. Even if you seal off the six windows completely, where could the ape fail to meet? Do you all want to see the old fellows’ playful deception? Every one of you has a face skin three inches thick. Wansong said: I cannot find even one man who knows shame. Only old Tiantong is a little better. The verse says:
Frozen sleep in a snow hut, the years wear all down; the deep vine-covered gate stays shut through the night. The hibernating door does not open A dragon with no dragon phrase

text_zh: 師云。汝南先賢傳曰。時大雪積地丈餘。洛陽 令躬出按行見。人除雪出有乞食者。至袁安 門。無有行路。謂安已死。令人除雪。入戶見安 僵臥。問何以不出。安曰。大雪人皆餓。不宜干 人。令以為賢。舉為孝廉。此頌中邑說喻。睡語 一上。終是不惺惺。窈窕蘿門夜不開也。忽被 仰山點破。中邑便全體作用。枯木重陽。春風 吹起律筒灰也。蔡邕月令。截竹為管。謂之律。 置之密室。以葭莩為灰。以實其端。其月氣至 則飛灰而管空。陽氣生。死中活也。如中邑仰 山作家相見。見了後如何不勞久立。
text_en: personally went out on inspection. He saw people clearing snow, and among them one begging for food. When he came to Yuan An’s gate, there was no sign of traffic, so he thought Yuan An must be dead. He ordered men to clear the snow, entered the house, and found Yuan An lying stiff. He asked why he had not gone out. An said: In a great snow everyone is hungry; it is not fitting to trouble others. The magistrate took him for a worthy man and recommended him as filial and incorrupt. This verse on Zhongyi’s analogy and his sleepy talk— once it rises, in the end it is still not fully awake: the deep vine-covered gate does not open at night. But suddenly, when Yangshan punctured it, Zhongyi immediately functioned with his whole being. Dry wood in double-yang; spring wind blows up the ash in the pitch-pipe. In Cai Yong’s Monthly Ordinances, bamboo is cut into tubes, called pitch-pipes. They are placed in a sealed chamber, and reed membrane is made into ash to fill the ends. When the monthly qi arrives, the ash flies out and the tube is emptied. Yang energy is born—life within death. Just like Zhongyi and Yang- shan, adepts meeting adepts. After meeting, why trouble to stand long?

text_zh: 師云。僧問同安威禪師。牛頭未見四祖時如 何。安云。路邊神廟子。見者盡擎拳。僧云。見 後如何。安云。室內無靈床。渾家不著孝。這僧 問靈衣不掛時如何。洞山初道。卸了炙脂帽 子。脫却狐臭布衫。作箇脫灑衲僧。後來僧問 如何是佛。答麻三斤。若到這箇時節。便會曹 山今日孝滿。這僧也好。要見今日曹山行履。 問孝滿後如何。山云。曹山好顛酒。覺範道。心 如明鏡口如醉漢。一日僧問。清稅孤貧乞。師 拯濟。山召清稅。僧應喏。山云。清源白家酒三 盞。猶道未沾脣。又有僧。問金峯。金柸滿酌時 如何。峯云。金峯不勝酩酊。佛果拈云。承言會 宗。明機普應。則不無金峯。子細點檢。將來也 太漏逗。若有人。問蔣山金柸滿酌時如何。只 對他道。山僧自來天戒。又有僧問曹山。十二 時中如何保任。山云。如過蠱毒之鄉。水也不 得沾他一滴。曹山有時醉醉裏醒醒。有時醒 不分晝夜。為他黃糧夢斷閨閤情忘。洞山問 雲居。大闡提人。殺父害母。孝養何在。居云。 始成孝養。此名孝滿顛酒底人。洞山道。觸目 荒林論年放曠。天童慣曾游戲其間。頌云。
text_en: Tong’an said: A roadside shrine—everyone who sees it raises clasped hands. The monk said, After he met him, how was it? Tong’an said: Inside the room there is no spirit-bed; the whole household wears no mourning. This monk asked, When the mourning clothes are not worn, what then? Dongshan once said first: Take off the grease-stiffened cap, strip off the fox-smelling cloth jacket, and become a free-and-easy patchrobed monk. Later, when monks asked him What is Buddha? he answered, Three pounds of hemp. If you arrive at this point, then you will understand Caoshan’s today has fulfilled mourning. This monk too was good—he wanted to see Caoshan’s conduct today. He asked, After mourning is fulfilled, what then? Caoshan said, Caoshan likes wild drunken wine. Juefan said: The mind is like a bright mirror; the mouth is like a drunkard. One day a monk said, Qingrui is lonely and poor, begging the master for rescue. Caoshan called, Qingrui! The monk answered, Yes. Caoshan said, Three cups of the Bai family wine of Qingyuan, and you still say your lips are not yet wet. There was another monk who asked Jinfeng, When the golden cup is filled and poured, what then? Jinfeng said: Jinfeng cannot withstand deep drunkenness. Foguo commented: To understand the school by following words, and to respond everywhere with clear function—Jinfeng is not without that. But examined carefully, what he brought out still leaks too much. If someone asked Jiangshan, When the golden cup is filled and poured, what then? I would only answer him: This mountain monk has from the start kept the heavenly precept. Again a monk asked Caoshan, Through the twelve hours, how does one preserve and sustain it? Caoshan said: It is like passing through a land of poison—one must not let even a drop of water touch it. Caoshan was sometimes sober within drunkenness; sometimes awake without dividing day and night. For him, the millet dream was cut off and the chambered affections forgotten. Dongshan asked Yunju: A great icchantika kills father and harms mother—where is filial support then? Yunju said: Only then is filial support fulfilled. This is called a person of fulfilled mourning and topsy-turvy drunkenness. Dongshan said: Before the eyes, a wild forest—year after year free and unrestrained. Tiantong was long accustomed to wandering and playing there. The verse says:

text_zh: 師云。眼裏著沙。不得底太局狹生。曹山道。若 是世間麁重貪嗔癡。雖難斷。却是輕。若是無 事無為淨潔。此箇重無以加也。所以洞山道。 明月堂前時時九夏也。至道不可形容。古人 近取諸身。遠取諸物。比興連類以喻至道。報 慈贊龍牙半身頌云。日出連山。月圓當戶。不 是無身。不欲全露。二老皆洞山兒孫。覺範云。 其家風機貴迴互。使不犯正位。語忌十成。使 不墮今時。而報慈匠心獨妙語不失宗。為可 貴也。此光明轉處。傾殘月。喻孝滿逢春也。周 易乾卦。九二見龍在田。利見大人疏。九二當 據建寅建丑之間。於時地之萌芽初有出者。 即是陽氣發見之義。乾卦之象其應然也。老 杜飲中八仙歌。脫巾露頂王公前。與天子呼 來不上舡。皆忘形忽禮。非可以涯岸檢束也。 丹霞天然。一日橫臥天津橋上。留守鄭公前 導喝之。師不顧問之。徐曰。我無事僧也。鄭敬 異之。雪峯眾晚參。峯在中庭臥。太原孚上座 云。五州管內只有這箇和尚較些子。峯便起 去。此皆披襟散髮無事酒徒。曹山孝滿如何 受用。四時春富貴。萬物酒風流。
text_en: though hard to cut off, still they are light. But if it is idle purity and stainless quietism, this is heavier than anything. Therefore Dongshan said: Before the bright moon hall, it is always midsummer. The utmost Way cannot be given form. The ancients took examples from the body nearby and from things afar, linking images and analogies to illustrate the utmost Way. Bao- ci praised Longya’s Half-Body Verse, saying: The sun rises over linked mountains; the moon is full at the door. It is not that there is no body; it is just not willing to show itself entirely. Both elders were descendants of Dongshan. Juefan said: In that house style, the subtle mechanism values mutual turning, so as not to violate the central position. Their speech avoids complete fullness, so as not to fall into present-time fixation. Yet Bao-ci’s artisan mind is uniquely wondrous, and his words do not lose the school—this is what is precious. This line, Where the light turns, the waning moon tilts, is a metaphor for mourning fulfilled meeting spring. In the Zhou Changes, Hexagram Qian, the second nine says, Seeing the dragon in the field; it is beneficial to see the great person. The commentary says the second nine corresponds to the interval between Jianyin and Jianchou, when the first shoots of earth just begin to emerge. This is precisely the meaning of yang energy appearing and issuing forth; this is as the image of the Qian hexagram should be. Old Du in his Song of the Eight Immortals of Wine says: He drops his cap and bares his crown before princes; when summoned by the Son of Heaven, he will not board the boat. All of them forgot form and slighted ceremony; they cannot be constrained by ordinary bounds. Danxia Tianran one day lay crosswise on Tianjin Bridge. Zheng, the military governor, with his attendants in front, shouted at him, but the master paid no heed. Asked about it, he slowly said: I am an idle monk. Zheng respectfully marveled at him. At Xuefeng’s evening assembly, Xuefeng was lying in the middle courtyard. Senior monk Fushangzuo of Taiyuan said: In all the five prefectures, only this monk is a little something. Xuefeng then got up and left. These are all open-robed, loose-haired, idle wine-drinkers. How does Caoshan’s fulfilled mourning function and enjoy itself? In all four seasons it is springtime wealth and honor; all things are wine and elegance.

text_zh: 師云。文殊問維摩。身孰為本。答貪欲為本。問 貪欲孰為本答。虛妄分別為本。問虛妄分別 孰為本。答顛倒想為本。問顛倒想孰為本。答 無住為本。又問無住孰為本。答無住則無本。 文殊師利從無住本。立一切法。肇公注云。心 猶水也。靜則有照。動則無鑑。癡愛所濁。邪風 所扇。湧溢波蕩。未始暫住。以此觀法。何往不 倒。譬如臨面湧泉責己本狀者。未之有也。又 云。若以心動為本。則有因相。生理極初動。更 無本也。若以無法為本。則有因無生。無不因 無。更無本也。又云。無住故倒想。倒想故分 別。分別故貪欲。貪欲故有身。既有身也。則善 惡並陳。善惡既陳。則萬法斯起。自茲以往。言 數不能盡也。肇公以最初動念根本不覺。為 無住本。傳燈清涼國師。答皇太子心要云。至 道本乎其心。心法本乎無住。無住心體靈知 不昧。安國師舉。金剛經云。應無所住。而生其 心。無所住者不住色不住聲。不住迷不住悟。 不住體不住用。而生其心者。則是一切處。而 顯一心。若住善生心則善現。若住惡生心則 惡現。本心則隱沒。若無所住。十方世界唯是 一心也。六祖問荷澤。知識遠來也。大艱辛。將 本來否。若有本則合識其主試說看。澤曰。以 無住為本。見則為主。荷澤顯宗記云。自世尊 滅後。西天二十八祖。共傳無住之心。此無住 本即以本分事。名無住也。若以真妄融即。一 有多種。二無兩般。法眼答處。出寶藏論。形興 未質。名起未名。形名既兆。游氣亂清。雪竇拈 起拄杖云。大眾拄杖。是形名雙舉。形即無形。 名即無名。一等沒見識瞎漢。只認箇無形段 無名姓底。便為極則。辜負法眼。違背永明。壽 禪師唯心訣云。無一名不播如來之號。無一 物不闡遮那之形。又有一等孤陋寡聞。不肯 究理參問。只道。本來有甚。萬松道已。太多 生。他云。如何免得。萬松道。本來少甚。爾但 恁麼會去。因參法眼兼見天童。頌云。
text_en: What is the root of desire? he answered, False discrimination is the root. Asked, False discrimination— what is its root? he answered, Inverted thinking is the root. Asked, What is the root of inverted thinking? he answered, Non-abiding is the root. Asked again, What is the root of non-abiding? he answered, Non-abiding has no root. Manjushri then said: From the root of non-abiding all dharmas are established. Sengzhao’s commentary says: The mind is like water. When still, it reflects; when stirred, it does not mirror. Muddy from delusion and craving, fanned by the winds of error, it surges and billows, never dwelling even for a moment. Viewed this way, in observing dharmas, where would one not be upside down? It is like facing a gushing spring and trying to inspect one’s original face—such a thing has never been. He also says: If one takes the stirring of mind as root, then there is the mark of causation. But tracing life to the very first stirring, there is no further root. If one takes non-dharma as root, then there is non-arising through a cause; yet even non-being is not apart from causes, so again there is no root. He also says: From non-abiding comes inverted thinking; from inverted thinking comes discrimination; from discrimination comes desire; from desire comes body. Once there is body, then good and evil both appear. Once good and evil appear, then the myriad dharmas arise. From this point on, words and categories cannot exhaust them. Sengzhao takes the very first stirring of thought, the root ignorance, as the root of non-abiding. In the Transmission of the Lamp, National Teacher Qingliang, answering the Crown Prince on the essential point of mind, said: The utmost Way is rooted in mind; the Dharma of mind is rooted in non-abiding. The substance of non-abiding mind is numinous knowing, never obscured. National Teacher An cited the Diamond Sutra: One should produce that mind without abiding anywhere. Not abiding anywhere means not abiding in form, not abiding in sound; not abiding in delusion, not abiding in awakening; not abiding in essence, not abiding in function. Producing that mind means that in every place the one mind is manifest. If one abides in good and produces mind, then good appears; if one abides in evil and produces mind, then evil appears. Then the original mind is hidden. If one does not abide anywhere, then the worlds of the ten directions are only one mind. The Sixth Patriarch asked Heze: You have come from afar, friend, with great hardship. Have you brought your original thing with you? If there is an original, you should know its master—try to speak. Heze said: Taking non-abiding as root, seeing is the master. In Heze’s Record of Revealing the School it says: Since the World-Honored One’s passing, the twenty-eight patriarchs of the Western Heaven all transmitted the mind of non-abiding. This non-abiding root is simply the fundamental matter itself, named non-abiding. If one fuses true and false, then the one has many kinds, while the two are not two kinds. Fayan’s answer comes from the Treatise on the Treasury: Form arises before substance; name appears before naming. Once form and name give signs, wandering vapors disturb the clear. Xuedou raised his staff and said: Great assembly, this staff is form and name both presented. Form is precisely no-form; name is precisely no-name. A whole class of blind men without understanding only recognize some no-form piece and no-name thing and take that as the ultimate rule. They let Fayan down and go against Yongming. Chan Master Shou’s Formula of Mind-Only says: There is not a single name that does not proclaim the Tathagata’s title; there is not a single thing that does not reveal Vairocana’s form. Then there is another sort, narrow and ill-informed, unwilling to investigate principle or inquire with teachers, who only say: What was there originally? Wansong said: Already too much! They say: How can we avoid that? Wansong said: Originally what was lacking? You just understand it this way and go on. Because he had studied Fayan and also seen Tiantong, the verse says:
No tracks, no traces; news cut off—white clouds without root, pure The antelope hangs by its horns Long burdened, never meeting The wondrous body originally has no fixed place

text_zh: 沒蹤跡羚羊挂角　斷消息久負不逢　白雲無根妙體本來無處所　清 風何色通身那更有蹤由散乾蓋而非心尚能出岫　持坤輿 而有力不費精神洞千古之淵源盡向這裏流出　造萬象之 模則一法之所印剎塵道會也。處處普賢欄街截巷　樓閣 門開也頭頭彌勒築著磕著
text_en: wind, what color? Through the whole body, where could there be any trace It spreads the heaven-canopy yet is not mind; it upholds the earth-carriage It can still emerge from the mountain cleft and yet has power. It costs no effort It penetrates the source of a thousand ages and fashions the model of ten thousand forms; All of it flows out here the pattern and rule. What is sealed by the one dharma When the paths meet in dust-mote lands, everywhere are Samantabhadra’s towers and pavilions; Barricading streets and blocking alleys their gates stand open. At every point, Maitreya. Bumping into it and knocking against it
The master said: Look at it—without form, filling heaven and covering earth. Listen to it—without sound, yet the perfect tone has no end.

text_zh: 師云。視之無形。普天匝地。聽之無聲圓音無 間。雲雖無根。太虛為片雲所點。風雖無色。大 地為風輪所持。劉禹端公問雲居。雨從何來。 居曰。從端公問處來。公喜而謝之。居却問曰。 問從何來。公無語西禪與官員坐次。禪云。風 作何色。官無語。禪却問僧。僧拈起衲衣云在 府中鋪。禪云。用多少帛子。僧云。勿交涉。禪 無語。雲門代云。咄這話墮阿師。雪竇併作兩 頌。雨從何來。風作何色。龍門萬仞曾留宿客。 進退相將誰遭點額。風作何色。雨從何來。不 用彈指。樓閣門開。波波稜稜南方未迴。天童 頌無住本。白雲無根。清風何色。頌立一切法。 散乾蓋而非心。持坤輿而有力。善慧大士心 王銘。觀心空王。玄妙難測。無形無相。有大神 力。管子曰水出而不流曰淵水。遠而流曰源。 上古之前。千古淵源也。萬象自茲而形。華嚴 普賢行願品。佛說菩薩說。剎說眾生說。三世 一切說。又普眼不見普賢。見與不見俱普賢 也。若不見處無。不名普也。入法界品時。彌勒 菩薩前詣樓閣彈指出聲。其門即開。命善財 入。乃至悉見三千大千世界百億四天下。兜 率陀天。一一皆有彌勒。又有頌云。彌勒真彌 勒。化身千百億。時時示時人。時人皆不識。此 皆立一切法之標榜也。還見法眼麼。常因送 客處。記得別家時。
text_en: Meanwhile: though clouds have no root, vast space is marked by a patch of cloud. Though wind has no color, the great earth is upheld by the wheel of wind. Duke Liu Yu asked Yunju, "From where does the rain come?" Yunju said, "It comes from where the Duke asks." The Duke was delighted and thanked him. Yunju then asked, "From where does the question come?" The Duke had no reply. Xichan was seated with an official and said, "The wind— what color is it?" The official had no reply. Chan then asked a monk. The monk lifted his patched robe and said, "In the prefectural storehouse cloth." Chan said, "How many bolts of silk did it use?" The monk said, "No entangling." Chan had no reply. Yunmen answered on his behalf: "Tut! This talk falls on the teacher." Xuedou then composed two verses together: "From where comes rain? What color is wind? At Dragon Gate, ten thousand fathoms high, a traveler once lodged. Advancing and retreating together—who gets marked on the forehead? What color is wind? From where comes rain? No need to snap fingers; the tower gate opens. Billowing, jagged and sharp, he has not yet returned from the south." Tiantong versifies the root of non-abiding: white clouds have no root; what color is the clear wind? He versifies establishing all dharmas. It scatters the heavenly canopy yet is not mind; it holds up the earth-carriage and has power. In the Mind- King Inscription by the Great Being Good Wisdom: "Observe the mind, empty king—mysterious, subtle, hard to fathom; without form, without appearance, with great spiritual power." The Guanzi says: water that emerges yet does not flow is called deep water; when it flows far, it is called a source. Before high antiquity—this is the abyssal source through a thousand ages. From this the myriad forms take shape. In the Huayan, in the Samantabhadra Practices and Vows chapter: Buddha speaks, bodhisattvas speak, lands speak, beings speak; the three times— all speak. Also, Universal Eye does not see Samantabhadra; seeing and not seeing are both Samantabhadra too. If where one does not see were absent, it would not be called universal. In the Entry into the Dharma Realm chapter, Maitreya Bodhisattva goes before the tower and snaps his fingers with a sound; its gate immediately opens. He bids Sudhana enter, and thereupon he sees completely the three-thousand great-thousand worlds, the hundred million four-continents, and the Tushita heaven. In each and every one there is Maitreya. There is also a verse: "Maitreya, true Maitreya, manifests in hundreds of billions of bodies, constantly appearing to people of the time; people of the time all do not recognize him." This is all a signboard for establishing all dharmas. Do you still see Dharma Eye? "Often because at the place of seeing off a guest, one remembers the time of parting from home."

text_zh: 75 瑞巖常理
text_en: 75. Ruiyan's Constant Principle Instruction to the assembly: Calling it suchness is already change. Where knowledge does not reach, above all avoid

text_zh: 示眾云。喚作如如早是變也。智不到處。切忌 道著。這裏還有參究分也無。
text_en: speaking of it. Is there still any share for investigation here, or not?
Raised: Ruiyan asked Yantou, "What is the original constant principle?" When reason is present, it is not in loudness

text_zh: 舉。瑞巖問巖頭。如何是本常理有理不在高聲頭 云。動也可知理也巖云。動時如何再犯不容頭云。不見 本常理相物作價巖佇思却識慚愧頭云。肯即未脫根 塵箇中無肯路不肯即永沈生死當堂不正坐那赴兩頭機。
text_en: Yantou said, "It moves." Ruiyan said, "When it moves, then what?" Yantou said, "You do not see Then one may know the principle A second offense will not be tolerated the original constant principle." Ruiyan stood there thinking. Yantou said, "If you assent, you have not yet escaped the sense-roots and Price it by the thing itself Yet he knows shame sense-dusts; if you do not assent, you sink forever in birth and death." In this there is no road of assent If you do not sit upright in the hall, how will you meet the two-sided occasion
The teacher said: Chan Master Shiyan of Ruiyan in Taizhou was a Min man, surname Xu. When he first asked

text_zh: 師云。台州瑞巖師彥禪師。閩人。姓許氏。始問 巖頭。安箇名立箇字。創號本常理。巖頭有 時放過。只與照破道。動也。瑞巖好彩三十棒。 何幸免却來。是他尚不顧危亡。道動時如何。 撩虎頭編虎尾。巖頭半醉半醒又放過。只與 照破道。不見本常理。大方之家。容物如此。 巖方佇思。這裏正到枯木巖前差路多處也。 頭已是不惜身命。與截斷走路。剖開當陽長 安官道云。肯即未脫根塵。不肯即永沈生死。 溈山喚作法窟爪牙。生擒活捉。略無閑暇功 夫。夾山會下一僧到石霜。入門便道。不審。霜 云。不必闍黎。僧云。恁麼則珍重。又到巖頭如 前。頭乃噓兩聲。僧云。恁麼則珍重。纔廻步。 頭云。雖是後生。亦能管帶。僧歸舉似夾山。山 明日上堂。喚僧如法舉似前話。山云。大眾還 會麼。若無人道。老僧不惜兩莖眉毛道去也。 乃曰。石霜雖有殺人刀。且無活人劍。巖頭且 有殺人刀。亦有活人劍。臨濟下謂之七事隨 身。巖頭見瑞巖志誠請益。非是機鋒勘辨之 時。故憫物垂慈道眼相見。瑞巖隨言領悟。後 來自喚主人翁。莫受人謾。蓋為曾遭毒手永 劫難忘。此話古今無人拈掇。不是天童。憑誰 賞鑒。頌云。
text_en: Yantou, he set a name and coined a term, first labeling it "original constant principle." Yantou at times let him pass, only illuminating and shattering it by saying, "It moves." Ruiyan was lucky to escape thirty blows. How fortunate he got off. Yet he still did not regard danger or ruin, and said, "When it moves, how is it then?" Stroking the tiger's head, braiding the tiger's tail. Yantou, half drunk and half sober, again let him pass, only illuminating and shattering it, saying, "You do not see the original constant principle." Such is the magnanimity of a great house, able to contain others. Ruiyan then stood thinking. Right here he had reached the place before the dead-tree cliff where side paths are many. Yantou was already sparing no life of his own, cutting off the running road for him, splitting open the broad avenue of Chang'an before the sun, saying: "If you assent, you have not yet escaped roots and dusts. If you do not assent, you sink forever in birth and death." Guishan called this the claws and fangs of the Dharma cave—seizing alive, capturing living; there is not the slightest spare-time practice involved. A monk from Jia-shan's assembly went to Shishuang. As soon as he entered the gate he said, "I respectfully inquire." Shuang said, "No need, reverend." The monk said, "In that case, take care." He then went to Yantou and, just as before, did the same. Yantou merely gave two huffs. The monk said, "In that case, take care," and had just turned to leave. Yantou said, "Though a youngster, he can still carry it through." The monk returned and related this to Jia-shan. Jia-shan ascended the hall the next day, had the monk properly repeat the earlier exchange, and said, "Great assembly, do you understand? If no one can speak, this old monk will not begrudge two eyebrows to speak it out." Then he said, "Though Shishuang has a sword to kill people, he does not yet have a sword to bring people to life. Yantou, moreover, has a sword to kill people and also a sword to bring people to life. In Linji's line this is called the seven things always at hand. Yantou saw Ruiyan's sincere resolve in seeking instruction; it was not a time for sharp repartee and testing discrimination, so, pitying the man and hanging down compassion, he met him with the Dharma eye. Ruiyan understood with the words, and later he called to himself, "Master!" and said, "Do not be deceived by others!" It was because he had once met a deadly hand and forever could not forget through kalpas. This story, past and present, no one has brought up. If not Tiantong, on whom could one rely to appreciate it? The verse says:
The round pearl is unbored, the great jade block uncarved; what the Wayfarer esteems is being without edges Where do you set your hand What a pity for the effort

text_zh: 圓珠不穴甚處下手　大璞不琢可惜功夫　道人所貴無稜 角就理藏鋒拈却肯路根塵空十二處忘閑影響　脫體無依 活卓卓三千界放淨光明
text_en: or corners. In accord with principle, hide the edge Lift away the road of assent, and roots and dust are empty; body dropped free, with nothing to rely on— In the twelve fields, idle traces and echoes are forgotten vividly alive, bright and clear. Through the three thousand worlds pure light shines forth
The teacher said: In secular records, Pan Yue and Xiahou Zhan were friends; both men were of fine appearance.

text_zh: 師云。世記潘岳與夏侯湛為友。二人並美姿 容。張謂贊和氏之璧瑩而無瑕。隋侯之珠圓 而不穴。削圓方竹杖絕却紫絨氈。白玉碾做 象牙梳。黃金打作鍮石筋。弓絃上結紐子。鉢 盂上安柄。爾試廻光定省看。何人不如是。百 丈道。靈光獨耀逈脫根塵。既肯則未脫根塵。 拈却肯路根塵自空也。六根六塵既空。六識 自歸覺海。凡物有圭角即不能圓轉。欲要活 卓卓無粘綴無依倚。但向肯不肯處著眼。自 然不住此岸。不住彼岸。不住中流。洞山所以 半肯半不肯。疎山所以肯諾不得全也。還識 此人歸計麼。金鎖玄關留不住。行於異路且 輪廻。
text_en: Zhang Wei praised the He clan jade as lustrous and flawless, and the Sui lord's pearl as round yet unbored. To shave a square bamboo staff round, to cut off the purple felt, to grind white jade into an ivory comb, to hammer gold into brass ribs, to tie knots on a bowstring, to put a handle on an alms bowl— just turn the light around and examine steadily: who is not like this? Baizhang said, "The numinous light shines alone, far transcending roots and dust." If one assents, one has not yet escaped roots and dust. Lift away the road of assent, and roots and dust are themselves empty. Once the six roots and six dusts are empty, the six consciousnesses return of themselves to the sea of awakening. Anything with sharp corners cannot turn freely. If you want to be vividly alive, clear and bright, without sticking or leaning, just place your eye on the point of assent and non-assent. Then naturally you do not abide on this shore, do not abide on the other shore, do not abide midstream. This is why Dongshan was half-assenting and half-not-assenting, and why Shushan's assent could not be complete. Do you yet recognize this person's homeward reckoning? The golden lock and dark gate cannot hold him. He travels on a different road and yet still turns in the wheel.

text_zh: 76 首山三句
text_en: 76. Shoushan's Three Sentences Instruction to the assembly: One sentence clarifies three sentences; three sentences clarify one sentence. Three and one do not

text_zh: 示眾云。一句明三句。三句明一句。三一不相 涉。分明向上路。且道。是那一句在先。
text_en: intermingle. The upward road is perfectly clear. Tell me: which sentence comes first?
Raised: Shoushan instructed the assembly, "If you grasp the first sentence, you can be teacher to Buddhas and patriarchs.

text_zh: 舉。首山示眾云。第一句薦得。與佛祖為師。 猶是萬松兒孫第二句薦得與人天為師教壞人家男女第三 句薦得自救不了說這不唧嬼漢僧云。和尚是第幾 句薦得儞試卜度山云。月落三更穿市過三句可辨一鏃遼空。
text_en: If you grasp the second sentence, you can be teacher to humans and gods. The third Still Wansong's descendants Spoiling other people's sons and daughters sentence grasped, you cannot even save yourself." A monk said, "Master, by which sentence do you Talking like this, that noisy fellow grasp it?" Shoushan said, "At third watch, with the moon set, I pass through the market." You try to reckon it out Three phrases can discern one arrow flying across the sky
The teacher said: The making of the three sentences begins with Baizhang Dazhi and is rooted in the Diamond Prajna.

text_zh: 師云。三句之作。始於百丈大智。宗於金剛般 若。丈云。夫教語皆三句相連。初中後善。初直 須教渠發善心。中破善心。後始名好善。則菩 薩即非菩薩。是名菩薩。法非法非非法。總恁 麼也。若只說一句。令眾生入地獄。若三句一 時說。渠自入地獄。不干教主事。說道如今鑒 覺是自己佛。是初善。不守住如今鑒覺。是中 善。亦不作不守住知解。是後善。雲門有時云。 天中函蓋乾坤。目機銖兩不涉春緣。作麼生 承當。自代云。一鏃破三關。然雖有此意。未甞 立為三句。後得鼎州德山第九世圓明大師 諱緣密。上堂云。德山有三句語。一句函蓋乾 坤。一句隨波逐浪。一句截斷眾流。後得鼎州 普安山道禪師。頌上三句。一函蓋乾坤頌。乾 坤并萬象。地獄及天堂。物物皆真見。頭頭用 不傷。二截斷眾流頌。堆山積嶽來。一一盡塵 埃。更擬論玄妙。氷消瓦解摧。三隨波逐浪頌。 辯口利舌問。高低應不虧。還如應病藥。診候 在臨時。三句外。當人如舉唱。三句豈能該。有 問如何事。南嶽與天台。往往指此頌。為雲門 所作。此皆看閱之不審也。道嗣德山密。密嗣 雲門。雲門雖有天中函蓋一鏃三關之語。因 密公拈出。道公頌之。祖述三世而三句始明。 此與大陽三句。三玄三要。大同小異。首山示 眾云。第一句薦得與佛祖為師。黃蘗為南泉 首座。一日占泉座位。泉至問。首座甚年行 道。蘗云。威音王佛以前。泉云。猶是王老師兒 孫下去。蘗便退歸本位坐。鏡清道毘盧有師 法身有主。謂之佛祖向上人。此所以謂第一 句薦得與佛祖為師也。靈樹遺封盒子。云堂 中首座人天眼目。首座乃雲門也。此所以謂 第二句薦得與人天為師也。爾莫見萬松恁 麼道。便謂南泉可與佛祖為師。雲門只可與 人天為師。可謂癡人面前不得說夢。萬松且 略舉一二以為榜樣。其自救不了者。不入祖 位。何足道哉。僧便問。和尚是第幾句薦得。爛 埿裏有刺。山云。月落三更穿市過。此乃行人 更在青山外也。天童見此話無人敢下口。遂 向査手刺脚處。交加頌出。頌云。
text_en: Baizhang said, "Teaching words are all linked in three sentences: good at first, middle, and end. At first one must directly make him arouse a good mind; in the middle, break the good mind; only afterward is it called truly good. Thus 'a bodhi- sattva is no bodhisattva; this is called bodhisattva.' Dharma, non-dharma, and not non-dharma—all are like this. If one speaks only one sentence, one makes beings enter hell. If the three sentences are spoken at once, he himself enters hell; it does not concern the teacher. To say that present illumining awareness is one's own Buddha—that is the first good. Not clinging to present illumining awareness—that is the middle good. Not even making an understanding of not clinging—that is the final good. Yunmen at times said: "Within heaven, it envelops heaven and earth; in the eye's function, fine as grains, not touching any conditioned ties. How do you bear it?" He answered for himself: "One arrowhead smashes three barriers." Yet though he had this meaning, he never established it as three sentences. Later there was in Dingzhou, at Deshan, the ninth-generation Perfect Illumination Master, named Yuanmi, who ascended the hall and said: "Deshan has three sentences: one sentence envelops heaven and earth, one sentence follows the waves and rides the swells, one sentence cuts off all streams." Later in Dingzhou Chan Master Dao of Pu'an Mountain versified these three sentences. Verse on enveloping heaven and earth: "Heaven and earth and the myriad forms, hell and heaven too—thing by thing all are true seeing; in every case function does no harm." Verse on cutting off all streams: "Piled mountains and heaped peaks come; each and every one is exhausted to dust. If one still intends to discuss mystery and subtlety, ice melts and tiles shatter." Verse on following waves and riding swells: "Eloquent mouths and sharp tongues ask; high and low are answered without fail. It is like medicine suited to illness, diagnosis depending on the moment." Outside the three sentences, when the person himself raises the tune, how could the three sentences contain it? If there is a question, "What is this matter?" Nan'yue and Tiantai often point to this verse as Yunmen's composition. This is all from careless reading. Dao was heir to Deshan Mi, and Mi was heir to Yunmen. Though Yunmen had the sayings of "enveloping heaven and earth" and "one arrowhead, three barriers," because Master Mi brought them up and Master Dao versified them, across three generations of ancestral transmission the three sentences first became clear. This and Dayang's three sentences, and the three mysteries and three essentials, are largely the same with minor differences. Shoushan instructed the assembly: "If you grasp the first sentence, you are teacher to Buddhas and patriarchs." Huangbo was Nanquan's head monk. One day he occupied Nanquan's seat. Nanquan came and asked, "Head monk, in what year did you begin practice?" Huangbo said, "Before King Sounding-Wisdom Buddha." Nanquan said, "Still the descendants of old teacher Wang— step down!" Huangbo then withdrew and returned to his own place to sit. Jingqing said, "Vairocana has a teacher, the Dharma-body has a master"—this is called a person beyond Buddhas and patriarchs. Therefore it is said the first sentence, when grasped, makes one teacher to Buddhas and patriarchs. Lingshu left behind a sealed casket saying, "The hall's head monk is the eye of humans and gods." That head monk was Yunmen. Therefore it is said the second sentence, when grasped, makes one teacher to humans and gods. Don't, on hearing Wansong speak like this, then say Nanquan can only be teacher to Buddhas and patriarchs while Yunmen can only be teacher to humans and gods. Truly, before a fool one must not speak dreams. Wansong is only briefly citing one or two examples as models. As for those who cannot save themselves, they do not enter the ancestral rank—what is there to say? The monk then asked, "Master, by which sentence do you grasp it?" In rotten mud there is a thorn. Shoushan said, "At third watch, with the moon set, I pass through the market." This is a traveler still beyond the green hills. Tiantong saw that no one dared open his mouth on this saying, so he struck in where it pricks the hands and stabs the feet, and brought out an interwoven verse. The verse says:
Buddhas' and patriarchs' skulls threaded on one string; the palace clepsydra drips deep in the night, secretly passing the arrow. Let him jump as he pleases Not allowed

text_zh: 佛祖髑髏穿一串一任伊𨁝跳　宮漏沈沈密傳箭不許 外人知人天機要發千鈞以輕勞重　雲陣輝輝急飛電 眨眼蹉過箇中人看轉變計在臨時　遇賤則貴貴則賤心知 本自同所以無欣怨得珠罔象兮至道綿綿一念不生全體現　游 刃亡牛兮赤心片片泪出痛腸
text_en: For outsiders to know The pivotal essentials for humans and gods release a thousand-catty force; cloud battalions flash and flash like swift flying lightning. Using the light to labor over the heavy In a blink, it slips by The person in the midst sees the turns and changes: meeting the lowly, it becomes noble; meeting the noble, it becomes lowly. The plan lies in the critical moment The heart knows Originally they are the same, so there is no joy or resentment Getting the pearl through Wangxiang, ah—the utmost Way goes on and on, unbroken; When not a single thought arises, the whole body appears gliding the blade where the ox is gone, ah—a red heart in piece after piece. Tears come forth and the guts ache
The teacher said: Only after threading the skulls of Buddhas and patriarchs on one string can one be teacher to

text_zh: 師云。佛祖髑髏一串穿却。然後可與佛祖為 師。可謂透出毘盧頂𩕳行。却來化佛舌頭坐。 宮漏沈沈密傳箭。殷蘷漏刻法曰。為器三重。 圓皆徑尺。差立於方輿踟蹰之上。為金龍口 吐水。轉注入踟蹰經緯之中。蓋上鑄金為司 晨。具衣冠。兩手執箭。又軍中密令。夜中傳 箭。此言向朕兆未分以前。薦得可與佛祖為 師。纔落今時為第二頭。且於人天路上作箇 小歇場。心地觀經。電光三昧。衲僧喚作瞥地 處。若是箇中人。有時佛祖頭上行。有時人天 路上走。水牯牛隊裏。異類中行。王荊公觀俳 優。詩云。諸優戲場中。一貴復一賤。心知本自 同。所以無欣怨。莊子天地篇。黃帝遊乎赤水 之北。登崐崘之丘。而南望還歸。遺其玄珠。使 智索之而不得。使離朱索之而不得。使喫詬 索之而不得。使象罔。象罔得之。黃帝曰。異 哉。象罔乃可以得之。養生篇。庖丁為文惠公 解牛曰。彼節者有閒。而刀刃者無厚。以無厚 入有閒。恢恢乎其於游刃。必有餘地矣。是以 十九年。而刀刃若新發於硎。文惠君曰。善哉 吾聞庖丁之言。得養生焉。此二事頌月落三 更穿市過。至道綿綿密密。宮漏傳箭相似。赤 心片片為人。如游刃恢恢得珠罔象也。今人 見天童用莊子。便將老莊。雷同至道。殊不知 古人借路經過。暫時光景耳。忽有箇出來道。 莊子豈不知首山行履處。但向道。月落三更 穿市過。是外篇是內篇。
text_en: Buddhas and patriarchs. This may be called walking out beyond Vairocana's crown, then returning to sit on the Buddha's tongue. "The palace clepsydra drips deep in the night, secretly passing the arrow." The Yin Kui method of water clocks says: the instrument is made in three tiers, all circular, each one chi in diameter, set in graduated levels upon a square base and stand, with a golden dragon mouth spouting water, which turns and pours into the mechanism of warp and weft. On top is cast a golden timekeeper, fully clothed and capped, both hands holding an arrow. Also, in the army, secret orders are by night passed with an arrow. This means: before signs and traces have divided, if one grasps it, one can be teacher to Buddhas and patriarchs. But as soon as it falls into the present moment, it becomes the second level—then one makes a small resting place on the road of humans and gods. In the Mind-Ground Contemplation Sutra, the lightning samadhi; monks call it the fleeting-flash place. If one is a person of the midst, at times he walks atop the heads of Buddhas and patriarchs; at times he runs upon the road of humans and gods. He moves within the herd of water buffaloes, travels among different kinds. Wang Jinggong, watching actors, wrote a poem: "Among the players on the stage, one noble and then one base; in their hearts they know they are originally the same, and so have neither delight nor resentment." In Zhuangzi's "Heaven and Earth" chapter, the Yellow Emperor wandered north of Red Water, climbed Kunlun Hill, looked south, and on returning lost his dark pearl. He sent Knowledge to seek it and could not get it; he sent Lih Zhu to seek it and could not get it; he sent Chigou to seek it and could not get it. He sent Wangxiang, and Wangxiang got it. The Yellow Emperor said, "Strange indeed! Wangxiang could get it." In the "Nourishing Life" chapter, Cook Ding was butchering an ox for Lord Wenhui and said: "At the joints there are gaps, while the blade's edge has no thickness. Using what has no thickness to enter what has gaps—vast, vast! In the play of the blade there is surely ample room. Therefore after nineteen years, the blade is as if newly sharpened on the whetstone." Lord Wenhui said, "Excellent indeed! Hearing Cook Ding's words, I have gained the way of nourishing life." These two stories verse the line "moon set, third watch, passing through the market." The utmost Way is continuous and fine, like the palace clepsydra passing the arrow. A red heart, piece by piece, is for people, like the broad free blade and like getting the pearl through Wangxiang. People nowadays see Tiantong use Zhuangzi and then lump Lao and Zhuang together with the utmost Way. They do not know that the ancients merely borrowed the road to pass through, only for the moment's scene. If suddenly someone comes out and says, "Did not Zhuangzi know the place where Shoushan walked?" just say to him: "Moon set, third watch—" passing through the market. Is this the outer section or the inner section?

text_en: 77. Yangshan According to Portion Instruction to the assembly: If a man draws in empty space, the moment he puts down the brush he is already wrong. How much worse to set up patterns and make forms.

text_zh: 示眾云。如人畫空下筆即錯。那堪起模作樣。 堪作甚麼。○萬松已是露栓索。有條攀條。無 條攀例。

text_zh: 舉。僧問仰山。和尚還識字否是甚麼字山云。隨 分當仁不讓僧乃右旋一匝云。是甚麼字已見偏傍山 於地上書箇十字更書畫點僧左旋一匝云。是甚 麼字半滿俱分形聲轉注山改十字作卍字機輪轉處智眼猶迷僧畫 一圓相。以兩手托。如修羅掌日月勢云。是 甚麼字細看切脚山乃畫圓相。圍却卍字天下衲僧跳不出 僧乃作樓至勢門外金剛笑汝山云。如是如是。汝善 護持關空鎖夢牢收掌。

The slant is already evident. wrote a cross on the ground. The monk turned once to the left and said, What Add more strokes and dots. character is this? text_zh: 師舉。慈覺勸孝文首篇頌云。父母未生前。凝 然一相圓。釋迦猶不會。迦葉豈能傳。十四祖 龍樹。於法座上隱身現○相。提婆曰。此尊者 現佛體相。以示吾輩也。以此無相三昧形如 滿月。佛性之義廓然虛明。譬此而已。圓相之 作東土。始於忠國師。付侍者耽源。承讖記傳 於仰山。今遂目為溈仰家風。明州五峯良和 尚。甞製四十則。嵩明教為序稱之。良云。圓相 總六名。一圓相。二義海。三暗機。四字學。五 意語。六默論。溈仰宗派云。躭源謂仰山曰。國 師傳六代祖師圓相九十七箇。吾滅後三十 年。南方有一沙彌。到來大興此道。吾詳此讖 事。在汝躬。仰山既得以火燔之。源一日又謂 曰。向傳圓相宜深祕之。山曰。已燒却了也。源 曰。於子即得。來者如何。仰曰。和尚若要重錄 一本。山乃重錄呈似。一無差失。耽源一日上 堂。仰出眾作○相。以手托呈。却叉手立。源 以兩手。交拳示之。仰進前三步。作女人拜。源 點頭。仰禮拜。九十七種圓相交拳。名羅剎三 昧。女拜名女人三昧。此皆三昧。王三昧中流 出普門示現也。又有一梵僧來參。仰於地上 畫半月相。僧近前添作圓相。以脚抹却。仰展 兩手。僧拂袖便出曰。我來東土禮文殊。却遇 小釋迦。又僧禮拜了。仰不顧。僧問和尚。還識 字否。仰曰。隨分。僧畫○相托呈。仰以衣袖拂 之。僧又作半月相托呈。仰以兩手作背拋勢。 僧以目視之。仰低頭。僧遶師一匝。仰便打。僧 遂出。此仰山壁立千仞。與德山臨濟峻機不 別。仰坐次。又有僧來作禮。仰不顧。僧問。師 識字否。仰云。隨分。僧右旋一匝曰。是甚麼 字。這般施設待教有識情。成何宗旨。若總無 道理。西天東土凡聖同參。觀音會下一僧來 參巖頭。以手左邊作一圓相。又右邊作一圓 相。又中心作一圓相。欲成未成。頭以手一撥。 僧無對。頭乃喝出。僧方跨門。頭却喚迴問。 汝是洪州觀音來麼。僧云。是。頭問。只如適來 左邊圓相作麼生。僧曰。是有句。頭曰。右邊圓 相聻。僧曰。是無句。頭曰。中間圓相作麼生。 僧曰。是不有不無句。頭曰。只如吾恁麼又如 何。僧曰。如刀畫水。頭打趁出。這僧不得圓相 宗旨。妄生穿鑿。若不是巖頭。幾被惑亂一上。 據這僧見仰山問識字否。乃右旋一匝。伎倆 已盡。仰山十字注也注了。說也說破。更要後 面許多粥飯氣作麼。那裏待到如此。當初纔 問師識字否。只道自來文寡。看他如何。不見。 昔有一僧。居常閑過。一僧勸云。上座年雋。可 惜虛擲寸陰。僧云。爾待教我作甚即得。勸云。 何不看經。僧云。不識字。勸云。何不問人。僧 云。是甚麼字。其勸者無語。可謂文不加點樂 不加聲也。僧又左旋一匝曰。是甚麼字。此與 尋常從東過西却從西過東。拍左邊膝此是 教意。拍右邊膝此是祖意。是同是別。仰山星 移斗轉。改十字作卍字。梵語修羅此云非天。 梵語羅睺此云障蔽。以手障日月故。此僧畫 圓相。如修羅掌日月勢。九十七種圓相。名為 修羅三昧。梵語樓至此云啼泣。賢劫千佛。為 千王子。末後得籌。最後成佛。遂啼泣云。我何 薄祐。窮底得籌。忽復笑云。我當盡取九百九 十九佛方便粧嚴。今護法神執杵者是。僧末 後作樓至勢。其意可知。仰云。如是如是。此是 諸佛護念。汝亦如是。吾亦如是。汝善護持。善 哉善哉。好去。其僧禮謝了。騰空而去。時有一 道者。曾見經五日來問。仰云。汝還見否。者 云。某正見出門騰空而去。仰云。此是西天羅 漢故來探吾。者云。某雖覩種種三昧。不辨其 理。仰云。吾以義為汝解釋。此是八種三昧。是 覺海變為義海。其體則同。然此義有因有果。 即時異時。總別不離隱身三昧也。所以道。涅 槃心易得。差別智難明。試看。天童如何下手。 頌云。
text_en: there is a single round form. Even Shakyamuni did not understand it; how could Kashyapa transmit it? The Fourteenth Patriarch, Nagarjuna, on the Dharma seat concealed his body and manifested a circle sign. Deva said, This venerable one manifests the Buddha-body form to show us. This formless samadhi takes shape like the full moon; the meaning of Buddha-nature is vast, empty, and bright, just like this. The making of circle signs in the eastern land began with National Teacher Zhong, who entrusted them to his attendant Danyuan, receiving the prophecy and transmitting them to Yangshan. Thus now they are regarded as the Guiyang house style. Monk Lianghe of Wufeng in Mingzhou once composed forty cases; Song Mingjiao wrote a preface praising them. Liang said, Circle signs have six general names: first, circle sign; second, sea of meaning; third, hidden device; fourth, study of characters; fifth, language of intent; sixth, silent discourse. The Guiyang lineage record says: Danyuan told Yangshan, The National Teacher transmitted ninety-seven circle signs of the six generations of patriarchs. Thirty years after my passing, in the south there will be a novice who will come and greatly flourish this way. I examined this prophecy in detail; it concerns your person. After Yangshan received them, he burned them with fire. One day Danyuan again said to him, The transmitted circle signs should be kept deeply secret. Yangshan said, I already burned them. Danyuan said, That works for you, but what about those who come later? Yangshan said, If the monk wants me to copy another copy, I can. Yangshan then recopied and presented it, without a single error. One day Danyuan ascended the hall; Yangshan came forth from the assembly, made a circle sign, supported it with his hands, presented it, then stood with hands crossed. Danyuan used both hands to show a crossed-fist gesture. Yangshan advanced three steps and made a woman's bow. Danyuan nodded, and Yangshan bowed. Among the ninety-seven kinds of circle signs, the crossed fists are called Rakshasa Samadhi, and the woman's bow is called Woman Samadhi. These are all samadhis, flowing forth from the King of Samadhis as universal manifestations. Also, there was an Indian monk who came to visit. Yangshan on the ground drew a half-moon sign. The monk stepped forward, added to it to make a full circle, and wiped it away with his foot. Yangshan spread both hands. The monk flicked his sleeves and went out, saying, I came to the eastern land to pay respect to Manjushri, but instead I met a little Shakyamuni. Again, a monk finished bowing, and Yangshan paid no attention. The monk asked, master, do you still recognize characters or not? Yangshan said, According to portion. The monk drew a circle sign and held it up. Yangshan brushed at it with his sleeve. The monk then made a half-moon sign and held it up. Yangshan used both hands to make a backward-throwing gesture. The monk looked at him. Yangshan lowered his head. The monk circled the master once, and Yangshan struck him. The monk then left. Here Yangshan stands like a cliff a thousand fathoms high, no different from Deshan and Linji in their steep devices. While Yangshan was seated, another monk came and bowed. Yangshan paid no attention. The monk asked, Master, do you know characters? Yangshan said, According to portion. The monk turned once to the right and said, What character is this? With setups like this, if you wait for understanding and feeling, what doctrine could it become? If there were altogether no principle, then in west and east, ordinary and sage could not study together. A monk from Guanyin's assembly came to visit Yantou. With his hand he made a circle sign on the left, then on the right made another circle sign, then in the center made a third circle sign, not yet complete. Yantou brushed with his hand once. The monk had no reply. Yantou shouted him out. As the monk was stepping across the threshold, Yantou called him back and asked, Are you from Guanyin in Hongzhou? The monk said, Yes. Yantou asked, Then just now, what was the circle sign on the left? The monk said, It is the phrase of being. Yantou said, And the right-side circle sign? The monk said, It is the phrase of nonbeing. Yantou said, What about the center circle sign? The monk said, It is the phrase of neither being nor nonbeing. Yantou said, Then what about my doing this? The monk said, Like cutting water with a knife. Yantou beat him and drove him out. This monk did not grasp the circle-sign purport, but vainly produced forced interpretations. If not for Yantou, he would almost have confused and misled people once. Judging from this monk meeting Yangshan and asking whether he knew characters, then turning once to the right, his tricks were already exhausted. Yangshan's cross annotation was already annotated; what was said was already laid bare. Why still want all the later porridge-and-rice breath? Why wait until this point? At the start, as soon as he asked whether the master knew characters, he should simply have said, I have always been sparse in letters, and see what he would do. Have you not seen: Formerly there was a monk who spent his time idly. Another monk urged him, Elder brother, you are young; it is a pity to waste every inch of time. The monk said, What exactly do you want me to do? The other urged him, Why not read sutras? The monk said, I do not know characters. The other urged him, Why not ask someone? The monk said, What character is this? The one urging him had no words. This can be called writing needing no punctuation, music needing no added tones. The monk then turned once to the left and said, What character is this? This is like the usual going from east to west and then again from west to east, slapping the left knee saying this is the teaching intent, slapping the right knee saying this is the patriarchal intent. Are they the same or different? Yangshan shifted the stars and turned the Dipper, changing the cross into a swastika sign. In Sanskrit asura means non-heavenly being. In Sanskrit Rahu means obstructing, because with his hands he obstructs sun and moon. This monk drew a circle sign like the posture of an asura holding sun and moon. Among the ninety-seven kinds of circle signs, this is called Asura Samadhi. In Sanskrit Ruci means weeping. In the Bhadrakalpa there were a thousand Buddhas, originally a thousand royal sons. He drew the lot last and became the final Buddha, so he wept and said, Why am I so thinly blessed, to draw the lot at the very end? Then suddenly he laughed and said, I shall take all the adornments and skillful means of the nine hundred and ninety-nine Buddhas. The Dharma-protecting deity now holding the pestle is he. At the end the monk made the Ruci posture; his meaning can be known. Yangshan said, Thus, thus. This is what all Buddhas protect and keep in mind. You are thus; I too am thus. You should guard it well. Good, good indeed. Go well. That monk bowed in thanks, then rose into the air and departed. At that time there was a Daoist who, having seen this, came after five days and asked. Yangshan said, Did you see it? The Daoist said, I personally saw him leave the door and soar into the air. Yangshan said, This was a western land arhat who came deliberately to test me. The Daoist said, Though I saw various samadhis, I cannot distinguish their principle. Yangshan said, I will explain them to you in terms of meaning. These are eight kinds of samadhi; this is the sea of awakening transformed into the sea of meaning. Their substance is the same, yet these meanings have cause and effect, immediate and delayed time, total and particular, not departing from the hidden-body samadhi. Therefore it is said, Nirvana mind is easy to attain; discriminating wisdom is hard to clarify. Just watch how Tiantong sets his hand to it. The verse says:
The Way circles in emptiness, never filling; the sky-seal's character not yet formed, subtly moving Carry snow to fill the river Above all avoid carving
